what_it_does: Public one-liner that empties the control (Text := '').
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas public block lines 141-174 has InjectKey/SelectAll/ClearSelection/Copy/Cut/Paste/Undo/Redo but no Clear. grep -rin 'procedure +Clear *;' over source/ hits Calculator, Cascader, Grid, HeaderControl etc. but NOT tyControls.Edit.pas / .Memo.pas / .MaskEdit.pas.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:844 'procedure Clear;'; implementation customedit.inc:106-109.
user_impact: Every ported line of Edit1.Clear / Memo1.Clear / MaskEdit1.Clear fails to compile; the workaround (Text := '') is not obvious for the memo (Lines.Clear vs Text). Inherited by TTyMemo and TTyMaskEdit as well.

what_it_does: Read/write dirty flag: set True by any user text change, cleared by a programmatic Text assignment; the standard 'has the user edited this field' test.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'Modified' over the whole source/ tree returns only unrelated hits (Controller.pas file-timestamp comments, FileSystem.pas TDateTime field, ShellListView column). No Modified/IsModified/Dirty property on any control; TTyEdit has no such field (private block Edit.pas:14-78).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:867 'property Modified: Boolean read GetModified write SetModified'; set in customedit.inc:616 (TextChanged -> Modified := True) and reset in customedit.inc:559 (RealSetText -> Modified := False).
user_impact: No way to ask whether the user touched the field; save/validate/'discard changes?' logic ported from LCL or Delphi must be rewritten with a manual OnChange flag. Missing on all three controls.

what_it_does: EchoMode (emNormal/emPassword/emNone) selects how text is echoed; PasswordChar is a single Char (default #0 = no masking) and the two are kept in sync (setting one drives the other).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas:179 'property PasswordChar: string read FPasswordChar write SetPasswordChar;' (a UTF-8 string, no default, '' = off; setter clamps to 1 codepoint, Edit.pas:605-613). grep -rin 'EchoMode' over source/ returns NOTHING.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:870 'property PasswordChar: Char read FPasswordChar write SetPasswordChar default #0'; stdctrls.pp:863 'property EchoMode: TEchoMode ... default emNormal'; coupling in customedit.inc:374-387 and 409-425 (emNone == PasswordChar ' ').
user_impact: Ported code assigning Edit.PasswordChar := '*' compiles (string accepts a char literal) but PasswordChar := #0 to turn masking OFF silently masks with NUL instead, and any use of EchoMode (notably emNone, 'show nothing at all') does not compile and has no equivalent.

what_it_does: When True (the default) the selection highlight is hidden while the control is not focused; the selection itself is preserved.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'HideSelection' over source/ hits ONLY tyControls.Memo.pas (field 151, setter 180, published 539, honoured in paint at 2781-2782) and Grid's unrelated HideSelectionWhenInactive. tyControls.Edit.pas has no HideSelection field or property; its RenderTo paints the band on 'if HasSelection' alone (Edit.pas:1658) with no focus test.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:865 'property HideSelection: Boolean read FHideSelection write SetHideSelection default True'; published on TEdit at stdctrls.pp:973; drives ES_NOHIDESEL in customedit.inc:37-38.
user_impact: An unfocused TTyEdit keeps painting its selection band, so a form with several edits shows two or three 'active-looking' selections at once. The capability is already implemented one unit away (TTyMemo) and simply not wired to the Edit.

what_it_does: Default True: the whole text is selected when the control gains focus by keyboard/Enter and on the first left click, so typing replaces the old value. AutoSelected is the 'already did it' latch.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'AutoSelect' over source/ returns NOTHING. TTyEdit.DoEnter (Edit.pas:257-268) only resets the caret blink and the IME; MouseDown (Edit.pas:1118-1147) positions the caret and collapses the selection.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:838 'property AutoSelect: Boolean read FAutoSelect write FAutoSelect default True', published on TEdit at stdctrls.pp:959, AutoSelected at 953; behaviour in customedit.inc:630-639 (DoEnter), 520-532 (MouseUp) and 460-472 (Enter key).
user_impact: Tabbing into a TTyEdit leaves the caret wherever it was instead of selecting the value, so the standard 'tab in, type the new number' data-entry flow needs an explicit SelectAll in every OnEnter handler, and forms ported from LCL/Delphi behave differently.

what_it_does: Default True on TCustomEdit: the control's height follows the font (CalculatePreferredSize returns the font-derived height and ignores width).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas published block 175-197 does not publish AutoSize, and the unit has no CalculatePreferredSize/preferred-height override; the constructor hardcodes Height := TyDensityHeight(ActiveController, 28) (Edit.pas:206). Other controls DO publish it (tyControls.Button.pas:145, Alert.pas:226, Breadcrumb.pas:269), so the mechanism exists and is simply not offered here.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:858 'property AutoSize default True' on TCustomEdit, published on TEdit at stdctrls.pp:958; customedit.inc:15-21 CalculatePreferredSize, customedit.inc:503-507 ShouldAutoAdjust.
user_impact: Raising Font.Size on a TTyEdit leaves the box its original height and clips the glyphs; the designer/user must re-height every edit by hand, and a .lfm ported from LCL (which relied on AutoSize) comes out the wrong height.

what_it_does: Caret position as a TPoint (X = character index in the line, Y = line index; for a single-line edit Y is always 0).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas:164 'property CaretPos: Integer read FCaret write SetCaretPos' — a bare codepoint index, public (not published).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:861 'property CaretPos: TPoint read GetCaretPos write SetCaretPos'; getter/setter contract documented at customedit.inc:128-143 and 670-685.
user_impact: Code written against LCL/Delphi (Edit.CaretPos := Point(n, 0), or reading CaretPos.X) does not compile; a same-named property with an incompatible type is worse than an absent one because the porting error surfaces at every call site with no hint of what the replacement is.

what_it_does: LCL: DELETES the selected text (SelText := '' when SelLength > 0).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas:150 declares it public; the body (Edit.pas:474-480) is 'BreakCoalescing; FSelAnchor := FCaret; ResetCaretBlink; Invalidate' — it only COLLAPSES the selection and never touches the text. Deleting is a different, protected method, DeleteSelection (Edit.pas:63, body 484-506).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:846 'procedure ClearSelection; virtual;'; body customedit.inc:238-242: 'if SelLength > 0 then SelText := '''';' with the doc comment 'Delete selected text.'
user_impact: The single most dangerous entry in this group: ported code that calls ClearSelection to delete the highlighted text silently keeps the text (a Delete/Clear menu item stops working) and the compiler cannot warn, because the name and signature match exactly.

what_it_does: Multicast OnChange: several observers can subscribe to text changes without stealing the single OnChange slot.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'AddHandlerOnChange' over source/ hits only tyControls.Badge.pas:329 'FTarget.AddHandlerOnChangeBounds' (the LCL TControl bounds handler, a different thing). TTyEdit has exactly one FOnChange field (Edit.pas:39) fired from DoChange (Edit.pas:286-296); same for TTyMemo (Memo.pas:131).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:853-855 AddHandlerOnChange/RemoveHandlerOnChange; TMethodList field stdctrls.pp:776; implementation customedit.inc:91-97 and the fan-out in customedit.inc:622-628 (Change).
user_impact: Library or framework code that wants to observe an edit (a validator, a dirty-tracker, a live preview) must take the one OnChange property away from the application, or the application must chain the calls by hand.

member: DragMode / DragKind / DragCursor + OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnStartDrag / OnEndDrag
what_it_does: The whole LCL drag-and-drop surface: make the control a drag source (dmAutomatic) or drop target and handle the four drag events.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Edit.pas published block 175-197 publishes none of them (and neither does the base, tyControls.Base.pas:196-246). grep over source/ for DragMode / OnDragDrop hits ONLY tyControls.Memo.pas:566-568 and 571-574 — the sibling memo publishes the full set, so this is an unwired omission on the Edit, not a library-wide policy.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:967-969 (DragCursor, DragKind, DragMode) and 995, 996, 998, 1013 (OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDrag) on TEdit.
user_impact: An edit cannot participate in drag-and-drop from the designer at all: no drop-target handler can be assigned in the Object Inspector, and a .lfm ported from LCL that sets DragMode/OnDragOver fails to stream. TTyMaskEdit inherits the same hole.

what_it_does: Right-to-left support: mirrors text direction, caret side, alignment and the horizontal scroll origin for Hebrew/Arabic.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'BidiMode' over the whole source/ tree returns exactly one hit — the comment tyControls.Memo.pas:557 'Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope.' No control implements RTL; the Edit's text layout is left-origin only (TextStartX Edit.pas:671-678, AlignOffset 680-703, DrawText always taLeftJustify at Edit.pas:1703-1715).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:960 'property BidiMode' and 976 'property ParentBidiMode' on TEdit (same pair on TMemo at 1025 and 1040).
user_impact: RTL languages are unusable in every text-input control of this library: the caret, the selection band and the horizontal scroll all run the wrong way and there is no property to ask for the other direction. Concept has no themed equivalent — a theme cannot mirror text layout.

what_it_does: TCustomEdit's constructor announces itself to assistive technology as a single-line text editor; a memo inherits the same role.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'Accessible' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING — no ty control ever assigns AccessibleRole/AccessibleName, so a TTyEdit/TTyMemo keeps TControl's default larUnknown. (The property itself is inherited and settable: controls.pp:1166.)
theirs_evidence: customedit.inc:87 'AccessibleRole := larTextEditorSingleline;' inside TCustomEdit.Create (comment '// Accessibility').
user_impact: A screen reader reads a TTyEdit as an unidentified custom control rather than a text field, so the whole self-drawn text-input family is opaque to assistive technology. One assignment per control class fixes it.

what_it_does: Public convenience method: appends one line to the end of the text (Lines.Add).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas public block 474-512 has no Append; grep -rin 'procedure Append' over source/ hits only unrelated local routines (HtmlLabel.pas:193 AppendRun, ListView.Layout.pas:759, ValueListEditor.pas:119 AppendFlat).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:936 'procedure Append(const AValue: String);'; body custommemo.inc:40-43.
user_impact: The most common memo idiom in ported code — Memo1.Append('log line') — does not compile. Lines.Add works, so this is pure API surface.

what_it_does: Two public scrollbar sub-objects exposing Position, Range, Page, Increment, Smooth, Size and Visible, so code can read or drive the memo's scroll state (e.g. pin a log view to the bottom).
ours_evidence: TTyMemo owns two TTyScrollBar instances but both are PRIVATE fields with no accessor: tyControls.Memo.pas:90 FScrollBar, :93 FHScrollBar; the only exposed handles are the protected TopRow/TopLine/SetTopLine (Memo.pas:415-423) and ScrollBarVisible (Memo.pas:431). grep over source/ for VertScrollBar/HorzScrollBar finds only Grid's unrelated VertScrollBarMode/HorzScrollBarMode enums (Grid.pas:1124-1127) — no memo-side equivalent, and no item/sub-object class is published.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:940-941 'property HorzScrollBar: TMemoScrollBar' / 'property VertScrollBar: TMemoScrollBar'; the TMemoScrollbar class with its published surface at stdctrls.pp:885-897; created in custommemo.inc:26-27.
user_impact: No public way to query or set the scroll position of a memo: 'scroll to bottom after appending', 'restore the previous scroll offset', or reading Range/Page for a custom indicator are all impossible from outside the class.

what_it_does: TCustomMemo ships with ScrollBars = ssNone and WordWrap = True: a memo dropped on a form wraps its text and shows no bars.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas:530-531 'property ScrollBars ... default ssAutoVertical' (constructor Memo.pas:638 FScrollBars := ssAutoVertical) and :534 'property WordWrap ... default False' (constructor Memo.pas:615 FWordWrap := False).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:942 'property ScrollBars: TScrollStyle ... default ssNone'; stdctrls.pp:945 'property WordWrap: Boolean ... default true'; constructor custommemo.inc:24 FWordWrap := True.
user_impact: Both defaults are inverted relative to TMemo, and because each side declares its own 'default', a .lfm streamed from an LCL form (which omits the properties it considers default) produces the OPPOSITE behaviour after porting: long lines stop wrapping and scroll sideways, and a vertical bar appears where the design had none.

what_it_does: Alignment left/center/right-justifies every line of the memo; CharCase force-uppercases or lowercases typed and assigned text.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas:556-557 states the omission explicitly ('Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope'); neither appears in the published block 513-587 and there is no FAlignment/FCharCase field. Both ARE implemented on the sibling Edit (tyControls.Edit.pas:181 Alignment with AlignOffset 680-703; :182 CharCase with ApplyCharCase 645-653), so the code to copy exists in the same library.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:1023 'property Alignment' and stdctrls.pp:1028 'property CharCase' on TMemo (declared on TCustomEdit at 857 and 862; CharCase behaviour customedit.inc:322-335 and 586-610).
user_impact: A centred title block or an upper-case-only note field cannot be built from TTyMemo, and .lfm/code ported from TMemo that sets either property fails to stream/compile.

what_it_does: Horizontal wheel / tilt-wheel notifications, which is how a non-wrapping memo is scrolled sideways on a trackpad or tilt wheel.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'MouseWheelHorz' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING. tyControls.Memo.pas publishes only OnMouseWheel (:586) and the base adds OnMouseWheelUp/Down (tyControls.Base.pas:221-222); DoMouseWheel (Memo.pas:470-471) handles the vertical axis only.
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:1076-1078 'property OnMouseWheelHorz; property OnMouseWheelLeft; property OnMouseWheelRight;' on TMemo.
user_impact: With WordWrap=False the memo can scroll horizontally (FScrollX/FHScrollBar exist) but a two-finger sideways swipe or a tilt wheel produces nothing, and an application cannot even implement it itself because the events are not surfaced.

what_it_does: Caret position as a TPoint on a multi-line control: X = column, Y = line — the natural addressing for a memo (status bar 'Ln 12, Col 4', jump-to-line, error highlighting).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas:512 'property CaretPos: Integer read GetCaretPos write SetCaretPos' — a FLAT codepoint offset (mapping helpers LineColToFlat/FlatToLineCol are PRIVATE, Memo.pas:189-190). The 2-D accessors exist but are PROTECTED: CaretLine (Memo.pas:371), CaretCol (:372), SetCaret (:373).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:919 'function GetCaretPos: TPoint; override;' / 921 SetCaretPos, inherited property declaration stdctrls.pp:861; body custommemo.inc:176-179.
user_impact: Same name, incompatible type, and the information a memo user actually wants (line and column) is not reachable at all from outside the class — every 'Ln/Col' indicator or go-to-line feature has to subclass to get at the protected getters.

what_it_does: LCL: public, DELETES the selected text. A memo inherits it unchanged from TCustomEdit.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas:392 declares ClearSelection in the PROTECTED section (protected block starts at :249, public at :474) and its documented job is the opposite of LCL's: ':391 // Collapse the selection onto the caret (anchor := caret)'. The deleting routine is the separate protected DeleteSelection (Memo.pas:282).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:846 'procedure ClearSelection; virtual;' (public on TCustomEdit, inherited by TCustomMemo); body customedit.inc:238-242 'if SelLength > 0 then SelText := '''';'.
user_impact: Two failures at once: Memo1.ClearSelection does not compile (protected), and a developer who reaches it via a subclass gets the collapse-don't-delete behaviour, so a Delete/Clear command silently leaves the text in place.

what_it_does: TCustomMemo overrides TWinControl.ScrollBy to scroll the memo's TEXT VIEW by a pixel delta (ScrollBy_WS).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas does not override ScrollBy (public block 474-512; grep for ScrollBy over source/ hits only tyControls.ScrollBox.pas), so TTyMemo inherits TWinControl.ScrollBy, which repositions CHILD CONTROLS — for a TTyMemo that is just the two embedded scrollbars (FScrollBar/FHScrollBar, Memo.pas:90/93). The real view offsets are FTopRow (:64) and FScrollX (:73), reachable only through the protected SetTopLine (:423).
theirs_evidence: stdctrls.pp:937 'procedure ScrollBy(DeltaX, DeltaY: Integer); override;'; body custommemo.inc:45-48 calling ScrollBy_WS (declared controls.pp:2385; the inherited TWinControl.ScrollBy is controls.pp:2386).
user_impact: A ported Memo1.ScrollBy(0, -40) compiles and runs but does not scroll the text — instead it drags the memo's own scrollbar children out of position, i.e. it visibly corrupts the control rather than failing loudly.

what_it_does: On an LCL memo the flat offsets index the same string Text returns — Lines.Text, whose separators are LineEnding (two characters, CR+LF, on Windows).
ours_evidence: tyControls.Memo.pas:185-188 and 502-508 define the offset as counting ONE codepoint per newline ('The flat offset counts one codepoint for the newline BETWEEN consecutive logical lines'); implemented in the private LineColToFlat/FlatToLineCol (Memo.pas:189-190) behind SelStart (:509), SelLength (:510), CaretPos (:512).
theirs_evidence: custommemo.inc:150-156 'RealGetText: Result := Lines.Text' (LineEnding-separated), and customedit.inc:118-121 'GetSelText: UTF8Copy(Text, SelStart + 1, SelLength)' — so SelStart/SelLength are offsets into that CRLF-bearing string.
user_impact: Any ported code that computes a flat offset from the text itself (Pos(...)-1, Length of a prefix, a saved caret offset) lands one character earlier per preceding line on Windows: the caret/selection drifts further off the longer the document, and the error is invisible in single-line tests.

what_it_does: LCL/Delphi mask language: ~20 token codes (l/L letter, a/A alphanumeric, c/C any UTF-8 char, 9/0 digit, # digit-or-sign, h/H hex, b/B binary, > < case forcing, \\ escape, [abc] sets, : / locale separators, ! trim), plus the three-field 'mask;save;blank' form.
ours_evidence: tyControls.MaskEdit.pas:63 'property EditMask: string read FMask write SetMask stored False' — an alias on our own three-code language (TyMaskSlotAccepts, MaskEdit.pas:68-77: '#' digit, 'L' letter, 'C' non-space; everything else literal). The unit documents the trap itself at MaskEdit.pas:51-62: a Lazarus mask 'is ACCEPTED and will silently mean something else -- '!90:00;1;_' has no '#' in it, so every character of it becomes a literal and the field takes no input at all'. Note 'C' also cannot take a multibyte char: UTF8KeyPress only handles Length(UTF8Key)=1 and swallows the rest (MaskEdit.pas:173, 181), while LCL's 'c'/'C' accept any UTF-8 codepoint.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:307 'property EditMask: string read FRealEditMask write SetEditMask'; token constants maskedit.pp:67-90; the case-folding/optional/set machinery in tMaskedType maskedit.pp:101-138; UTF-8 char insertion via CanInsertChar(Ch: TUtf8Char) maskedit.pp:260.
user_impact: The worst kind of porting break: same property name, same type, compiles clean, and the field then silently accepts no input (or the wrong input) because the mask string means something else. Also blocks copying any of the thousands of published Delphi/Lazarus mask strings.

what_it_does: The raw contents of the control INCLUDING mask literals and blank placeholders, as distinct from Text (the data). Read/write; the pair is how mask edits separate presentation from value.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'EditText' over source/ hits only tyControls.SpinEdit.pas's unrelated private FEditText buffer. TTyMaskEdit exposes only Mask/EditMask (MaskEdit.pas:50, 63) and IsComplete (:48); the raw significant characters can be recovered only by calling the unit-level TyMaskExtract(Mask, Text) function (MaskEdit.pas:17) by hand.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:303 'property EditText: string read GetEditText write SetEditText' (protected) promoted to public on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:329.
user_impact: No supported way to read or set the field's literal display string, so 'restore exactly what the user saw' and partial-value round-tripping have no API; the value/display split that defines a mask edit is missing.

what_it_does: Read-only Boolean: is a (non-empty, valid) mask currently in force? The standard guard before running mask-specific logic.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'IsMasked' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING. TTyMaskEdit's public surface is one method, IsComplete (MaskEdit.pas:48, body 229-232), which answers a different question (are all slots FILLED); callers must test Mask <> '' themselves.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:304 'property IsMasked: Boolean read GetIsMasked' (protected), public on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:328; getter declared maskedit.pp:240.
user_impact: Generic code that handles both masked and unmasked edits has no property to branch on, and IsComplete is easy to mistake for it (an empty mask makes IsComplete return False, not 'unmasked').

what_it_does: The blank placeholder character (default '_') that fills unentered slots, so an empty date field reads '__/__/____' and the user can see how much is left to type.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'SpaceChar' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING. Our model has no placeholder concept at all: display text is rebuilt from the significant characters by TyMaskApply, which stops at the end of input and deliberately drops the pending literal (MaskEdit.pas:79-101, ':93 out of input: drop any pending trailing literal'), so an empty masked field renders EMPTY.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:305 'property SpaceChar: Char read FSpaceChar write SetSpaceChar' (protected), published on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:364; default '_' documented at maskedit.pp:214 and the DefaultBlank constant at maskedit.pp:93.
user_impact: A masked field gives the user no shape to fill in — no '__/__/____' skeleton, no indication of how many characters the mask wants — which is the main reason mask edits exist. TextHint partly compensates but disappears as soon as one character is typed.

what_it_does: Public virtual: validates the current contents against the mask and, if incomplete/invalid, raises EDBEditError or fires OnValidationError (per ValidationErrorMode). The documented 'is this field acceptable?' entry point, also called on exit.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ValidateEdit' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING. The nearest thing is the query-only function IsComplete (MaskEdit.pas:48, body 229-232 -> TyMaskIsComplete) which returns a Boolean and never raises, never notifies, and is not called on focus loss (no DoExit override in the unit).
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:315 'procedure ValidateEdit; virtual;'; error routing DoValidationError maskedit.pp:268, mode property 318, event 321.
user_impact: There is no built-in validation moment: a half-typed '12/__/____' leaves the control silently and reaches business code unless the developer remembers to poll IsComplete at every exit point.

what_it_does: Opts the mask parser into Lazarus set syntax — [abc], [a-z], [!abc] negation, [|abc] optional — so a slot can accept an arbitrary character class.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'EnableSets' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING; our parser accepts exactly three slot codes and treats '[', ']', '!', '|', '-' as literals (TyMaskSlotAccepts MaskEdit.pas:68-77, TyMaskApply 79-101).
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:317 'property EnableSets: Boolean read FEnableSets write FEnableSets', published on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:346; set tokens maskedit.pp:86-90; parser ParseSet maskedit.pp:239.
user_impact: Custom character classes are impossible: masks like a product code whose second slot must be one of [ABX] cannot be expressed, and a mask string using set syntax degrades into literals with no error.

what_it_does: Chooses how a failed validation is reported: mvemException (raise, the default) or mvemEvent (call OnValidationError instead).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ValidationError' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING; TTyMaskEdit has no validation reporting at all (published surface is Mask + EditMask only, MaskEdit.pas:49-63).
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:318 'property ValidationErrorMode: TMaskEditValidationErrorMode ... default mvemException', published on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:358; enum declared maskedit.pp:148.
user_impact: Applications cannot choose between an exception and a quiet callback for bad input — there is no reporting channel to configure in the first place.

what_it_does: Fired when the contents fail mask validation (under mvemEvent), letting the form show its own message instead of an exception dialog.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnValidat' over the whole source/ tree returns NOTHING. TTyMaskEdit publishes no events of its own (MaskEdit.pas:49-63); the inherited surface stops at TTyEdit's OnChange/OnClick (Edit.pas:195-196) plus the base events (Base.pas:212-239).
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:321 'property OnValidationError: TNotifyEvent read FOnValidationError write FOnValidationError', published on TMaskEdit at maskedit.pp:389.
user_impact: No notification hook for invalid input: the designer's Events tab offers nothing between 'text changed' and manual polling of IsComplete.

what_it_does: Resets the field to the EMPTY MASK — all literals restored, every editable slot back to the blank char — not merely to an empty string.
ours_evidence: grep for 'procedure Clear;' in tyControls.MaskEdit.pas / .Edit.pas / .Memo.pas returns nothing (MaskEdit.pas public section is just IsComplete, :46-48). The closest equivalent is what SetMask does internally, 'Text := ''' (MaskEdit.pas:154), which leaves the control blank rather than showing the mask skeleton.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:313 'procedure Clear;' declared separately on TCustomMaskEdit (shadowing TCustomEdit.Clear at stdctrls.pp:844) precisely because a masked clear must re-apply the mask.
user_impact: A Reset/Clear button on a form with masked fields cannot restore the '__/__/____' starting state; ported MaskEdit1.Clear does not compile.

what_it_does: LCL routes every Text assignment through the mask: RealSetText -> SetTextApplyMask/ApplyMaskToText pads, truncates and restores literals so the control can never hold a value the mask disallows.
ours_evidence: tyControls.MaskEdit.pas overrides UTF8KeyPress (:36), KeyDown (:37) and FilterInsert (:45) — but NOT the Text setter. A direct write therefore lands in the plain TTyEdit.SetText (tyControls.Edit.pas:558-574), which stores the string verbatim; the mask is never consulted, so MaskEdit.Text := 'hello' sticks in a '####-##-##' field and the subsequent TyMaskExtract/IsComplete read back nonsense. This is the same hole the unit's own comment (MaskEdit.pas:38-44) describes for the paste path, which WAS fixed via FilterInsert.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:270 'procedure RealSetText(const AValue: TCaption); override;' plus maskedit.pp:274 SetTextApplyMask and 265 ApplyMaskToText; the design note at maskedit.pp:184-196 explains that all writes must funnel through the masked setter.
user_impact: Programmatic assignment (loading a record into the form, restoring a draft) bypasses the mask entirely, so the control's central invariant — 'contents always conform to the mask' — does not hold, and IsComplete then answers about a string the mask never approved.

what_it_does: LCL mask editing is positional overwrite: the caret can be placed in (or arrowed/tabbed to) any editable slot, typing overwrites just that slot, literals are skipped automatically, and Backspace/Delete blank the slot under the caret.
ours_evidence: TTyMaskEdit is append-only by construction: ApplyRaw always parks the caret at the end ('append-only: caret always at the end', tyControls.MaskEdit.pas:157-161), UTF8KeyPress only ever appends to the extracted raw string (MaskEdit.pas:163-182) and KeyDown maps BOTH Backspace and Delete to 'drop the last significant char' regardless of caret position (MaskEdit.pas:184-200, comment at 189-192). Inherited caret navigation (TTyEdit.KeyDown arrows/Home/End, Edit.pas:1460-1613) still moves the caret, so the visible caret and the edit point disagree.
theirs_evidence: maskedit.pp:244-249 SetCursorPos / SelectNextChar / SelectPrevChar / SelectFirstChar / GotoEnd, maskedit.pp:259-262 InsertChar / CanInsertChar / DeleteSelected / DeleteChars(NextChar), and the protected maskedit.pp:302 CheckCursor that keeps the caret on an editable slot.
user_impact: Correcting one wrong digit in the middle of a date means deleting everything after it and retyping; and because arrows still move the caret while typing still appends, the control does something other than what the caret shows — a usability break, not just a missing API.

what_it_does: Chooses which side of the caption the check/radio indicator sits on. taLeftJustify sets BS_RIGHTBUTTON, i.e. the indicator is drawn to the RIGHT of the text; the default taRightJustify is the normal indicator-then-text order.
ours_evidence: tyControls.CheckBox.pas:53-75 (TTyCheckBox published) and :109-125 (TTyRadioButton published) contain no Alignment. Case-insensitive grep for '\bAlignment\b' over all of source/*.pas returns 30+ hits but none on either class — the only nearby one is tyControls.GroupBox.pas:28 'property Alignment: TAlignment ... default taLeftJustify', which is the group-box CAPTION alignment, a different type and a different meaning. Grep for 'TLeftRight' over source/ returned nothing. RenderTo hard-codes indicator-left: tyControls.CheckBox.pas:256-268 builds BoxRect at ContentRect.Left then TextRect at BoxRect.Right+Gap (same shape at :534-549 for the radio).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1358 'property Alignment: TLeftRight read GetAlignment write SetAlignment default taRightJustify'; republished at :1376 (TCheckBox) and :1503 (TRadioButton). Implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckbox.inc:74-88 and :269-274 (CreateParams adds BS_RIGHTBUTTON when taLeftJustify).
user_impact: A form ported from Lazarus that set Alignment=taLeftJustify (a common look for right-hand-side option lists, and the standard order in RTL locales) will not compile against TTyCheckBox/TTyRadioButton, and there is no way to get the indicator on the right at all.

what_it_does: Whether the control sizes itself to its caption out of the box.
ours_evidence: tyControls.CheckBox.pas:58 'property AutoSize;' (TTyCheckBox) and :112 (TTyRadioButton) re-publish the inherited declaration, so the declared default stays TControl's False; the comment at :54-57 says so explicitly ('默认关'). Constructors instead pin a size: :136-137 Width:=130; Height:=TyDensityHeight(...,22) and :416-417 the same. Grep 'property AutoSize' over source/ shows 20 controls re-publish it the same way (Button.pas:145, TyLabel.pas:95, ...), so the omission of 'default True' here is a deliberate library-wide convention, not an oversight — but it still differs from LCL.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1379 'property AutoSize default True;' (TCheckBox) and :1505 the same for TRadioButton. TCustomCheckBox.TextChanged calls InvalidatePreferredSize + AdjustSize (include/customcheckbox.inc:260-267).
user_impact: A .lfm streamed from Lazarus carries no AutoSize line when it is True (that being the declared default there); loaded here it silently becomes False, so a checkbox whose caption is longer than the designed width (a translation, a denser skin, a heavier font) gets ellipsised instead of growing.

what_it_does: Whether every radio button in a set is its own Tab stop. LCL deliberately keeps radios OUT of the Tab cycle (the group is entered once, then arrow keys move within it).
ours_evidence: tyControls.CheckBox.pas:119 'property TabStop default True;' with the comment at :118 stating the default was changed to match the constructor; constructor sets TabStop:=True at :415.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1527 'property TabStop default False;' (TRadioButton). Compare :1402 where TCheckBox uses 'default True' — the asymmetry is intentional. TCustomRadioGroup reinforces it by leaving TabStop on only the checked child (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:553-563 UpdateTabStops).
user_impact: On a ported form with five radio options, Tab now visits all five instead of one, so keyboard traversal of a dialog takes many more presses and no longer matches the platform convention.

what_it_does: Exposes the accelerator LCL derived from the '&' in the caption, so host code (a keyboard-shortcut cheat-sheet, a help overlay, an automated test) can read what key activates this control.
ours_evidence: Grep for 'ShortCut' (case-insensitive) over source/ returns hits only in Form.pas (IsShortcut/menu dispatch, :285/:1591-1601) and Menu.pas (menu item ShortCutToText, :466-470) — nothing on either checkbox class and no TShortcut-typed property anywhere outside the menu path. Our accelerator machinery is tyControls.Accel (TyAccelRegister/TyIsAccelKey, tyControls.CheckBox.pas:134, :146-155) which handles the key but publishes nothing readable.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1361-1362 'property ShortCut: TShortcut read FShortCut; property ShortCutKey2: TShortcut read FShortCutKey2;' both in the public section; filled in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckbox.inc:240-258 (WSSetText → DeleteAmpersands → Menus.ShortCut).
user_impact: Code that enumerated controls to build a shortcut list, or asserted on the parsed accelerator in a test, has nothing to read here and must re-parse Caption itself.

what_it_does: Two-way binding between a linked TAction's Checked and the control's Checked/State: assigning Action checks the box, clicking the box updates the action (and, in LCL, TAction.Grayed follows cbGrayed).
ours_evidence: Grep for 'GetActionLinkClass', 'ActionLink' and 'IsCheckedLinked' (case-insensitive) over the whole of source/ returned NO matches. Action is published only via the base class (tyControls.Base.pas:231 'property Action;'), which inherits TWinControl's link — Caption/Enabled/Hint/Visible/OnExecute sync, but nothing for Checked. Our SetState (tyControls.CheckBox.pas:173-179) touches FState and OnChange only.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1185 'function GetActionLinkClass: TControlActionLinkClass; override;' on TButtonControl, and :1200-1207 TButtonActionLink with 'procedure SetChecked' + 'function IsCheckedLinked: Boolean; override'. The state path honours it: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckbox.inc:32-42 and :55-69 route through TCustomAction.Checked/Grayed.
user_impact: A ported form that drove a checkbox from a TAction (the standard way to keep a menu item, a toolbar toggle and a checkbox in sync) silently loses the sync: the checkbox no longer reflects Action.Checked and clicking it no longer updates the action or the menu item.

what_it_does: Right-to-left layout: mirrors the control's content (indicator moves to the right of the caption, text aligns right, child grids fill right-to-left) for Arabic/Hebrew locales.
ours_evidence: BiDiMode is inherited PUBLIC from TControl so it can be assigned, but nothing in the library reads it: grep for 'BidiMode' over source/ returns exactly one hit, a comment in tyControls.Memo.pas:557 that explicitly declares it out of scope ('Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope'). Grep for 'IsRightToLeft', 'RightToLeft' and 'bdRightToLeft' over all of source/ returned NO matches, so neither the painter nor any control mirrors. No ty class publishes BiDiMode/ParentBiDiMode.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1380 + :1397 (TCheckBox BidiMode/ParentBidiMode), :1506 + :1519 (TRadioButton), :189 + :205 (TGroupBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:793 + :811 (TRadioGroup), :919 + :936 (TCheckGroup). Backed by TControl.BiDiMode at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1834-1835 (public, default bdLeftToRight).
user_impact: An app localised to an RTL language cannot mirror any control in this group; the whole family stays LTR (indicator left, caption left-aligned, columns filling left-to-right) while the surrounding native LCL controls flip, so the form looks half-mirrored.

member: DragMode, DragKind, DragCursor, OnStartDrag, OnDragOver, OnDragDrop, OnEndDrag
what_it_does: The LCL drag-and-drop / drag-docking surface every TControl implements: dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down, and the four events let a target accept the payload.
ours_evidence: Neither base class publishes any of them — tyControls.Base.pas:196-246 (TTyCustomControl published) lists no Drag* or OnDrag*; nor do tyControls.CheckBox.pas:53-75/:109-125, tyControls.GroupBox.pas:26-33, tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:53-57, tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:52-63. Grep 'property DragMode|property DragCursor|property DragKind|property OnDragDrop|property OnDragOver|property OnEndDrag|property OnStartDrag' over source/ shows the capability IS wired elsewhere in this library — tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574 publishes all seven — so this is a not-wired case, not an unimplemented one (TControl supplies the machinery).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1387-1389 and :1408-1411/:1426 (TCheckBox), :1513-1515 and :1533-1535/:1550 (TRadioButton), :199-201 and :219-224/:241 (TGroupBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:804-805 and :825-827/:845 (TRadioGroup), :930-931 and :950-952/:968 (TCheckGroup). Declared on TControl at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1571-1572.
user_impact: A ported form that dragged an item onto a group box, or set DragMode=dmAutomatic on a checkbox, will not compile and cannot get the behaviour back — the properties are simply not visible in the OI or streamable from a .lfm even though the underlying TControl support is there.

member: State: TCheckBoxState / AllowGrayed (tri-state on the button-shaped checkbox)
what_it_does: TToggleBox is a checkbox drawn as a latching push button, and it keeps the full checkbox contract: Checked, State (cbUnchecked/cbChecked/cbGrayed) and AllowGrayed.
ours_evidence: There is no TTyToggleBox: grep for '\bToggleBox\b' over source/ returns no type. The two nearest are tyControls.ToggleSwitch.pas — which itself claims the role at :88 ('Optional text label drawn to the RIGHT of the switch (TToggleBox parity)') but publishes only 'property Checked: Boolean' (:87), no State/AllowGrayed — and tyControls.Button.pas:159 'property Down: Boolean ... default False' (a latching :selected button, also two-state only). So the toggle shape exists under two other names; the third (grayed) state does not.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1432-1486 TToggleBox = class(TCustomCheckBox), publishing 'property AllowGrayed;' at :1441 and 'property State;' at :1464 alongside Checked at :1448.
user_impact: A ported TToggleBox has to be hand-mapped to TTyToggleSwitch or TTyButton.Down, and any code that used its indeterminate state (State := cbGrayed for 'mixed', the usual 'some children selected' indicator) has nowhere to go.

what_it_does: Lets the frame size itself to the children it contains.
ours_evidence: tyControls.GroupBox.pas:26-33 published block = Caption, Alignment, Align, Anchors, StyleClass, Controller — no AutoSize; the base tyControls.Base.pas:196-246 does not publish it either, and TTyCheckGroup (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:53-57) / TTyRadioGroup (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:52-63) add nothing. Grep 'property AutoSize' over source/ shows 20 other ty controls DO re-publish it (Button.pas:145, CheckBox.pas:58, ToggleSwitch.pas:86, ...), so the container family is the odd one out. TTyGroupBox has no CalculatePreferredSize override either, so publishing alone would not be enough.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:188 'property AutoSize;' (TGroupBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:792 (TRadioGroup) and :918 (TCheckGroup).
user_impact: A group box cannot be made to hug its contents; every ported form that relied on AutoSize gets a fixed 185x105-ish frame that either clips its children or leaves a wide empty margin, and the property is missing from the OI so the user cannot even try.

what_it_does: LCL's per-container child layout engine: Layout (cclLeftToRightThenTopToBottom / cclTopToBottomThenLeftToRight), ControlsPerLine, LeftRightSpacing / TopBottomSpacing, HorizontalSpacing / VerticalSpacing, EnlargeHorizontal/Vertical and ShrinkHorizontal/Vertical (crsHomogenousChildResize, crsScaleChilds, crsAnchorAligning). It is how LCL group boxes tile their children into a grid.
ours_evidence: Grep 'property ChildSizing' over the whole of source/ returned NO matches; grep for 'ChildSizing' at all returns nothing. TTyGroupBox insets a client rect (tyControls.GroupBox.pas:46-65 AdjustClientRect) and leaves placement to LCL anchors; the two group subclasses each hand-roll their own grid instead — TyCheckGroupCellRect (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:72-103) and TyRadioGroupCellRect (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:85-126) — with the row pitch and column split hard-coded rather than driven by a ChildSizing object.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:192 'property ChildSizing;' (TGroupBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:796 (TRadioGroup), :922 (TCheckGroup). Both LCL group constructors configure it heavily — C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:130-137 and C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:80-87 — and Columns/ColumnLayout/AutoFill are implemented purely by writing into it (customcheckgroup.inc:258-268, :179-195).
user_impact: A ported .lfm that carried a ChildSizing block on a group box will not load that block, so the child grid (spacing, controls per line, homogeneous resize) silently reverts to plain anchoring, and there is no property to reconfigure it here.

what_it_does: Sets/streams the size of the CLIENT area rather than the outer bounds — on a group box the two differ by the caption band and the frame, so it is the natural way to say 'I need this much room inside'.
ours_evidence: Not published anywhere: grep 'property ClientWidth|property ClientHeight' over source/ returned NO matches. They exist at runtime only because TControl declares them public, so this is purely a design-time/streaming gap. Our client inset is real and non-trivial (tyControls.GroupBox.pas:46-65 subtracts the caption band plus themed padding on three sides), which is exactly what makes the outer-vs-client distinction matter here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:193-194 'property ClientHeight; property ClientWidth;' (TGroupBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:797-798 (TRadioGroup), :923-924 (TCheckGroup). Declared public with stored-flags on TControl at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1796-1799.
user_impact: A .lfm ported from Lazarus that pinned ClientHeight/ClientWidth on a group box loses those lines on load, and a designer user cannot type a client size in the OI — they have to add the frame/caption inset by hand.

member: DockSite + OnDockDrop, OnDockOver, OnEndDock, OnGetSiteInfo, OnStartDock, OnUnDock
what_it_does: Makes the group box a docking host: other controls can be docked into it, with the six events driving accept/place/undock.
ours_evidence: Grep over source/ for these names finds nothing on any ty container: no 'DockSite', no 'OnDockDrop', no 'OnGetSiteInfo'. tyControls.GroupBox.pas:26-33 is the complete published list (Caption, Alignment, Align, Anchors, StyleClass, Controller) and tyControls.Base.pas:196-246 adds no docking members. TTyGroupBox does set csAcceptsControls (tyControls.GroupBox.pas:73) so it is a real container — the docking layer on top is what is missing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:197 'property DockSite;' and the events at :220-221 (OnDockDrop/OnDockOver), :223 (OnEndDock), :227 (OnGetSiteInfo), :240 (OnStartDock), :242 (OnUnDock). TWinControl.DockSite at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2336.
user_impact: A ported form that used a group box as a dock target (a common shape for tool panels) will not compile against these names and cannot get docking back on this control.

what_it_does: Switches the child grid between 'stretch the items to fill the box evenly' (True → ChildSizing.Enlarge* = crsHomogenousChildResize) and 'leave each item its natural size and just anchor them' (False → crsAnchorAligning).
ours_evidence: Grep 'property AutoFill' and 'AutoFill' (case-insensitive) over the whole of source/ returned NO matches. Both groups always fill: TyCheckGroupCellRect divides the full client width by the column count and gives the last column the remainder (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:91-102), and TyRadioGroupCellRect does the same plus vertically centres the grid (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:104-125). There is no way to opt out.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:900 'property AutoFill: boolean read FAutoFill write SetAutoFill;' (TCustomCheckGroup, published on TCheckGroup at :917) and :772 the same on TCustomRadioGroup (published on TRadioGroup at :791). Implementations: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:179-195 and C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:583-599; both constructors set FAutoFill:=true (customcheckgroup.inc:129, radiogroup.inc:74).
user_impact: A ported group that set AutoFill=False to keep short captions from being stretched across a wide box will not compile, and the stretched layout cannot be turned off.

member: Buttons[Index]: TCheckBox (public) — ours is CheckBoxAt(), protected
what_it_does: Hands out the hosted child checkbox so host code can reach anything the group does not re-expose (its Font, Hint, Enabled, PopupMenu, an event hook).
ours_evidence: tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:39 'function CheckBoxAt(AIndex: Integer): TTyCheckBox;' — declared under 'protected' (the section opens at :34) with a comment at :35-38 saying that handing children out publicly is deliberately refused; implementation at :282-286 returns nil out of range instead of raising. So the capability exists, under a different name AND a narrower visibility.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:901 'property Buttons[Index: integer]: TCheckBox read GetButton;' in the public section, republished implicitly on TCheckGroup; getter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:321-326 (raises rsIndexOutOfBounds out of range).
user_impact: Ported code written as CheckGroup1.Buttons[2].Enabled := False does not compile, and because our equivalent is protected it cannot even be renamed at the call site — the caller has to subclass the group.

what_it_does: Hands out the hosted child radio button by index.
ours_evidence: No accessor of any visibility: tyControls.RadioGroup.pas keeps FButtons as a private 'array of TTyRadioButton' (:28) and the class has no Buttons property and no ButtonAt/RadioAt function — the protected section is only SetParent/DoOnResize/SetController (:41-46) and the public section only Create/Destroy/Count (:47-51). Grep over source/ finds no 'property Buttons'. Note the sibling TTyCheckGroup does at least offer the protected CheckBoxAt (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:39), so this class is missing even that.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:773 'property Buttons[Index: integer]: TRadioButton read GetButton;' (public on TCustomRadioGroup); getter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:534-540.
user_impact: There is no way to reach an individual option — to disable one choice, retint it, attach a hint, or assert on it in a test — short of walking Controls[] and type-casting, which also picks up nothing useful because the children are internal.

what_it_does: Enables/disables ONE item of the check group while the rest stay usable (and, in LCL, the flag is persisted with the checked state).
ours_evidence: Grep 'CheckEnabled' (case-insensitive) over the whole of source/ returned NO matches. tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:53-57 published = Items, Columns, OnItemChange; public surface = Count (:47), CheckedCount (:49), Checked[] (:52). Per-item enabling is not reachable another way either, because the children are handed out only through the protected CheckBoxAt (:39).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:904 'property CheckEnabled[Index: integer]: boolean read GetCheckEnabled write SetCheckEnabled;'; implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:288-301, and it is part of the streamed state (inc:98-99, :381, :400).
user_impact: The standard 'this option is not available in your edition' pattern — one greyed line in an otherwise live check list — is impossible; the only lever is Enabled on the whole group.

what_it_does: Chooses the fill order of the item grid: clHorizontalThenVertical fills across each row first, clVerticalThenHorizontal fills down each column first.
ours_evidence: The property does not exist — grep 'ColumnLayout' over source/ returns exactly ONE hit, a comment: tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:21 ('LCL's own TRadioGroup defaults the other way -- ColumnLayout = clHorizontalThenVertical (extctrls.pp) -- so a form ported from Lazarus will see its items in a different order here'). Both of our layouts are hard-wired column-major: tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:102-103 'col := AIndex div rows; row := AIndex mod rows' and tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:87-88 the same over rowsPerCol.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:906 (TCustomCheckGroup) and :777 (TCustomRadioGroup) 'property ColumnLayout: TColumnLayout read ... default clHorizontalThenVertical'; enum at :712-715; implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:303-312 and radiogroup.inc:601-610; both constructors seed clHorizontalThenVertical (customcheckgroup.inc:127, radiogroup.inc:79).
user_impact: Two failures at once: the property is missing so ported code that set it will not compile, AND the default differs — a ported 6-item, 2-column group that read 1 2 / 3 4 / 5 6 in Lazarus now reads 1 4 / 2 5 / 3 6, silently reordering a visible option list.

what_it_does: Reports how many rows the current item count occupies at the current Columns — the number host code needs to compute a sensible height for the box.
ours_evidence: Grep 'function Rows' over source/ returns nothing for these classes (the only near hit is tyControls.Grid.pas:1560 RowsDisplayedConsecutively, unrelated). Public surface is Count/CheckedCount only (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:47-52) and Count only (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:51). The row count IS computed internally — tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:84 'rowsPerCol := (ACount + cols - 1) div cols' and tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:98 'rows := (ACount + AColumns - 1) div AColumns' — but only inside the pure cell-rect helpers, never surfaced.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:898 'function Rows: integer;' (TCustomCheckGroup, public) and :770 the same on TCustomRadioGroup; bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:438-444 and radiogroup.inc:139-145.
user_impact: Code that sized a group box from its content (Height := Group.Rows * RowHeight + Margin — the usual way to fit a dynamically-populated group, and doubly needed here because AutoSize is unpublished) has to duplicate the ceil-divide.

member: DefineProperties / ReadData / WriteData — the binary 'Data' property that streams per-item Checked + CheckEnabled
what_it_does: Persists which items are ticked (and which are individually enabled) into the .lfm, so a designer-set or programmatically-set check state survives save/load.
ours_evidence: Grep for 'DefineProperties', 'ReadData' and 'WriteData' over the WHOLE of source/ returned NO matches — no ty control streams custom data. TTyCheckGroup publishes Items and Columns (tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:54-55) but Checked[] is public-only (:52), so nothing about the check state is written; on load, RebuildCheckBoxes creates every child unchecked (:192-209, checked state only restored from an in-memory snapshot taken moments earlier at :184-186).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:886-888 'procedure DefineProperties(Filer: TFiler); override; procedure ReadData(Stream: TStream); procedure WriteData(Stream: TStream);'; bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:361-405 — Filer.DefineBinaryProperty('Data', ...) packs bit 0 = Checked, bit 1 = CheckEnabled per item.
user_impact: Ticking boxes in the designer, or loading a Lazarus .lfm that has a Data blob, produces an all-unchecked group at run time — the designer state is silently dropped and every default has to be re-applied in FormCreate.

member: OnItemClick: TCheckGroupClicked — ours is OnItemChange: TCheckGroupItemEvent
what_it_does: Fires when the user toggles item Index. Identical signature (Sender: TObject; Index/AIndex: Integer), different event and type name.
ours_evidence: tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:9 'TCheckGroupItemEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; AIndex: Integer) of object;' and :56 'property OnItemChange: TCheckGroupItemEvent read FOnItemChange write FOnItemChange;'. Grep 'OnItemClick' over source/ shows the LCL name IS used elsewhere in the library — tyControls.ListGroupPanel.pas:216 'property OnItemClick: TTyListGroupItemEvent' — so the divergence is local to this control, not a library-wide convention.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:852 'TCheckGroupClicked = procedure(Sender: TObject; Index: integer) of object;' and :907 'property OnItemClick: TCheckGroupClicked read FOnItemClick write FOnItemClick;', published on TCheckGroup at :955. Fired from C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:206-211 (DoClick).
user_impact: Every ported handler assignment and every .lfm OnItemClick= line has to be renamed by hand, and the handler's declared type changes too; the compiler error points at the property name, not at the fact that the feature exists under another one.

member: Child key-event forwarding (ItemKeyDown / ItemKeyUp / ItemKeyPress / ItemUTF8KeyPress → the group's OnKeyDown / OnKeyUp / OnKeyPress / OnUTF8KeyPress)
what_it_does: LCL hooks every child item's key events and re-raises them on the GROUP, so a handler on the group sees keys typed while focus is on any item — that is the only reason TRadioGroup/TCheckGroup can publish OnKeyDown at all, since the group itself never holds focus.
ours_evidence: Our groups wire only OnChange on each child — tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:206 'cb.OnChange := @ChildChanged;' and tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:217 'rb.OnChange := @ChildChanged;' — and nothing else; there is no ItemKeyDown/ItemKeyUp/ItemKeyPress/ItemUTF8KeyPress anywhere (grep over source/ finds no such handlers). The group therefore publishes OnKeyDown/OnKeyUp/OnKeyPress/OnUTF8KeyPress only through the base (tyControls.Base.pas:233-236), where they can never fire: focus lives on the child TTyCheckBox/TTyRadioButton (TabStop:=True in their constructors, tyControls.CheckBox.pas:135 and :415).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:147-171 (four Item* handlers calling the group's KeyDown/KeyUp/KeyPress/UTF8KeyPress) wired at inc:238-241; the same in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:312-329 wired at inc:188-191. Published on the groups at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:956-958 + :969 and :832-834 + :846.
user_impact: A ported form with an OnKeyDown on the radio/check group (the usual place to catch Enter or a letter shortcut for the whole option block) silently never fires — the handler is still assignable, which is what makes it a silent failure rather than a compile error.

member: Out-of-range index handling on Checked[] / ItemIndex (raise vs. silent)
what_it_does: LCL raises a descriptive exception (rsIndexOutOfBounds / rsIndexOutOfBoundsMinusOne naming the class, the bad index and the maximum) when an item index is out of range.
ours_evidence: Deliberately silent, and documented as such: tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:50-51 'Out-of-range read -> False; out-of-range write -> ignored', implemented at :255-260 (GetChecked → Exit(False)) and :262-267 (SetChecked → Exit); CheckBoxAt at :282-286 returns nil. TTyRadioGroup.SetItemIndex goes further and treats any out-of-range value as 'clear the selection' (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:290-311, the else-branch at :304-306 unchecks everything). Grep over source/ finds no rsIndexOutOfBounds-style raise for these classes.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcheckgroup.inc:173-177 RaiseIndexOutOfBounds, called from GetChecked/SetChecked/GetCheckEnabled/SetCheckEnabled/GetButton (inc:288-338). C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:387-388 'if (Value < -1) or (Value >= FItems.Count) then raise Exception.CreateFmt(rsIndexOutOfBoundsMinusOne, ...)'.
user_impact: An off-by-one that Lazarus reported immediately as an exception at the guilty line now fails silently: Checked[n] reads False for an item that does not exist, a write is dropped, and ItemIndex := (stale index) quietly wipes the user's selection instead of complaining.

what_it_does: The 'may the user change the selection?' hook — always True in the base, overridden by descendants (this is the seam TDBRadioGroup and read-only variants use) and callable by host code before offering a change.
ours_evidence: Grep 'CanModify' (case-insensitive) over the whole of source/ returned NO matches. TTyRadioGroup's public surface is Create/Destroy/Count only (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:47-51) and there is no protected virtual gate either (:41-46 = SetParent/DoOnResize/SetController); clicks go straight through TTyRadioButton.Click → SetChecked (tyControls.CheckBox.pas:478-483).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:768 'function CanModify: boolean; virtual;' (public on TCustomRadioGroup); body C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:493-496.
user_impact: Ported code that called CanModify, or a descendant that overrode it to make a group read-only, has no counterpart; there is no single place to veto a selection change short of disabling the whole group.

what_it_does: Fire when focus enters/leaves an individual radio item, with Sender = that item — the hook for per-option help text, a status-bar hint, or a preview that follows the keyboard.
ours_evidence: Grep 'OnItemEnter' and 'OnItemExit' over the whole of source/ returned NO matches. TTyRadioGroup publishes only Items, Columns, ItemIndex, OnSelectionChanged, Caption, Alignment (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:52-63); the children get exactly one hook, OnChange (:217), so nothing observes their focus. The base's OnEnter/OnExit (tyControls.Base.pas:237-238) fire for the group itself, which never holds focus.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:779-780 'property OnItemEnter: TNotifyEvent ...; property OnItemExit: TNotifyEvent ...;', published on TRadioGroup at :830-831; wired onto each child at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:186-187 (OnEnter := @Self.ItemEnter; OnExit := @Self.ItemExit) with the relays at inc:147-155.
user_impact: A ported dialog that showed a description for whichever option the keyboard was on goes dead — and there is no accessor for the children either (no Buttons[]), so it cannot be rebuilt from outside the class.

member: OnClick (redeclared: fires on ItemIndex change, not on a mouse click)
what_it_does: TCustomRadioGroup shadows TControl.OnClick with its own FOnClick and fires it whenever the selection changes — Delphi compatibility, so OnClick and OnSelectionChanged are two names for the same notification.
ours_evidence: We inherit the plain TControl meaning: tyControls.Base.pas:213 'property OnClick;' on TTyCustomControl, and TTyRadioGroup does not redeclare it (published block is tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:52-63). Grep over source/ shows no OnClick override on any group class. Our selection notification is only OnSelectionChanged (:61), fired from ChildChanged (:263-278).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:778 'property OnClick: TNotifyEvent read FOnClick write FOnClick;' declared ON TCustomRadioGroup (shadowing TControl's), published at :823. Fired from C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:460-464 ('for Delphi compatibility: OnClick should be invoked, whenever ItemIndex has changed') and again at inc:428.
user_impact: Same property name, opposite trigger: a ported handler written for 'the selection changed' now runs when the user clicks the group's frame or caption instead — and never runs when the selection changes by keyboard. It compiles cleanly, so the break only shows up at run time.

member: ItemIndex — programmatic write fires OnClick + OnSelectionChanged in LCL, silent here
what_it_does: In LCL, setting ItemIndex from code notifies exactly as a user click does (explicitly, for Delphi compatibility and for issue #15989 even with no handle allocated).
ours_evidence: Ours suppresses it on purpose and documents it: tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:55-58 'Setting it programmatically does NOT fire OnSelectionChanged (that is reserved for user clicks)'; SetItemIndex raises FUpdatingIndex around the write (:296-309) and ChildChanged bails on that flag (:269). RebuildButtons does the same when restoring a selection (:228-233).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:414 SetItemIndex → CheckItemIndexChanged, which fires both events at inc:462-464; the no-handle branch fires them directly at inc:426-431 with the comment 'trigger event to be delphi compat, even if handle isn't allocated'.
user_impact: A ported form that relied on 'set ItemIndex, let the OnClick/OnSelectionChanged handler update the dependent UI' now sets the radio silently and leaves the rest of the form stale — the initial-state case (FormCreate assigning a default option) breaks first and most often.

what_it_does: Left/Right/Up/Down move the selection to the neighbouring item, honouring the column layout, wrapping at the ends and skipping hidden/disabled items, then focusing the newly selected radio. This is the standard radio-group keyboard contract.
ours_evidence: Nothing in the group handles arrows: tyControls.RadioGroup.pas wires only OnChange on each child (:217) and has no KeyDown override (protected section :41-46). The children handle exactly one key — tyControls.CheckBox.pas:485-494 TTyRadioButton.KeyDown acts on VK_SPACE only; grep over source/ finds no VK_LEFT/VK_RIGHT/VK_UP/VK_DOWN handling in RadioGroup.pas or for TTyRadioButton.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:257-310 — ItemKeyDown with the nested MoveSelection(HorzDiff, VertDiff), dispatching VK_LEFT/VK_RIGHT/VK_UP/VK_DOWN at inc:300-307, skipping invisible/disabled items at inc:292 and focusing at inc:294-295; wired onto every child at inc:188.
user_impact: Keyboard-only users cannot move within a ported radio group: arrows do nothing, so the only way to change the option is Tab-to-each-item plus Space — which also means the selection changes as they traverse.

member: UpdateTabStops — the group is ONE tab stop (only the checked child has TabStop)
what_it_does: LCL keeps TabStop True on the selected radio and False on all the others, so Tab enters the group once, lands on the current selection, and arrows move within it.
ours_evidence: Every child is a tab stop and nothing ever changes that: TTyRadioButton's constructor sets TabStop := True (tyControls.CheckBox.pas:415) with 'property TabStop default True' at :119, and RebuildButtons (tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:208-220) never touches TabStop — grep over source/ finds no UpdateTabStops or any TabStop assignment in RadioGroup.pas. The children are csNoDesignVisible (:212) but they are real windowed controls, so they all take part in the tab order.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/radiogroup.inc:553-563 'UpdateTabStops ... RadioBtn.TabStop := RadioBtn.Checked;', called from SetItemIndex (inc:415), UpdateItems (inc:238) and UpdateRadioButtonStates (inc:631). Reinforced by TRadioButton's own 'property TabStop default False' at C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1527.
user_impact: Tab traversal of a ported dialog gets much longer — a 6-item group adds 6 stops instead of 1 — and, combined with the missing arrow navigation, the platform-standard 'one stop per group, arrows inside' behaviour is unreachable.

what_it_does: Lets the control display one entry from an image list instead of a TPicture; the list is the DPI-aware icon source, and AutoSize/DestRect fall back to the list's size when Picture is empty.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Image.pas:45-58 published block has only Picture/Stretch/Proportional/Center/Transparent + Enabled/AutoSize/Align/Anchors/StyleClass/Controller/OnClick — no image-list reference. grep -rn 'property Images' over source/ returns 14 controls that DO have it (tyControls.AdvancedListBox.pas:74, tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:62, tyControls.Grid.pas:1253, tyControls.Menu.pas:411, tyControls.ToolBar.pas:64, tyControls.TreeView.pas:599, tyControls.ValueListEditor.pas:208 ...) — so TTyVirtualImageList/TTyImageCollection wiring is a solved pattern in this library, just never wired to TTyImage.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:588 'property Images: TCustomImageList read FImages write SetImages'; used in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:198-199 (DestRect), :256-260 (CalculatePreferredSize), :315-316 (Paint -> Images.StretchDraw).
user_impact: A single themed icon on a form cannot be sourced from the app's shared image list; the user must duplicate the bitmap into the control's Picture, losing the one-place-to-change icon set and the per-DPI rendering the collection already does.

what_it_does: Selects which entry of Images is shown (default 0); changing it repaints.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ImageIndex' over tyControls.Image.pas, tyControls.ImageView.pas, tyControls.CharImage.pas returned nothing; whole-of-source/ grep finds ImageIndex only on unrelated controls, never on an image control.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:586 'property ImageIndex: Integer read FImageIndex write SetImageIndex default 0'; setter at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:138-143.
user_impact: No way to say 'show icon 3 of the shared list'; a ported .lfm carrying ImageIndex= fails to stream.

what_it_does: Picks WHICH resolution of the image list to draw (a specific logical width, 0 = the list's default), so the same control can request 16px or 32px art.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ImageWidth' over source/ returned nothing (no file mentions it at all).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:587 'property ImageWidth: Integer read FImageWidth write SetImageWidth default 0'; consumed via Images.SizeForPPI[ImageWidth, Font.PixelsPerInch] at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:199 and :258.
user_impact: Even once Images exists there is no way to ask for a specific icon size; the control cannot express 'draw the 24px variant here'.

what_it_does: Chooses the scaling/AA quality used when the picture is drawn scaled (amDontCare/amOn/amOff), i.e. smooth interpolation vs hard nearest-neighbour edges.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'AntialiasingMode' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Image.pas:263-267 hardcodes the choice: PutImage when the fit rect equals the source size, otherwise StretchPutImage with BGRA's default (interpolating) resample — no property, no override.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:579 'property AntialiasingMode: TAntialiasingMode read FAntialiasingMode write SetAntialiasingMode default amDontCare'; applied at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:306 'C.AntialiasingMode := FAntialiasingMode'.
user_impact: Pixel art / QR codes / sprite sheets scaled up come out blurred with no way to ask for crisp nearest-neighbour, and a ported .lfm with AntialiasingMode= will not stream.

what_it_does: Default True. Gate on ENLARGING: when False a picture smaller than the control is never scaled up, even with Stretch/Proportional set.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'StretchInEnabled' over source/ returned nothing. TyImageFitRect (tyControls.Image.pas:89-111) has no such gate: Proportional always computes sc from the dest, so a 16x16 picture in a 300x300 control is blown up to 300x300.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:602 'property StretchInEnabled: Boolean read FStretchInEnabled write SetStretchInEnabled default True'; enforced at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:211-212 '(FStretchOutEnabled or PicOutsidePartial) and (FStretchInEnabled or PicInside)'.
user_impact: Small icons in a large placeholder get upscaled to mush with no opt-out; the standard LCL recipe 'shrink big photos, never enlarge small ones' is unexpressible.

what_it_does: Default True. Gate on SHRINKING: when False a picture larger than the control is not scaled down (it clips instead).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'StretchOutEnabled' over source/ returned nothing; no equivalent flag in TyImageFitRect (tyControls.Image.pas:80-124) or in the published list (tyControls.Image.pas:45-58).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:601 'property StretchOutEnabled: Boolean read FStretchOutEnabled write SetStretchOutEnabled default True'; enforced at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:211-212.
user_impact: Cannot ask for 'show at 1:1 and clip if too big' while still letting Stretch/Proportional handle the other direction; ported .lfm values silently vanish.

what_it_does: Two published Booleans (default False). When Center is on and the picture is BIGGER than the control, centring would push the origin negative and cut off the top/left; these pin the origin at 0 on that axis so the top-left of the image stays visible.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'KeepOriginX'/'KeepOriginY' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Image.pas:113-122 computes ox/oy := (dst-w) div 2 unconditionally, so an oversized unscaled picture is always clipped symmetrically with no way to bias to the origin.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:583-584 declare both (default False); logic at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:234-235 'if FKeepOriginXWhenClipped and (ChangeX<0) then ChangeX := 0'.
user_impact: Showing the top-left corner of an oversized image (maps, screenshots, scans) is impossible: it is always centre-cropped.

what_it_does: Whether an unscaled picture is centred in the client area or placed at the top-left.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Image.pas:49 'property Center: Boolean ... default True' and ctor tyControls.Image.pas:133 'FCenter := True'.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:582 'property Center: Boolean read FCenter write SetCenter default False'; ctor C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:18 'FCenter := False'.
user_impact: Silent layout change when porting: a .lfm converted from TImage does not store Center (it was the default False), so on TTyImage the image jumps to the middle of the control instead of the top-left, and pixel-exact layouts shift.

what_it_does: On LCL, Transparent is pushed into the GRAPHIC (Picture.Graphic.Transparent), i.e. it turns the bitmap's own mask/transparent colour on so the form shows through the image's background pixels; default False.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Image.pas:50 'property Transparent ... default True' plus tyControls.Image.pas:179-184 SetTransparent, which only Invalidates; the flag is consumed at tyControls.Image.pas:230-233 to decide whether to paint the CONTROL's TyPanel surface. Nothing ever touches FPicture.Graphic.Transparent (grep '.Transparent' in tyControls.Image.pas hits only our own field).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:603 default False; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:116-123 SetTransparent assigns FPicture.Graphic.Transparent, and PictureChanged re-asserts it at :175-176 'Picture.Graphic.Transparent := FTransparent'.
user_impact: Same property name, opposite default and different subject: setting Transparent=False on a masked BMP under LCL makes the mask colour paint solid; here it paints the panel background instead and the bitmap's mask is never touched, so masked/keyed bitmaps render with their key colour showing and the porter has no property that fixes it.

what_it_does: LCL's Proportional only engages when the picture is bigger than the control (PicOutsidePartial) unless Stretch is also set — a small picture stays at native size. It is a 'shrink to fit, never grow' switch.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Image.pas:89-99 — 'if AProportional then' scales unconditionally, including UP (scW/scH computed from the dest, no size comparison); documented that way at tyControls.Image.pas:16-17 and :71-72.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:206-226: 'if Stretch or (Proportional and PicOutsidePartial) then ...' — with Stretch=False and a picture smaller than the control the whole block is skipped and DestRect stays at native size (C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:604 declares the property).
user_impact: Identical .lfm, different picture: a 32x32 logo in a 200x200 Proportional image stays 32x32 under LCL but is upscaled to 200x200 here — blurry logos appear after a port with nothing in the form file to blame.

what_it_does: Fires whenever the assigned picture changes (assigned, edited in place, or cleared) so the host can re-caption, enable a Save button, update a status bar.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnPictureChanged' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Image.pas:186-194 PictureChanged does AutoSize + Invalidate and notifies nobody; no event field exists on the class (tyControls.Image.pas:26-35).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:605 'property OnPictureChanged: TNotifyEvent read FOnPictureChanged write FOnPictureChanged' (republished on TImage at :659); fired at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:179-180.
user_impact: Hosts cannot react to a new image (dimensions label, dirty flag, thumbnail refresh) without polling or subclassing.

what_it_does: Called during Paint with the canvas and the computed destination rect, BEFORE the image is drawn, so the host can paint a checkerboard/matte/gradient behind a transparent PNG.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnPaintBackground' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Image.pas:213-279 RenderTo either paints the themed frame or skips it (tyControls.Image.pas:230-233); there is no hook between background and blit. (The nearest thing in the library is TTyPaintPanel.OnPaintSurface, tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42, on a different control.)
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:606 'property OnPaintBackground: TImagePaintBackgroundEvent ...' (republished at :660); invoked at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:309-310 'FOnPaintBackground(Self, C, R)'.
user_impact: The standard 'alpha checkerboard behind a transparent image' pattern is impossible on this control; the user must drop a TTyPaintPanel behind it and keep the two rects in sync by hand.

what_it_does: Lets the host draw over the control after the image has been painted (TImage runs inherited Paint with the ancestor canvas specifically so OnPaint fires).
ours_evidence: grep -rln 'OnPaint' over source/ returns only tyControls.PaintPanel.pas, tyControls.PreviewBox.pas, tyControls.TreeView.pas — never Base.pas, so neither TTyGraphicControl (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 published block) nor TTyImage (tyControls.Image.pas:45-58) exposes it; TTyImage.Paint (tyControls.Image.pas:281-284) also never calls inherited Paint, so the LCL event would not fire even if published.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:658 'property OnPaint;' on TImage (declared protected on the ancestor at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2457); reached via C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:321-326 which flips FUseAncestorCanvas and calls inherited Paint.
user_impact: No way to annotate on top of the image (crop rectangle, hotspot markers, watermark) from the form's code.

what_it_does: Public virtual function returning the rect (in client coords) the picture actually occupies right now — the basis for hit-testing a click back to an image pixel, drawing selection handles, or overriding placement.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'DestRect' over source/ hits only tyControls.ImageView.pas (TyImageViewDestRect, a free function for the OTHER control, lines 137/183/712). TTyImage has the equivalent maths as a module-level pure function TyImageFitRect (tyControls.Image.pas:75-124) but it is not exposed as an instance member and requires the caller to re-derive picture and client sizes; not virtual, so placement cannot be overridden.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:575 'function DestRect: TRect; virtual;'; body C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:183-238.
user_impact: 'Which image pixel did the user click?' needs the user to re-implement the fit maths, and a descendant cannot change placement by overriding one function.

what_it_does: Public read-only Boolean: True when there is anything to draw (a picture OR a valid image-list entry). Guards Paint and AutoSize.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'HasGraphic' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Image.pas re-tests the condition inline in two places instead (:201 'if (FPicture.Graphic <> nil) and not FPicture.Graphic.Empty' and :237-238), and exposes no query.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:577 'property HasGraphic: Boolean read GetHasGraphic'; implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:270-273.
user_impact: Host code must reach into Image.Picture.Graphic and null/Empty-check it by hand to decide whether to show a placeholder.

what_it_does: On TCustomImage, Canvas is REDIRECTED to the picture's own bitmap canvas (auto-creating a TBitmap the size of the control if Picture is empty), so 'Image1.Canvas.LineTo(...)' draws INTO the image and persists.
ours_evidence: TTyImage inherits TGraphicControl.Canvas unchanged (tyControls.Base.pas:68 'TTyGraphicControl = class(TGraphicControl, ITyStyleable)'; no GetCanvas/Canvas override anywhere in tyControls.Image.pas), and TTyImage.Paint (tyControls.Image.pas:281-284) repaints the whole client area from FPicture every time. grep -rin 'GetCanvas' over source/ finds no image-control override.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:574 'property Canvas: TCanvas read GetCanvas'; GetCanvas at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:41-64 creates a backing TBitmap and returns TCustomBitmap(FPicture.Graphic).Canvas.
user_impact: The very common LCL idiom 'use a TImage as a scratch drawing surface' compiles here and then silently loses every stroke at the next repaint, because the same property name now means the transient control canvas.

what_it_does: At design time TCustomImage always outlines itself with a black dashed rectangle so an empty image control is visible and selectable on the form.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Image.pas:281-284 Paint -> RenderTo only; RenderTo (tyControls.Image.pas:213-242) returns early with nothing drawn when the picture is empty, and in the default Transparent=True mode (tyControls.Image.pas:50, :230-233) it does not even paint a surface. No csDesigning branch exists in the unit (grep 'csDesigning' in tyControls.Image.pas: no hits).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customimage.inc:277-289 (local DrawFrame, dashed black) called at :298-299 'if csDesigning in ComponentState then DrawFrame'.
user_impact: A freshly dropped or not-yet-assigned TTyImage is completely invisible in the Lazarus form designer — it cannot be found, clicked or resized without going through the Object Inspector's component list.
