what_it_does: Published LCL drag-and-drop configuration: dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down, DragCursor sets the cursor shown while dragging.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'dragmode' over source/ hits only tyControls.Memo.pas:568 (published) and tyControls.CoolBar.pas (an unrelated internal band-axis enum, FDragMode/TyCoolDragMode at :118/:229); grep 'dragcursor' hits only tyControls.Memo.pas:566. Neither TTyGraphicControl's published block (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141) nor TTyImage's (tyControls.Image.pas:45-58) lists them — and TTyMemo proves the LCL properties are publishable on this library's controls.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:623-624 'property DragCursor; property DragMode;' on TImage.
user_impact: An image cannot be made a drag source from the Object Inspector; drag-to-reorder / drag-an-image-onto-a-target UIs need hand-written mouse code.

what_it_does: The four LCL drag-and-drop events that make a control a drop target and a drag source.
ours_evidence: grep -rin over source/: OnDragDrop only in tyControls.Memo.pas:571; OnDragOver in tyControls.Memo.pas:572, tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas, tyControls.TreeView.pas; OnEndDrag in tyControls.Memo.pas:573, tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas; OnStartDrag in tyControls.Memo.pas:574. Absent from tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 and from tyControls.Image.pas:45-58.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:644-646 and :662 publish OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDrag on TImage.
user_impact: 'Drop a picture file / another image here' cannot be built on TTyImage from the designer, although TTyMemo in the same library already publishes exactly these.

what_it_does: Horizontal wheel / trackpad side-scroll notifications, separate from the vertical trio.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnMouseWheelHorz' / 'OnMouseWheelLeft' / 'OnMouseWheelRight' over source/ returned nothing at all. Both bases publish only the vertical set: tyControls.Base.pas:123-125 (OnMouseWheel/Up/Down) and :220-222.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:655-657 publish OnMouseWheelHorz, OnMouseWheelLeft, OnMouseWheelRight on TImage.
user_impact: Trackpad and tilt-wheel horizontal gestures over an image are unreachable — notable for a control people pan; the whole library is missing the horizontal half of wheel handling.

member: design-time / streamed image storage (DefineProperties, Bitmap+Data pseudo-properties)
what_it_does: TCustomImageList streams its actual PIXELS into the form file via DefineProperties/WriteData/ReadData, which is what makes the IDE image-list editor (add/delete/preview images at design time) possible and what makes a designer-populated list survive a save/reload.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:76-166: TTyImageCollection's only published surface is the inherited Version (tyControls.Component.pas:34); FItems (tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:78) is private with no published accessor, ChangeStamp/CacheCapacity (:161/:165) are public-only, images enter exclusively through runtime AddBitmap/AddPicture (:108/:112). grep -rn 'DefineProperties' in tyControls.ImageCollection.pas / tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas / tyControls.IconFont.pas returned nothing. designtime/tyControls.Design.pas:1052-1053 registers the components on the palette but registers no editor for their contents (the only image-group editor is CharImage.GlyphName at designtime/tyControls.Design.pas:1106).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:314 'procedure DefineProperties(Filer: TFiler); override;' with C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:334-337 WriteData/ReadData/WriteAdvData/ReadAdvData, plus the resolution writers at :142-143.
user_impact: A TTyImageCollection dropped on a form is permanently empty: there is no designer editor and nothing persists to the .lfm, so every icon set must be built in code at runtime. This is the single biggest usability gap versus TImageList, and it also blocks the Images property other controls already publish from being usable design-time-only.

what_it_does: Batches a run of mutations: change notifications are suppressed and coalesced into one Change at EndUpdate.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'BeginUpdate' over source/ hits tyControls.FontComboBox.pas, tyControls.FontListBox.pas, tyControls.Grid.pas, tyControls.ListView.pas, tyControls.MRUComboBox.pas, tyControls.ValueListEditor.pas — never the image units. tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:295-301 Changed increments FChangeStamp on EVERY mutation, and StoreMaster calls it per image (:371), so loading 200 icons invalidates the whole render cache 200 times (SyncCache/FlushCache at :303-313).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:339-340 'procedure BeginUpdate; procedure EndUpdate;' (with FUpdateCount at :281 and DoAfterUpdateStarted/DoBeforeUpdateEnded at :318-319).
user_impact: Bulk-loading an icon set thrashes the LRU cache and, once consumers observe changes, will fan out one notification per image; there is no way to say 'I am about to change many entries'.

what_it_does: Push notification that the image list changed: a direct OnChange event plus a TChangeLink registry so every consuming control repaints itself automatically when the list is edited.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'RegisterChanges' / 'UnRegisterChanges' / 'TChangeLink' over source/ returned nothing; grep 'OnChange' inside tyControls.ImageCollection.pas returned nothing. The design is PULL-only: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:154-161 documents ChangeStamp as a counter consumers must compare themselves, and consumers like tyControls.Grid.pas:1253 / tyControls.Menu.pas:411 just hold the reference.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:412 'property OnChange: TNotifyEvent ...'; :392 'procedure RegisterChanges(Value: TChangeLink)'; :394 UnRegisterChanges; TChangeLink class at :71-84; NotifyChangeLink at :287. Republished on TImageList at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2504.
user_impact: Adding or replacing an icon at runtime does not repaint the toolbars/trees/menus that display it — every consuming control would have to poll ChangeStamp on a timer or the app must Invalidate everything by hand.

what_it_does: Remove one image, insert one at a position, and reorder entries.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:102-165 public section offers only AddBitmap (:108), AddPicture (:112) and Clear (:114) as mutators — there is no way to remove a SINGLE image or to change entry order; grep 'procedure Delete'/'procedure Insert'/'procedure Move' in tyControls.ImageCollection.pas returned nothing. (TTyVirtualImageList escapes this because its Names is a published TStrings, tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:207, so Names.Delete/Move work there — but the underlying pixels cannot be dropped.)
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:355 'procedure Delete(AIndex: Integer)'; :381 'procedure Insert(AIndex: Integer; AImage, AMask: TCustomBitmap)'; :384 'procedure Move(ACurIndex, ANewIndex: Integer)'.
user_impact: An icon added at runtime can never be released except by Clear-ing and rebuilding the entire collection; memory for a large replaced image is held for the app's lifetime.

member: Draw(..., AEnabled: Boolean) / Draw(..., ADrawEffect: TGraphicsDrawEffect)
what_it_does: Draws the image with a visual effect — most importantly the greyed/faded 'disabled' rendering (AEnabled=False, gdeDisabled), also gdeHighlighted/gdeShadowed.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:201 'procedure Draw(ACanvas: TCanvas; AIndex, AX, AY, ASizePx: Integer)' and tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas:52 (same plus AColor) have no effect/enabled parameter; grep -rin 'gdeDisabled' / 'DrawEffect' / 'gdeNormal' over source/ returned nothing. The only related machinery is the whole-bitmap recolour TyTintBitmapAlpha (tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:46) and TTyImageView's FilterGrayscale (tyControls.ImageView.pas:255), neither reachable from a list Draw.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:356-361 the four Draw overloads (AEnabled: Boolean = True / ADrawEffect: TGraphicsDrawEffect), also on the resolution class at :161-166.
user_impact: A disabled toolbar button or menu item cannot render its icon greyed through the list; every consuming control must roll its own dimming, so disabled icons look inconsistent (or fully saturated) across the library.

what_it_does: Same method name, different signature: LCL is Draw(ACanvas, AX, AY, AIndex[, AEnabled]); ours is Draw(ACanvas, AIndex, AX, AY, ASizePx) — index and coordinates are swapped and a size argument is mandatory.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:201 'procedure Draw(ACanvas: TCanvas; AIndex, AX, AY, ASizePx: Integer);' and tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas:52 'procedure Draw(ACanvas: TCanvas; AIndex, AX, AY, ASizePx: Integer; AColor: TTyColor);' — all parameters are Integer, so a wrong order still compiles.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:356 'procedure Draw(ACanvas: TCanvas; AX, AY, AIndex: Integer; AEnabled: Boolean = True)'.
user_impact: Porting 'Images.Draw(C, X, Y, Idx)' to 'Draw(C, X, Y, Idx, 16)' compiles clean and silently draws image number X at position (Y, Idx) — a wrong-icon-in-a-wrong-place bug with no compiler help.

what_it_does: Overlay support: mark up to 15 images as overlay masks, then draw any image with one composited on top (the standard shortcut-arrow / share-badge / state-marker mechanism used by list and tree views).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'DrawOverlay' and 'HasOverlays' over source/ returned nothing; 'Overlay' hits only CSS tokens (--overlay-hover in tyControls.BuiltinThemeData.pas) and unrelated style-override comments (tyControls.Base.pas:500). Neither list class has an overlay index or a two-image draw (tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:177-201, tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas:39-52).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:366-369 the three DrawOverlay overloads; :385 'procedure Overlay(AIndex: Integer; Overlay: TOverlay)'; :386 'property HasOverlays: boolean'; TOverlay = 0..14 at :112.
user_impact: State badges on icons (link arrow, error marker, checked-out marker) must be pre-composited into separate images, multiplying the icon set instead of overlaying at draw time.

what_it_does: The other standard ways to get pixels into a list: AddMasked(TBitmap, MaskColor) makes a colour-key transparent; AddIcon/InsertIcon/ReplaceIcon take a TCustomIcon (multi-size .ico); AddLazarusResource/AddResourceName load straight from an embedded .lrs/PE resource by name.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:106-112 offers exactly two entry points, AddBitmap(TBGRABitmap) and AddPicture(TPicture). grep -rin over source/: 'AddIcon', 'AddLazarusResource', 'AddResourceName' return nothing; 'AddMasked' returns only tyControls.Dialogs.SelectPath.pas:217 'FIcons.AddMasked(bmp, clFuchsia)' — and FIcons there is a plain LCL TImageList (tyControls.Dialogs.SelectPath.pas:24, :197), i.e. the library itself reaches for LCL because its own collection cannot do it. No colour-key transparency exists anywhere in the image units.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:350 AddMasked; :348 AddIcon (with :382 InsertIcon, :390 ReplaceIcon); :351 AddLazarusResource; :352 AddResourceName.
user_impact: Legacy icon assets (magenta-keyed BMP strips, .ico files, resource-embedded glyphs) cannot be loaded into the themed collection without the caller writing its own key-to-alpha conversion first — as the library's own SelectPath dialog demonstrates by falling back to TImageList.

what_it_does: Cuts one source bitmap into a grid of images (AHorizontalCount x AVerticalCount) or takes one sub-rectangle out of it — the usual way an icon SHEET becomes an image list.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'AddSliced' / 'AddSlice' / 'ReplaceSlice' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:106-112 only accepts one whole bitmap or picture per name, and RenderMaster (:432-470) always fits the ENTIRE master into the square — there is no source-rect parameter anywhere.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:345-347 AddSliced/AddSlice/AddSliceCentered; :388-389 ReplaceSlice/ReplaceSliceCentered.
user_impact: A sprite sheet (very common for icon sets) has to be cut up by the caller with BGRA code before each piece can be added, and there is no way to reference a sub-rect of an existing master.

what_it_does: Exports one entry into an LCL TBitmap or TIcon (optionally with a draw effect) so it can be handed to native LCL controls, a clipboard, a TPicture, or saved to a file.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:134/:145 expose only GetBitmap(AName; ASizePx): TBGRABitmap (owned copy) and GetCachedBitmap (borrowed) — both BGRA-typed and name-keyed; grep -rin 'GetIcon' over source/ returned nothing. Every export therefore needs the caller to bridge BGRA -> TBitmap themselves, and MEMORY.md records that this round-trip is exactly where images have gone black before.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:371-372 GetBitmap overloads; :376-377 GetIcon overloads; :373 GetFullBitmap.
user_impact: Handing a themed icon to a native LCL control, a TPicture, the clipboard or a file needs a hand-written BGRA-to-TBitmap conversion at every call site — the known-fragile path in this codebase.

member: multi-resolution masters (AddMultipleResolutions / RegisterResolutions / Resolution[] / ResolutionByIndex / ResolutionCount / SizeForPPI / DrawForPPI)
what_it_does: One logical image can hold several hand-authored resolutions (16/24/32/48...); the list then serves the best one for a target PPI, and exposes per-resolution objects plus the SizeForPPI/WidthForPPI/HeightForPPI queries consumers use to lay out.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:57-64 TTyImageEntry holds exactly ONE FMaster per name, and RenderMaster (:432-470) always resamples that single master (rmFineResample at :458) to the requested square — a second AddBitmap with the same name REPLACES the first (StoreMaster, :363-371). grep -rin 'AddMultipleResolutions', 'RegisterResolutions', 'ResolutionCount', 'SizeForPPI', 'WidthForPPI', 'HeightForPPI', 'DrawForPPI' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:343-344 AddMultipleResolutions; :396-398 RegisterResolutions/DeleteResolution/FindResolution; :416-421 Resolution[]/ResolutionByIndex/ResolutionForPPI/ResolutionCount/Resolutions; :407-411 HeightForPPI/WidthForPPI/SizeForPPI; :362-365 DrawForPPI; the per-resolution class TCustomImageListResolution at :114-182.
user_impact: Small sizes can only be produced by downscaling the big master, so a hand-tuned 16px icon (redrawn, not shrunk) is impossible — the exact reason LCL added multi-resolution lists. Consumers also have no 'what size will you give me at this PPI' query to lay out against.

what_it_does: TImageList publishes Width and Height (both default 16) as the list's nominal image size — two independent axes, so non-square icons (e.g. 24x16 flags) are first class — and StretchDraw(Canvas, Index, ARect) draws an entry into an arbitrary rect.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:209 'property DefaultSize: Integer ... default 16' (also tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas:60) — a single scalar; every render path is a SQUARE: RenderMaster builds 'TBGRABitmap.Create(ASizePx, ASizePx, ...)' (tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:440) and letterboxes the master into it (:446-462), and Draw/RenderIndex/CachedIndex take one ASizePx (:191, :198, :201). TTyImageCollection itself publishes no size at all. grep -rin 'StretchDraw' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2498 and :2503 publish Height and Width on TImageList; declared at C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:406 'Height ... default 16' and :409 'Width ... default 16'; StretchDraw at C:/lazarus/lcl/imglist.pp:393.
user_impact: Non-square icons are padded into a transparent square and cannot be drawn to a non-square rect, so wide glyphs (flags, logos, 24x16 toolbar art) render smaller than intended with dead space; a porter looking for Width/Height finds a differently named single-axis property.

what_it_does: LCL's Date is a STRING (parsed with StrToDate, raises on bad input); the TDateTime accessor there is called DateTime.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.Calendar.pas:126 `property Date: TDateTime read FDate write SetDate;` plus the alias at :131 `property DateTime: TDateTime ... stored False`. grep -i 'property Date' over source/ shows only TDateTime forms; the unit comment at :120-125 says the divergence is deliberate.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:123 `property Date: String read GetDate write SetDate stored False;` and :124 `property DateTime: TDateTime`; GetDate/SetDate at :255-273 go through StrToDate.
user_impact: Ported code that does `Cal.Date := DateToStr(D)` or `S := Cal.Date` fails to compile here; conversely code written here does not compile there. Same identifier, different static type -- the worst-shaped porting break, and the compiler error is at a call site, not at the control.

what_it_does: A set property (TDisplaySettings) with dsShowHeadings, dsShowDayNames, dsNoMonthChange, dsShowWeekNumbers, controlling which calendar chrome is drawn; default [dsShowHeadings, dsShowDayNames].
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'DisplaySettings' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. Nearest is the single Boolean WeekNumbers at tyControls.Calendar.pas:135; the header band and weekday row are drawn unconditionally in RenderTo (tyControls.Calendar.pas:748-794).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:37-46 (TDisplaySetting / TDisplaySettings / DefaultDisplaySettings), :125-126 property declaration, :151 `property DisplaySettings;` on TCalendar.
user_impact: A .lfm streamed from Lazarus containing `DisplaySettings = [dsShowHeadings, dsShowDayNames]` fails to load, and no single property exists to configure calendar chrome. Also blocks the three flags listed separately below.

what_it_does: When excluded, the month/year title band (and its navigation buttons) is not drawn at all -- a bare day grid.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'ShowHeadings' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.Calendar.pas:669 always reserves HeaderH from --control-height and :748-765 always paints arrows + title; CalcLayout has no zero-header path.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:38 `dsShowHeadings`, included in DefaultDisplaySettings at :46, forwarded to the widgetset at :426 `SetDisplaySettings(Self, FDisplaySettings)`.
user_impact: A user embedding the calendar in a panel that already shows the month elsewhere cannot suppress our header; ~28-40px of the control is permanently spent on chrome they do not want.

what_it_does: When excluded, the Su/Mo/Tu weekday-name row is not drawn.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'ShowDayNames' over source/ returned nothing; grep -i 'daynames' finds only DefaultFormatSettings.ShortDayNames at tyControls.Calendar.pas:786. WeekdayH is unconditional at :671-673 and the row is always painted at :783-794.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:39 `dsShowDayNames`, in DefaultDisplaySettings at :46.
user_impact: No way to build a compact date grid; the weekday row always consumes a row of height even at tiny control sizes.

what_it_does: When included, clicking a spill-over day from the previous/next month does not scroll the view to that month.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'NoMonthChange' over source/ returned nothing. Our MouseDown hard-rejects out-of-month cells instead (tyControls.Calendar.pas:1029 `if (CellM <> FViewMonth) or (CellY <> FViewYear) then Exit;`) -- an unconditional, unconfigurable behaviour, and the opposite default from LCL (which DOES change month by default).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:40 `dsNoMonthChange` (absent from DefaultDisplaySettings at :46, so month change is the default).
user_impact: Two divergences at once: LCL users who relied on clicking a grey day to jump to that month find the click silently ignored here, and users who want LCL's dsNoMonthChange discipline have no property to set.

what_it_does: Shows the ISO week-number column at the left of the day grid.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.Calendar.pas:135 `property WeekNumbers: Boolean read FWeekNumbers write SetWeekNumbers default False;` -- the capability exists (rendered at :864-879 via TyISOWeekNumber).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:41 `dsShowWeekNumbers` inside the DisplaySettings set, :151 published.
user_impact: Same feature, incompatible spelling and shape: `Cal.DisplaySettings := Cal.DisplaySettings + [dsShowWeekNumbers]` must be rewritten as `Cal.WeekNumbers := True` when porting a form.

what_it_does: Which weekday occupies grid column 0.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.Calendar.pas:134 `property FirstDayOfWeek: TTyWeekDay ... default wdSunday;` with TTyWeekDay = (wdSunday..wdSaturday) at :9-10 -- Sunday-based ordinals, no locale-default member.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:127 `property FirstDayOfWeek: TCalDayOfWeek ... default dowDefault;` with TCalDayOfWeek = (dowMonday..dowSunday, dowDefault) at :69-72 -- Monday-based ordinals plus dowDefault.
user_impact: `Cal.FirstDayOfWeek := dowMonday` does not compile; worse, an .lfm/RTTI value that survives (integer 0) means Monday there and Sunday here, so a ported form silently shifts the whole grid by one column.

what_it_does: LCL's default dowDefault defers to the widgetset/locale, so the calendar starts on Monday in de/fr/zh locales and Sunday in en-US.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.Calendar.pas:134 `default wdSunday` and :279 `FFirstDayOfWeek := wdSunday;`. grep -ril 'dowDefault' over source/ returned nothing, and no locale query (no DefaultFormatSettings/GetLocaleInfo path) feeds FFirstDayOfWeek -- the grid always starts Sunday.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:72 `dowDefault`, :127 `default dowDefault`, :211 `FFirstDayOfWeek := dowDefault;`, pushed to the widgetset at :427.
user_impact: Out of the box in every Monday-first locale (most of Europe/Asia) our calendar shows a US week layout, and there is no value the user can set that means "follow the system" -- they must hardcode wdMonday and it then stays wrong if the app is relocalised.

what_it_does: Fires only when the day-of-month component of the selection changed.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'OnDayChanged' / 'DayChanged' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. Our event set is OnChange / OnAccept / OnViewChange only (tyControls.Calendar.pas:138-144).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:131 `property OnDayChanged: TNotifyEvent read FDayChanged write FDayChanged;`, :167 published, fired at :453 and :459.
user_impact: Handlers that need to react to day-only movement must re-derive the old day themselves in OnChange (we do not pass the previous value), and a ported form's OnDayChanged= assignment fails to load.

what_it_does: Fires when the month component of the selection changed (e.g. arrow-navigating across a month boundary).
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'OnMonthChanged' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing; only OnChange/OnAccept/OnViewChange exist (tyControls.Calendar.pas:138-144). Note OnViewChange (:144) fires on zoom level change, NOT on month change -- our month navigation (SetViewMonth, :364-373) fires nothing at all.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:132 `property OnMonthChanged`, :169 published, fired at :452 and :471.
user_impact: The common "load this month's appointments when the user pages the calendar" wiring has no hook: paging with our header arrows raises no event whatsoever.

what_it_does: Fires when the year component of the selection changed.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'OnYearChanged' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing (tyControls.Calendar.pas:138-144 is the full event list).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:133 `property OnYearChanged`, :183 published, fired at :451 and :477.
user_impact: No hook for year rollover; ported forms lose the handler assignment.

what_it_does: Classifies a point into cpNoWhere/cpDate/cpWeekNumber/cpTitle/cpTitleBtn/cpTitleMonth/cpTitleYear -- the public way to ask what part of the calendar the mouse is over.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'HitTest' over source/ hits Badge, Cascader, Chart, Dialogs, Form, ListGroupPanel, ListView(.Layout), StatusBar, Win32WS, WindowEffects -- NOT Calendar. The nearest capability is the free function TyCalendarHitCell (tyControls.Calendar.pas:44/252) which returns a bare cell index for a supplied grid rect, and the private geometry (CalcLayout at :88, header/arrow rects computed inline in MouseDown at :997-1018) is not reachable from outside. No TCalendarPart-equivalent enum exists anywhere in source/.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:121 `function HitTest(APoint: TPoint): TCalendarPart;`, enum at :49-57, implementation :219-225.
user_impact: A host that wants a context menu or custom tooltip per calendar region ("you right-clicked the year in the title") has to reimplement our private layout maths, and it cannot -- CalcLayout is private.

what_it_does: Reports which drill-down level the calendar is currently showing (month / year / decade / century).
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.Calendar.pas:114 `property ViewMode: TTyCalView read FViewMode;` (public, read-only), type TTyCalView = (cvmDays, cvmMonths, cvmYears, cvmDecades) at :11. grep -ril 'CalendarView' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:122 `function GetCalendarView: TCalendarView;`, enum TCalendarView = (cvMonth, cvYear, cvDecade, cvCentury) at :62-67, implementation :227-233.
user_impact: Same concept, different name AND different enum identifiers (cvMonth vs cvmDays, and ours names the CELL granularity while theirs names the PAGE granularity), so `if Cal.GetCalendarView = cvMonth` must be rewritten as `if Cal.ViewMode = cvmDays` -- an easy off-by-one-level mistake when porting.

what_it_does: Published AutoSize; the control reports a preferred size and shrink-wraps to it.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'AutoSize' over source/ lists 36 units (Button, TyLabel, Grid, TreeView, ...) but NOT tyControls.Calendar.pas -- so the capability exists in this library and is simply not wired here. TTyCustomControl's published block (tyControls.Base.pas:196-246) does not publish AutoSize, and TTyCalendar has no CalculatePreferredSize/GetControlClassDefaultSize override; Create just assigns Width/Height (tyControls.Calendar.pas:285-295). TControl.AutoSize is public in LCL (C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1789), so setting it compiles but reports no preferred size.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:142 `property AutoSize;` on TCalendar, with GetControlClassDefaultSize at :463-467.
user_impact: AutoSize=True on a .lfm ported from Lazarus does not stream (unknown property) and, if set in code, our control has no preferred size to grow to -- the skin-variance failure mode this codebase already logged: a roomier skin's larger fonts overflow a fixed 240x220 box instead of the control growing.

what_it_does: Horizontal-wheel (tilt-wheel / trackpad two-finger sideways) notification events.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'MouseWheelHorz' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing (and no MouseWheelLeft/Right). TTyCustomControl publishes only OnMouseWheel/OnMouseWheelUp/OnMouseWheelDown (tyControls.Base.pas:221-223), so no ty control anywhere exposes the horizontal trio.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:178-180 `property OnMouseWheelHorz; property OnMouseWheelLeft; property OnMouseWheelRight;`.
user_impact: Trackpad/tilt-wheel horizontal gestures are unreportable on every control in this library; a ported form assigning OnMouseWheelHorz fails to load.

what_it_does: Assigning a date outside MinDate..MaxDate (or outside SysUtils.MinDateTime..MaxDateTime) RAISES EInvalidDate with a formatted message.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'EInvalidDate' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing; no exception class is declared in tyControls.Calendar.pas. SetDate silently clamps: tyControls.Calendar.pas:311 `clamped := DateOf(TyCalendarClampDate(AValue, FMinDate, FMaxDate));` (helper at :199-206).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/calendar.pp:74 `EInvalidDate = class(Exception);`, CheckRange at :293-304 (three raise sites), called from SetDateTime :329-332 and SetMinDate/SetMaxDate :386/:405.
user_impact: Opposite failure modes for the same statement: validation code built around `try Cal.DateTime := X except on EInvalidDate ...` never fires here and the bad value is quietly coerced instead, so an out-of-range date from a DB/user is accepted-looking rather than rejected.

what_it_does: LCL's TDateTimeKind has three members -- dtkDate, dtkTime and dtkDateTime -- the last showing date AND time in one field.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:78 `TTyDateTimeKind = (dtkDate, dtkTime);` -- two members only. grep -ril 'dtkDateTime' over source/ returned nothing. ActiveFormat (:758-774) picks EITHER DateFormat OR TimeFormat, never a concatenation, so even a hand-written 'dd/mm/yyyy hh:nn' would have to go in one of the two slots and the other kind's format is ignored.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:110 `TDateTimeKind = (dtkDate, dtkTime, dtkDateTime);`, property at :424-425, published :521; FKind default dtkDate at :4063.
user_impact: `DTP.Kind := dtkDateTime` does not compile, and there is no supported way to edit a timestamp (date + time) in one control -- the single most common use of the LCL picker. Users must place two controls and recombine the values.

what_it_does: LCL's TimeFormat is an enum TTimeFormat = (tf12, tf24) selecting 12-hour-with-am/pm vs 24-hour display.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:298 `property TimeFormat: string read FTimeFormat write SetTimeFormat;` -- a FormatDateTime pattern string, not an enum. grep -in 'TimeFormat' over source/ shows only this string form (plus ListView.Layout's TFormatSettings use). The 12h capability itself exists (skAMPM segment at :80, 'am/pm' scanning at :460-486).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:105-107 `TTimeFormat = (tf12, tf24)`, property :434, published :524, default tf24 at :4106.
user_impact: Same property name, incompatible type: `DTP.TimeFormat := tf24` fails to compile and an .lfm carrying `TimeFormat = tf24` fails to stream into a string property. This is the picker's twin of the Calendar Date-string trap -- code compiles against one library and not the other with no hint at the control.

what_it_does: Selects which time fields are editable: tdHM, tdHMS or tdHMSMs (with milliseconds); default tdHMS.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'TimeDisplay' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. Nearest is the free-form TimeFormat string (tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:298) which changes the RENDERED pattern; there is no enum and no default matching tdHMS (our default is the locale ShortTimeFormat, :770-772, typically hh:nn only).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:100-103 `TTimeDisplay = (tdHM, tdHMS, tdHMSMs)`, property :435, published :525, default at :4105.
user_impact: No declarative way to say "I want seconds" -- users must know FormatDateTime pattern syntax and hand-write 'hh:nn:ss'; a ported `TimeDisplay = tdHMS` line does not load.

what_it_does: A fourth time field for milliseconds, separately selectable and spinnable (SelectMiliSec / IncreaseMiliSec / DecreaseMiliSec), separated by DecimalSeparator.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'MiliSec' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing; 'Millisecond' hits only Animation/ExPanel/ImageView/ListView (timers, unrelated). Our segment kind list has no millisecond member: tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:80 `TTySegKind = (skNone, skDay, skMonth, skYear, skHour, skMinute, skSecond, skAMPM)`, and the scanner (:496) recognises only y/m/d/h/n/s -- a 'z'/'zzz' in a format is treated as a literal, so milliseconds can be displayed by accident but never selected, typed or stepped.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:113-114 `dtpMiliSec` in TDateTimePart, tdHMSMs at :102, digit width N:=3 for dtpMiliSec at :3525-3526, SelectMiliSec/IncreaseMiliSec/DecreaseMiliSec at :367/:354/:358.
user_impact: Sub-second timestamps (logs, lab/instrument data) cannot be edited at all; our EncodeDateTime keeps the MS component (:641) so the value silently carries a millisecond the user can never see or change.

what_it_does: The whole null/empty-date model: NullInputAllowed (default True) lets the user clear the field to a null value (Ctrl-free single 'N' key), represented by the NullDate sentinel and shown as TextForNullDate.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'NullInputAllowed' / 'NullDate' / 'DateIsNull' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ each returned nothing. FDateTime is always a real date (Create seeds Now, tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:719) and every write path clamps into [MinDate,MaxDate] (CommitAndFire :960-968), so no representable empty state exists; our KeyDown (:1317-1366) has no VK_N branch.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:60 `NullDate = TDateTime(1.7e+308)`, property NullInputAllowed :412-413 (default True), published :520, VK_N handler :3731-3733 `if (not FReadOnly) and FNullInputAllowed then SetDateTime(NullDate)`, IsNullDate :600-604.
user_impact: A database NULL date cannot be represented or entered -- the explicit reason the LCL control has the feature. Binding our picker to a nullable column forces the app to invent its own sentinel and to intercept every edit.

what_it_does: The caption drawn when the value is null; default the literal 'NULL'.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'TextForNullDate' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. RenderTo always renders a formatted date (tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1220 `Txt := ActiveSegDisplayText;`), with no empty/placeholder branch.

ours_evidence: grep -in 'BiDiMode' over source/ returns exactly one line -- tyControls.Memo.pas:557, a comment saying "Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope" -- so no ty control supports it. Our picker's geometry is unconditionally LTR: TextR grows from R.Left (tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1184-1188), the checkbox is always leftmost (:1195/:1206), the button always rightmost (TyDateTimeButtonRect :682-689).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:534-535 `property BiDiMode; property ParentBiDiMode;`, override `procedure SetBiDiMode(AValue: TBiDiMode); override;` at :340, and RTL-aware geometry helpers GetCheckBoxRect(IgnoreRightToLeft) :318 / GetTextOrigin(IgnoreRightToLeft) :322.
user_impact: Arabic/Hebrew forms get an LTR field inside an RTL layout -- the checkbox and drop-down button land on the wrong side and the ported BiDiMode property fails to load. Fixing it means mirroring every rect and the click hit-test.

what_it_does: LCL snapshots the value on focus-in (FConfirmedDateTime) and Escape restores that whole snapshot, then fires EditingDone.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1285-1298: Escape closes the dropdown if open, otherwise only `FDigitBuffer := ''` -- already-committed segment edits stay. There is no confirmed-value snapshot anywhere: grep for ConfirmChanges/UndoChanges/FConfirmedDateTime over source/ returned nothing, and DoExit commits rather than reverts (:1141-1152).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:3725-3730 `VK_ESCAPE: if not FReadOnly then begin UndoChanges; EditingDone; end;`, UndoChanges :1985-1997 restoring FConfirmedDateTime, ConfirmChanges :1979-1983.
user_impact: The universal "Escape undoes my edit" reflex silently does almost nothing here: a user who spun the month with the arrow keys and pressed Escape keeps the changed month, believing they cancelled.

member: separator keys advance the selection (/ . , - etc.)
what_it_does: Typing a date/time separator (or the numpad divide/minus/decimal keys) moves the selection to the next field, so a user can type 12/25/2026 straight through.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1317-1366 -- our KeyDown case handles only VK_LEFT/RIGHT/HOME/END/UP/DOWN/RETURN (Escape earlier); UTF8KeyPress accepts only digits (:1378 `if (Length(UTF8Key) = 1) and (UTF8Key[1] in ['0'..'9'])`). grep for VK_OEM_COMMA / VK_DIVIDE / VK_SUBTRACT over source/ finds no picker use, so separator keys are swallowed.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:3690-3697: `VK_LEFT, VK_RIGHT, VK_OEM_COMMA, VK_OEM_PERIOD, VK_DIVIDE, VK_OEM_MINUS, VK_SEPARATOR, VK_DECIMAL, VK_SUBTRACT: ... MoveSelectionLR(K = VK_LEFT);`.
user_impact: Touch-typing a full date fails at the first slash: with a 1-digit day the field never auto-advances (2 digits are required, :890-893) and the '/' does nothing, so '1/5/2026' silently becomes something else. This is the most common way people enter dates.

what_it_does: With the AM/PM part selected, pressing A or P sets AM or PM directly.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1378 -- UTF8KeyPress only accepts '0'..'9', so letters are ignored; the skAMPM segment can be changed only with the arrow keys/wheel via TySegmentStep's skAMPM branch (:631-638). grep over source/ for any 'A'/'P' AM-PM key handling found none.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:3510-3517 `if FSelectedTextPart = 8 then case upCase(Key) of 'A': S := 'AM'; 'P': S := 'PM';` plus SendExternalKeyCode accepting 'a','A','p','P' at :2931.
user_impact: In a 12-hour format the user must arrow/spin the AM/PM field instead of typing the letter -- the standard gesture on every other date picker, and the one keystroke that makes 12-hour entry fast.

what_it_does: When ShowCheckBox is on, the Space key toggles Checked from the keyboard.
ours_evidence: D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/tyControls.DateTimePicker.pas:1317-1366 -- no VK_SPACE branch in KeyDown; the only toggle is a mouse hit on the box rect (:1461-1472). grep for VK_SPACE over the picker found nothing (TTyCalendar uses VK_SPACE for accept, :1168, a different control).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/datetimectrls/datetimepicker.pas:3683-3685 `if (Key = VK_SPACE) then begin if ShowCheckBox then Checked := not Checked;`.
user_impact: A keyboard-only or accessibility user cannot clear/set the checkbox at all -- the control is reachable by Tab but its checkbox is mouse-only, and clearing it is what makes the field null-ish in the first place.

what_it_does: Puts the tab band on the top, bottom, left or right edge (tpTop/tpBottom/tpLeft/tpRight), default tpTop.
ours_evidence: grep -ril "tabposition" over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. The header engine hard-codes a top band: RebuildLayout lays headers left-to-right at y=0..TabH (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425-450), AdjustClientRect insets only Top (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:667-671), RenderTo paints the strip at Rect(0,0,W,TabH) and the body below it (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:784-797).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:353 (TTabPosition), :510 (property, default tpTop); published TPageControl :644, TTabControl :885; setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customnotebook.inc:875-880.
user_impact: No vertical/sider tab layout and no bottom tabs at all — a very common design (left-hand settings tabs, bottom-docked output tabs) is unbuildable; a ported .lfm with TabPosition=tpLeft fails to load.

what_it_does: Forces every tab to a fixed pixel width (0 = size to caption).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "tabwidth" over source/ hits only tyControls.Ribbon.pas:141 FileTabWidth (the width of the ribbon's single leftmost File tab). Tab widths in the strip are always caption-derived: TW := TabCaptionWidth + 2*Pad, floored by --tab-min-width (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425-437) with no override.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:511 (stored TabWidthIsStored); published TPageControl :646, TTabControl :890 (default 0).
user_impact: Cannot make tabs equal-width; captions of differing length give a ragged strip, and there is no way to pin a uniform grid of tabs.

what_it_does: Boolean that hides the whole tab band while keeping the pages (default True).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "showtabs" over source/ returned nothing. The capability EXISTS under a different spelling: TabHeight := 0 means no strip at all (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:740-744 setter comment, :819-823 RenderTo early-out, :349-356 TabHPx returns 0).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:507 (default True); published TPageControl :639; setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customnotebook.inc:849-854.
user_impact: Ported code and .lfm files that set ShowTabs=False do not compile/load; and hiding the band via a magic 0 in a size property is not discoverable in the object inspector, nor reversible without remembering the old height.

what_it_does: Height of the tab band. In LCL it is a Smallint where 0 means 'let the widget size it from the font' and it is stored only when > 0.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TabStrip.pas:200 declares TabHeight: Integer read GetTabHeight write SetTabHeight stored FTabHeightExplicit; 0 is redefined to mean NO strip (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:740-744, :354), and 'unset' resolves to the density token instead (:730-736).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:509 (Smallint, stored TabHeightIsStored); TTabControl :886 (default 0); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customnotebook.inc:859-870 (setter + TabHeightIsStored = TabHeight > 0).
user_impact: Same property name, opposite meaning at the boundary value: a ported form that leaves TabHeight=0 for 'automatic' gets a page control with no tab band at all and looks broken. Type also narrows/widens (Smallint vs Integer).

what_it_does: Renders the tab band as classic tabs, as raised buttons, or as flat buttons (tsTabs/tsButtons/tsFlatButtons), default tsTabs.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "tabstyle\|tsbuttons\|tsflatbuttons" over source/ finds only a local variable TabStyle: TTyStyleSet in tyControls.TabStrip.pas:405,758 (a resolved style record, not a mode). No mode property exists; the strip always paints one 'TyTab' shape (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:838-908). The nearest existing hook is the inherited StyleClass (tyControls.Base.pas:236) plus a theme rule, which no built-in theme defines for a button-style tab band.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:355 (TTabStyle), :508 (default tsTabs); published TPageControl :640, TTabControl :884.
user_impact: The button-strip look (used for wizard/segment style tab bars) is unavailable, and Style=tsButtons in a ported form is a load error.

what_it_does: The multi-row tab band: wrap tabs onto several rows (MultiLine), do not stretch the last row to full width (RaggedRight), keep the selected row on the opposite side (ScrollOpposite), and report how many rows resulted (RowCount).
ours_evidence: grep -ril "multiline" over source/ hits only tyControls.Button.pas / Memo.pas / Painter.pas (text wrapping); "raggedright" and "scrollopposite" return nothing; "rowcount" hits Grid/ListView/Menu/ColorGrid only. The strip is single-row by construction — RebuildLayout advances X monotonically and handles overflow by scroll arrows instead of wrapping (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425-479), and nboMultiLine has no analogue.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:491 MultiLine, :505 RaggedRight, :506 ScrollOpposite; published TPageControl :629,:636,:637; TTabControl :875,:881,:882; RowCount :708 (TTabControlStrings) and :861 (TTabControl).
user_impact: A page control with 20 tabs can only be scrolled, never wrapped, so users must hunt with arrows where LCL shows all tabs at once; RowCount-based layout code cannot be ported.

what_it_does: The whole tab-icon feature: an image list on the control, a per-resolution width, a per-page ImageIndex, a callback to supply an index per tab, and a public getter.
ours_evidence: No member of the tab family references images. grep -rn "property Images\b" over source/ shows the capability is built and wired elsewhere — tyControls.Grid.pas:1253, tyControls.Menu.pas:411, tyControls.ListGroupPanel.pas:214, tyControls.ValueListEditor.pas:208, tyControls.AdvancedListBox.pas:74 (TTyVirtualImageList), tyControls.ToolBar.pas:64 and tyControls.TreeView.pas:599 (TImageList) — but never on TTyCustomTabStrip/TTyPageControl/TTyTabSheet. grep -ri "imageswidth" over source/ returns nothing anywhere. RebuildLayout reserves no icon slot (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425-450) and RenderTo draws caption + close glyph only (:876-907).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:489 Images, :490 ImagesWidth, :496 OnGetImageIndex, :477 GetImageIndex, :269 TCustomPage.ImageIndex (default -1); published TPageControl :627,:628,:662, TTabSheet :543, TTabControl :873,:874,:879,:858.
user_impact: Tabs cannot carry icons at all — the single most requested tab decoration, and standard in every ported Delphi/Lazarus form. TTyVirtualImageList already exists, so this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

what_it_does: Set of behaviour flags: nboShowCloseButtons, nboMultiLine, nboHidePageListPopup, nboKeyboardTabSwitch, nboShowAddTabButton, nboDoChangeOnSetIndex.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property Options" over source/ shows the pattern exists on Columns.pas:96/:217, Dialogs.FileDialog.pas:137, Dialogs.Find.pas:78, TreeView.pas:587 — but no Options on the tab family. Two flags have hard-wired equivalents: nboShowCloseButtons ≈ TabsClosable (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:201), nboKeyboardTabSwitch ≈ always-on Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn (:1164-1204); nboMultiLine, nboHidePageListPopup, nboShowAddTabButton (the '+' tab) and nboDoChangeOnSetIndex have no counterpart (grep for "pagelistpopup", "addtabbutton" returns nothing).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:362-366 (TCTabControlOption/TCTabControlOptions), :498 (default []); published TPageControl :630, TTabControl (via Options) :908 region.
user_impact: No add-tab '+' button and no page-list popup for overflow (LCL's alternative to scroll arrows); OnChange always fires on a programmatic index set, with no nboDoChangeOnSetIndex opt-out; Options=[...] in a ported form fails to load.

what_it_does: HotTrack: highlight the tab under the mouse (default False). MultiSelect: allow several tabs selected in button styles (default False). OwnerDraw: let the app paint tabs itself (default False; the paired OnDrawTab/TDrawTabEvent is declared but commented out of both published lists).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "hottrack" over source/ hits Columns/ListView/ShellTreeView/TreeView/Dialogs.SelectPath only; "multiselect" hits ButtonGroup/ListBox/ListView/Transfer/TreeSelect/TreeView/FileDialog only; "ownerdraw" hits tyControls.TreeView.pas only — none on the tab family. Our strip hot-tracks unconditionally and offers no opt-out (FHoverTab in tyControls.TabStrip.pas:1044-1084, rendered at :849-852); selection is a single Integer FTabIndex (:81).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:488 HotTrack, :492 MultiSelect, :499 OwnerDraw, :370 TDrawTabEvent; published TPageControl :626 (OwnerDraw commented at :631, OnDrawTab at :657), TTabControl :872,:876,:880.
user_impact: Hover highlight cannot be turned off (a deliberate design choice in flat/static skins); no multi-select tab strip; an app that owner-draws its tabs has no escape hatch, and HotTrack/MultiSelect/OwnerDraw in a ported .lfm fail to load.

what_it_does: The active page object, PUBLISHED on TPageControl so the designer/.lfm can select the shown page by page name (TCustomTabControl also has ActivePage: String, the active page's caption).
ours_evidence: tyControls.PageControl.pas:41 declares ActivePage: TTyTabSheet in the PUBLIC section only; the published selection is ActivePageIndex (tyControls.PageControl.pas:43). grep -rn "ActivePage" over source/ shows no published TTyTabSheet-typed property anywhere.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:611 (published ActivePage: TTabSheet on TPageControl); :459 (TCustomTabControl.ActivePage: String, stored IsStoredActivePage).
user_impact: A .lfm cannot say which page is active by name — only by numeric index, which silently points at the wrong page after pages are reordered or inserted. The object inspector shows no page picker.

what_it_does: LCL publishes TabIndex (index among VISIBLE tabs) and exposes PageIndex (index among ALL pages) as the selection; the two differ when a page has TabVisible=False.
ours_evidence: tyControls.PageControl.pas:43 publishes ActivePageIndex only; TabIndex exists but is PUBLIC on the engine (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:194) and is published only on TTyTabSet (tyControls.TabSet.pas:36). grep -rni "pageindex" over source/ finds only ActivePageIndex here and the unrelated TTyPagination.PageIndex (tyControls.Pagination.pas:277).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:471 (TabIndex, default -1) and :502 (PageIndex, default -1); published TPageControl :642, TTabControl :887.
user_impact: Ported code doing PC.TabIndex := n or PC.PageIndex := n does not compile against TTyPageControl, and a .lfm containing TabIndex= fails to load; the visible-tab vs all-pages distinction does not exist at all.

what_it_does: DisplayRect: the rectangle the active page occupies inside the control. TabRect(Index): the rectangle of one tab header.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "displayrect" over source/ returns nothing (the only *Rect hits are BalloonHint's local bodyRect/contentRect); the page-area inset is computed but never exposed — AdjustClientRect adds TabHPx to Top (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:667-671). TabRect DOES exist under a different name: TyTabHeaderRect(AIndex) (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:148, body :482-489), with TyTabCloseRect/HeaderRectShifted alongside (:149,:164).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:469 (DisplayRect, protected on TCustomTabControl) and :870 (public on TTabControl); TabRect :476, :709, :860.
user_impact: PC.TabRect(i) and PC.DisplayRect do not compile after a port; custom drawing/hit-testing code that positions overlays over a tab or over the page area must be rewritten against Ty-prefixed names, and there is no accessor at all for the page rectangle.

what_it_does: Point-to-index hit testing: which tab is under a point, which page is under a point, and what part of the control a point falls on (THitTests).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "indexoftabat\|indexofpageat\|gethittestinfoat" over source/ returns nothing. The nearest thing is TyDropIndexAt(X, APPI) (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:177, body :632-653) — a drag-reorder helper that returns the nearest DROP slot by shifted midpoints, clamps into [0,Count-1] and can never say 'no tab here', so it is not a hit test. MouseDown does its own inline scan instead (:972-996).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:450-453 (virtual on TCustomTabControl), :602-605 (public overrides on TPageControl), :707/:855-857 (TTabControl, incl. GetHitTestInfoAt).
user_impact: No supported way to write a tab context menu, tooltip-per-tab, or drag-to-another-pager: you cannot ask 'which tab did the user right-click?'. Ported code calling IndexOfTabAt does not compile.

member: IndexOf(APage) / CanChangePageIndex / GetMinimumTabWidth / GetMinimumTabHeight / DoCloseTabClicked / IndexOfTabWithCaption
what_it_does: Public query/notify API: index of a given page object, whether the selection may change right now, the widget's minimum tab width/height, the public close-tab entry point, and the index of the tab with a given caption.
ours_evidence: grep -ri over source/ for each: "indexof" in the tab-family units returns nothing; "canchangepageindex", "getminimumtab", "indexoftabwithcaption" return nothing anywhere. Partial counterparts: the close path exists but is PRIVATE (DoCloseClick, tyControls.TabStrip.pas:73, body :655-665) with only the OnTabClose veto public (:202); the minimum width exists only as the internal --tab-min-width metric read inside RebuildLayout (:416); an index-by-caption search is available on TTyTabSet via Tabs.IndexOf because Tabs is a TStrings (tyControls.TabSet.pas:35), but not on TTyPageControl.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:478 IndexOf, :480 CanChangePageIndex, :481-482 GetMinimumTabWidth/Height, :487 DoCloseTabClicked (public virtual), :859 IndexOfTabWithCaption.
user_impact: Callers must write their own loops over Pages[]/TabCaption() for what LCL provides directly, and cannot close a tab programmatically through the same path a click takes (so OnTabClose vetoes are bypassed or duplicated by hand).

what_it_does: Maps between the visible-tab index space and the all-pages index space, and lets a page report its own position in each (VisibleIndex, TabSheet.TabIndex).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "tabtopageindex\|pagetotabindex\|visibleindex" over source/ returns nothing. TTyPageControl has one index space only — FPages plus FTabIndex (tyControls.PageControl.pas:15, tyControls.TabStrip.pas:81) — and TTyTabSheet exposes no index of its own (published surface is Caption/StyleClass/Controller, tyControls.TabSheet.pas:28-32).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:484-485 (TabToPageIndex/PageToTabIndex), :265 (TCustomPage.VisibleIndex), :531 (TTabSheet.TabIndex, read-only).
user_impact: Directly follows from the missing TabVisible: with hidden tabs impossible there is nothing to map, but ported code that calls these (very common in wizards that hide steps) will not compile, and a page still cannot answer 'what number am I?'.

what_it_does: Deletes and frees every page in one call.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "procedure Clear" over the tab-family units (tyControls.PageControl.pas, TabSet.pas, TabStrip.pas, TabSheet.pas) returns nothing; the only removal API is RemovePage(AIndex)/RemoveTabData (tyControls.PageControl.pas:38, :182-191), so callers must loop downward themselves.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:597 (public procedure Clear on TPageControl); implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/pagecontrol.inc.
user_impact: Rebuilding a dynamic pager (a document-tab UI) needs a hand-written reverse loop; a forward loop — the natural first attempt — skips pages because indices shift under it.

what_it_does: Finds, or moves the selection to, the next/previous page, optionally skipping pages whose tab is hidden.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "findnextpage\|selectnextpage" over source/ returns nothing. Equivalent movement exists only as KEYBOARD handling inside the engine (Ctrl+Tab wrap, Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn clamp, Home/End, arrows — tyControls.TabStrip.pas:1164-1204); nothing programmatic and nothing that skips hidden tabs.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:598-599 (FindNextPage), :600-601 (SelectNextPage, two overloads).
user_impact: A wizard's Next/Back buttons cannot be wired with one call: the app must re-derive the next index itself and duplicate the wrap/clamp policy the keyboard handler already implements.

what_it_does: Creates a new page owned by the pager and returns it (no caption argument).
ours_evidence: The capability exists under different names with a different signature: AddPage(const ACaption: string): TTyTabSheet and its alias AddTab(const ACaption: string) (tyControls.PageControl.pas:36-37, bodies :193-206). grep -ri "addtabsheet" over source/ returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:606 (function AddTabSheet: TTabSheet).
user_impact: PC.AddTabSheet does not compile after a port — a one-line fix per call site, but it is the single most common way pages are created in existing code.

what_it_does: Scrolls the tab band by Delta tabs.
ours_evidence: Scrolling exists but in DEVICE PIXELS and under other names: SetHeaderScroll(AValue) (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:166, body :567-577) and ScrollTabIntoView(AIndex) (:167, body :584-618), with TyMaxHeaderScroll/TyHeaderStripWidth as the bounds (:160-161). grep -ri "scrolltabs" over source/ returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:711 (TTabControlStrings.ScrollTabs, virtual), :862 (TTabControl.ScrollTabs).
user_impact: Ported calls do not compile, and the unit differs (px vs tabs), so a mechanical rename produces a scroll of the wrong distance.

what_it_does: Brackets a batch of tab insertions/deletions so the band is measured and repainted once, and reports whether an update is in flight.
ours_evidence: grep -rl "BeginUpdate" over source/ hits FontComboBox, FontListBox, Grid, ListView, MRUComboBox, ValueListEditor — the pattern is established in the library but absent from the tab family; grep -ri "isupdating" returns nothing anywhere. Every tab-data change goes straight to TabsChanged -> Invalidate (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:287-290) and each geometry query re-runs RebuildLayout (:482-541). Partial cover: TTyTabSet.Tabs is a TStringList so TStrings.BeginUpdate suppresses its OnChange (tyControls.TabSet.pas:35,43-44), but the control itself has no update lock.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:714-716 (TTabControlStrings, virtual), :863-865 (TTabControl).
user_impact: Adding pages in a loop re-measures every caption on every iteration (RebuildLayout calls TabCaptionWidth per tab through a scratch TBitmap) and flickers; there is no supported way to suppress that.

what_it_does: Pre-switch veto fired before the selection moves.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TabStrip.pas:16-17 declares TTyTabChangingEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; ANewIndex: Integer; var AllowChange: Boolean), published at :204 and fired at :699-701 — three parameters where LCL has two.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:350-351 (TTabChangingEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; var AllowChange: Boolean)), :493; published TPageControl :650, TTabControl :878.
user_impact: Same event name, incompatible signature: an existing OnChanging handler will not assign, and the .lfm event link resolves to a method the compiler rejects. (Ours carries more information, so the break is one-directional but unavoidable.)

what_it_does: Fires when the user clicks a tab's close button.
ours_evidence: The capability exists under another name and signature: OnTabClose: TTyTabCloseEvent = procedure(Sender; AIndex: Integer; var AllowClose: Boolean) (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:10-11, published :202, fired :655-665). grep -ri "oncloseTabclicked" over source/ returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:494-495 (OnCloseTabClicked: TNotifyEvent); published TPageControl :651; public DoCloseTabClicked(APage) :487.
user_impact: Ported handlers do not compile and the .lfm event name is unknown; LCL also hands the handler the PAGE while ours hands an index, so the body needs rewriting too.

what_it_does: TWinControl layout properties LCL publishes on the pager and the page: size to content (AutoSize), an inner margin inside the page (BorderWidth), and the child auto-layout collection (ChildSizing).
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property BorderWidth;" over source/ returns nothing (every other BorderWidth hit is the CSS/style-set border width, e.g. tyControls.TabStrip.pas:808); grep -ri "childsizing" over source/ returns nothing anywhere; AutoSize IS published on ~10 controls (tyControls.Button.pas, CheckBox.pas, Breadcrumb.pas, Empty.pas, GlyphButtons.pas …) but not on the tab family, and neither base class publishes it (tyControls.Base.pas:195-240 published block contains no AutoSize/BorderWidth/ChildSizing).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:616 (TPageControl.AutoSize), :533-534 (TTabSheet.AutoSize, BorderWidth), :537 (TTabSheet.ChildSizing).
user_impact: A page cannot inset its children with one property (every child needs its own BorderSpacing) and cannot use LCL's ChildSizing auto-layout; a pager cannot size itself to its largest page.

what_it_does: Right-to-left layout and reading order for the control and its children.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "bidimode" over the whole source/ returns exactly one hit — a comment declaring it out of scope for a different control: tyControls.Memo.pas:557 ("Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope"). The strip hard-codes LTR: RebuildLayout advances X left-to-right (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425-450), the close glyph is pinned to the right edge (:443-444), and the overflow arrows are fixed left/right (:461-462).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:618,:632 (TPageControl), :535,:546 (TTabSheet), :894 (TTabControl); declarations C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1834-1835.
user_impact: No Arabic/Hebrew tab layout: tabs, close buttons and overflow arrows stay left-to-right regardless of locale. The concept has a real themed equivalent (mirrored layout) that the painter would have to grow.

member: DragMode / DragKind / DragCursor / OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnStartDrag / OnEndDrag
what_it_does: LCL's drag-and-drop surface, published on both the pager and each page — lets the app accept drops on a tab or a page and start drags from them.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "dragmode\|ondragdrop\|ondragover\|onstartdrag\|onenddrag" over source/ finds no published counterpart; neither base class publishes them (tyControls.Base.pas:195-240 for TTyCustomControl, :100-137 for TTyGraphicControl). The only drag machinery in the strip is its own internal tab-REORDER gesture (FDragTab/FDragging, tyControls.TabStrip.pas:44-56, :1016-1042) exposed as OnReorder (:205) — unrelated to LCL drag objects.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:621-623 (DragCursor/DragKind/DragMode), :655-656,:659,:674 (TPageControl events), :556-558,:572 (TTabSheet events).
user_impact: You cannot drop a file or a list item onto a tab to switch/populate it, and cannot start a drag from a page — standard interactions in document-tab UIs — because the events are not published for the designer or reachable in the .lfm.

member: DockSite / OnDockDrop / OnDockOver / OnStartDock / OnEndDock / OnUnDock / OnGetSiteInfo / OnGetDockCaption
what_it_does: TPageControl is a dock site: controls can be docked into it as pages, with the full dock notification set and a caption callback.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "docksite" over source/ returns nothing; no dock events are published anywhere in the library. TTyPageControl's only page-acquisition path is TTyTabSheet.SetParent -> RegisterPage (tyControls.TabSheet.pas:62-70, tyControls.PageControl.pas:137-154); there is no DoAddDockClient/DockOver/ChildClassAllowed analogue.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:620,:612,:653-654,:658,:663,:673,:675 (published), plus the overrides that implement it at :590-595 (DoAddDockClient, DockOver, DoRemoveDockClient, DoUndockClientMsg, ChildClassAllowed, UpdateDockCaption).
user_impact: IDE-style dockable tabbed panels cannot be built on TTyPageControl, and a ported form that used it as a dock site loses that behaviour silently (the properties simply do not exist).

what_it_does: Hides this page's TAB while the page itself stays in the collection (default True) — the standard way to build wizards and conditional steps.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "tabvisible" over the whole source/ returns nothing. Our page count and the header count are the same list with no visibility filter: GetTabCount := Length(FPages) and GetTabCaption reads FPages[i].Caption (tyControls.PageControl.pas:58-69), and RebuildLayout iterates 0..GetTabCount-1 unconditionally (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:425). TTyTabSheet.Visible (published via tyControls.Base.pas:206) hides the whole page, not just its tab.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:268 (TCustomPage.TabVisible, default True), :551 (republished on TTabSheet); getter/setter :254,:245.
user_impact: A wizard cannot pre-create its steps and reveal them progressively — pages must be created and destroyed instead, losing child state — and any ported form with TabVisible=False fails to load.

what_it_does: A page's position in the pager, ASSIGNABLE — setting it moves the page (and its tab) to that position.
ours_evidence: grep -rni "pageindex" over source/ finds only TTyPageControl.ActivePageIndex (tyControls.PageControl.pas:43) and the unrelated TTyPagination.PageIndex (tyControls.Pagination.pas:277); TTyTabSheet publishes only Caption/StyleClass/Controller (tyControls.TabSheet.pas:28-32). Reordering exists only as the internal drag hook DoReorderTabs(AFrom,ATo) (tyControls.PageControl.pas:121-135), which is protected and has no public/property entry point, and there is no InsertPage(APage, Index) either (grep "insertpage" returns nothing).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:267 (TCustomPage.PageIndex read GetPageIndex write SetPageIndex), :545 (republished on TTabSheet, stored False); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompage.inc holds SetPageIndex.
user_impact: Pages can only be reordered by the user dragging tabs; code cannot move a page (or insert one at a position) at all, so ordering that depends on data — most recently used tabs, sorted documents — is impossible.

what_it_does: The pager this page belongs to, READ/WRITE — assigning it moves the page to another pager.
ours_evidence: The read direction is available as the inherited Parent (set in tyControls.TabSheet.pas:62-70, where SetParent self-registers with TTyPageControl), but there is no typed PageControl property: grep -rn "property PageControl" over source/ returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:530 (property PageControl: TPageControl read GetPageControl write SetPageControl), getters at :522-524.
user_impact: Sheet.PageControl does not compile after a port; callers must use Parent and hard-cast, losing the compile-time type check that the parent really is a pager.

what_it_does: Fire when this page becomes the active page and when it stops being it — the per-page activation hooks (lazy content loading, validation on leave).
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property On(Show|Hide)" over source/ shows the pattern is used widely — tyControls.Dialogs.pas:117/141/167/201/250, Dialogs.About.pas:67, Dialogs.Color.pas:121, Popover.pas:363/367 — but never on TTyTabSheet (published surface: tyControls.TabSheet.pas:28-32). The page switch just toggles Visible + csNoDesignVisible with no notification (ShowOnlyPage, tyControls.PageControl.pas:96-114); only the CONTROL-level OnChange exists (tyControls.TabStrip.pas:203).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:276-277 (TCustomPage.OnShow/OnHide), :561,:571 (republished on TTabSheet); fired from DoShow/DoHide :257-258 via CMVisibleChanged :251.
user_impact: Per-page code must be centralised into the pager's OnChange and dispatched with a case/if chain on the index; a page cannot own its own enter/leave logic, and ported OnShow/OnHide handlers are dropped silently by the .lfm loader.

member: Left / Top / Width / Height / TabOrder / Visible (stored False)
what_it_does: LCL redeclares all of a page's bounds plus TabOrder and Visible as stored False, so a page never streams geometry or visibility — the pager owns both.
ours_evidence: TTyTabSheet does not redeclare any of them (published surface is Caption/StyleClass/Controller, tyControls.TabSheet.pas:28-32), so it inherits them as normally-stored: Visible and TabOrder from tyControls.Base.pas:206,210 and Left/Top/Width/Height from TControl's published block (C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1842-1846). Meanwhile the constructor forces Visible := False (tyControls.TabSheet.pas:45) and Align := alClient (:44), and the host toggles Visible per page at runtime (tyControls.PageControl.pas:96-114).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:270-275 (Left/Top/Width/Height/TabOrder/Visible stored False on TCustomPage), :542,:544,:552,:553 (repeated on TTabSheet).
user_impact: Every page writes Visible = False and stale bounds into the .lfm; the file is noisier, diffs churn on every designer visit, and a page's persisted Visible=False depends on Loaded/ShowOnlyPage running to undo it rather than never having been saved.

what_it_does: On LCL a page's Caption IS TControl.Caption (backed by Text via RealSetText, which also refreshes the tab), so Caption and Text are one value.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TabSheet.pas:17,29 declare a private FCaption plus property Caption: TCaption read FCaption write SetCaption (:54-60) — a SHADOW of TControl.Caption (C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1793, read GetText write SetText), which TTyCustomControl never publishes (no Caption in the tyControls.Base.pas:195-240 published block). SetCaption only invalidates the parent; it never touches Text.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:536 (TTabSheet republishes the inherited Caption), :259 (TCustomPage.RealSetText override keeps the tab in sync).
user_impact: Sheet.Text and Sheet.Caption diverge: generic code that walks controls as TControl and reads Caption/Text (translation passes, accessibility, docking captions, LCL's own Text-based paths) sees an empty string, while the tab shows the real label.

what_it_does: One property turns a button into a stock dialog button: bkOK/bkCancel/bkHelp/bkYes/bkNo/bkClose/bkAbort/bkRetry/bkIgnore/bkAll/bkNoToAll/bkYesToAll each set the localized Caption, the stock glyph and the ModalResult (and Default/Cancel) in one assignment.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'Kind' over source/ returns 666 hits but NONE is a button Kind property (all are TTyFill.Kind / TTyGlyphKind / TTyAlertType); grep -ri 'DefaultCaption' = 0 hits; TTyButton's published list (tyControls.Button.pas:139-184) and TTyGlyphButtonBase's (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:140-167) have no Kind. Caption, ModalResult and the glyph must each be set by hand.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:158-161 (TBitBtnKind), :225 property Kind default bkCustom, :540-548 BitBtnModalResults/BitBtnImages tables; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/bitbtn.inc:225 SetKind, :281 RealizeKind, :354 GetCaptionOfKind.
user_impact: Every ported dialog loses its one-line button setup: `Btn.Kind := bkCancel` does not compile, and the author must restate caption text (untranslated), ModalResult and Cancel on each button — three chances to disagree, and the stock check/cross/question glyphs are unavailable entirely.

what_it_does: Per-control right-to-left mode: mirrors the glyph/caption layout and switches text reading order (LCL also flips the glyph layout for you via BidiAdjustButtonLayout).
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'bidi|RightToLeft' over source/ returns exactly ONE hit, a comment: tyControls.Memo.pas:557 "Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope". No control publishes BiDiMode, and no paint path consults IsRightToLeft — TTyButton.DrawContent (tyControls.Button.pas:691-703) always draws taCenter LTR, TyGlyphButtonSplit (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:260-301) always anchors the glyph LEFT.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1834-1835 (public on TControl); published on the concrete controls at buttons.pp:445 (TSpeedButton BidiMode/ParentBidiMode :477), buttons.pp:244+269 (TBitBtn), stdctrls.pp:1273+1286 (TButton); buttons.pp:700-703 BidiAdjustButtonLayout.
user_impact: An Arabic/Hebrew form cannot be built: BiDiMode is settable from code (it is public on TControl) but our self-drawn buttons ignore it, so glyphs stay on the left of the caption and nothing mirrors, while the surrounding native LCL controls do mirror — the form reads half-flipped.

what_it_does: Assign an ordinary TBitmap as the button icon; NumGlyphs (1..5) splits that bitmap into an up/disabled/down/exclusive/hot strip so one image supplies every state.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'NumGlyphs' over source/ = 0 hits. grep -n 'property Glyph' source/*.pas returns only GlyphName/GlyphSize/GlyphColor/GlyphLayout (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:137-159) and TTyGlyphImageList.Glyphs: TStrings — never a bitmap. Our only icon sources are an icon-FONT name (IconFont+GlyphName, GlyphButtons.pas:150/153) or a named entry in a TTyImageCollection (:164/166); ResolveGlyphBitmap (:362-374) can consume nothing else. The precedent for a direct bitmap exists elsewhere: TTyImageView.AssignBitmap (tyControls.ImageView.pas:95).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:219 property Glyph: TBitmap stored IsGlyphStored, :220 NumGlyphs default 1 (TCustomBitBtn); :420 Glyph, :428 NumGlyphs (TCustomSpeedButton); include/speedbutton.inc:199-203 SetGlyph, :277 SetNumGlyphs.
user_impact: A user with a .bmp/.png icon (or a runtime-generated bitmap) has no way to put it on a button: they must first build a TTyImageCollection or an icon font. Every ported .lfm that streams a Glyph.Data blob loses its icons silently — the button just renders its caption.

what_it_does: The image source is any standard LCL TCustomImageList/TImageList — including the IDE's LCLGlyphs and multi-resolution lists, with change-link tracking so edits to the list repaint the button.
ours_evidence: tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:164 `property Images: TTyImageCollection read FImages write SetImages` — a library-private collection class, not a TCustomImageList. grep -ri 'TCustomImageList' over source/ finds no button accepting one.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:222 property Images: TCustomImageList (TCustomBitBtn), :423 (TCustomSpeedButton); include/speedbutton.inc:222-240 SetImages with RegisterChanges/FreeNotification.
user_impact: Same property name, incompatible type: `Btn.Images := ImageList1` fails to compile, and an app that already keeps its icons in a TImageList (shared with menus, tree views, third-party controls) must duplicate every icon into a second, ty-only collection.

what_it_does: Per-state icons: a different image index for disabled, hover, pressed and exclusive-down, each defaulting to -1 (fall back to the normal image).
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'HotImage|PressedImage|DisabledImage|SelectedImage' over source/ = 0 hits each. The glyph is resolved once from a single name with no state input: ResolveGlyphBitmap(ASizePx, AColor) (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:362-374) is called from DrawContent (:550) with only a colour, never CurrentStates.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:417,422,429,430 (TCustomSpeedButton DisabledImageIndex/HotImageIndex/PressedImageIndex/SelectedImageIndex, all default -1) and :218,221,228 (TCustomBitBtn); published on TSpeedButton at :453,463,470,471.
user_impact: A toolbar cannot show a greyed icon when disabled or a coloured/filled variant on hover — only the theme's opacity/tint can change, so an icon set designed with explicit disabled and hover artwork (the normal case for hand-drawn 16px icons) cannot be used.

what_it_does: Published four-way glyph placement relative to the caption: blGlyphLeft (default), blGlyphRight, blGlyphTop, blGlyphBottom.
ours_evidence: Our equivalent is `GlyphLayout: TTyGlyphLayout` declared in the PROTECTED section (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:137) — not published, so it cannot be set in the designer or streamed from a .lfm — and the enum has only two members: `TTyGlyphLayout = (glLeft, glTop)` (:75). TyGlyphButtonSplit (:260-301) implements exactly those two; there is no right/bottom branch anywhere in source/.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:42-48 TButtonLayout (4 values), :426 property Layout default blGlyphLeft (TCustomSpeedButton), :226 (TCustomBitBtn); published TSpeedButton :467, TBitBtn :262; include/speedbutton.inc:1065 SetLayout.
user_impact: Two of the four layouts do not exist (icon to the RIGHT of the caption — the common 'more ▾' / trailing-icon pattern — and icon BELOW), and even the two we have cannot be chosen from the Object Inspector: the app must subclass to reach a protected property.

member: class ancestry: graphic vs windowed control
what_it_does: TCustomSpeedButton is a TGraphicControl: no window handle, so it is genuinely transparent over the parent's painted background, cannot take focus, cannot clip sibling graphic controls, and costs no OS handle per toolbar button.
ours_evidence: tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:197 `TTySpeedButton = class(TTyGlyphButtonBase)` -> :80 `TTyGlyphButtonBase = class(TTyButton)` -> tyControls.Button.pas:16 `TTyButton = class(TTyCustomControl)` -> tyControls.Base.pas:143 `TTyCustomControl = class(TCustomControl)` (a TWinControl). The consequences are visible in the code that works around them: TabStop must be forced off in the constructor (GlyphButtons.pas:610), DrawFrame must re-fill corner gaps because a windowed child cannot cast onto its parent (Base.pas:1127-1129), and TyFillParentBg exists solely to fake the parent's background (Base.pas:664-695). A graphic base class DOES exist in the library (TTyGraphicControl, Base.pas:68) — the speed button just does not use it.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:322 `TCustomSpeedButton = class(TGraphicControl)`; C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2446 TGraphicControl = class(TControl) (no handle); buttons.pp:434 Transparent default true.
user_impact: A speed button on a gradient/image panel shows a rectangular patch of the resolved parent colour rather than the real backdrop, it clips any graphic-control sibling it overlaps (the known windowed-sibling clipping trap), and a 30-button toolbar burns 30 window handles. Porting a TSpeedButton onto a picture-backed toolbar therefore looks wrong in a way no property can fix.

member: DragMode / DragKind / DragCursor + OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnStartDrag / OnEndDrag
what_it_does: The LCL drag-and-drop surface: dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down, dkDock vs dkDrag chooses docking, DragCursor sets the feedback cursor, and the four events accept/reject/complete the drop.
ours_evidence: grep -ri over source/: 'DragMode' hits only TTyCoolBar's unrelated internal FDragMode/TyCoolDragMode; 'DragKind' and 'DragCursor' and 'OnDragDrop' and 'OnStartDrag' each have exactly ONE hit, all in tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574 (the memo re-publishes them). Neither TTyGraphicControl (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141) nor TTyCustomControl (:196-246) publishes any of them, and TTyButton's own list (tyControls.Button.pas:139-184) does not either.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1568-1572 declares them PROTECTED on TControl ("optional properties (not every descendent supports them)"), and the concrete buttons publish them: buttons.pp:455-457 + 485-487+498 (TSpeedButton), buttons.pp:253-255 + 284-286+301 (TBitBtn), stdctrls.pp:1281-1283 + 1299-1301+1316 (TButton).
user_impact: Drag-and-drop is not merely absent from the Object Inspector — because these members are protected on TControl, an app CANNOT reach them from code either. A palette of draggable command buttons (drag a tool onto a canvas, drag a button into a customizable toolbar) is impossible without subclassing every button, and any ported .lfm carrying DragMode=dmAutomatic fails to load.

what_it_does: Horizontal alignment of the caption inside the button — taLeftJustify / taRightJustify / taCenter.
ours_evidence: grep -in 'alignment' over the four button units returns NOTHING; the alignment is hard-coded taCenter at tyControls.Button.pas:701 (DrawContent) and taLeftJustify at tyControls.ColorButton.pas:169. The concept is plainly supported elsewhere in the library — TTyEdit.Alignment (tyControls.Edit.pas:181), TTyLabel/TTyGlowLabel (tyControls.GlowLabel.pas:70), TTyDivider (:58), TTyColumn (tyControls.Columns.pas:92) — it was simply never wired to a button.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:414 property Alignment: TAlignment read FAlignment write SetAlignment default taCenter; published TSpeedButton buttons.pp:444; include/speedbutton.inc:118 SetAlignment.
user_impact: Left-aligned command buttons — the standard look for a vertical navigation rail or a ribbon's file-menu column, where icon+label must line up down the left edge — cannot be built; every caption is force-centred.

what_it_does: Per-instance switch between a flat, borderless resting look (frame appears on hover/press) and full push-button chrome.
ours_evidence: grep -in 'flat' over source/*.pas as a property finds only tyControls.ToolBar.pas:63 `property Flat: Boolean ... default True` — a container-level property on the BAR, not on the button.
