TTySpeedButton (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:197-241) has no Flat; flatness is delegated entirely to the theme via its own typeKey ('TySpeedButton', :596-599) as the comment at :210-218 explains.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:419 property Flat: Boolean read FFlat write SetFlat default false; published TSpeedButton :459, TColorButton dialogs.pp:377; include/speedbutton.inc:188 SetFlat.
user_impact: An app cannot mix flat and framed speed buttons on the same form (e.g. a flat toolbar plus one framed primary action): the resting frame is a theme-wide decision for the whole TySpeedButton key, so the only per-instance lever is inventing a StyleClass and shipping .tycss with the app — and TTyToolBar.ApplyToButton overwrites its children's StyleClass wholesale.

what_it_does: A design-time reference to a configured TColorDialog component (its CustomColors list, Options, Title, OnShow/OnClose handlers), plus an overridable ShowColorDialog hook; with none assigned LCL creates a throw-away dialog.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ShowColorDialog' over source/ = 0 hits; grep -ri 'CustomColors' = 0 hits. TTyColorButton's whole published surface is SelectedColor/ShowText/DialogCaption/OnColorChange (tyControls.ColorButton.pas:73-84) and the dialog is hard-wired inside Click as `TySelectColor(FDialogCaption, newColor)` (:260) with no seam to override. This is the wired-up-nowhere case: a designable dialog component ALREADY EXISTS — TTyColorDialog with Caption/Color/Alpha/OnShow/OnClose/OnCanClose at tyControls.Dialogs.Color.pas:105-123 — the button simply has no property to point at one.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:371 property ColorDialog: TColorDialog read FColorDialog write FColorDialog; :354 ShowColorDialog virtual; include/colorbutton.inc:65-83 (uses the assigned dialog, else creates and frees one); dialogs.pp:323-324 TColorDialog.CustomColors/Options.
user_impact: There is no way to preset the palette, add custom colours, keep the dialog's state between openings, hook OnCanClose, or substitute a different picker — the button always opens the one built-in dialog, configurable only by its title string.

member: inherited TCustomSpeedButton surface: Flat / GroupIndex / AllowAllUp / Down / Layout / Margin / Spacing / Transparent
what_it_does: TColorButton IS a TCustomSpeedButton, so it publishes the whole speed-button surface: it can be flat, grouped as a radio, glyph-laid-out, spaced and transparent.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorButton.pas:25 `TTyColorButton = class(TTyButton)` — it descends from the plain push button, NOT from TTySpeedButton, so of that list it inherits only Down (tyControls.Button.pas:159). GroupIndex/AllowAllUp exist solely on TTySpeedButton (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:234-235) and are unreachable here; Flat/Layout/Margin/Spacing/Transparent exist nowhere (greps above).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:330 `TColorButton = class(TCustomSpeedButton)`, with :363 AllowAllUp, :375 Down, :377 Flat, :379 GroupIndex, :381 Layout, :382 Margin, :383 Spacing, :384 Transparent all published.
user_impact: A ported colour button loses eight properties at once. Concretely, a palette row of grouped colour buttons (GroupIndex so exactly one swatch is selected) cannot be built, and the .lfm of any TColorButton that set Flat=True or GroupIndex fails to load.

what_it_does: Per-control pixel gap between the glyph and the caption (-1 centres the pair).
ours_evidence: grep -in 'spacing' over source/ finds BorderSpacing (re-published TControl property, tyControls.Base.pas:131/228), TTyGridPanel.Spacing (tyControls.GridPanel.pas:122), TTyRelativePanel.Spacing (:134) and TTyControlBar.BandSpacing — never on a button. Our glyph/caption gap is a THEME-WIDE metric with no per-instance override: ActiveController.Metric('--glyph-button-gap', TyGlyphButtonGap) at tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:433, :476 and :532.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:433 property Spacing: integer read FSpacing write SetSpacing default 4 (TCustomSpeedButton), :230 (TCustomBitBtn); published TSpeedButton :472, TBitBtn :276, TColorButton dialogs.pp:383; include/speedbutton.inc:295 SetSpacing.
user_impact: One tight icon+label button next to one airy one is impossible: changing the gap retunes every glyph button in the application, so a designer who wants a 12px gap on a single hero button has to change the skin.

what_it_does: Inset of the glyph from the button edge; -1 means centre the glyph+caption block instead of pinning the glyph.
ours_evidence: grep -in 'margin' over source/ finds TTyScrollPanel.EdgeMargin (tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas:85), TTyTitleBar.CapMarginPx, TTyNotification.MarginLogical and TyDialogButtonBar's AMargin parameter — nothing on a button. The glyph is pinned flush to the content-rect edge by TyGlyphButtonSplit (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:294 uses AContentRect.Left directly), and the only inset is the theme's Padding applied in RenderTo (tyControls.Button.pas:556-562).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:427 property Margin: integer read FMargin write SetMargin default -1 (TCustomSpeedButton), :227 (TCustomBitBtn); published TSpeedButton :468, TBitBtn :263, TColorButton dialogs.pp:382; include/speedbutton.inc:260 SetMargin; colorbutton.inc:97-99 shows Margin overriding BorderWidth in the swatch layout.
user_impact: The glyph's distance from the edge is whatever the skin's padding says; a ported button that used Margin to nudge its icon inward (or Margin=-1 to keep the icon+text pair centred while the button is wide) lays out differently and the property does not compile.

what_it_does: A user paint hook fired from Paint, so an app can draw over/instead of the button's own rendering.
ours_evidence: TCustomControl.OnPaint IS inherited (it is public on the ancestor) but is (a) not published by TTyCustomControl (tyControls.Base.pas:196-246 — the list has no OnPaint) and (b) DEAD even from code, because TTyButton.Paint never calls inherited: `procedure TTyButton.Paint; begin RenderTo(Canvas, ClientRect, Font.PixelsPerInch); end;` (tyControls.Button.pas:705-708), while the only thing TCustomControl.Paint does is fire FOnPaint. The library's own paint hook, OnPaintSurface, exists on exactly one control (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42) and is not on any button.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2486 property OnPaint (public on TCustomControl) / :2457 (TGraphicControl); published on the concrete buttons: buttons.pp:496 (TSpeedButton), dialogs.pp:398 (TColorButton); include/customcontrol.inc:57-60 TCustomControl.Paint fires it.
user_impact: Assigning Button.OnPaint compiles (it is inherited) and then silently never fires — the worst failure mode, since there is no error to chase. Any ported code that decorated a speed button in OnPaint stops drawing with no diagnostic.

what_it_does: The colour the button displays and returns from the picker.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorButton.pas:76 `property SelectedColor: TTyColor read FSelectedColor write SetSelectedColor default $FF3B82F6` — different name AND different type (TTyColor, an ARGB value, vs LCL TColor); default is the library accent blue, not clBlack. grep -ri 'ButtonColor' over source/ returns only TyGlyphButtonColorDefault/GlyphColor hits in tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:370 property ButtonColor: TColor read FButtonColor write SetButtonColor; include/colorbutton.inc:34-42.
user_impact: `Btn.ButtonColor := clRed` — the single line every TColorButton user writes — does not compile, and even after renaming, a TColor must be converted (TyColorFromLCL) or the value is misread as ARGB. A .lfm carrying ButtonColor fails to load.

what_it_does: Fired when the button's colour changes.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorButton.pas:83 `property OnColorChange: TNotifyEvent read FOnColorChange write FOnColorChange` — singular 'Change', not 'Changed'. grep -ri 'OnColorChanged' over source/ = 0 hits on any control (the two matches are WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED comments in tyControls.Controller.pas:98 and tyControls.Form.pas:1662).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:387-388 property OnColorChanged: TNotifyEvent read FOnColorChanged write FOnColorChanged.
user_impact: A one-character difference that breaks every ported handler assignment and every .lfm event binding, with a compiler error that reads like the event is missing altogether.

what_it_does: LCL fires OnColorChanged on ANY colour change (programmatic assignment included), suppressed only while csLoading — so one handler keeps the app in sync however the colour was set.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorButton.pas:112-117 SetSelectedColor deliberately does NOT fire: `Invalidate;   // programmatic set: repaint only, no OnColorChange (dialog-driven only)`, documented again at :74-75 and :82. The event fires only from the dialog path, Click (:266-268), and only when the value actually changed.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/colorbutton.inc:34-42 — `if Assigned(FOnColorChanged) and (not (csLoading in ComponentState)) then FOnColorChanged(Self);` inside SetButtonColor.
user_impact: Ported code that relies on the handler running when the app restores a saved colour (Btn.ButtonColor := Config.Color) silently skips its side effects — the preview pane or document does not update, and the difference is invisible until a user notices the colour and the drawing disagree.

what_it_does: Swatch sizing: with ButtonColorAutoSize the swatch expands to fill the button minus the caption/margins; turn it off and the swatch is a fixed ButtonColorSize square.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ButtonColorSize|ButtonColorAutoSize' over source/ = 0 hits. Our swatch size is entirely derived and non-configurable: `cw := content height` (with text) or the whole content width (without), floored by the compile-time constant TyColorButtonMinSwatch = 8 (tyControls.ColorButton.pas:16, 138-149). There is no fixed-size mode and no published size at all.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:366-369 (ButtonColorAutoSize stored IsButtonColorAutoSizeStored, ButtonColorSize); include/colorbutton.inc:20-22 (defaults 16 / True), :85-118 GetGlyphSize branches on ButtonColorAutoSize, :169-175 SetButtonColorSize.
user_impact: A row of colour buttons cannot show a consistent small square swatch beside varying captions — the swatch always tracks the button's height — and a 16x16 swatch on a tall button is unobtainable.

what_it_does: Width of the frame drawn around the colour swatch, which also serves as the swatch's margin when Margin is -1.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'BorderWidth' over source/ returns 107 hits, ALL of them the theme's resolved AStyle.BorderWidth (e.g. tyControls.Base.pas:719-721, tyControls.Arrow.pas:235) — no control publishes a BorderWidth property, and TTyColorButton's swatch frame is hard-coded: `radius := 3` and `StrokeBorder(swatch, ..., 1, borderCol)` (tyControls.ColorButton.pas:160-161), i.e. always exactly 1px.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/dialogs.pp:365 property BorderWidth: Integer read FBorderWidth write SetBorderWidth; include/colorbutton.inc:21 (default 2), :44-50 SetBorderWidth, :97 M := BorderWidth used as the swatch margin.
user_impact: The swatch outline is a fixed hairline; a light-yellow or white swatch on a light surface cannot be given a heavier frame to stay visible, and porting a TColorButton with BorderWidth=0 (no frame) or 4 changes its appearance with no property to restore it.

what_it_does: ImageIndex selects the icon by integer index in the image list; ImageWidth picks which resolution of a multi-resolution list to draw at.
ours_evidence: We address the icon by STRING name instead: `property ImageName: string` (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:166) and `property GlyphName: string` (:153); the nearest analogue of ImageWidth is `property GlyphSize: Integer ... default 0` (:156), which is a drawn edge length in logical px, not an image-list resolution. grep -ri 'ImageWidth' over source/ = 0 hits; the 127 'ImageIndex' hits are all other controls' own item indices (e.g. tyControls.AdvancedComboBox.pas:58/64) — none on a button.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:424 ImageIndex default -1 and :425 ImageWidth default 0 (TCustomSpeedButton); :223-224 (TCustomBitBtn); published TSpeedButton :465-466, TBitBtn :267-268.
user_impact: Icon assignment does not port: `Btn.ImageIndex := 3` must become a name lookup, and code that walks a toolbar assigning sequential indices from a shared TImageList has to be rewritten around string keys — with no compile error if a name is misspelled, just a missing icon.

what_it_does: Hide the caption while keeping it set — an icon-only button that still has text for its hint, action and accelerator.
ours_evidence: grep -in 'ShowCaption' over source/ finds only TTyRibbonGroup.ShowCaption (tyControls.Ribbon.pas:217) and TTyToolBar.ShowCaptions (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:62) — a container-wide switch on the BAR, not on the button. TTySpeedButton (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:197-241) has none; DrawContent decides purely on `Caption <> ''` (:561), so the only way to hide the text is to blank the Caption, which also throws away the mnemonic (TyAccelRegister/DialogChar use Caption, tyControls.Button.pas:217-225).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:432 property ShowCaption: boolean read FShowCaption write SetShowCaption default true; published TSpeedButton :475; include/speedbutton.inc:518 SetShowCaption.
user_impact: An icon-only toolbar button loses its Alt-accelerator and its action text along with its label; and a user-toggleable 'show text labels' toolbar option must clear and restore every Caption by hand instead of flipping one property per button.

what_it_does: Four public one-call glyph loaders: from a named resource in any module instance, from a Lazarus resource, from the widgetset's themed stock icon by idButton, and the DPI-aware LCLGlyphs variant.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'LoadGlyph' over source/ = 0 hits. The only ways in are the property setters IconFont/GlyphName (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:150/153) and Images/ImageName (:164/166); ResolveGlyphBitmap (:362-374) has no resource or stock-icon path.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:210-213 (TCustomBitBtn, all four) and :411-412 (TCustomSpeedButton, two); implementations at include/bitbtn.inc:70,75,80,85 and include/speedbutton.inc:1131,1136; unit-level helpers buttons.pp:523-526.
user_impact: An app that ships its icons as .res/.lrs resources (the normal Lazarus pattern) cannot load them onto a ty button at all, and there is no access to the platform's themed stock icons — so ty buttons in a dialog cannot match the OS's own OK/Cancel iconography.

what_it_does: Whether the glyph is shown always, never, per the application setting (Application.ShowButtonGlyphs) or per the OS/desktop setting — the mechanism behind LCL's app-wide 'no icons on buttons' preference (CM_APPSHOWBTNGLYPHCHANGED).
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'GlyphShowMode' over source/ = 0 hits; grep -ri 'ShowButtonGlyphs' = 0 hits. The glyph draws whenever a source is set — HasGlyphSource (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:376-382) consults only Images/ImageName and IconFont/GlyphName, and DrawContent (:502) mirrors it, with no application or system gate.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:231 property GlyphShowMode: TGlyphShowMode read GetGlyphShowMode write SetGlyphShowMode default gsmApplication, :205 CMAppShowBtnGlyphChanged; published TBitBtn :259; include/bitbtn.inc:98 CanShowGlyph, :159 SetGlyphShowMode.
user_impact: An application that honours the desktop's 'don't show icons on buttons' setting (or offers it as a preference) cannot include ty buttons — theirs keep their icons while the native TBitBtns next to them drop them, so one dialog shows two conventions at once.

what_it_does: Public query: will this button actually paint a glyph right now (optionally also honouring GlyphShowMode)?
ours_evidence: Our equivalent is `function HasGlyphSource: Boolean` declared in the PROTECTED section (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:110, implemented :376-382) — a different name, no AWithShowMode parameter, and unreachable from application code. grep -ri 'CanShowGlyph' over source/ = 0 hits.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:214 (public section of TCustomBitBtn) `function CanShowGlyph(const AWithShowMode: Boolean = False): Boolean;`; implementation include/bitbtn.inc:98.
user_impact: Layout code that asks a button whether it is currently showing an icon — to decide a toolbar's row height or to align a column of labels — must subclass to reach the protected twin.

what_it_does: Makes the Caption follow Kind automatically (and re-follow it on a language change) instead of holding a hand-typed string.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'DefaultCaption' over source/ = 0 hits. Caption is a plain streamed string on our side (tyControls.Button.pas:168) with no Kind to derive from and no re-derivation hook; TextChanged (:607-618) only re-measures.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:217 property DefaultCaption: Boolean read FDefaultCaption write SetDefaultCaption default False; published TBitBtn :251; include/bitbtn.inc:340 SetDefaultCaption, :281 RealizeKind, :354 GetCaptionOfKind.
user_impact: Dialog buttons cannot pick up the LCL's already-translated stock captions (rsmbOK/rsmbCancel/...); each app re-types and re-translates 'OK'/'Cancel'/'Yes'/'No' per form, and a runtime language switch leaves the old text in place.

what_it_does: Per-instance switch: paint no background at all (the parent shows through) vs paint the button face.
ours_evidence: No Transparent property on any button — grep -in 'transparent' over source/*.pas as a property finds only TTyImage.Transparent (tyControls.Image.pas:50) and TTyLabel.Transparent (tyControls.TyLabel.pas:96). The equivalent here is the themed 'ghost' variant: StyleClass := 'ghost' resolves a transparent resting background (source/tyControls.BuiltinThemeData.pas:52 and :688 define TyButton.ghost / TySpeedButton.ghost with transparent rest + hover wash), or a per-instance StyleOverride (tyControls.Base.pas:244). Note it is only ever a THEME-level transparency: the control is windowed, so it still composites the resolved parent colour (TyFillParentBg, tyControls.Button.pas:553).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:434 property Transparent: Boolean read GetTransparent write SetTransparent default true; published TSpeedButton :473, TColorButton dialogs.pp:384; include/speedbutton.inc:1206-1212 GetTransparent.
user_impact: The capability exists but under a name nobody will guess when porting: `Btn.Transparent := False` does not compile, and the replacement is a magic StyleClass string whose behaviour depends on the loaded skin defining a .ghost rule.

what_it_does: Turn '&' mnemonic processing off so the caption is rendered literally.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ShowAccelChar' over source/ = 0 hits. Mnemonic parsing is unconditional: every caption goes through TyParseMnemonic in DrawContent (tyControls.Button.pas:697) and in MeasureCaption (:656), and Alt+letter is always registered (TyAccelRegister in the constructor, :190). The only escape is doubling the ampersand — TyParseMnemonic treats '&&' as a literal '&' (tyControls.Accel.pas:63-64).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:431 property ShowAccelChar: boolean read FShowAccelChar write SetShowAccelChar default true; include/speedbutton.inc:306 SetShowAccelChar.
user_impact: A caption that legitimately contains an ampersand ('AT&T', 'Save & Close', or any string coming from data) silently loses the character and acquires a stray accelerator; the fix requires escaping every value at every assignment site, and there is no switch to disable the behaviour once.

what_it_does: Public query returning the currently-pressed button of this button's group (nil when all are up).
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'FindDownButton' over source/ = 0 hits, and there is no equivalent under another name: the grouping code only ever walks siblings to RELEASE them (UnpressSiblings, tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:627-647) — there is no read-side query. An app must write the Parent.Controls loop itself.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/buttons.pp:409 `function FindDownButton: TCustomSpeedButton;` (public); implementation include/speedbutton.inc:81.
user_impact: Reading back which tool is selected in a radio group — the single most common thing you ask a speed-button group — requires hand-rolling a typed sibling scan in every app, and ported code calling FindDownButton does not compile.

member: Click / OnClick ordering relative to the colour dialog
what_it_does: LCL runs the inherited Click (firing OnClick) FIRST and opens the picker afterwards, so an OnClick handler observes the pre-dialog colour and can prepare state for it.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorButton.pas:252-271 — TySelectColor is called first (:260), FSelectedColor and OnColorChange are updated (:263-268), and only then `inherited Click` fires OnClick (:270), with the comment documenting the choice.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/colorbutton.inc:195-199 — `procedure TColorButton.Click; begin inherited Click; ShowColorDialog; end;`
user_impact: A ported OnClick handler that guarded the dialog (validating, stashing the previous colour for undo, or vetoing) now runs after the user has already picked, so its 'before' snapshot is the 'after' value — an undo step records the wrong colour and no error is raised.

what_it_does: Changing AllowAllUp re-evaluates the whole group (UpdateExclusive) so the group's pressed/unpressed invariant is restored immediately and the affected buttons repaint.
ours_evidence: tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:235 `property AllowAllUp: Boolean read FAllowAllUp write FAllowAllUp default False` — a RAW field write: no group update, not even an Invalidate. The group invariant is only ever enforced from SetDown/Click (:649-678), so it is not re-checked when the flag itself changes.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/speedbutton.inc:133-140 — SetAllowAllUp assigns then calls UpdateExclusive; buttons.pp:415 property AllowAllUp default false.
user_impact: Flipping AllowAllUp to False while the whole group happens to be up leaves the group in a state LCL forbids (no button down, yet no click can produce one via the AllowAllUp path), and setting it in code produces no repaint — the button keeps drawing its previous state until something else invalidates it.

member: Active / ShortCut / ShortCutKey2 (read-only) + the ActiveDefaultControl protocol
what_it_does: Active is True while this button currently OWNS the default role (LCL hands the role to a focused button, which is why ExecuteDefaultAction clicks when FActive or FDefault); ShortCut/ShortCutKey2 expose the accelerators LCL derived from the caption.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ShortCutKey2' over source/ = 0 hits; grep -ri 'ActiveDefaultControl' over source/ = 0 hits (so the role-transfer protocol is not implemented at all); 'property Active' matches only unrelated Boolean run/stop flags (tyControls.ActivityBar.pas:45, tyControls.Hint.pas:51). TTyButton has FDefault/FCancel only (tyControls.Button.pas:153-154) and TTyButton.ExecuteDefaultAction clicks solely `if FDefault` (:415-421).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1254 property Active: boolean read FActive stored false, :1257 ShortCut, :1258 ShortCutKey2; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/buttons.inc:141-144 ExecuteDefaultAction uses `FActive or FDefault`, :180-210 ActiveDefaultControlChanged maintains it.
user_impact: Two things: ported code reading Btn.Active or Btn.ShortCut does not compile; and the behaviour behind Active is missing too — with focus on a non-default TTyButton, Enter still fires the form's Default button instead of the focused one, which is the opposite of what every LCL/VCL dialog does.

member: TToolButton (whole class: Style tbsButton/tbsCheck/tbsDropDown/tbsSeparator/tbsDivider/tbsButtonDrop, Down, Grouped, AllowAllUp, Marked, Indeterminate, ImageIndex, MenuItem, DropdownMenu, Wrap, ShowCaption, Index, OnArrowClick, ArrowClick, CheckMenuDropdown, PointInArrow, GetCurrentIcon)
what_it_does: The LCL toolbar's item class. One TGraphicControl per tool with six styles (push / latching check / dropdown-with-arrow / separator / divider / button+arrow), radio grouping via Grouped+AllowAllUp, an icon by ImageIndex into the bar's Images, a TMenuItem it can clone its caption/shortcut/OnClick from, a DropdownMenu opened by the arrow half, Wrap to force a row break at this item, and Index/PointInArrow/CheckMenuDropdown for hit and menu logic.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'toolbutton' over source/ returned nothing — the class does not exist under any name. Nothing equivalent: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:174-231 AlignControls just lays out whatever generic TControl children the host parented, and :198 special-cases only `is TTyButton` to stamp StyleClass='ghost'. The nearest analogues live elsewhere and are NOT toolbar items: TTySpeedButton (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:197, has GroupIndex/AllowAllUp/Images/ImageName), TTyDropDownButton (tyControls.DropButtons.pas:55), TTyToolSeparator (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:9-20, a separate control ≈ tbsDivider only). No Wrap, no MenuItem cloning, no ImageIndex, no Marked/Indeterminate anywhere: grep 'property Marked|property Indeterminate|property MenuItem|PointInArrow|CheckMenuDropdown' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2103-2236 (declaration; Style :2215, Down :2199, Grouped :2205, AllowAllUp :2196, Marked :2209, Indeterminate :2208, ImageIndex :2207, MenuItem :2210, DropdownMenu :2203, Wrap :2218, ShowCaption :2213, Index :2192, OnArrowClick :2219, PointInArrow :2193, CheckMenuDropdown :2183); implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/toolbutton.inc
user_impact: Every ported form that declares `object ToolButton1: TToolButton` fails to stream. There is no latching/radio tool, no per-item icon index, no per-item dropdown arrow, and no Wrap, so a ported toolbar has to be rebuilt out of unrelated button classes and its row breaks re-hand-placed.

what_it_does: The uniform width side of button metrics: ButtonWidth forces every tool to the same width (paired with ButtonHeight), DropDownWidth sizes the arrow half of a tbsDropDown tool, ButtonDropWidth is the read-only resolved arrow width for tbsButtonDrop, and SetButtonSize(w,h) sets both metrics in one pass without two relayouts.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:53-69 publishes ButtonHeight (:56) but no width counterpart; grep -ri 'buttonwidth' over source/ hits only unrelated controls (tyControls.ComboBox.pas, tyControls.SpinEdit.pas, tyControls.Cascader.pas, tyControls.ToolBarEx.pas's local `widths` array) — never a TTyToolBar property. grep 'ButtonDropWidth|SetButtonSize' over source/ returned nothing; grep 'DropDownWidth' hits only tyControls.Grid.pas and tyControls.TreeSelect.pas. Layout uses each child's own Width verbatim (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:199).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2378 (ButtonWidth), :2387 (DropDownWidth), :2370 (ButtonDropWidth), :2363 (SetButtonSize)
user_impact: A ported ToolBar with ButtonWidth=64 loses uniform buttons: each tool keeps whatever width it happens to have, so the bar reads ragged and .lfm ButtonWidth/DropDownWidth values are silently dropped.

member: ButtonCount, Buttons[Index], ButtonList, RowCount, GetEnumerator (TToolBarEnumerator), BeginUpdate, EndUpdate
what_it_does: The bar's programmatic surface: a typed indexed list of its tools, the count, the raw TList, how many wrapped rows the current layout produced, a for-in enumerator, and BeginUpdate/EndUpdate to batch many item changes into one relayout.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ToolBar.pas has no such members (whole file read; published block :53-69, public block :51-52 declares only the constructor). Host code is left with TWinControl.ControlCount/Controls[] returning untyped TControl. RowCount in particular IS computed and then thrown away: `rows` is an out-param of TyToolbarLayout (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:210) used only to size the bar at :222-226 and never exposed. grep -ri 'ButtonCount|ButtonList|GetEnumerator|SetButtonSize' over source/ returned nothing for this unit (ButtonCount hits only tyControls.Dialogs.pas / tyControls.Form.pas); grep 'BeginUpdate' over source/ shows it on TTyGrid (tyControls.Grid.pas:1197) and collections, never on any of the four bar units.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2366 (ButtonCount), :2367 (Buttons[]), :2368 (ButtonList), :2369 (RowCount), :2362 (GetEnumerator) + :2240-2249 (TToolBarEnumerator); BeginUpdate/EndUpdate C:/lazarus/lcl/toolwin.pp:67-68, override at comctrls.pp:2360
user_impact: `for i := 0 to Bar.ButtonCount-1 do Bar.Buttons[i].Enabled := ...` — the single most common toolbar idiom — does not compile; nor does `for B in Bar do`. Adding ten tools in a loop re-runs the full layout ten times because there is no update lock, and a wrapping bar cannot report how many rows it took.

what_it_does: On LCL the bar's image list is the icon source for every child tool: TToolButton.ImageIndex selects from it, GetCurrentIcon resolves list+index+effect, and assigning it re-measures and repaints every button through a TChangeLink.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:64 `property Images: TImageList read FImages write SetImages;` — but the setter only calls Relayout (:149) and the field is read by nothing except Notification (:236). The admission is in the code: :164 `// (Images/ShowCaptions propagation hooks here if/when TTyButton exposes them.)`. Also a TYPE narrowing: ours is TImageList (:31), theirs TCustomImageList, so a TCustomImageList descendant (including the library's own TTyGlyphImageList in tyControls.GlyphImageList.pas) cannot be assigned. No change-link either: grep 'TChangeLink' in tyControls.ToolBar.pas returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2396 (`property Images: TCustomImageList`), consumed via TToolButton.GetCurrentIcon (:2186-2188) and re-measured through FImageChangeLink (:2282, :2318)
user_impact: Setting Bar.Images does nothing visible — the property exists, streams from a ported .lfm, and silently has no effect, which is worse than a compile error. And a TCustomImageList-typed list (the usual case, including this library's own) will not even assign.

what_it_does: The rest of the icon-list family: a separate hover image set, a separate greyed image set used when a tool is disabled (instead of auto-greying), and ImagesWidth to pick the HiDPI resolution to draw from a multi-resolution list.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'hotimages|disabledimages|imageswidth' over the whole source/ directory returned nothing — none of the three exists anywhere in the library, under any name.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2395 (HotImages), :2383 (DisabledImages), :2397 (ImagesWidth)
user_impact: Ported .lfm properties are lost; there is no way to supply hover or disabled artwork, and no way to tell a multi-resolution image list which pixel size to use on a HiDPI screen.

what_it_does: Turns the tools' text on: with ShowCaptions=False a tool is icon-only, with True the caption is drawn too, and the bar re-measures every button so the row grows.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:62 publishes it with the right name, type and default (False), but the two lines above say so explicitly: :60-61 `{ Reserved (not yet wired): in the reuse-TTyButton model each child button owns its own caption + image, so these have no effect today; kept for forward LCL-parity. }`. The setter (:148) only calls Relayout; FShowCaptions is read nowhere else in the unit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2404 (`ShowCaptions ... default False`), honoured in TToolButton.CalculatePreferredSize / Paint (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/toolbutton.inc)
user_impact: Toggling ShowCaptions at design time or run time changes nothing at all, so an icon-only bar cannot be switched to icon+text (or back) the way the LCL property implies.

what_it_does: Places each tool's caption to the RIGHT of its icon instead of below it — the classic 'large icons with text beside' toolbar mode; the bar re-measures buttons horizontally when it flips.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'property List' over source/ returned nothing (all 'list' hits in tyControls.ToolBar.pas — :181, :189-219 — are the local `list: array of TControl` layout variable). The concept does not exist under another name either: grep 'GlyphLayout' shows a per-button layout on TTyGlyphButtonBase (tyControls.GlyphButtons.pas:137) but the BAR cannot set it — ApplyToButton (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:152-165) only writes StyleClass.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2399 (`property List: Boolean ... default False`)
user_impact: No bar-wide icon/text arrangement switch. Every child must be configured individually (and only if it happens to be a TTyGlyphButton), so a ported List=True toolbar loses its layout mode.

what_it_does: Blank space reserved at the leading edge of the bar before the first tool.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:58 `property Indent: Integer read FIndent write SetIndent default 4;` and the constructor sets FIndent := 4 (:130). It is also used as a VERTICAL pad (:81 `y := AIndent`, :224 `newH := FIndent*2 + ...`), which LCL's Indent never is.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2398 `property Indent: Integer read FIndent write SetIndent default 1;` and constructor `FIndent := 1` (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/toolbar.inc:103)
user_impact: A ported .lfm that omits Indent (i.e. relied on LCL's 1) silently gets 4 logical px of leading gap, and because our Indent doubles as the vertical pad the whole bar also gets 8 px taller than the same value produced in LCL.

what_it_does: The bar's own chrome: EdgeBorders picks WHICH sides get an edge (TToolBar defaults to [ebTop]), EdgeInner/EdgeOuter choose raised/lowered/none for the inner and outer bevel of those edges, and Transparent stops the bar painting a background at all so the parent shows through.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'edgeborders|edgeinner|edgeouter' over the whole source/ returned nothing. Our bar hard-codes a single BOTTOM hairline with no way to move or remove it: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:256-260 `P.FillBackground(Rect(0, H - bw, W, H), bg, 0); // bottom hairline`. grep 'property Transparent' over source/ finds it only on TTyImage (tyControls.Image.pas:50) and TTyLabel (tyControls.TyLabel.pas:96), never a bar. Partial themed equivalents do exist and should be named: an alpha `background:` via StyleOverride (tyControls.Base.pas:244) approximates Transparent, and `render-style: bevel3d|inset3d` (TyApplyRenderStyle, tyControls.Base.pas:801-822) approximates EdgeInner/EdgeOuter — but neither is reachable as a published property and neither can select the SIDE.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2388-2390 (EdgeBorders default [ebTop], EdgeInner, EdgeOuter) re-published from C:/lazarus/lcl/toolwin.pp:70-72; Transparent at comctrls.pp:2408
user_impact: A ported bar's edge always lands on the bottom regardless of EdgeBorders, an ebLeft/ebRight-bordered vertical bar is impossible, and Transparent=True cannot be expressed as a property (only by hand-writing CSS into StyleOverride).

what_it_does: OnPaintButton(Sender: TToolButton; State: integer) lets the app custom-draw an individual tool; OnPaint lets it draw over the bar's own surface after the bar paints. (TControlBar publishes OnPaint too.)
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'onpaintbutton' over source/ returned nothing. grep 'property OnPaint' over source/ finds only unrelated, differently-named hooks on other controls (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42 OnPaintSurface, tyControls.PreviewBox.pas:94 OnPaintPreview, tyControls.TreeView.pas:637 OnPaintText) — none on any bar. TTyToolBar.Paint/RenderTo (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:239-263) offers no application hook; the only extension seam is subclassing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2416 (OnPaintButton, type at :2253), :2428 (OnPaint); TControlBar's OnPaint at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1679/1746
user_impact: An app that decorated one tool (an overlay badge, a custom pressed look) or drew on the bar background has nowhere to hook and must subclass the control instead of assigning an event.

what_it_does: Switches the bar between one full-width SimpleText line (True) and the Panels collection (False).
ours_evidence: tyControls.StatusBar.pas:64 `property SimplePanel: Boolean read FSimplePanel write SetSimplePanel default False;` and the constructor (:142-150) never sets FSimplePanel, so it starts False = panel mode.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:198 `property SimplePanel: Boolean read FSimplePanel write SetSimplePanel default True;` and C:/lazarus/lcl/include/statusbar.inc:22 `FSimplePanel := True;`
user_impact: Opposite out-of-the-box behaviour and an inverted streaming rule. A ported .lfm that set SimplePanel=False (a value LCL had to stream because its default is True) is fine, but one that relied on the True default — the common `StatusBar1.SimpleText := 'Ready'` case — streams nothing, so our bar comes up in panel mode and the SimpleText never appears.

what_it_does: Per-panel frame: pbLowered (the default sunken well), pbRaised, or pbNone for a flat panel.
ours_evidence: tyControls.StatusBar.pas:18-21 publishes only Text, Width and Alignment. grep -ri 'property Bevel|BevelInner|BevelOuter|BevelWidth' over the whole source/ returned nothing. The painter draws a 1px separator LINE before each panel instead (tyControls.StatusBar.pas:223-227) with no per-panel control at all; the only lever is a bar-wide theme border colour.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:89 `property Bevel: TStatusPanelBevel read FBevel write SetBevel default pbLowered;` (enum at :46), ctor default C:/lazarus/lcl/include/statuspanel.inc:19
user_impact: Individual panels cannot be flattened or raised; a ported bar that used pbNone on its stretch panel loses that and gets the separator rule anyway.

what_it_does: Owner-drawn panels: set a panel's Style to psOwnerDraw and the bar fires OnDrawPanel(StatusBar, Panel, Rect) so the app paints that cell itself (progress bars, icons, coloured indicators in a status cell).
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'psOwnerDraw|OnDrawPanel' over the whole source/ returned nothing. TTyStatusPanel has no Style member (tyControls.StatusBar.pas:8-22) and RenderTo unconditionally draws text for every panel (:228-229 `P.DrawText(...)`), with no per-panel escape.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:92 (Style, enum at :45), :209 (OnDrawPanel, type at :115-116), dispatched by TStatusBar.DrawPanel (:159) / LMDrawItem (:160)

On the collection side each panel can reach its owning bar (TStatusPanel.StatusBar), the collection exposes StatusBar and a writeable Items[], GetDisplayName gives designer-readable item names, and OnCreatePanelClass lets an app substitute its own panel class.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'BeginUpdate|EndUpdate|InvalidatePanel|UpdatingStatusBar|SizeGripEnabled|OnCreatePanelClass' over tyControls.StatusBar.pas returned nothing (whole file read; public section is tyControls.StatusBar.pas:58-61 = Create, Destroy, PanelAtPos only). Every panel setter calls Changed(False) (:123-127) → TTyStatusPanels.Update → full Invalidate (:135-139), so N edits = N repaints. TTyStatusPanel has no StatusBar back-reference and no GetDisplayName override (:8-22) — note the sibling TTyCoolBand DOES override GetDisplayName (tyControls.CoolBar.pas:404), so this is an inconsistency inside our own library, not a policy. what_it_does: Break=True means this band starts a new row; Width is the band's assigned width (180 default); MinWidth is its resize floor (100 default).
ours_evidence: tyControls.CoolBar.pas:86 `property Break: Boolean ... default False;`, :88 `property Width: Integer ... default 0;` (0 = 'auto, use the control's own width', see :438-442), :89 `property MinWidth: Integer ... default 0;`. LCL gives each band its own row unless told otherwise; ours packs them all onto row 1 unless every band's Break is set. A ported .lfm that omitted Width/MinWidth (relying on 180/100) gets 0/0, so bands take whatever width the hosted control happens to have and can be dragged down to our DefaultBandMinWidth (24, :186) instead of 100.

what_it_does: Chooses how the grab handle is drawn: gsSimple, gsDouble (the default), gsHorLines, gsVerLines, gsGripper, gsButton.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'grabstyle' over the whole source/ returned nothing. The gripper look is hard-coded to exactly one of those six variants — two vertical rails, i.e. gsDouble — in TTyControlBar.DrawGripper (tyControls.ControlBar.pas:355-381, `// Two rails centred in the gripper column`, :378-380), which TTyCoolBar reuses through PaintGrippers (tyControls.CoolBar.pas:772). Not themeable either: DrawGripper takes its colour from the style but its SHAPE from code, and grep over the theme sources for a gripper token returns nothing.

user_impact: A ported bar's GrabStyle is dropped and every grip looks the same. gsButton in particular (a raised button-like grab) is a visibly different affordance that cannot be reproduced, not even via the theme.

what_it_does: GrabWidth is the width of the grab handle strip; HorizontalSpacing and VerticalSpacing are the independent gaps between bands along a row and between rows.

The two spacings collapse into ONE property: tyControls.ControlBar.pas:88 `property BandSpacing: Integer read FBandSpacing write SetBandSpacing default 3;`, and TyCoolBarPack uses that single ASpacing for both axes — horizontal advance at tyControls.CoolBar.pas:294 `x := rowStart + w + ASpacing;` and row advance at :282 `Inc(y, ABandHeight + ASpacing);`. grep -ri 'grabwidth|horizontalspacing|verticalspacing' over source/ returned nothing.

what_it_does: Draws each band's Text caption beside its grip and reserves layout room for it.

user_impact: Inverted default and inverted streaming. A ported .lfm that set band captions and relied on LCL's ShowText=True streams nothing for the property, so all the band captions silently disappear and the bands also pack tighter (the caption strip is no longer reserved).

what_it_does: FixedSize on the BAR makes every band the same height and suppresses band resizing bar-wide; FixedOrder forbids dragging bands into a different order (they may still move between rows).
ours_evidence: TTyCoolBar publishes no FixedSize or FixedOrder (tyControls.CoolBar.pas:182-201) — only the PER-BAND TTyCoolBand.FixedSize exists (:92), so there is no one switch for the whole bar. grep -ri 'fixedorder' over the whole source/ returned nothing. Reordering is not implemented at all, and is documented as such: tyControls.CoolBar.pas:20-22 `NOT implemented: reordering bands WITHIN a row. That needs a child-index primitive and the LCL exposes only SetZOrder(TopMost)` (repeated at :871-873), so FixedOrder has nothing to forbid.

The deeper issue is that our bands cannot be reordered within a row in the first place, so a user who drags a band sideways gets a resize where LCL gives a reorder.

what_it_does: AutosizeBands shrinks every band to its content in one call; MouseToBandPos(X, Y; out ABand: Integer; out AGrabber: Boolean) is the public hit-test telling the app which band index is under a point and whether the point is on its grab handle; EndUpdate ends the batched-layout lock; FindBandIndex(AControl) returns a band's ordinal.

Our nearest hit-test is deliberately NOT public: `function BandAtPoint(AX, AY: Integer): TControl;` sits in the PRIVATE section (:134, body :785-807), returns the hosted TControl rather than an index, and reports no grabber flag. FindBand(AControl): TTyCoolBand exists (:109/:479) but no index form. No BeginUpdate/EndUpdate anywhere in the unit.

user_impact: An app cannot ask which band the mouse is over (the code exists but is private), cannot autosize the bar's bands, cannot batch a bulk band edit into one relayout, and cannot get a band's index for insert/move arithmetic.

what_it_does: The ControlBar's whole customization contract: OnBandDrag vetoes a band drag per control, OnBandInfo supplies a band's Insets/PreferredSize/RowCount so the app can size it, OnBandMove reports/adjusts the target rect while a band is dragged, OnBandPaint hands the app the canvas and a TBandPaintOptions set (bpoGrabber/bpoFrame/bpoGradient/bpoRoundRect) to draw a band itself, and OnCanResize/OnConstrainedResize/OnPaint are the resize and paint hooks.

TTyControlBar publishes exactly four properties and no events at all (tyControls.ControlBar.pas:77-89: BandHeight, RowSize, GripperWidth, BandSpacing). grep 'OnCanResize' over source/ finds only TTySplitter's own differently-typed event (tyControls.Splitter.pas:47). Painting is closed: Paint (:383-408) draws the panel frame then PaintGrippers with no application hook; the only seams are the PROTECTED virtual PackBands/PaintGrippers (:64-67), i.e. subclass-only.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1674 (OnBandDrag), :1676 (OnBandMove), :1675 (OnBandInfo), :1677 (OnBandPaint), :1678 (OnCanResize), :1679 (OnPaint) — all re-published on TControlBar at :1720-1727, :1746; event types at :1504-1509; dispatch via DoBandMove/DoBandPaint/GetControlInfo (:1625-1633)
user_impact: Nothing about a band's size, drag permission or appearance can be customized from the application. Every ported form that assigned any of these seven handlers fails to compile, and the behaviour they implemented has to be re-created by subclassing the control.

member: AutoDrag, AutoDock, DockSite, RowSnap (and the band drag they configure)
what_it_does: A TControlBar's defining behaviour: the user grabs a band's grabber and drags it to another row or position, bands snap to the row grid (RowSnap, default True), AutoDrag (default True) lets a band be dragged out of the bar, and AutoDock/DockSite (both default True) make the bar a dock target that accepts a dragged toolbar.
ours_evidence: Our grippers are DECORATIVE and the unit says so up front: tyControls.ControlBar.pas:11-13 `Each band draws a left GRIPPER ... The gripper is DECORATIVE: there are no mouse handlers in this unit, so nothing can be grabbed by it yet.` Confirmed by structure — TTyControlBar declares no MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp (protected section :55-70). grep -ri 'autodrag|autodock|rowsnap' over the whole source/ returned nothing, and grep 'property DockSite' over source/ returned nothing. The per-child band assignment that a drag would update is admitted to be write-only: :46-48 `NOTE it is currently write-only from the layout's point of view: AlignControls rebuilds it FROM the packing result, and TyControlBarPack takes no preferred-band parameter, so setting it does not steer the packer.` (The sibling TTyCoolBar does implement gripper dragging — tyControls.CoolBar.pas:809-891 — so this is a gap in this class, not a library-wide policy.)
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1664 (AutoDrag default True), :1663 (AutoDock default True), :1666 (DockSite default True), :1673 (RowSnap default True) — re-published on TControlBar at :1688-1689, :1698, :1715; drag implementation MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp + MoveBand/NormalizeRows/ShiftBands (:1639-1649), docking events OnDockDrop/OnDockOver/OnUnDock/OnGetSiteInfo at :1728-1729, :1737, :1750
user_impact: The control looks like a ControlBar and lays out like one but cannot be manipulated: dragging a gripper does nothing, so the end user cannot rearrange bands, and no toolbar can be docked into it. Four published .lfm properties are also silently dropped.

member: DrawingStyle, GradientDirection, GradientStartColor, GradientEndColor, Picture, BevelInner, BevelOuter, BevelWidth
what_it_does: The bar's own look: DrawingStyle dsNormal/dsGradient, the gradient's direction and start/end colours, a Picture tiled behind the bands, and the inherited panel bevels (TControlBar re-defaults BevelInner to bvRaised and BevelOuter to bvLowered — the classic recessed rebar frame).

member: TCtrlBand (band object) + HitTest, MouseToBandPos, StickControls, BeginUpdate, EndUpdate

BandCount is protected, not public (:59).

what_it_does: Lets the bar size itself to its content through CalculatePreferredSize — a status bar takes its height from the font, a wrapping toolbar grows/shrinks by rows, a cool bar/control bar by band rows — and, crucially, lets the host turn that OFF and pin the height.
ours_evidence: None of the four publishes AutoSize: tyControls.ToolBar.pas:53-69, tyControls.StatusBar.pas:62-71, tyControls.CoolBar.pas:182-201, tyControls.ControlBar.pas:77-89; and TTyCustomControl does not publish it either (tyControls.Base.pas:196-245) — though many sibling controls do (`grep 'property AutoSize'` hits tyControls.Button.pas:145, tyControls.CheckBox.pas:58, tyControls.Breadcrumb.pas:269, and ~20 more, so this is an omission on the bars, not a library policy). Instead the behaviour is hard-wired and cannot be switched off: TTyToolBar assigns Height unconditionally when docked top/bottom (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:221-227) and TTyControlBar does the same (tyControls.ControlBar.pas:314-322); TTyStatusBar has NO auto-height at all — a one-shot constructor value, tyControls.StatusBar.pas:149 `Height := TyDensityHeight(ActiveController, 22);`. No CalculatePreferredSize override exists in any of the four.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:180 `property AutoSize default true;` (TStatusBar, with CalculatePreferredSize :147-149 and ctor `AutoSize := True` at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/statusbar.inc:28), :2374 (TToolBar, with DoAutoSize :2337 + WrapButtons :2351), :2666 (TCoolBar), C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1665/:1690 (TControlBar)
user_impact: A host cannot pin a toolbar/control bar height (the auto-grow always wins and overwrites a designed Height), and cannot get a status bar to follow the font — a larger UI font overflows its fixed 22px bar. AutoSize=False in a ported .lfm is silently dropped, which is the case where the layout visibly changes.

member: DragCursor, DragKind, DragMode, OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnStartDrag, OnEndDrag (+ DockSite, OnDockDrop, OnDockOver, OnStartDock, OnEndDock, OnUnDock, OnGetSiteInfo on the two dockable bars)
what_it_does: LCL drag-and-drop and docking, published on all four bars: DragMode dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down, DragKind dkDock turns the drag into a dock operation, and the OnDrag*/OnDock* events let the app accept a payload or dock a toolbar. This is TControl-level machinery unrelated to how the control paints itself.
ours_evidence: None of the four bar units publishes any of it (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:53-69, tyControls.StatusBar.pas:62-71, tyControls.CoolBar.pas:182-201, tyControls.ControlBar.pas:77-89) and the base classes do not either (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-245). Library-wide grep is nearly empty: `grep -rin 'property DragMode|property DragKind|property DragCursor'` over source/ hits ONLY tyControls.Memo.pas:566-568, and `grep 'OnDragDrop|OnStartDrag|OnEndDrag'` only tyControls.Memo.pas:571-574 (TTyTreeView's OnDragOver at tyControls.TreeView.pas:658 is its own internal node-drag type, not TControl's). `grep 'property DockSite|OnDockDrop|OnDockOver|OnUnDock|OnStartDock|OnEndDock|OnGetSiteInfo'` over the whole source/ returned nothing. So one control in the library proves the mechanism is publishable on a ty control — the bars just never did.
user_impact: None of the four bars can be a drag source or a drop target, and neither dockable bar can host a docked toolbar. Any ported form that assigned OnDragOver/OnDragDrop on a bar, or set DragMode/DragKind/DockSite in the .lfm, fails to compile or loses the setting.

what_it_does: Right-to-left support. All four LCL bars publish BiDiMode, TStatusPanel adds its own BidiMode/ParentBiDiMode, and the layout code actually honours it — the cool bar keeps FRightToLeft and mirrors band packing, the control bar passes ARightToLeft into AlignControlToBand, and the status bar overrides SetBiDiMode to re-lay its panels.
ours_evidence: grep -ric 'bidi' over the whole source/ returns exactly one file, tyControls.Memo.pas, with a single hit (a comment); grep -ric 'righttoleft' over source/ returns nothing at all. None of the four bar units mentions it, the base classes do not publish it (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-245), and every layout function assumes left-to-right unconditionally: TyToolbarLayout (tyControls.ToolBar.pas:75-94, `x := AIndent` then increasing), TyStatusPanelRects (tyControls.StatusBar.pas:85-113), TyControlBarPack (tyControls.ControlBar.pas:110-151), TyCoolBarPack (tyControls.CoolBar.pas:252-297). There is no themed equivalent — direction is not a style token.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:181 (TStatusBar.BiDiMode) with SetBiDiMode override :150; :90-91 (TStatusPanel.BidiMode / ParentBiDiMode); :2670 (TCoolBar.BiDiMode) with FRightToLeft :2605 and CMBiDiModeChanged :2615; C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1694 (TControlBar.BiDiMode) with AlignControlToBand(ABand, ARightToLeft) :1612 and CMBiDiModeChanged :1622
user_impact: An Arabic/Hebrew UI gets left-to-right bars: status panels start at the left, toolbar buttons and rebar bands pack from the left with the grip on the wrong side. Ported .lfm BiDiMode settings are dropped silently, and there is no property or theme token to compensate.

what_it_does: Selects the drawing/data model of the list: standard text rows, owner-drawn fixed-height rows, owner-drawn variable-height rows, or a virtual list whose rows are supplied on demand.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'TListBoxStyle|lbOwnerDraw|lbVirtual' over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. TTyListBox's whole published block is tyControls.ListBox.pas:106-123 and contains no Style. The only owner-draw seam is the PROTECTED virtual PaintItemContent (tyControls.ListBox.pas:58-59), reachable from a descendant unit only, never from a host application.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:528 (TListBoxStyle), :681 (property Style ... default lbStandard), :724 (published on TListBox); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:82-85 maps it onto LBS_OWNERDRAWFIXED/VARIABLE.
user_impact: A host cannot switch our list box into owner-draw mode at all, and there is no virtual mode, so a list of 100k rows must be materialised as 100k TStringList entries.

what_it_does: Per-row custom paint callback giving the host the Canvas, the row rect and the TOwnerDrawState (selected/focused/disabled/background-painted).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnDrawItem' over source/ returned nothing. Row painting is closed: RenderTo owns the row loop (tyControls.ListBox.pas:822-880) and calls the protected virtual PaintItemContent(P: TTyPainter; ...) (tyControls.ListBox.pas:890-904) — a TTyPainter, not a TCanvas, and no state parameter.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:652 (property OnDrawItem), :735 (published); DrawItem hook stdctrls.pp:605 with body C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:519-531; dispatched from LMDrawListItem, customlistbox.inc:308-334.
user_impact: Any per-row decoration a user wants (icons, two-line rows, progress bars in rows) requires subclassing our unit instead of assigning one event handler.

what_it_does: Asks the host for the height of an individual row, so rows may differ in height (lbOwnerDrawVariable).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnMeasureItem' over source/ hits only tyControls.TreeView.pas:132/231/642 (TTyTreeView has exactly this capability, per-node) — nothing on the list box. TTyListBox has ONE height for every row: ItemHeight (tyControls.ListBox.pas:115) scaled in ScaledItemHeight (350-354) and used for every row rect (837-842).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:658 (property OnMeasureItem), :742 (published), :627 (MeasureItem); bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:728-732 and LMMeasureItem :336-352.
user_impact: Variable-height rows are impossible; a list mixing one-line and two-line entries cannot be built even by subclassing, because the row loop assumes a uniform height.

what_it_does: Newspaper-style multi-column layout: the list wraps into N columns and scrolls horizontally instead of vertically.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'property Columns' over source/ hits tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:55, tyControls.ColorGrid.pas:42, tyControls.RadioGroup.pas:54 and tyControls.Columns.pas:211 (grid columns) — none of them the list box. RenderTo lays out a single column of full-width rows (tyControls.ListBox.pas:837-842) and MaxTopIndex/VisibleRows assume one column (322-326, 356-366).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:639 (property Columns ... default 0), :700 (published); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:79-80 (LBS_MULTICOLUMN) and :244-251 (SetColumns).
user_impact: A short-item picker that should show 3 columns in a wide box can only be shown as one tall scrolling column.

what_it_does: Sets the horizontal scroll extent so items wider than the client area can be scrolled into view.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ScrollWidth' over source/ returned nothing. UpdateScrollBar only ever creates a vertical bar: FScrollBar.Kind := sbVertical; Align := alRight (tyControls.ListBox.pas:552-566); there is no horizontal bar and DoMouseWheel only moves TopIndex (727-747).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:676 (property ScrollWidth ... default 0), :721 (published); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:253-258 (SetScrollWidth), :268-274 (GetScrollWidth); WS_HSCROLL in CreateParams :86-87.
user_impact: Long item text is simply cut off at the right edge with no way to read the rest — a file-path or SQL list is unusable.

what_it_does: With MultiSelect on, chooses between extended selection (plain click replaces, Ctrl toggles, Shift ranges) and simple multi-select (every plain click toggles that row, no modifier needed).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ExtendedSelect' over source/ returned nothing. MouseDown hard-codes the extended behaviour: Shift = range, Ctrl = toggle, plain = clear-then-select (tyControls.ListBox.pas:667-690).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:642 (property ExtendedSelect ... default true), :706 (published); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:70-78 (LBS_MULTIPLESEL vs LBS_EXTENDEDSEL) and :393-400 (SetExtendedSelect).
user_impact: Touch/kiosk style pick-many lists, where each tap toggles a row without holding Ctrl, cannot be built.

what_it_does: Controls whether a focus rectangle is drawn on the FOCUSED row, which in a multi-select list is distinct from the selected rows.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'lboDrawFocusRect' and 'TListBoxOptions' over source/ returned nothing; TTyListBox publishes no Options (tyControls.ListBox.pas:106-123). RenderTo resolves only tysActive (selected), tysHover, tysNormal per row (tyControls.ListBox.pas:824-834), so in MultiSelect the keyboard focus row FItemIndex — which arrow keys move independently of the selection bits (639-649) — is painted with no marker of any kind.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:530-533 (TListBoxOption/lboDrawFocusRect), :671 (property Options ... default DefOptions), :714 (published); drawn at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:330-331.
user_impact: In a multi-select list the user cannot see where the keyboard cursor is, so Shift+arrow extension is blind guessing.

what_it_does: When true (the Delphi default), a selection change — including a keyboard-driven one — also fires OnClick; the flag lets a host turn that coupling off.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ClickOnSelChange' over source/ returned nothing. Our OnChange fires from SelectItem (tyControls.ListBox.pas:396-397) and OnClick fires only from LCL's mouse click path, with no way to couple or decouple them.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:637-638 (property ClickOnSelChange ... default true), :698 (published); logic at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:546-557 plus the double-click-suppression in WMLButtonUp :363-371.
user_impact: Delphi/LCL code that hangs its logic on OnClick and relies on arrow-key selection firing it silently stops working after a port.

member: OnSelectionChange(Sender; User: Boolean) — ours is OnChange(Sender) (plus LockSelectionChange/UnlockSelectionChange)
what_it_does: Selection-changed notification carrying whether the change came from the USER or from code, with a lock pair so bulk programmatic updates fire it once (or not at all).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListBox.pas:117 `property OnChange: TNotifyEvent` — different name, and no User flag. grep -rin 'OnSelectionChange' over source/ shows the identifier is already used elsewhere in the library (tyControls.ButtonGroup.pas:99, tyControls.Memo.pas:554), so the naming is inconsistent rather than unavailable. grep -rin 'LockSelectionChange' returned nothing; our internal bulk paths instead suppress by hand (FSuppressItemsChanged, tyControls.ListBox.pas:24, and the deliberately silent ResyncSelectionFromTexts, 240-267).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:668-669 (OnSelectionChange), :755 (published), :608 (DoSelectionChange), :625/:631 (Lock/UnlockSelectionChange); bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:546-557 and :708-716.
user_impact: Ported handlers do not compile under the LCL name, and a handler that must ignore programmatic selection (to avoid feedback loops when code sets ItemIndex) has no User flag to test and no lock to hold.

what_it_does: The item collection. LCL types it as the abstract TStrings so any TStrings descendant can be assigned or passed.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListBox.pas:107 `property Items: TStringList read FItems write SetItems`, setter signature SetItems(const AValue: TStringList) (line 25, body 169-195); the field is a concrete TStringList (line 11).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:647 `property Items: TStrings read FItems write SetItems`; setter takes TStrings, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:594-602.
user_impact: `LB.Items := AnyTStrings` and `procedure P(L: TStrings)` call sites that compile against TListBox fail to compile here; hosts must copy through a temporary TStringList.

what_it_does: Count is the Delphi-compatibility alias for Items.Count on the control itself; IntegralHeight makes the box show only whole rows (no clipped last row).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'property Count' over source/ hits only tyControls.Rating.pas:54 and tyControls.Sparkline.pas:54; grep -rin 'IntegralHeight' returned nothing. TTyListBox exposes neither (tyControls.ListBox.pas:106-123); a partial last row is in fact possible because VisibleRows truncates (356-366) while the box height is arbitrary.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:641 (property Count, commented 'for Delphi compatability'), :644 + :709 (IntegralHeight — LCL's own comment says 'not implemented').
user_impact: `if LB.Count = 0` — a very common idiom — does not compile; IntegralHeight is a straight porting break (though a no-op in LCL too, so behaviour parity is already there for it).

member: Clear; AddItem(const Item: String; AnObject: TObject); DeleteSelected; SelectRange(ALow, AHigh, ASelected); GetSelectedText
what_it_does: The control-level list-manipulation surface: empty the list (also resetting ItemIndex), append text+object, delete every selected row, select/deselect a range programmatically, and read all selected item texts joined by LineEnding.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'procedure Clear;' over source/ hits Calculator/Cascader/Grid/ImageCollection/ImageView/ListGroupPanel — never the list box; TTyColorListBox has only ClearColors (tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:23). grep -rin 'procedure AddItem' hits tyControls.OfficeListBox.pas:31 (AddItem(const S: string)) and tyControls.AdvancedListBox.pas:64 (title/subtitle/imageindex) — different signatures on descendants, never (Item, AnObject) on TTyListBox. grep -rin 'DeleteSelected' and 'GetSelectedText' returned nothing. grep -rin 'SelectRange' hits tyControls.Grid.pas:1930 and tyControls.ListView.pas:337; on the list box the equivalent is the PRIVATE ApplyRangeSelection(ALo, AHi) (tyControls.ListBox.pas:50, 528-538) with no ASelected parameter. Our public surface is only SelectItem/VisibleRows/SimulateKeyDown/SelCount/ClearSelection/SelectAll (tyControls.ListBox.pas:93-100).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:614 (AddItem), :616 (Clear), :629 (SelectRange), :630 (DeleteSelected), :620 (GetSelectedText); bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:637-640, :691-695, :743-759, :761-777, :801-814.
user_impact: `LB.Clear`, `LB.AddItem(s, obj)`, `LB.DeleteSelected` and `LB.SelectRange(...)` are everyday LCL/Delphi calls that all fail to compile; a 'remove selected' button has to be hand-written with a reverse loop.

member: ItemAtPos(Pos, Existing); GetIndexAtXY(X, Y); GetIndexAtY(Y); ItemRect(Index): TRect; ItemVisible(Index); ItemFullyVisible(Index); MakeCurrentVisible
what_it_does: The public hit-test / row-geometry / scroll-into-view surface: which row is under a point, where a row is on screen, whether it is (fully) visible, and scroll the current row into view.
ours_evidence: grep -rin over source/ for ItemAtPos, GetIndexAtXY, GetIndexAtY, ItemVisible, ItemFullyVisible, MakeCurrentVisible returned nothing at all; 'ItemRect' matches only a TTyBreadcrumb record field (tyControls.Breadcrumb.pas:79). The two near-equivalents are non-public: RowAtY is PROTECTED and Y-only (tyControls.ListBox.pas:68, body 906-913) and EnsureSelectionVisible is PRIVATE (tyControls.ListBox.pas:41, body 368-381).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:618-626 declares all seven as public; bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:784-794 (GetIndexAtXY/Y), :822-835 (ItemAtPos), :843-856 (ItemRect), :863-874 (ItemVisible), :881-892 (ItemFullyVisible), :894-905 (MakeCurrentVisible).
user_impact: A host cannot implement drag-to-reorder, a per-row context menu, a row tooltip, or 'scroll the current item into view' — every one of those needs a public hit-test or row rect.

what_it_does: Turns the control's frame on or off (bsNone / bsSingle).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'BorderStyle' over source/ shows no TTy control publishes it (matches are internal: tyControls.BalloonHint.pas:187 sets a form's, tyControls.Base.pas:718/805-809 is the theme's own tbsInset/tbsOutset enum). The themed equivalent DOES exist — per-instance StyleOverride, e.g. 'border-width: 0' (tyControls.Base.pas:240-244) or the TyListBox theme tokens consumed by DrawFrame (tyControls.ListBox.pas:782) — so this is a naming/porting break, not a missing capability.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:635 (property BorderStyle default bsSingle), :697 (published on TListBox); default set in the constructor, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:611.
user_impact: `LB.BorderStyle := bsNone` does not compile and there is no borderless option in the Object Inspector; the user must learn the CSS-ish StyleOverride string instead.

member: DragCursor / DragKind / DragMode + OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnEndDrag / OnStartDrag
what_it_does: LCL drag-and-drop: automatic drag start, drop targeting, and the four notification events.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'DragMode|DragKind|DragCursor|OnDragDrop|OnDragOver|OnEndDrag|OnStartDrag' over source/ shows TTyMemo publishes exactly this set (tyControls.Memo.pas:566-568 and 571-574) — the capability is inherited from TControl and merely needs publishing — while the list-box family publishes none of it (tyControls.ListBox.pas:106-123; base published blocks tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 and 196-246).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:703-705 (DragCursor/DragKind/DragMode), :733-734, :737, :757 (the four events), declared on TControl at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1570-1572; TCustomListBox also overrides the drag hooks, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:43-52.
user_impact: Dragging items out of the list (to another list, to a tree, to a file drop target) is not configurable in the designer; a user who sees it work on TTyMemo will report the list box as broken.

what_it_does: Hint-about-to-show customisation (per-row tooltips) and horizontal mouse-wheel / tilt-wheel notifications.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnShowHint' over source/ finds only a comment (tyControls.Chart.pas:360 notes it must not collide with TControl's OnShowHint); grep -rin 'OnMouseWheelHorz|OnMouseWheelLeft|OnMouseWheelRight' returned nothing. The base publishes only OnMouseWheel / OnMouseWheelUp / OnMouseWheelDown (tyControls.Base.pas:220-222) and Hint/ShowHint/ParentShowHint without the event (tyControls.Base.pas:202-203, 230).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:751-753 (OnMouseWheelHorz/Left/Right), :756 (OnShowHint); declarations C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1597 and :1813.
user_impact: Per-row tooltips (the normal way to show a truncated item's full text) cannot be built, and a horizontal-tilt wheel or trackpad two-finger swipe reports nothing.

what_it_does: Right-to-left layout: mirrors item alignment, the scrollbar side, and (on TCheckListBox) the check column.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'bidimode' over source/ returns exactly one hit — a comment in tyControls.Memo.pas:557 declaring 'Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope'; grep -rin 'UseRightToLeft' returned nothing. Our painting is unconditionally LTR: text is drawn taLeftJustify (tyControls.ListBox.pas:902), the swatch/checkbox column is always on the left (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:96, tyControls.ColorBox.pas:143) and the scrollbar is always alRight (tyControls.ListBox.pas:558).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:695 (BidiMode), :715 (ParentBidiMode) published on TListBox; declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1834-1835; honoured per-row by the check list box at C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:199-202 (UseRightToLeftAlignment).
user_impact: Arabic/Hebrew UIs get a mirrored form with a stubbornly left-aligned, left-scrollbar list — the library cannot ship into RTL locales.

what_it_does: In LCL, an unset (0) ItemHeight makes each row as tall as the control's Font needs, recomputed when the font changes; writing 0 again returns the list to that automatic mode.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListBox.pas:304-310: GetItemHeight returns ActiveController.Metric('--item-height', 24) — a density token — and never consults Font. SetItemHeight (312-320) sets FItemHeightExplicit := True BEFORE the equality test and then clamps FItemHeight to a minimum of 1, so (a) writing 0 yields a 1px row rather than 'auto', and (b) once written the control can never fall back to the token/auto height. grep -rin 'CalculateStandardItemHeight' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:645 (ItemHeight, no default) and :584 (CalculateStandardItemHeight); bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlistbox.inc:472-492 (0 => derived) and :54-68 (TextHeight('Fj') from Font), used by LMMeasureItem :343-346; DPI rescale at :533-544.
user_impact: Setting Font.Size := 20 leaves 24px rows and vertically clipped text, and there is no way to get font-sized rows back after any ItemHeight write; TCheckListBox's font-driven re-height (checklst.pas:440-445) has no counterpart either.

what_it_does: Per-row three-state check value, and the tri-state cycle Unchecked -> Checked -> Grayed on toggle.
ours_evidence: Only a Boolean Checked[] exists, stored as PtrInt 0/1 in Items.Objects (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:30, 37-49), and the paint path resolves just [tysActive]/[tysNormal] with a plain tgCheck glyph (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:98-105). grep -rin 'TCheckBoxState' over source/ shows full tri-state support already exists elsewhere — tyControls.CheckBox.pas:10/59 (property State ... default cbUnchecked), its cbGrayed cycle at :194-198 and its '--glyph-check-indeterminate' render at :265, plus tyControls.Grid.pas:1880 CellCheckState — so the type and the glyph are built but not wired to the check list box.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:85 (property State[AIndex]: TCheckBoxState), getter :302-310, setter :356-368, tri-state cycle in Toggle :233-243.
user_impact: A 'partially selected' row (a parent whose children are mixed) cannot be shown, and ported code using CLB.State[i] does not compile.

what_it_does: Decides whether the user's toggle cycles through the grayed state or only Checked/Unchecked.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'AllowGrayed' over source/ hits tyControls.CheckBox.pas:11/60 (published, default False) and tyControls.Grid.pas:1437/2227 — built twice already — but nothing in tyControls.CheckListBox.pas, whose ToggleCheck is a plain Boolean flip (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:51-56).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:79 (property AllowGrayed ... default False), published :96, consumed by Toggle's NextStateMap :242.
user_impact: Even after tri-state is added there is no switch to opt in/out, and the property name that exists on our own TTyCheckBox is missing here — inconsistent within the library.

what_it_does: Disables an individual row: it renders greyed and neither the click nor the Space key can toggle it.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ItemEnabled' over source/ returned nothing. Every row is unconditionally toggleable: MouseDown toggles any row hit in the check column (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:113-126) and KeyDown toggles whatever ItemIndex points at (128-137), with no per-row gate; the only Enabled test is the whole-control one in the base (tyControls.ListBox.pas:600, 659).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:84 (property ItemEnabled[AIndex]), getter :292-300, setter :346-354, and the keyboard gate `if (ItemIndex >= 0) and ItemEnabled[ItemIndex]` at :336.
user_impact: An options list where some choices are unavailable (licence-gated, mutually exclusive) must instead delete the rows or fight the control in an event handler.

what_it_does: Marks a row as a group header: it is drawn without a checkbox, in the header colours, spanning the full row width.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'Header' over source/ shows the concept exists on the SIBLING class — tyControls.OfficeListBox.pas:15-33 has AddHeader/IsHeader with non-selectable tinted bands, flag stored in Items.Objects — but nothing on TTyCheckListBox, and it cannot simply be reused there because Items.Objects is already occupied by the checked state (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:47). Our PaintItemContent draws a checkbox on every single row (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:82-111).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:81 (property Header[AIndex]), getter :312-320, setter :370-378, and DrawItem's no-check-indent branch `if not Header[AIndex]` :198-203.
user_impact: A grouped check list ('Fonts / Effects / Advanced' bands) is not expressible; the user would have to fake headers as checkable rows.

what_it_does: The ink and band colour used for header rows (LCL defaults clInfoText on clInfoBk).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'HeaderColor|HeaderBackgroundColor' over source/ returned nothing. There is no header row at all here (see the Header[] gap), and no header token either: the sibling TTyOfficeListBox derives its band from the 'TyGroupBox' style token (tyControls.OfficeListBox.pas, TyDrawOfficeHeaderBand), which the check list box does not use.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:82-83 (both properties with defaults clInfoBk/clInfoText), published :109-110, setters :380-392, initialised :221-222.
user_impact: Porting code that sets these fails to compile. Note the raw-TColor form is wrong for this library anyway — the themed equivalent would be a header/band token, which is what should be added instead of the two properties.

member: Toggle(AIndex); CheckAll(AState, aAllowGrayed, aAllowDisabled); Exchange(AIndex1, AIndex2)
what_it_does: Programmatically toggle one row, set every row at once (optionally skipping grayed/disabled rows), and swap two rows together with their check state.
ours_evidence: ToggleCheck exists but is PRIVATE (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:21, body 51-56), so no host can call it and no descendant can override it; grep -rin 'CheckAll' and 'procedure Exchange' over source/ returned nothing. Public surface is only CheckedCount + Checked[] (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:29-30). (Exchange is a naming gap only: because our state lives in Items.Objects, Items.Exchange(i,j) already carries it — but `CLB.Exchange(i,j)` does not compile.)
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:75 (Toggle), :76 (CheckAll), :77 (Exchange); bodies :233-243, :245-254, :256-264.
user_impact: A 'check all / uncheck all' button — the single most common companion of a check list — must be hand-written as a loop, and there is no supported way to toggle a row from code.

what_it_does: Streams every row's check state into the .lfm alongside Items, so boxes ticked at design time come back at run time.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'DefineProperties' over the whole of source/ returned nothing — no control in this library streams a custom binary property. Our check state lives in Items.Objects (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:47), and TStrings streaming persists only the strings, so nothing about the checks reaches the .lfm.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/checklst.pas:65-67 (DefineProperties/ReadData/WriteData declarations) and :447-484 — Filer.DefineBinaryProperty('Data', ...) writes one byte of State per item.
user_impact: A developer who ticks rows in the Object Inspector sees them all unchecked when the program runs, with no error to explain it; defaults must be re-applied in FormCreate.

member: Style: TColorBoxStyle (cbStandardColors, cbExtendedColors, cbSystemColors, cbIncludeNone, cbIncludeDefault, cbCustomColor, cbPrettyNames, cbCustomColors)
what_it_does: Declaratively composes which colour groups populate the list — the 16 standard colours, the 4 extended ones, the system (clBtnFace…) colours, a clNone row, a clDefault row, a user-picked custom row, prettified names, and an OnGetColors pass.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'cbStandardColors|cbSystemColors|cbPrettyNames|ExtendedColors|TColorBoxStyle' over source/ returned nothing. The palette is fixed in the constructor — TyAddDefaultColorPalette(Items) (tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:34) — whose body is a hard-coded list of the 16 VGA colours (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:92-110). No system colours, no clNone/clDefault rows, no pretty names.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:35-43 (TColorBoxStyles/TColorBoxStyle), :209-210 (property Style ... default [cbStandardColors, cbExtendedColors, cbSystemColors]), published :229; population via SetColorList/ColorProc :196, :191.
user_impact: A colour picker that must offer system colours, or a 'None'/'Default' entry, cannot be configured — the host has to ClearColors and re-add every colour with its own name strings.

what_it_does: Width of the colour swatch and its inset from the row edge (LCL defaults 14 and 3), both DPI-adjusted.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ColorRectWidth|ColorRectOffset' over source/ returned nothing. The geometry is hard-coded in the shared TyDrawColorRow: pad := P.Scale(4) and a SQUARE swatch derived from the row height (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:136-143), so the swatch is not even independently sized — it changes whenever ItemHeight changes.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:28-29 (cDefaultColorRectWidth = 14, cDefaultColorRectOffset = 3), :207-208 (the two properties, ColorRectWidth with a stored-function), published :224-225; DPI rescale in DoAutoAdjustLayout :199-200.
user_impact: Wide 'colour bar' rows or tight compact swatches are impossible, and this is exactly the kind of visual value that should be a theme token in this library — it is currently a literal 4 in shared code.

member: Colors[Index]: TColor (read AND write); ColorNames[Index]: string
what_it_does: Indexed access to a row's colour — readable and writable — and to its display name.
ours_evidence: Ours is a read-only FUNCTION under a different name: ColorAt(AIndex): TColor (tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:25, body 55-58, delegating to TyColorOfItem, tyControls.ColorBox.pas:79-85).
