There is no setter anywhere: grep -rin 'ColorNames' returned nothing and the only mutators are ClearColors/AddColor (tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:23-24). The name of a row is Items[i].
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:211 (property Colors[Index]: TColor read GetColors write SetColors — note the list box, unlike the combo, has a SETTER at :186) and :212 (ColorNames[Index] read GetColorName).
user_impact: `CLB.Colors[3] := clRed` — recolouring one row in place, e.g. after the user edits it — does not compile and has no equivalent; the whole palette must be rebuilt. Ported reads also need renaming to ColorAt.

what_it_does: The colour actually painted in the swatch for the clDefault and clNone rows (both default clBlack).
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'DefaultColorColor|NoneColorColor' over source/ returned nothing. Consequence of the missing Style set: our palette has no clDefault/clNone rows at all (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:92-110), and TyDrawColorRow paints whatever TColor it is given via TyTColorToTy (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:146) with no special case — TySelectColorIndex treats clNone only as 'clear the selection' (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:117).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:214-215 (both properties, default clBlack), published :226-227.
user_impact: Once None/Default rows exist there is no way to say what they should look like; and today, code that sets these properties after a port simply fails to compile.

what_it_does: Fires while the palette is being (re)built (cbCustomColors) so the host can append its own colours into the Items it is handed — and is re-fired whenever the list rebuilds.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'OnGetColors' over source/ returned nothing, and there is no DoGetColors hook: the palette is built exactly once, in the constructor (tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:31-36), so a host has no rebuild point to hook.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:168 (TLBGetColorsEvent), :216 (property OnGetColors), published :230, invoked from DoGetColors :201.
user_impact: Brand/theme palettes have to be pushed in imperatively after construction, and anything that would rebuild the list silently loses them.

member: ColorDialog: TColorDialog (+ protected PickCustomColor, cbCustomColor row)
what_it_does: Links a colour dialog to the list so the first row ('Custom…') opens the picker and the chosen colour becomes that row's value.
ours_evidence: grep -rin 'ColorDialog' over source/ shows a colour dialog component ALREADY EXISTS and is unwired: TTyColorDialog with Execute/Color/LCLColor (tyControls.Dialogs.Color.pas:105-124), plus TySelectColor helpers (:101-102). Nothing references it from the list box: tyControls.ColorListBox.pas has no dialog member and grep -rin 'PickCustomColor' returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:217 (property ColorDialog), published :231; protected PickCustomColor :203, driven by the cbCustomColor style flag :40.
user_impact: The standard 'pick any colour' affordance is missing even though the library ships its own colour dialog — each host must wire a button plus TySelectColor by hand.

what_it_does: The chosen colour, settable and streamable from the designer with a documented default.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:26 declares `property Selected: TColor read GetSelected write SetSelected` inside the PUBLIC section, and the unit has no published section at all (class body is lines 14-27), so Selected never reaches the Object Inspector or the .lfm and carries no default. The same shape applies to TTyFontListBox.SelectedFont (tyControls.FontListBox.pas:23, also public-only).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:213 (property Selected: TColor read GetSelected write SetSelected default clBlack) and published on the concrete control at :228.
user_impact: A form's initial colour selection cannot be set at design time or streamed; it must be assigned in code at run time, and the default is implicit (our constructor happens to select index 0 = Black, tyControls.ColorListBox.pas:35).

what_it_does: LCL's Style has 7 values (csDropDown, csSimple, csDropDownList, csOwnerDrawFixed, csOwnerDrawVariable, csOwnerDrawEditableFixed, csOwnerDrawEditableVariable) and defaults to csDropDown (editable). csSimple = a permanently visible list under the edit; the csOwnerDraw* modes enable OnDrawItem/OnMeasureItem. A TComboBoxStyleHelper adds HasEditBox/SetEditBox/IsOwnerDrawn/IsVariable.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:14 `TTyComboBoxStyle = (csDropDownList, csDropDown)` — 2 values only; :143 `property Style: TTyComboBoxStyle ... default csDropDownList` (opposite default). grep of source/ for csSimple / csOwnerDraw / HasEditBox / IsOwnerDrawn returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:262-270 (enum), :272-278 (TComboBoxStyleHelper), :441 `property Style: TComboBoxStyle ... default csDropDown`, :487 published on TComboBox.
user_impact: A ported .lfm/.pas that sets Style := csSimple or any csOwnerDraw* value will not compile. Worse, the DEFAULT is inverted: an LCL combo is editable out of the box, ours is pick-only, so a form ported without an explicit Style silently loses its edit field.

what_it_does: LCL types Items as TStrings so any TStrings source (Screen.Fonts, a TMemo.Lines, a TStringList) can be assigned directly, and the widgetset can substitute its own TStrings descendant.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:128 `property Items: TStringList read FItems write SetItems`; :292 `procedure TTyComboBox.SetItems(const AValue: TStringList)`. Nothing in source/ exposes a TStrings-typed Items on a combo (tyControls.ListBox.pas:107 has the same TStringList narrowing).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:435 `property Items: TStrings read FItems write SetItems`; :362 `procedure SetItems(const Value: TStrings); virtual`.
user_impact: `Combo.Items := SomeTStrings` (e.g. Screen.Fonts, ShellList.Items) is a compile error on our side — the caller must rewrite it as Items.Assign(...). A silent porting break in every place LCL code assigns Items.

what_it_does: ItemHeight fixes the pixel height of a dropdown row (and drives AdjustDropDown's popup height); ItemWidth (default 0) sets the minimum pixel width allocated to the dropdown list, letting the list be wider than the closed field.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ finds ItemHeight only on the list box — tyControls.ListBox.pas:115 `property ItemHeight: Integer read GetItemHeight write SetItemHeight stored FItemHeightExplicit` — and TTyComboBox READS it (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:521 `if FPopupList <> nil then RowH := FPopupList.ItemHeight`) but publishes no way to SET it: the whole published block, tyControls.ComboBox.pas:127-152, has neither. ItemWidth: grep over source/ returned nothing (only unrelated local AItemWidths params in Segmented/RibbonQuickAccess).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:394-395 (ItemHeight, ItemWidth default 0), published on TComboBox at :473 and :476; used in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:279-289 (AdjustDropDown).
user_impact: No design-time control over dropdown row height or dropdown width. Rows always follow the theme's --item-height, so a combo of long paths cannot widen its list beyond the field, and an ItemHeight=32 in a ported .lfm is dropped on load.

what_it_does: Grey placeholder text shown in the (empty) edit field, e.g. 'Select a country'. LCL emulates it where the widgetset lacks it, tracked via EmulatedTextHintStatus.
ours_evidence: The capability EXISTS and is unwired: tyControls.Edit.pas:180 `property TextHint: TCaption read FTextHint write SetTextHint` (published) with a themed 'TyTextHint' token (tyControls.DefaultTheme.pas:623, painted at tyControls.Edit.pas:1688-1691). TTyComboBox owns exactly such a TTyEdit (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:27 FEditor) and forwards only MaxLength (:350) and CharCase (:361) to it — no TextHint anywhere in tyControls.ComboBox.pas.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:444 `property TextHint: TTranslateString read FTextHint write SetTextHint`, published on TComboBox at :491 (also on TColorBox/TComboBoxEx/TCheckComboBox/TFilterComboBox).
user_impact: No placeholder on any combo. Forms ported from LCL lose their hint text silently, and the one-line forward to the embedded editor is already sitting there unused.

what_it_does: Makes the edit portion non-typable while the dropdown still works — the standard way to get 'pick from list, but keep the edit look/selection API' on an editable combo.
ours_evidence: Again built-not-wired: tyControls.Edit.pas:177 `property ReadOnly: Boolean read FReadOnly write SetReadOnly default False` (published, enforced at Edit.pas:445/514/539/1029). tyControls.ComboBox.pas has no ReadOnly at all; the only substitute is switching Style to csDropDownList, which removes the edit field entirely.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:437 `property ReadOnly: Boolean read FReadOnly write SetReadOnly default False`, published on TComboBox at :484.
user_impact: `Combo.ReadOnly := True` does not compile. There is no way to have an editable-looking combo that rejects typing but still exposes SelStart/SelText — the only option changes the control's whole appearance.

what_it_does: On LCL a combo auto-sizes its height to the font/theme by DEFAULT; ShouldAutoAdjust restricts it to the height axis.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ shows the library does use published AutoSize on self-drawn controls — tyControls.Alert.pas:226 `property AutoSize;` (+ Alert.pas:455), tyControls.Breadcrumb.pas:269, tyControls.Button.pas — but neither TTyCustomControl's published block (tyControls.Base.pas:196-245) nor TTyComboBox's (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:127-152) publishes it. Height is fixed once in the ctor: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:201 `Height := TyDensityHeight(ActiveController, 26)`.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:429 `property AutoSize default True; // Overrides default value`, published on TComboBox at :459; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:734 ShouldAutoAdjust.
user_impact: A combo whose font grows (or a skin with fatter padding) clips its text instead of growing, and the LCL default is inverted: ported code that relies on auto-height gets a hard 26px-derived height. This is exactly the failure mode recorded in the skin-variance lesson.

what_it_does: Four separate behaviour switches for the editable field: AutoComplete/AutoCompleteText (default [cbactEndOfLineComplete, cbactSearchAscending]) COMPLETE the typed text in place, with options for case retention, case-sensitive search and search direction; AutoDropDown (default False) opens the list as soon as the user types; AutoSelect (default True) selects the whole text on focus-in.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ (case-insensitive) for AutoComplete / AutoCompleteText / AutoDropDown / AutoSelect / cbact returned no members — only prose comments in tyControls.ComboBox.pas (13, 28, 617) describing our prefix-FILTER popup. Our behaviour is hard-wired and non-optional: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:429-443 EditorChange always filters and always calls DropDownFiltered (i.e. AutoDropDown is permanently ON with no opt-out), and it never appends the matched remainder into the field, so no in-field completion exists at all.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:250-259 (option enum + DefaultComboBoxAutoCompleteText), :422-428 (AutoComplete, AutoCompleteText, AutoDropDown, AutoSelect, AutoSelected), published on TComboBox at :455-458; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:150 DoAutoCompleteSelect.
user_impact: Four ported properties fail to compile, and the runtime behaviour differs both ways: users get a dropdown on every keystroke they cannot switch off, and never get the LCL 'type P, see Portugal completed and selected' in-field completion.

what_it_does: On LCL DroppedDown is a read/WRITE property: assigning True opens the list programmatically, False closes it.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:122 `function DroppedDown: Boolean;` — a read-only function, not a property (impl :555). Open/close only via the separate DropDown (:123) / CloseUp (:124). Same shape on tyControls.Cascader.pas:503, so it is a library-wide convention, not an oversight local to the combo.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:420 `property DroppedDown: Boolean read GetDroppedDown write SetDroppedDown`; setter at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:837.
user_impact: `Combo.DroppedDown := True` — a common idiom for opening a combo from a button or a shortcut — does not compile; the caller must find and call DropDown instead. Reading also differs syntactically (DroppedDown vs DroppedDown()) in strict-property contexts such as RTTI/property-editor code.

what_it_does: The text-selection API of the combo's edit portion (UTF-8 positions), plus SelectAll to highlight everything — used to preselect on focus, to replace the selection, or to read what the user highlighted.
ours_evidence: Fully built one class away and not forwarded: tyControls.Edit.pas:172-174 `property SelStart / SelLength / SelText` (public) and :149 `procedure SelectAll` — on the very TTyEdit instance the combo embeds (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:27 FEditor, created :207). FEditor is strictly private and tyControls.ComboBox.pas exposes only EditorVisibleForTest (:118) and EditorMaxLengthForTest (:119); no Sel* / SelectAll appears in the unit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:438-440 (SelLength, SelStart, SelText), :421 SelectAll; implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:309-407.
user_impact: On an editable combo there is no way to read or set the selection, or to select-all — so 'highlight the text when the field gets focus' and 'replace what the user selected' cannot be written at all, even though TTyEdit already implements both.

member: Clear, ClearSelection, AddItem(const Item: String; AnObject: TObject), MatchListItem
what_it_does: Four public list methods: Clear empties Items AND blanks Text; ClearSelection unselects (ItemIndex := -1); AddItem appends a caption with an associated object; MatchListItem finds the item matching a caption honouring the AutoCompleteText case/direction options and returns its index.
ours_evidence: grep over source/: no Clear, ClearSelection, MatchListItem or two-arg AddItem on TTyComboBox. `AddItem` exists only with DIFFERENT signatures on other classes — tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:50 `AddItem(const S: string; AImageIndex: Integer)`, tyControls.AdvancedComboBox.pas:58, tyControls.OfficeComboBox.pas:43 — so `AddItem('x', nil)` resolves to none of them. ClearSelection exists on tyControls.ListBox.pas:98, tyControls.Edit.pas:150 and tyControls.ListView.pas:469 but not on the combo; ClearColors (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:59) is the only Clear-ish method in the family. Callers must hand-write Items.Clear + Text := '' and ItemIndex := -1.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:411 AddItem, :412 MatchListItem, :417 Clear, :418 ClearSelection; implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:929, :458, :985 (`Items.Clear; Text:='';`), :996.
user_impact: Four routine calls break on port. The Clear one is a semantic trap rather than just a compile error: the obvious substitute Items.Clear leaves the old caption painted in the field (our SelectItem is what blanks FText), so a ported Clear() silently leaves stale text.

what_it_does: Promotes an item to the top of the list, de-duplicating (with a CaseSensitive flag), capping the list at MaxHistoryCount, optionally setting it as Text, and with an overload carrying an associated TObject. Available on EVERY LCL combo, so any combo can be an MRU box.
ours_evidence: The capability exists under another name on a SUBCLASS only: tyControls.MRUComboBox.pas:32 `procedure AddToHistory(const S: string)` (impl :58-89) with the cap as a published property, :35 `property MaxItems: Integer ... default 10`. grep over source/ for AddHistoryItem / MaxHistoryCount returned nothing. TTyComboBox itself has no history method (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:113-126 public block).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:413-416 (both overloads); implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:941 and :955.
user_impact: Ported code calling Combo.AddHistoryItem(s, 10, True, False) fails to compile, and the rename comes with three lost knobs: no per-call cap, no CaseSensitive choice (ours is always case-insensitive, MRUComboBox.pas:69 SameText), no AnObject overload, and no history at all unless the author switches the class to TTyMRUComboBox.

what_it_does: The owner-draw contract: with a csOwnerDraw* Style, OnDrawItem(Control, Index, ARect, State) lets the application paint each row on the combo's Canvas, and OnMeasureItem(Control, Index, var AHeight) gives per-row heights for the *Variable styles.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for OnDrawItem returned nothing anywhere; OnMeasureItem exists only as the TreeView's own unrelated event (tyControls.TreeView.pas:642, TTyTreeMeasureItemEvent). Our substitutes are PROTECTED virtual painter hooks, not events: tyControls.ComboBox.pas:101 `procedure PaintFieldContent(P: TTyPainter; ...); virtual` and :104 `function CreatePopupList: TTyListBox; virtual` (+ TTyListBox.PaintItemContent, used by tyControls.ColorBox.pas:39 and tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:33). Row height is uniform — tyControls.ComboBox.pas:511-525 ComputePopupHeight multiplies one ItemHeight by the row count.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:282-285 (event types), :399 OnDrawItem and :402-403 OnMeasureItem, published on TComboBox at :501 and :511; dispatch at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:111 (DrawItem) and :283 (MeasureItem).
user_impact: Custom row rendering requires SUBCLASSING (a new unit, a CreatePopupList override) where LCL needs one event handler in the form — so no design-time custom drawing at all, and no variable-height rows: a combo of two-line entries cannot be built without a descendant class.

what_it_does: Fires when the list is about to be shown so the application can populate Items just-in-time (lazy/expensive lists — files, DB lookups) instead of filling them up front.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for OnGetItems returned nothing (only tyControls.ListView.pas:530 OnGetItemState, an unrelated per-row state callback). TTyComboBox.DropDown (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:582-615) fires only DoDropDown/OnDropDown at :614 — AFTER FPopup.Popup and after the `if FItems.Count = 0 then Exit` guard at :587, so an OnDropDown handler cannot be used as a substitute: with an empty list the popup never opens and the event never fires.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:401 `property OnGetItems: TNotifyEvent read FOnGetItems write FOnGetItems`, published on TComboBox at :507; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcombobox.inc:249 GetItems, :297 IntfGetItems.
user_impact: No lazy population hook. Because DropDown early-exits on an empty Items list, the natural workaround (fill in OnDropDown) is structurally impossible — the first click on an empty lazy combo does nothing.

member: DragMode, DragCursor, DragKind, OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnStartDrag, OnEndDrag
what_it_does: The standard LCL drag-and-drop surface — make the control a drag source (DragMode/DragKind/DragCursor) and a drop target (OnDragOver/OnDragDrop), with start/end notifications.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for `property DragMode` / `DragKind` / `DragCursor` / `OnDragDrop` / `OnDragOver` / `OnStartDrag` / `OnEndDrag` finds exactly one control that re-publishes them — tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574 — proving the pattern is intended and cheap here. Neither TTyCustomControl's published block (tyControls.Base.pas:196-245) nor TTyComboBox's (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:127-152) lists any of the seven.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:467-469 (DragCursor, DragKind, DragMode) and :499-500, :502, :521 (OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDrag); same set on TColorBox (colorbox.pas:119-120, 142-144), TComboBoxEx (comboex.pas:204-206) and TCheckComboBox (comboex.pas:347-349).
user_impact: A combo cannot participate in drag-and-drop from the Object Inspector; a ported .lfm carrying DragMode=dmAutomatic or an OnDragOver handler fails to load. All seven are inherited from TControl and only need re-publishing, exactly as TTyMemo already does.

what_it_does: On TColorBox, Style is a SET that composes the palette: cbStandardColors, cbExtendedColors, cbSystemColors (the default trio), cbIncludeNone, cbIncludeDefault, cbCustomColor (first row is a user-pickable custom colour), cbPrettyNames (Red instead of clRed), cbCustomColors (call OnGetColors last). Changing it rebuilds Items via SetColorList.
ours_evidence: TTyColorBox has NO palette-composition property, and the name Style is already taken by an incompatible inherited one: tyControls.ColorBox.pas:173-178 overrides `SetStyle(AValue: TTyComboBoxStyle)` to force csDropDownList, so `Style` on our colour box means the dropdown mode and silently ignores writes. The palette is a fixed 16-entry VGA list built in the ctor (tyControls.ColorBox.pas:165-171 -> TyAddDefaultColorPalette, :92-110); grep over source/ for cbStandardColors / cbSystemColors / cbPrettyNames / cbIncludeNone / TColorBoxStyle returned nothing. clNone cannot even be a palette member: TySelectColorIndex treats it as 'clear' (:117) and tyControls.ColorComboBox.pas:87 reuses clNone as the 'More...' sentinel.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:35-43 (TColorBoxStyles/TColorBoxStyle), :84-85 `property Style: TColorBoxStyle ... default [cbStandardColors, cbExtendedColors, cbSystemColors]`, published at :104; SetColorList declared :71.
user_impact: Two failures at once. Ported code assigning a set to Style does not compile, and code that assigns our inherited Style compiles but does nothing. Users also cannot get system colours, clNone/clDefault rows or pretty names — and the default palette differs (16 VGA entries vs LCL's standard+extended+system set), so a saved ItemIndex from an LCL form points at a different colour.

what_it_does: Selected is TColorBox's headline PUBLISHED property — the chosen colour, settable in the Object Inspector and streamed to the .lfm, default clBlack. Colors[Index] and ColorNames[Index] are indexed read accessors for the palette.
ours_evidence: Selected exists but is PUBLIC only, never published, and declares no default: tyControls.ColorBox.pas:57 `public` ... :66 `property Selected: TColor read GetSelected write SetSelected` — the class has no `published` section at all (:49-67), so Selected is invisible in the IDE and not streamed. Colors[]/ColorNames[]: grep over source/ for `property Colors` and ColorNames returned nothing; the equivalents are a method and the raw item text — tyControls.ColorBox.pas:62 `function ColorAt(AIndex: Integer): TColor` and Items[i] for the name.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:86-88 (Colors, ColorNames, `Selected: TColor read GetSelected write SetSelected default clBlack`), published on TColorBox at :103.
user_impact: A designer cannot pick the initial colour in the Object Inspector and it is not saved in the .lfm — every colour box must be seeded in code. Ported code reading Colors[i] or ColorNames[i] does not compile (ColorAt / Items[i] are the substitutes).

what_it_does: Published swatch appearance: ColorRectWidth (default 14, DPI-adjusted) and ColorRectOffset (default 3) size and inset the colour rectangle drawn on each row; DefaultColorColor and NoneColorColor (both default clBlack) say which real colour is painted for the clDefault and clNone rows.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ (case-insensitive) for ColorRectWidth, ColorRectOffset, DefaultColorColor, NoneColorColor returned nothing. Swatch geometry is hard-coded in the shared row painter: tyControls.ColorBox.pas:129-152 TyDrawColorRow uses `pad := P.Scale(4)` and derives the swatch as a square from the row height (`sw := (ARect.Bottom - ARect.Top) - 2*pad`), with no theme token or property behind either number — note this also violates the library's own rule that visual values go through theme tokens.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:27-29 (cDefaultColorRectWidth = 14, cDefaultColorRectOffset = 3), :82-83 (ColorRectWidth stored ColorRectWidthStored, ColorRectOffset default 3), :89-90 (DefaultColorColor, NoneColorColor default clBlack), published at :99-102.
user_impact: Swatch size/inset cannot be changed at all — not per instance and not via the theme — so a colour box cannot be made to match a denser or wider design, and a ported ColorRectWidth=24 is dropped. And since clNone/clDefault rows are unsupported, there is nowhere to say what colour they should show.

what_it_does: Published hook fired while the palette is being (re)built — the handler receives the Items list and appends application-specific colours (brand palette, recently used, colours found in the document). Runs last when cbCustomColors is in Style.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for OnGetColors and TGetColorsEvent returned nothing. The only extension path is imperative and one-shot: tyControls.ColorBox.pas:59-60 ClearColors + AddColor called by the application after construction, with no callback when the list is rebuilt (and nothing rebuilds it — the ctor fills it once, :165-171).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:44 `TGetColorsEvent = procedure(Sender: TCustomColorBox; Items: TStrings) of object`, :91 `property OnGetColors`, published at :105; invoked via DoGetColors (:76).
user_impact: No event-based way to contribute colours, so a colour box cannot show a live 'colours used in this document' section — the app must remember to re-run ClearColors/AddColor itself at every point the palette should change.

what_it_does: A published link to a TColorDialog component; with cbCustomColor in Style the first row opens THAT dialog (so the app controls its title, initial custom colours and options) and the chosen colour becomes the first palette entry.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for ColorDialog finds the component exists but is not linkable to the colour box: tyControls.Dialogs.Color.pas:105 `TTyColorDialog = class(TTyComponent)`. TTyColorBox has no ColorDialog property (:49-67) and no custom-colour row. The capability lives on a different class with a hard-coded dialog call: tyControls.ColorComboBox.pas:22 TTyColorComboBox, :115 `if TySelectColor(FMoreCaption, c, a) then`, driven by the fixed 'More...' sentinel row (:64, :69-76) rather than an assignable dialog.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/colorbox.pas:92 `property ColorDialog: TColorDialog read FColorDialog write FColorDialog`, published at :106; :78 `function PickCustomColor: Boolean; virtual`; :52 FColorDialog; Notification hookup at :79.
user_impact: You cannot point a colour box at your own configured colour dialog, and TTyColorBox offers no custom-colour row at all — the author must switch class to TTyColorComboBox and accept its hardcoded dialog and caption. A ported form with ColorBox1.ColorDialog = ColorDialog1 fails to load.

what_it_does: Published link to a TShellListView: selecting a filter row automatically pushes the new mask into that list view (and Notification nils the link if the view is freed). The whole point of the control — one design-time assignment wires the filter to the file list with no code.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for ShellListView shows the TARGET CLASS EXISTS — tyControls.ShellListView.pas:1 (TTyShellListView, also consumed at tyControls.Dialogs.FileDialog.pas:74/341) — but TTyFilterComboBox has no link property: its published block is tyControls.FilterComboBox.pas:51-57 (Filter, FilterIndex, OnFilterChange only), and the unit's uses clause (:18-19) pulls in tyControls.ComboBox and tyControls.FileSystem, not ShellListView. The header comment at :6-7 documents the manual substitute: `List.Mask := FilterCombo.Mask`.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/filectrl.pp:150 FShellListView, :167 `property ShellListView: TShellListView read FShellListView write SetShellListView`, published on TFilterComboBox at :195; pushed on selection in Select (:551) and unlinked via Notification (:156).
user_impact: The design-time wiring is gone: every filter combo needs a hand-written OnFilterChange/OnSelect handler that copies Mask into the list, and a ported .lfm with ShellListView = ShellListView1 fails to load. Both classes already exist in this library — only the property is missing.

what_it_does: A public CLASS method usable without an instance: parses an LCL filter string into a TStrings, with flags to clear the target, add the descriptions and/or add the patterns (AClearStrings, AAddDescription, AAddFilter). Callers use it to share one filter string between a combo and unrelated code.
ours_evidence: The parser exists as a free function with a different name and shape: tyControls.FileSystem.pas:95 `function TyFsParseFilter(const AFilter: string): TTyFsFilterSpecArray` (record array, :65-66) and :100 `function TyFsFilterPatterns(const AFilter: string; AIndex: Integer): string`; used by tyControls.FilterComboBox.pas:88. grep over source/ for ConvertFilterToStrings returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/filectrl.pp:163-164 `class procedure ConvertFilterToStrings(AFilter: string; AStrings: TStrings; AClearStrings, AAddDescription, AAddFilter: Boolean)`; used by GetMask at :517.
user_impact: Code calling TFilterComboBox.ConvertFilterToStrings(...) must be rewritten against a differently-shaped API (record array instead of filling a caller-supplied TStrings, and no 'append to an existing list' mode). Pure rename plus a shape change, no lost capability.

member: ItemsEx (TComboExItems collection of TComboExItem) — whole sub-object
what_it_does: TComboBoxEx's defining feature: a published, design-time-editable COLLECTION replacing the flat string list. Each TComboExItem carries Caption, ImageIndex, OverlayImageIndex, SelectedImageIndex (a different image once selected), Indent (tree-like left inset) and untyped Data; the collection (TListControlItems) adds CaseSensitive, SortType (stNone/stData/stText/stBoth/stCustom), an OnCompare event, Sort and CustomSort, plus typed Add/AddItem/Insert.
ours_evidence: We have no item class and no collection: tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas declares only TTyComboBoxExPopupList (:31) and TTyComboBoxEx (:39), whose single published member is `Images` (:62). Items stay the inherited TStringList (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:128) with ONE integer smuggled into Objects[] as imageIndex+1 (tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:106, read back at :112) — which means the Objects[] slot is spent and no other per-item data can coexist. grep over source/ for TComboExItem / ItemsEx / OverlayImageIndex / SelectedImageIndex / SortType returned nothing (TStringList.CustomSort/CaseSensitive are reachable in code, but there is no published/design-time sort).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:57-70 (TListControlItem: Caption, ImageIndex, Data), :73-90 (TComboExItem: Indent, OverlayImageIndex, SelectedImageIndex, all default -1), :93-116 (TListControlItems: CaseSensitive, SortType, OnCompare, Sort, CustomSort), :118-133 (TComboExItems.Add/AddItem/Insert), :181 `property ItemsEx: TComboExItems`, published at :213 with the ordering warning.
user_impact: There is no Object Inspector collection editor for items — every entry must be added in code via AddItem, and a ported .lfm streaming an ItemsEx block fails outright. Four per-item capabilities are simply unavailable: overlay images, a different image when selected, per-item indentation, and per-item user Data (the Objects[] slot already holds our image index).

what_it_does: Images is typed TCustomImageList — any LCL TImageList, TDragImageList or shared IDE image list can be assigned. ImagesWidth (default 0) selects the resolution to draw from a multi-resolution image list, the standard HiDPI knob.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:62 `property Images: TTyVirtualImageList read FImages write SetImages` — and that class is NOT an image list: tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:168 `TTyVirtualImageList = class(TTyComponent)`, name-keyed into a TTyImageCollection (:205 Collection, :207 Names). grep over source/ for ImagesWidth returned nothing; the nearest concept is tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:209 `property DefaultSize: Integer ... default 16`, which the combo ignores — it derives the icon size from the row height instead (tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:127-129 `sz := (ARect.Bottom - ARect.Top) - P.Scale(6)`).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:139 FImages, :179 `property Images: TCustomImageList read FImages write SetImages`, :180 `property ImagesWidth: Integer ... default 0`, published at :210-211.
user_impact: An existing TImageList cannot be assigned — `ComboEx.Images := ImageList1` does not compile, and the app must migrate its icons into a TTyImageCollection. A ported .lfm referencing an ImageList (or ImagesWidth) fails to load, and there is no per-control way to pin the icon resolution.

what_it_does: Two published option sets specific to the Ex combo. AutoCompleteOptions (default [acoAutoAppend]) selects the shell-style completion behaviour: acoAutoSuggest, acoAutoAppend, acoSearch, acoFilterPrefixes, acoUseTab, acoUpDownKeyDropsList, acoRtlReading. StyleEx (default []) tunes rendering/matching: csExCaseSensitive, csExNoEditImage (no icon in the closed field), csExNoEditImageIndent, csExNoSizeLimit, csExPathWordBreak.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for AutoCompleteOptions, StyleEx, aco (acoAutoAppend/acoAutoSuggest) and csEx returned nothing. TTyComboBoxEx publishes only Images (tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas:59-62), and the field always draws the icon with a fixed indent with no way to suppress it (:140-147 PaintFieldContent -> :117-138 DrawImageText, always `x := ARect.Left + P.Scale(4)` plus the image).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:40-46 (TAutoCompleteOptions and TComboBoxExStyles enums), :177-178 AutoCompleteOptions default cDefAutoCompOpts (:149 = [acoAutoAppend]), :183 StyleEx default [], published at :193 and :224.
user_impact: Two published sets are missing, so a ported form does not load. Concretely: no way to say 'do not draw the icon in the closed field' (csExNoEditImage) or to make matching case-sensitive, and no control over completion behaviour.

member: Add (2 overloads), Insert, Delete, DeleteSelected, AssignItemsEx (2 overloads); AddItem signature
what_it_does: The Ex combo's item-mutation API, all image-aware: Add returns a new index or appends (ACaption, AIndent, AImgIdx, AOverlayImgIdx, ASelectedImgIdx); Insert does the same at a position; Delete(AIndex) and DeleteSelected remove; AssignItemsEx bulk-loads from a TStrings or another TComboExItems. AddItem is also OVERRIDDEN keeping the base (Item: String; AnObject: TObject) signature.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ComboBoxEx.pas exposes exactly one mutator, :50 `procedure AddItem(const S: string; AImageIndex: Integer)` — an append-only method that also COLLIDES with the inherited LCL signature, so ported `AddItem('x', SomeObject)` fails to compile. grep over source/ for AssignItemsEx / DeleteSelected returned nothing; `procedure Delete` / `Insert` do not exist on the class, and there is no image-aware insert: callers must reach into Items.InsertObject and encode imageIndex+1 by hand (the encoding is only documented at :104-106).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:164-176 (Add overloads, AddItem override, AssignItemsEx overloads, Clear, Delete, DeleteSelected, Insert).
user_impact: Only appending is supported. Inserting an item with an image, deleting the selected item, or bulk-assigning items requires hand-writing the Objects[] +1 encoding — and if the caller gets it wrong the image silently shifts by one. AddItem is worse than absent: it has the same name and a different parameter type, so ported calls fail with a confusing type error.

what_it_does: Tri-state checks. State[] reads/writes cbUnchecked / cbChecked / cbGrayed per item and fires OnItemChange; AllowGrayed (default False) lets the user cycle into the grayed state. Grayed is how 'partially selected' / 'inherited' entries are shown.
ours_evidence: Ours is strictly boolean: tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas:38 `property Checked[AIndex: Integer]: Boolean read GetChecked write SetChecked`, backed by a 0/1 in Objects[] (:67 `Items.Objects[AIndex] := TObject(PtrInt(Ord(AValue)))`, read :58). grep over source/ shows the tri-state concept IS implemented elsewhere — tyControls.CheckBox.pas:60 `property AllowGrayed: Boolean ... default False` (painted :194) and tyControls.Grid.pas:2227 — but neither AllowGrayed nor State[] exists on the check combo or on tyControls.CheckListBox.pas (whose Checked[] is likewise Boolean, :30). The popup checklist paints only two states (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:97 `if isChecked then states := [tysActive] else [tysNormal]`).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:263-268 (TCheckComboItemState with State: TCheckBoxState), :323 AllowGrayed default False, :328 `property State[AIndex: Integer]: TCheckBoxState`, published AllowGrayed at :336; setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/comboex.inc:909.
user_impact: No third state anywhere in the check-combo path: a 'some children selected' row cannot be represented, and ported code reading or writing State[i] does not compile. The library already renders a grayed checkbox for TTyCheckBox, so the visual exists and is simply unreachable here.

what_it_does: LCL keeps each row's check state in a TCheckComboItemState object hung off Items.Objects[], and that state object carries a separate Data: TObject field, surfaced as the read/write Objects[AIndex] property. So the application still gets one free per-item payload (a record, an ID, a business object) alongside the check state.
ours_evidence: Our check state IS Items.Objects[] — tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas:67 writes the raw 0/1 into it and :58 reads it back, and PopupCheckClick copies Objects[] wholesale between the combo and the popup list (:113-115). There is no Objects[] property and no Data field on the class (:32-43). grep over source/ for a per-item Data/Objects accessor on a check control returned nothing; tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:38-47 uses the identical 0/1-in-Objects[] scheme. The class header (:10-16) states the design: 'the per-item checked state lives in THIS combo's Items.Objects[i] (0/1)'.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:263-268 (TCheckComboItemState.Data), :327 `property Objects[AIndex: Integer]: TObject read GetObject write SetObject`; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/comboex.inc:874 (`Result := TCheckComboItemState(Items.Objects[AIndex]).Data`) and :904.
user_impact: Silent data corruption on port, not a compile error. Existing code that stores a payload in a check combo's Objects[] still compiles against our inherited TStringList — and every write clobbers the check flags (a non-nil pointer reads back as 'checked'), while every user toggle overwrites the payload. The one per-item data slot LCL guarantees does not exist here.

what_it_does: Per-item enabled flag: a disabled row is drawn greyed and cannot be toggled by the user, while remaining visible and programmatically settable. CheckAll's AAllowDisabled parameter also honours it.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ (case-insensitive) for ItemEnabled returned nothing — not on tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas (public surface :32-38 is CheckedCount, CheckedText, Checked[]), not on tyControls.CheckListBox.pas, not on tyControls.ListBox.pas. The popup checklist toggles any row the click lands on with no per-item gate (tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:117-124 MouseDown -> ToggleCheck, and Space at :129+), and PaintItemContent has no disabled branch (:83-113).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:326 `property ItemEnabled[AIndex: Integer]: Boolean read GetItemEnabled write SetItemEnabled`; C:/lazarus/lcl/include/comboex.inc:870 and :896; honoured by CheckAll (:533-541) and by DrawItem's disabled themed parts (:601+).
user_impact: Rows cannot be individually disabled — the common 'this option is unavailable for the current licence, show it greyed' pattern is impossible; the app must delete the row or fight the user's clicks. Ported code touching ItemEnabled[i] does not compile.

what_it_does: Published event telling the application WHICH item changed, fired on both user toggles and programmatic Checked[]/State[] writes.
ours_evidence: Not present: tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas publishes only Separator (:41) and EmptyText (:43). A toggle re-fires the inherited index-less OnChange — :117 `if Assigned(OnChange) then OnChange(Self)` inside PopupCheckClick — and a programmatic SetChecked (:61-73) fires NOTHING at all, only Invalidate. grep over source/ shows the exact event shape already exists on a sibling: tyControls.CheckGroup.pas:56 `property OnItemChange: TCheckGroupItemEvent read FOnItemChange write FOnItemChange` (fired with the index at :250).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:52 `TCheckItemChange = procedure(Sender: TObject; AIndex: Integer) of object`, :329 `property OnItemChange`, published at :384; fired from SetChecked (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/comboex.inc:890) and SetState (:914).
user_impact: A handler cannot tell which row the user ticked — it must diff the whole list on every OnChange. And because SetChecked fires nothing, a programmatic Checked[i] := True notifies no one, so a view bound to the combo silently goes stale. The index-carrying event pattern is already implemented in TTyCheckGroup.

what_it_does: A published read-only item count, so the count is visible to RTTI/design-time consumers as well as to code.
ours_evidence: No Count on tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas (public block :32-38 has CheckedCount, CheckedText, Checked[]); the equivalent is the inherited Items.Count (tyControls.ComboBox.pas:128), which our own code uses everywhere (e.g. CheckComboBox.pas:86, :113). grep over source/ found no `property Count` on any combo/list control.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:324 `property Count: Integer read GetCount`, published on TCheckComboBox at :346.
user_impact: Trivial rename: ported `Combo.Count` must become `Combo.Items.Count`; a .lfm is unaffected (read-only). No lost capability.

member: CheckAll, Toggle, AddItem(AItem, AState, AEnabled), AssignItems, DeleteItem
what_it_does: The check combo's public mutation API: CheckAll(AState, AAllowGrayed, AAllowDisabled) bulk-sets every row honouring the grayed/disabled exclusions; Toggle(AIndex) flips one row and notifies; AddItem(AItem, AState, AEnabled) appends a row with its state in one call; AssignItems(TStrings) bulk-loads and initialises the states; DeleteItem(AIndex) removes a row and frees its state.
ours_evidence: grep over source/ for CheckAll, AssignItems and DeleteItem returned nothing. `Toggle`: the flip logic exists but is unreachable — tyControls.CheckListBox.pas:21 `procedure ToggleCheck(AIndex: Integer)` is declared in the PRIVATE section (:16-21) of the popup list, and TTyCheckComboBox exposes no Toggle (public block tyControls.CheckComboBox.pas:32-38). No state-carrying AddItem either: the documented recipe is 'Build with Items.Add + Checked[]' (:16), i.e. two statements and a manual index, and a bulk check requires a hand-written loop.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comboex.pas:317-322 (AddItem reintroduce, AssignItems, Clear override, DeleteItem, CheckAll, Toggle); implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/comboex.inc:516, :526, :533, :579, :842.
user_impact: Five ported calls break, and each substitute is more code with a correctness trap: a bulk 'check all' loop must skip nothing (no disabled/grayed notion), and Items.Add + Checked[Items.Count-1] is an index the caller has to get right — get it wrong and the tick lands on the previous row.

what_it_does: Roots the whole tree at one directory ('' = machine base path). Setting it clears and repopulates the tree, and propagates to the linked ShellListView.Root.
ours_evidence: grep -ril for Root/GetRootPath/GetBasePath over source/ returns nothing on the shell units (only tyControls.TreeView.pas RootNode, an unrelated sentinel node). TTyShellTreeView has no Root: its roots are always the machine-wide TyFsRoots places -- tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:340-349 PopulateRoots does Clear + one node per TyFsRoots entry, called unconditionally from the ctor (line 122).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:141 `property Root: string read FRoot write SetRoot;`, setter at 611-643 (clears Items, builds a root node, pushes FRoot to ShellListView).
user_impact: You cannot show a tree scoped to one folder (a project folder, a document root). Every TTyShellTreeView always shows all drives/places, so a chooser confined to one subtree is impossible without subclassing.

what_it_does: Which entries the tree enumerates: otFolders, otNonFolders (files shown as leaf nodes), otHidden. Default [otFolders]; assigning re-reads the view.
ours_evidence: grep -ril ObjectTypes over source/ hits tyControls.FileSystem.pas, ShellListView.pas, ShellTreeView.pas -- but on the tree the set is not a property: it is built inline as `opts := [fotFolders]; if FShowHidden then Include(opts, fotHidden)` (tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:262-264). Only ShowHidden: Boolean is published (line 90). No fotFiles is ever passed.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:138 `property ObjectTypes: TObjectTypes ... default [otFolders]`; type at 40-42; setter at 674-691 (calls UpdateView).
user_impact: A tree that shows files as well as folders (the classic Explorer left pane with otNonFolders) is impossible, and the hidden-files toggle is a different, narrower property name than every ported TShellTreeView code path expects.

what_it_does: Read/write the selected node's full path. Reading appends a trailing path delimiter for directories and prefixes GetRootPath for relative nodes; writing accepts absolute OR root-relative paths.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:87 `property Directory: string read SelectedPath write SelectPath` (+ public SelectedPath at 79/351 and SelectPath at 83/356). grep for Path over source/ confirms the concept exists, under the name Directory/SelectedPath.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:142 `property Path: string read GetPath write SetPath;` getter 1383-1386, setter 1421+.
user_impact: Porting break: `ShellTreeView1.Path := X` does not compile. Also a value difference -- ours returns the raw FullPath with no trailing delimiter and accepts absolute paths only (SelectPath, line 372-387), so root-relative writes that work on LCL silently do nothing.

what_it_does: Design-time two-way link to a shell list view: selecting a folder in the tree sets the list's Root, and the list's UpdateView refreshes the tree.
ours_evidence: grep -ril ShellListView over source/ hits Breadcrumb/Dialogs.FileDialog/ListView/ShellComboBox/ShellListView/ShellTreeView -- but every hit is a unit name or a local variable; there is no ShellListView property. The seam is the manual OnPathChange event (tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:92) which a host must wire in code.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:139 `property ShellListView: TCustomShellListView read FShellListView write SetShellListView;`; the tree pushes the path in DoSelectionChanged (1141-1163) and SetRoot (641-642); the list pushes back in UpdateView (2004-2011).
user_impact: The canonical two-control file browser cannot be assembled in the Object Inspector; every app must hand-write the OnPathChange -> Directory plumbing, and there is no reverse (list -> tree) refresh at all.

what_it_does: Chooses whether expanding a node re-reads its children from disk (ecmRefreshedExpanding, the LCL default), keeps already-built children (ecmKeepChildren), or discards children on collapse (ecmCollapseAndClear).
ours_evidence: grep -ril ExpandCollapseMode over source/ returned nothing. Our behaviour is hard-wired to the ecmKeepChildren shape: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:311-313 `if Node^.ChildCount = 0 then PopulateChildren(Node)` and there is no Collapse override.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:48-52 (type), :118 `property ExpandCollapseMode ... default ecmRefreshedExpanding`, honoured in CanExpand (723-745) and Collapse (753-771).
user_impact: Children are enumerated exactly once per node for the control's lifetime, so files/folders created or deleted after the first expand never appear; and because ours differs from the LCL DEFAULT, a port silently loses the refresh-on-expand behaviour rather than just an option.

what_it_does: Re-reads every currently expanded node from AStartDir down (or from the root), reacting to filesystem changes while preserving the expansion state and selection.
ours_evidence: grep -ril UpdateView over source/ hits only tyControls.Dialogs.Progress.pas (an unrelated progress-dialog method). The nearest thing is PopulateRoots (tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:340-349), which Clears the tree and re-seeds the roots -- destroying expansion and selection.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:134 (declaration), implementation 1250+ (walks expanded nodes, FindExistingSubPath, restores).
user_impact: There is no way to say 'the disk changed, refresh what is on screen'. The only refresh collapses the entire tree back to the drive list, which loses the user's place.

what_it_does: Re-reads one node's children (nil = the root), leaving the rest of the tree alone.
ours_evidence: grep -ril "procedure Refresh" over source/ finds no Refresh on TTyShellTreeView (only TTyShellListView.Refresh, ShellListView.pas:96, which is a different control and a different meaning). PopulateChildren (ShellTreeView.pas:256) is private and appends rather than replaces.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:133 `procedure Refresh(ANode: TTreeNode); overload;`, implementation 1209-1247.
user_impact: After the app itself creates or deletes a folder, it cannot refresh just the affected branch; the branch keeps showing stale children forever (see the ExpandCollapseMode entry).

what_it_does: Public node -> absolute path mapping, used by every consumer that walks or hit-tests the tree itself.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:68-70 declares `function NodePath(Node: PTyTreeNode): string;` under `protected`, with the comment 'Protected so a subclass/test can observe the node<->path mapping'. grep -ril GetPathFromNode over source/ returned nothing. From outside the class only the FOCUSED path is reachable (SelectedPath, line 351).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:131 `function GetPathFromNode(ANode: TTreeNode): string;` under public, implementation 1195-1207.
user_impact: An app cannot resolve the path of any node other than the focused one -- no multi-select harvesting, no path lookup from an OnGetImageIndex/OnDrawNode handler, no drag-source path -- without subclassing the control.

member: TShellTreeNode (per-node object: ShortFilename / FullFilename / IsDirectory / BasePath / FileInfo)
what_it_does: A dedicated node class that carries each node's TSearchRec plus its base path, so per-node attributes (size, timestamp, attributes, is-directory) are available without touching the disk again.
ours_evidence: Our node payload is a single Integer index into a private string array: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:45 `FPaths: array of string`, :109 `NodeDataSize := SizeOf(Integer)`, :236 `PInteger(GetNodeData(Result))^ := idx`. Nothing but the path is stored, and no node class is declared. grep -ril for ShortFilename/FullFilename/IsDirectory over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:413-425 TShellTreeNode with ShortFilename (420), FullFilename (421), IsDirectory (422), BasePath (424) and the protected FFileInfo: TSearchRec (417); installed via DoCreateNodeClass/CreateNode (104,106).
user_impact: Per-node file metadata is unavailable: code that needs a node's attributes, size or timestamp (icon overlays, tooltips, sorting) must re-stat the path itself, and IsDirectory cannot be asked at all.

what_it_does: How enumerated children are ordered: fstNone, fstAlphabet, fstFoldersFirst, fstCustom (defers to OnSortCompare).
ours_evidence: grep -ril FileSortType over source/ returned nothing. Children arrive in whatever order TyFsReadDirectory produced (tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:267-269 appends entries[i] straight into the tree); tyControls.FileSystem.pas:116 TyFsSortEntries exists but the tree never calls it.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:140 `property FileSortType: TFileSortType ... default fstNone`; type at 44; setter 648+ rebuilds the tree.
user_impact: Directory children appear in raw filesystem order (on NTFS roughly alphabetical, on ext4 effectively random), and there is no property to ask for alphabetical or folders-first. A capability that already exists in the FileSystem helper is simply not wired to the tree.

what_it_does: User comparator over two TFileItem entries; assigning it switches FileSortType to fstCustom and re-sorts the tree.
ours_evidence: grep -ril OnSortCompare over source/ returned nothing. TTyTreeView does publish OnCompareNodes (tyControls.TreeView.pas, published list line ~580), but TTyShellTreeView never routes its raw TTyFsEntry values into it, so a handler would only see rendered node text.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:144 `property OnSortCompare: TFileItemCompareEvent read FOnSortCompare write SetOnSortCompare;`, type at 73, setter 693+.
user_impact: Custom ordering of a directory's children (by extension, by date, natural-numeric) cannot be expressed on the raw file records.

what_it_does: Per-entry veto hook fired while a node is being populated: (ABasePath, AFileInfo, var CanAdd) lets the app filter out individual folders.
ours_evidence: grep -ril OnAddItem over source/ returned nothing. PopulateChildren adds every entry TyFsReadDirectory returned with no hook (tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:266-269).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:143 `property OnAddItem: TAddItemEvent`, type at 77-78, dispatcher DoAddItem at 111.
user_impact: No way to hide specific folders (.git, system junctions, symlink loops) from the tree; the only filter is the coarse hidden-attribute flag.

what_it_does: Switches the control's own drawn folder/drive glyphs off so an assigned Images list (or no icons at all) is used instead. Default True.
ours_evidence: grep -ril UseBuiltinIcons/UseBuiltInIcons over source/ returned nothing. Our ctor unconditionally builds two glyphs and assigns them: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:121 BuildGlyphs, :221 `Images := FImages`. An app can overwrite Images afterwards (TTyTreeView.Images is published) but cannot ask for no icons, and the built glyphs are always constructed.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:135 `property UseBuiltinIcons: Boolean read FUseBuiltinIcons write SetUseBuiltinIcons default true;`, consumed by DrawBuiltInIcon (114) / GetBuiltinIconSize (116).
user_impact: A text-only or app-iconography tree needs Images := nil after construction, and the two BGRA masters are rendered on every instance regardless. The themed equivalent is missing too -- there is no token to suppress the content glyphs.

what_it_does: Class/instance helpers exposing the platform base path, the effective root path, and a static directory enumerator that other classes reuse.
ours_evidence: The capabilities exist but on a helper unit, not the control: tyControls.FileSystem.pas:80 TyFsReadDirectory (= GetFilesInDir), :126 TyFsRoots (= GetBasePath, as an array of places). grep -ril GetBasePath/GetRootPath/GetFilesInDir over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:125-129 `class function GetBasePath`, `function GetRootPath`, `class procedure GetFilesInDir(...)`; bodies 964-995.
user_impact: Porting break only: code that calls TShellTreeView.GetFilesInDir(...) must be rewritten against tyControls.FileSystem. The functionality is present.

what_it_does: Assigning a Root or Path that does not exist (or selecting a node whose file has been deleted) raises a typed exception the app can catch and report.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:387 `if match = nil then Exit;   { no root is a prefix -- silent }` and :372-373 `if target = '' then Exit;` -- SelectPath fails silently, and :407 `if match = nil then Break;` stops at the deepest reachable node without signalling. grep -ril EInvalidPath/EShellCtrl over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:427-428 (EShellCtrl/EInvalidPath), raised at 625 (bad Root), 1549/1561/1580/1604 (bad Path), and 1163 (selected item no longer exists).
user_impact: A dialog that restores a saved last-used folder cannot tell whether the restore worked: the tree just focuses the nearest surviving ancestor (or nothing) with no error, so the app shows a stale path in its edit box.

what_it_does: On the LCL side, changing which object types are enumerated immediately refreshes the visible tree (BeginUpdate/UpdateView/EndUpdate).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:419-429 SetShowHidden sets the field and deliberately does nothing else ('Flag-only, deliberately ... A consumer that wants an immediate visible refresh calls PopulateRoots'); the published declaration at :88-90 documents the same.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:674-691 SetObjectTypes -> UpdateView inside BeginUpdate/EndUpdate.
user_impact: A 'Show hidden files' checkbox wired straight to ShowHidden appears broken: nothing changes until the user collapses and re-expands, and the only immediate refresh available (PopulateRoots) throws away the whole tree state.

what_it_does: On TShellTreeView all of these stay free for the application -- the shell behaviour lives in overridden virtuals (CanExpand, DoSelectionChanged, DrawBuiltInIcon, NodeHasChildren), so OnChange/OnExpanding/OnGetImageIndex are published for the user.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellTreeView.pas:110-114 the ctor claims all five published event slots (`OnGetText := @TreeGetText; OnInitNode := @TreeInitNode; OnExpanding := @TreeExpanding; OnGetImageIndex := @TreeGetImageIndex; OnChange := @TreeChange`), and they remain publicly writable via TTyTreeView (tyControls.TreeView.pas published OnGetText/OnInitNode/OnExpanding/OnGetImageIndex/OnChange). Nothing chains to a previously assigned handler.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:112-117 (protected virtual overrides CanExpand/Collapse/DrawBuiltInIcon/NodeHasChildren) while 206/219/220 publish OnChange/OnExpanding/OnGetImageIndex for the user.
user_impact: Assigning OnChange in the Object Inspector silently kills path caching and OnPathChange; assigning OnExpanding kills lazy population (the tree stops expanding); assigning OnGetText makes every node blank. The failure looks like a control bug, not a documented restriction.

what_it_does: The directory whose contents are listed; assigning it re-reads the folder.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:105 `property Directory: string read FDirectory write LoadDirectory;` -- same concept, different name. grep over source/ confirms no Root property on the shell list.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:300 `property Root: string read FRoot write SetRoot;` (published at 368).
user_impact: Porting break: `ShellListView1.Root := Dir` does not compile, and the tree/list linkage code in LCL examples (which assigns ShellListView.Root) has to be rewritten.

what_it_does: Published set choosing folders / non-folders / hidden. LCL default is [otNonFolders] -- a files-only pane.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:53 `FObjectTypes: TTyFsObjectTypes` is PRIVATE and fixed to [fotFolders, fotFiles] in the ctor (:207); only the hidden bit is reachable, through ShowHidden (:109, setter 600-609). grep -ril ObjectTypes over source/ shows the type exists (tyControls.FileSystem.pas:52) but no published property on the control.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:299 `property ObjectTypes: TObjectTypes ... default [otNonFolders]`, published at 367; setter 1762+.
user_impact: A files-only pane (the LCL default!) or a folders-only pane cannot be configured; every TTyShellListView always mixes folders and files. Also a silent default change for anyone porting a .lfm.

what_it_does: Whether the file Mask matches case-sensitively, case-insensitively, or per platform default (mcsPlatformDefault).
ours_evidence: grep -ril MaskCaseSensitivity over source/ returned nothing. The capability EXISTS one layer down but is hard-wired: tyControls.FileSystem.pas:88 `function TyFsMatchesFilter(const AName, APatterns: string; ACaseSens: Boolean)`, and TyFsReadDirectory calls it with a literal False (tyControls.FileSystem.pas:239 `TyFsMatchesFilter(sr.Name, AMask, False)`) with the comment 'Matching is case-insensitive (the file-dialog convention on every platform)'. TyFsReadDirectory has no case-sensitivity parameter at all (:209).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:298 `property MaskCaseSensitivity: TMaskCaseSensitivity ... default mcsPlatformDefault`, published at 342; type at 46; passed to GetFilesInDirectory at 1867.
user_impact: On Linux/macOS a mask of '*.PAS' matches lowercase .pas files, unlike a native TShellListView at its default setting, and an app that needs exact-case matching has no way to ask for it.

what_it_does: Redistributes the Name/Size/Type column widths as a percentage of the client width on every resize; default True.
ours_evidence: grep -ril AutoSizeColumns over source/ returned nothing. Our columns get fixed pixel widths once, in the ctor: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:259-262 AddCol('Name',220), ('Size',90), ('Type',120), ('Modified',140), and there is no DoOnResize/Resize override in the unit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:296 `property AutoSizeColumns: Boolean ... default true`, published at 316; AdjustColWidths at 1913-1945, driven from DoOnResize (283).
user_impact: Widening or narrowing the pane leaves a dead gap on the right (or clips Modified); with a wide window the Name column stays 220px while the rest is empty. Every host has to hand-code column sizing.

what_it_does: Turns the control's own file-kind glyphs off (default True), so an assigned Small/LargeImages list -- or no icon column -- is used.
ours_evidence: grep -ril UseBuiltInIcons over source/ returned nothing. The ctor always builds six BGRA masters and assigns them to both lists: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:227 BuildGlyphs, :369-370 `SmallImages := FImages; LargeImages := FImages`. GetItemImageIndex always returns a kind index (:444-450), so even after clearing the lists an index is still requested.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:302 `property UseBuiltInIcons: Boolean read FUseBuiltinIcons write SetUseBuiltInIcons default true;`, consumed in PopulateWithRoot 1894-1900 and GetBuiltinImageIndex (286).
user_impact: No supported way to run the list without the built-in content icons (a compact text-only file pane), and no themed equivalent of the switch either.

what_it_does: Design-time link to a shell tree; the list's UpdateView also refreshes the linked tree at the same directory (guarded against recursion by FLockUpdate).
ours_evidence: grep -ril ShellTreeView over source/ hits only unit names and locals; there is no property. The seam is the one-way OnDirectoryChange notification (tyControls.ShellListView.pas:118) which the host must wire.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:301 `property ShellTreeView: TCustomShellTreeView read FShellTreeView write SetShellTreeView;`, published at 369; used in UpdateView 2004-2011.
user_impact: Diving into a folder in the list does not move the companion tree unless the app writes the glue; and the pair cannot be connected in the designer at all.

what_it_does: Per-entry veto during population: (ABasePath, AFileInfo, var CanAdd).
ours_evidence: grep -ril OnAddItem over source/ returned nothing. ReloadEntries assigns the whole array with no per-entry hook: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:390 `FEntries := TyFsReadDirectory(FDirectory, FMask, FObjectTypes);`.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:303 `property OnAddItem: TAddItemEvent`, published at 407; DoAddItem at 285, called per file in PopulateWithRoot 1872-1873.
user_impact: Filtering beyond a filename mask -- by size, date, attribute, or an app blocklist -- requires post-processing that the control does not expose (FEntries is read-only, :102).

what_it_does: Fires with the freshly created TListItem for each accepted file, so the app can decorate the row (extra sub-items, state image, colour).
ours_evidence: grep -ril OnFileAdded over source/ returned nothing. Rows are virtual (OwnerData := True, tyControls.ShellListView.pas:213) so no per-item object is ever created to hand out; the available per-row hooks (OnGetItemText etc. on TTyListView) are already overridden as methods (:81-84).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:245 (type), :287 `property OnFileAdded: TCSLVFileAddedEvent`, published at 408, fired at 1902.
user_impact: No hook to annotate rows as the directory is read (e.g. mark read-only files, attach per-file data); an app must re-derive everything from Entries afterwards.

what_it_does: Maps a list item to its full path.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:99/581 `function FileAt(AIndex: Integer): string;` plus :98/576 SelectedFile -- index-based, not item-based (OwnerData means there are no TListItem objects). grep -ril GetPathFromItem over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:293 `function GetPathFromItem(ANode: TListItem): string;`, body 1984-1987.
user_impact: Porting break for any code holding a TListItem (drag payloads, OnSelectItem handlers written against LCL); callers must be rewritten to carry indices.

what_it_does: Re-reads the current directory in reaction to filesystem changes AND restores the previously selected row by CAPTION (FindCaption), then cascades the refresh to the linked ShellTreeView.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:95-96 `{ Re-read the current directory. } procedure Refresh; reintroduce;` -> body 415-418 is just `ReloadEntries;`. No selection capture/restore anywhere in the unit (LoadDirectory deliberately CLEARS selection at :407-408, and Refresh does nothing about it). grep -ril UpdateView over source/ hits only tyControls.Dialogs.Progress.pas.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:294 (declaration), body 1990-2011 (`selectedItem := Selected.Caption` ... `Selected := FindCaption(0, selectedItem, false, true, false)` + ShellTreeView.UpdateView).
user_impact: Two losses: the method name a port calls does not exist, and after a refresh the selection stays pinned to a row INDEX -- so if a file was added or removed above it, the highlighted row is now a different file than the user had selected.

what_it_does: On every LCL control Refresh means 'repaint now' (Invalidate + Update). LCL's shell list keeps that meaning and uses UpdateView for the disk re-read.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:96 `procedure Refresh; reintroduce;` with body 415-418 `ReloadEntries;` -- it re-enumerates the directory from disk and does not repaint by itself. `reintroduce` deliberately hides the inherited method.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1719 `procedure Refresh;` on TControl (repaint); C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:294 keeps the re-read under the separate name UpdateView.
user_impact: Generic code that calls Refresh on a control to force a repaint (a theme switch, a custom draw loop) unknowingly triggers a synchronous directory scan on every call -- a disk hit and a possible re-sort where a repaint was intended.

member: Items (TListItems of TShellListItem: isFolder, FileInfo: TSearchRec)
what_it_does: The per-file item objects, each carrying its TSearchRec, exposed publicly ('Protected properties which users may want to access, see bug 15374') plus Caption/SubItems/Data/ImageIndex per row.
ours_evidence: Our backing store is a read-only record array: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:102 `property Entries: TTyFsEntryArray read FEntries;` (fields Name/FullPath/IsDir/IsHidden/Size/Modified/Attr/TypeName, tyControls.FileSystem.pas:38-46). The inherited published Items (tyControls.ListView.pas:321) still exists but is EMPTY because OwnerData is forced True (ShellListView.pas:213), so reading it yields nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:249-255 TShellListItem (isFolder 253, FileInfo 254), :305 `property Items;`, populated at 1875-1878.
user_impact: Porting break plus a live trap: `ShellListView1.Items[i].Caption` compiles against our control (Items is published) and silently returns nothing, because the real data is in Entries. There is no per-item object to attach state to.

what_it_does: TShellListView publishes OnCompare for the application (its own sorting goes through SortType/SortColumn), and leaves OnDblClick/OnSelectItem free.
ours_evidence: The ctor claims both published slots for internal use: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:219 `OnCompare := @DoCompare;` and :224 `OnItemActivate := @HandleItemActivate;` with the in-code warning 'This means TTyShellListView OWNS OnItemActivate internally -- apps use OnFileActivate and must not reassign OnItemActivate.' Both remain publicly writable (tyControls.ListView.pas:350, :352).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:377 `property OnCompare;` published on TShellListView; the class's own ordering runs through Sort/SortType (358-359) and PopulateWithRoot's Sort call (1906).
user_impact: Assigning OnCompare in the Object Inspector silently reverts sorting to lexical display-string order -- exactly the '10 KB before 9 KB' bug the unit header warns about -- and assigning OnItemActivate kills folder navigation and OnFileActivate.

what_it_does: LCL renders the Size column through localized resourcestrings from LCLStrConsts, so the unit words follow the application language.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ShellListView.pas:129-153 TyFmtScaled/TyFormatFileSize hard-code the English suffixes ' B'/' KB'/' MB'/' GB'/' TB' and a literal '.' decimal separator ('built by hand rather than via FormatFloat so the decimal separator is always .'). grep -ril resourcestring in this unit returns nothing, so these strings are outside the package .po files.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/shellctrls.pas:1888-1892 `Format(sShellCtrlsBytes, [...])` / sShellCtrlsKB / sShellCtrlsMB, declared in LCLStrConsts (unit imported at line 27).
user_impact: The Size column cannot be translated and always shows English units with a dot decimal separator, even in a fully localized app -- and the strings are invisible to the project's i18n pass.

what_it_does: Whether the popup is left-aligned, right-aligned or centred on the invocation point (paLeft/paRight/paCenter).
ours_evidence: The property is inherited and therefore visible in the Object Inspector, but nothing reads it: tyControls.Menu.pas:1930-1931 PopUp builds a zero-size anchor `Rect(X, Y, X, Y)` and hands it to TTyMenuPopup.Popup, and ComputeBounds (1056-1096) only ever does `L := AAnchor.Left` (1080) with an overflow nudge. grep -ril Alignment over source/ finds only text alignment (taLeftJustify etc.), never TPopupAlignment.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:490 `property Alignment: TPopupAlignment ... default paLeft;` (type 462); consumed by the widgetset popup implementations.
user_impact: Setting Alignment := paRight/paCenter has no effect -- the menu always drops down-right of the cursor. A right-aligned drop-down under a right-hand toolbar button spills off the intended edge (it only reflows when it hits the screen edge).

what_it_does: Which mouse button tracks and activates rows once the menu is up (tbRightButton default, tbLeftButton for press-and-drag right-button menus).
ours_evidence: grep -ril TrackButton over source/ returned nothing. TTyMenuView activates only through Click (tyControls.Menu.pas:786-790, i.e. the left button via TControl) and MouseMove highlight (763-774); no button selection exists.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:493 `property TrackButton: TTrackButton ... default tbRightButton;`; honoured by the widgetset, e.g. C:/lazarus/lcl/interfaces/qt/qtwsmenus.pp:523 `if APopupMenu.TrackButton = tbLeftButton then`.
user_impact: The published property is inert: a press-hold-right-button-drag-release context menu (tbLeftButton semantics) cannot be built, and the OI setting misleads.

what_it_does: The menu-wide icon source every item's ImageIndex resolves against (TMenuItem.GetImageList walks SubMenuImages then the parent menu's Images), plus the width hint for HiDPI resolution.
ours_evidence: TTyPopupMenu inherits TMenu.Images but nothing reads it: EnsureRenderer only sets Controller and calls ConfigureRenderer, whose base body is empty (tyControls.Menu.pas:1863-1877). The renderer's icon source is a DIFFERENT type on a DIFFERENT class -- tyControls.Menu.pas:411 `property Images: TTyVirtualImageList` on TTyImagesMenu, plumbed at 1893-1897; the view reads only that (:944-954 `(FImages <> nil) and (FRows[i].ImageIndex ...)`). ImagesWidth: grep over source/ returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:430-431 `property Images: TCustomImageList` / `ImagesWidth: Integer` on TMenu; resolution at :264-265 GetImageList.
user_impact: A TTyPopupMenu with the ordinary LCL Images list assigned (which the OI offers and which every ported project uses) shows no icons at all; you must switch the class to TTyImagesMenu and rebuild the image list as a TTyVirtualImageList. Silent, and the OI gives no hint.

what_it_does: The owner-draw protocol: with OwnerDraw True, each item's size comes from OnMeasureItem/DoMeasureItem and its pixels from OnDrawItem/DoDrawItem (canvas, rect, TOwnerDrawState).
ours_evidence: All four properties are inherited and settable, and none is ever consulted. TTyMenuView.RenderTo paints every row itself (tyControls.Menu.pas:837-978); row height comes from ItemRowHeight (572-586) and width from MeasureWidth (604-641), both theme-token driven. grep -ril OnDrawItem over source/ returns nothing; OnMeasureItem hits only tyControls.TreeView.pas (an unrelated tree event).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:432-434 (TMenu.OwnerDraw/OnDrawItem/OnMeasureItem), :352-353 (TMenuItem.OnDrawItem/OnMeasureItem), dispatchers DoDrawItem/DoMeasureItem at :231-232.
user_impact: Any app that owner-draws menu items (colour swatches, font previews, two-line entries, per-item bitmaps) gets the plain themed row instead and its handlers never fire. There is no themed substitute hook on the view either.

what_it_does: Right-to-left menus: the check/icon column moves to the right, shortcut text to the left, submenu arrows point left and cascades open leftward.
ours_evidence: The properties are inherited and settable but the renderer is LTR-only and unconditional: check/icon slot at the left (tyControls.Menu.pas:935-954, `RowRect.Left + padL`), caption left-justified (961-962 taLeftJustify), shortcut right-justified (968-971), submenu arrow tgArrowRight at the right edge (965-967), and submenus always anchored to the parent's right (1278-1282, `AToRight=True`). grep -ril BidiMode over source/ hits only tyControls.Memo.pas; IsRightToLeft returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:427-428 (TMenu.BidiMode/ParentBidiMode), :415-417 (IsRightToLeft/UseRightToLeftAlignment/UseRightToLeftReading), :269 TMenuItem.GetIsRightToLeft.
user_impact: Arabic/Hebrew UIs get mirrored-language text in a left-to-right menu frame: glyph column on the wrong side, cascades opening off the reading direction. The published BidiMode gives no clue that it is inert.

what_it_does: A per-item glyph assigned directly as a bitmap, independent of any image list -- the oldest and most common way to put an icon on a Delphi/LCL menu item.
ours_evidence: TyBuildMenuRows copies only these item fields: Caption, ShortCut, Enabled, Checked, RadioItem, Count, Default, ImageIndex (tyControls.Menu.pas:464-475). TTyMenuRow (:29-43) has no bitmap member, and RenderTo's left slot draws only a check/radio glyph or FImages.CachedIndex(ImageIndex) (:934-954). grep -ril for Bitmap in tyControls.Menu.pas finds only BGRABitmap plumbing, never TMenuItem.Bitmap.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:332 `property Bitmap: TBitmap read GetBitmap write SetBitmap stored IsBitmapStored;`, :294 HasBitmap, :264-265 GetImageList.
user_impact: Items whose icon was assigned as Item.Bitmap (or streamed into a .lfm as an item Bitmap) render with an empty icon slot in every themed menu, with no error and no fallback.

what_it_does: Per-item control over whether the icon is drawn: gsmAlways / gsmNever / gsmApplication (Application.ShowMenuGlyphs) / gsmSystem (the OS setting). Default gsmApplication.
ours_evidence: grep -ril GlyphShowMode and ShowMenuGlyphs over source/ both returned nothing. RenderTo draws the icon whenever an image list and a valid ImageIndex exist, with no gate (tyControls.Menu.pas:944-954).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:334 `property GlyphShowMode: TGlyphShowMode ... default gsmApplication;`, evaluated in HasIcon (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/menuitem.inc:850-872, including Application.ShowMenuGlyphs and SystemShowMenuGlyphs).
user_impact: Items marked gsmNever still show their icon, and an app (or a user's OS preference) that turns menu glyphs off is ignored -- the themed menu always shows icons.

what_it_does: Highlighting a menu item publishes its Hint to Application.Hint, which is how a status-bar/long-hint description of the selected command appears.
ours_evidence: grep -ril IntfDoSelect and 'Application.Hint' over source/ both returned nothing. TTyMenuRow (tyControls.Menu.pas:29-43) does not carry Hint, TyBuildMenuRows never reads it (:464-475), and SetHighlight/UpdateHoverOpen (:717-726, 530-550) only invalidate and arm the submenu timer.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:337 `property Hint: TTranslateString ...`, :274 `procedure IntfDoSelect; virtual;`, body at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/menuitem.inc:468-470 `Application.Hint := GetLongHint(Hint);`.
user_impact: Apps that describe the highlighted command in a status bar (the standard OnHint/Application.Hint pattern) go silent under themed menus -- item hints are dead data.

what_it_does: Draws the item as checkable even when unchecked -- i.e. an empty check box/frame is painted in the glyph slot so the user can see it is a toggle.
ours_evidence: grep -ril ShowAlwaysCheckable over source/ returned nothing. TTyMenuRow has Checked/RadioItem but no ShowAlwaysCheckable (tyControls.Menu.pas:37-39), and RenderTo draws a glyph ONLY when Checked is True (`if FRows[i].Checked then ... DrawGlyph`, :935-943); an unchecked row paints nothing in the slot. The slot width itself is always reserved (leftSlot, :883), so only the empty-box mark is missing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:345-346 `property ShowAlwaysCheckable: boolean ... default False;`, and IsCheckItem at :290.
user_impact: A toggle item reads as an ordinary command until the first time it is switched on, so users cannot tell which entries are checkable. The property is settable and inert.

what_it_does: A per-submenu image list: items inside that submenu resolve their ImageIndex against SubMenuImages instead of the parent menu's Images (GetImageList checks it first).
ours_evidence: grep -ril SubMenuImages over source/ returned nothing. A cascade unconditionally inherits the PARENT level's list: tyControls.Menu.pas:1261 `FChild.Images := FImages;` inside DoOpenSubmenu, and the view only ever reads its own FImages (:944-954).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:347-348 `property SubMenuImages: TCustomImageList` / `SubMenuImagesWidth: Integer`, resolved by GetImageList at :264-265.
