user_impact: A submenu with its own icon set (a Recent Files list with per-app icons, an insert-symbol cascade) shows indices resolved against the wrong list -- wrong pictures rather than none, which is worse than a blank slot.

what_it_does: A disabled top-level menu is drawn greyed out and cannot be opened by click or by its Alt mnemonic.
ours_evidence: The bar's cell painter never resolves a disabled state: tyControls.Menu.pas:1804-1811 builds CellStates from FOpenIndex/FHotIndex only ([tysActive]/[tysHover]/[tysNormal]) -- tysDisabled is never included. And OpenTop does not check it: :1660-1661 `mi := VisibleTopItem(AIndex); if (mi = nil) or (mi.Count = 0) then begin ClosePopup; Exit; end;`. (DialogChar DOES check mi.Enabled at :1732, so the mnemonic path and the click path disagree.)
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:330-331 `property Enabled: Boolean ... default True` (stored IsEnabledStored); TMenuItem.Click bails on `if not Enabled then Exit` (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/menuitem.inc:66) and the native bar greys and blocks the item.
user_impact: Disabling a whole top menu (the common 'no document open -> Edit menu off' pattern) has no visible effect and the dropdown still opens on click, so users reach commands the app has declared unavailable.

member: top-level item with no children (Count = 0) never fires OnClick
what_it_does: In a native menu bar a childless top-level item is a command button: clicking it (or pressing its Alt mnemonic) fires its OnClick / its Action.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Menu.pas:1660-1661 OpenTop: `if (mi = nil) or (mi.Count = 0) then begin ClosePopup; Exit; end;` -- it returns without ever calling mi.Click. Every activation path funnels through OpenTop: MouseDown (:1768-1780), DialogChar (:1733-1735) and DeferredOpenTop (:1708-1712). grep for `.Click` in tyControls.Menu.pas finds it only at :1236 inside TTyMenuPopup.DoActivateRow, i.e. for dropdown ROWS.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:282 `procedure Click; virtual;` (body C:/lazarus/lcl/include/menuitem.inc:52+, fires FOnClick / the Action); reached for bar items through TMenu.DispatchCommand (:419) / FindItem (:411).
user_impact: A top-level command such as 'Help' or 'About' with no submenu is completely dead in a TTyMenuBar -- clicking it does nothing at all, silently. This is not a missing option; it is a working LCL menu that stops working when the bar is themed.

what_it_does: The TMainMenu-wide icon list that every item's ImageIndex resolves against, so bar dropdowns show icons.
ours_evidence: TTyMenuBar has no icon source and never plumbs one: its published list is Menu/AutoSizeWidth/TabStop/Align/Anchors/StyleClass/Controller (tyControls.Menu.pas:328-348), and OpenTop sets only Controller and SetRoot on the dropdown (:1664-1671) -- grep of tyControls.Menu.pas for `FPopup.` returns OnNavigateAdjacent, OnClose, Controller, SetRoot, Popup and nothing else. TTyMenuPopup.Images exists (:243) but only TTyImagesMenu ever assigns it (:1896).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:430-431 `property Images: TCustomImageList` / `ImagesWidth` on TMenu, inherited by TMainMenu; per-item resolution at :264-265.
user_impact: An application menu bar can never show item icons: assigning MainMenu1.Images (the only place the OI offers) is ignored, and unlike the context menu there is no TTyImagesMenu-style opt-in for the bar at all.

what_it_does: TMainMenu.MenuChanged fires on every structural or caption change and notifies the host window (CM_MENUCHANGED) so the bar re-measures and repaints; OnChange is the published user hook.
ours_evidence: grep -ril for OnChange in tyControls.Menu.pas returns nothing on TTyMenuBar; SetMenu only takes a FreeNotification and invalidates once (tyControls.Menu.pas:1430-1439), and Notification handles only opRemove (:1448-1458). Nothing re-runs ApplyAutoSizeWidth or Invalidate when an item's Caption/Visible/child list changes afterwards; the geometry seams (TopCount/TopCaption/TopCellWidth, :1460-1529) are recomputed only on paint or resize.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:456 `property OnChange;` published on TMainMenu (declared :405 on TMenu); TMainMenu.MenuChanged at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/mainmenu.inc:43-49 sends CM_MENUCHANGED to the owning window.
user_impact: Runtime menu edits do not reach the bar: renaming a top item, hiding one, or adding one leaves the painted cells stale (and an AutoSizeWidth bar the wrong width) until some unrelated repaint happens. Apps must call Invalidate by hand.

what_it_does: MDI/plugin menu merging: Merge(Menu) folds another TMainMenu's items into this one by GroupIndex, and the rendered menu is then driven by MergedItems (VisibleCount/VisibleItems), not by the raw Items list.
ours_evidence: grep -ril MergedItems over source/ returned nothing. Every render path walks the RAW child list: TyBuildMenuRows uses `ARoot.Count` / `ARoot.Items[i]` (tyControls.Menu.pas:443-444) and the bar's TopCount/VisibleTopItem walk `FMenu.Items.Count` / `FMenu.Items[i]` (:1465-1466, :1475-1480).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:451-452 `procedure Merge(Menu: TMainMenu); procedure Unmerge(...)` (bodies C:/lazarus/lcl/include/mainmenu.inc:52-64), :306-307/312 Merged/MergedWith/MergedItems; the LCL render path uses MergedItems.VisibleItems (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/menuitem.inc:455-465).
user_impact: Merged menus are invisible in a themed bar or popup: after MainMenu1.Merge(PluginMenu), the merged-in items simply do not appear (and replaced items are not hidden), so MDI/plugin menu architectures silently lose entries.

what_it_does: Pushes a top-level bar item to the right end of the bar (the classic right-aligned Help/Window menu).
ours_evidence: grep -in rightjustify tyControls.Menu.pas returns exactly one hit -- :971 `taRightJustify` for shortcut TEXT alignment inside a dropdown row -- not TMenuItem.RightJustify. Cells pack strictly left-to-right from the bar's left padding: TopLeft accumulates TopCellWidth over preceding indices (:1531-1541), and TopAtX mirrors it (:1543-1554).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:341 `property RightJustify: boolean read FRightJustify write SetRightJustify default False;` (setter :216).
user_impact: A right-aligned top-level menu is impossible; items marked RightJustify sit in normal left-packed order, so ported menu bars lose their intended layout with no diagnostic.

what_it_does: The root TMenuItem holding the bar's top-level items -- the object every add/remove/iterate call goes through.
ours_evidence: TTyMenuBar has no Items of its own; it renders an ASSOCIATED model reached one level deeper: tyControls.Menu.pas:332 `property Menu: TMainMenu read FMenu write SetMenu;` and all internal access is FMenu.Items (:1465, :1475). This mirrors the deliberate Form.Menu association pattern documented at :330-331.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/menus.pp:429 `property Items: TMenuItem read FItems;` on TMenu, inherited by TMainMenu.
user_impact: Porting break only: `Bar.Items[0]` must become `Bar.Menu.Items[0]`, and a TTyMenuBar cannot be dropped in as a drop-in TMainMenu replacement in code that assumes Items.

what_it_does: Binds the spin-button pair to a companion TWinControl (normally an edit): the up/down positions itself against that control, keeps its own bounds/enabled/visible in sync with it, and writes Position back into the control's text on every step.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85 published list is Min/Max/Position/Increment/Orientation/Wrap/OnChange/OnArrowClick/Align/Anchors/StyleClass/Controller only; the unit header (UpDown.pas:32-33) says outright 'no edit of its own -- bind it to any control via OnChange reading Position'. grep -ri 'Associate' over source/ hits only tyControls.Dialogs.pas, tyControls.FileSystem.pas, tyControls.Form.pas and tyControls.Menu.pas (unrelated uses of the word; no `property Associate` anywhere -- `grep -rn 'property Associate'` returns nothing).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1993 (protected declaration) and :2020 (published on TUpDown); implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:377 SetAssociate, :254 UpdateUpDownPositionText, :300-330 UpdateAlignButtonPos, plus OnAssociateChangeBounds/Enabled/Visible hooks at comctrls.pp:1973-1975.
user_impact: The headline reason people drop a TUpDown on a form -- 'glue this to Edit1' -- does not port. Every user must hand-write an OnChange handler that formats the number into the edit, re-parses it back, repositions the buttons when the edit moves, and mirrors Enabled/Visible; and none of that survives a .lfm that just said Associate=Edit1.

what_it_does: The whole fractional variant of the spin edit: a Double Value, DecimalPlaces to control the displayed precision, a Double Increment, and a decimal-separator-aware input filter.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:12 declares FMinValue, FMaxValue, FValue, FIncrement all as Integer, and published Value/MinValue/MaxValue/Increment are Integer (SpinEdit.pas:61-64); grep -ri 'FloatSpin' and 'DecimalPlaces' over source/ return nothing. The closest is TTyNumericEdit (tyControls.NumericEdit.pas:24) which does have Decimals/MinValue/MaxValue as Double (NumericEdit.pas:53-56) -- but it is a plain edit with no spin buttons and no Increment, so it is not a float spin edit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:33 TCustomFloatSpinEdit, :78 DecimalPlaces (default 2), :80 Increment: Double, :83 Value: Double, :89 TFloatSpinEdit republishing them at :101-105; implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:223 GetLimitedValue, :235 ValueToStr.
user_impact: Any form using a TFloatSpinEdit (prices, percentages, scale factors, coordinates) has no counterpart at all -- the user must either lose the spin buttons by moving to TTyNumericEdit or bolt a TTyUpDown onto it by hand.

what_it_does: Right-to-left mode: in RTL the horizontal bar's coordinate system is mirrored, so Position increases leftward and the arrow/page codes are applied with an inverted sign.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBar.pas:84-107 publishes no BidiMode/ParentBidiMode, and the geometry helpers are unconditionally left-to-right / top-to-bottom (TyScrollThumbRect, ScrollBar.pas:118-155, computes Offset from Pos0 with no mirroring). grep -ri 'BidiMode' over source/ hits only tyControls.Memo.pas (`grep -rn 'property BidiMode'` returns nothing anywhere).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:124 BidiMode and :137 ParentBidiMode published on TScrollBar; the mirroring machinery is FRTLFactor at stdctrls.pp:75, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollbar.inc:43,58-61 (SetScrollPos with FMax-FPosition) and :187-199 (SmallChange/LargeChange multiplied by FRTLFactor).
user_impact: An Arabic/Hebrew UI gets a scroll bar that scrolls the wrong way relative to the mirrored content, and a ported .lfm carrying BidiMode=bdRightToLeft will not even load.

what_it_does: The value step used for a page action (track click, PgUp/PgDn, scPageUp/scPageDown), independent of PageSize which only sizes the thumb.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBar.pas:84-107 has PageSize and SmallChange but no LargeChange; PageSize does double duty -- it sizes the thumb (TyScrollThumbRect, ScrollBar.pas:128-139) AND is the page step for track clicks (ScrollBar.pas:684-691) and for PgUp/PgDn (ScrollBar.pas:746-747). grep -ri 'LargeChange' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:106 `property LargeChange: TScrollBarInc read FLargeChange write FLargeChange default 1` (republished at :133); initialised in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollbar.inc:34 and used for scPageUp/scPageDown at :195,199 -- separately from FPageSize, which only feeds ScrollInfo.nPage (:55).
user_impact: You cannot have a proportional thumb and a page step that differ: setting PageSize=1 to get a small thumb also shrinks a page click to one line, and setting PageSize=50 to get a 50-unit page click fattens the thumb to half the track. LCL code that sets LargeChange does not compile.

what_it_does: Flips the value axis independently of Orientation, so a horizontal bar can run max-to-min left-to-right, or a vertical bar can put Min at the top.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 publishes no Reversed; inversion is a private, non-settable function hard-wired to Orientation -- `function Inverted: Boolean` at TrackBar.pas:39 with body `Result := (FOrientation = toVertical)` at :197-200, consumed at :256, :271, :530, :562. grep -ri 'Reversed' over source/ hits only a prose comment in tyControls.Chart.pas:1444; `grep -rn 'property Reversed'` returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2789 `property Reversed: Boolean read FReversed write SetReversed default False` (republished on TTrackBar at :2827); setter at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:193.
user_impact: Two whole configurations are unreachable: a horizontal bar counting down left-to-right, and a vertical bar with Min at the top (a volume/attenuation slider). Ours forces vertical=inverted and horizontal=normal with no opt-out.

what_it_does: A highlighted sub-range on the track (the classic 'selection' band drawn between two values), with ShowSelRange to toggle it.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 has no SelStart/SelEnd/ShowSelRange and RenderTo (TrackBar.pas:483-591) draws only frame, thumb, ticks and the optional value readout -- no band. grep -ri 'ShowSelRange' over source/ returned nothing; 'SelStart' hits only tyControls.Edit.pas / Grid.pas / Memo.pas (text selection, unrelated); 'SelEnd' only tyControls.Memo.pas.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2791-2793 SelEnd (default 0), SelStart (default 0), ShowSelRange (default True), republished at :2829-2832; clamping/consistency logic at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:316 UpdateSelection, setters at :390 and :399, default FShowSelRange:=True at :68.
user_impact: Any 'valid band' / 'selected interval' UI (audio trim, allowed-range indicator) cannot be expressed; a ported .lfm carrying SelStart/SelEnd/ShowSelRange fails to stream.

what_it_does: Which side of the groove the tick marks are drawn on: tmBottomRight (default), tmTopLeft, or tmBoth.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 has Frequency but nothing selecting the side; the tick loop hard-codes it -- vertical draws at R.Right-TickLen and horizontal at R.Bottom-TickLen (TrackBar.pas:564-569), i.e. tmBottomRight only. grep -ri 'TickMarks' over source/ matches only the local variable `tickMarkS` in tyControls.Meter.pas:201,214,228; `grep -rn 'property TickMarks'` returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2729 TTickMark = (tmBottomRight, tmTopLeft, tmBoth) and :2795 `property TickMarks: TTickMark ... default tmBottomRight` (republished at :2835); default set at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:64, setter at :268.
user_impact: Ticks can only sit below (horizontal) or right (vertical). A slider that needs ticks above its groove, or ticks on both sides, is impossible, and TickMarks=tmBoth in a ported .lfm will not load.

what_it_does: How ticks are generated: tsNone (none), tsAuto (one every Frequency units, the default), tsManual (only ticks explicitly added by SetTick).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 has no TickStyle; the only control is Frequency (TrackBar.pas:83, clamped >=0 at :338-346) and the tick loop runs whenever `FFrequency > 0` (TrackBar.pas:551). Frequency=0 therefore covers tsNone, but tsManual has no representation. grep -ri 'TickStyle' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2730 TTickStyle = (tsNone, tsAuto, tsManual) and :2796 `property TickStyle: TTickStyle ... default tsAuto` (republished at :2836); default at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:65, setter at :249.
user_impact: tsNone survives only as the non-obvious Frequency=0 idiom (a porting break for TickStyle:=tsNone), and tsManual -- irregular ticks at hand-chosen values, e.g. a gamma curve -- cannot be expressed at all.

what_it_does: Adds a single tick mark at a caller-chosen value (the companion of TickStyle=tsManual).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas public section is only Create/Destroy/ThumbRect/DragTo/AnimationsEnabled (TrackBar.pas:65-74); ticks are generated by the fixed `while V <= FMax do ... Inc(V, FFrequency)` loop at TrackBar.pas:560-571 with no per-value entry point and no tick list. grep -ri 'SetTick' over source/ matches only TTyMeter.SetTicks (tyControls.Meter.pas:37,57,189), which is an integer COUNT of evenly spaced ticks on a different control -- not an add-one-tick-at-value call.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2778 `procedure SetTick(Value: Integer);` (public); implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:115.
user_impact: Non-uniform scales (ticks at 0/1/2/5/10/20/50/100) cannot be drawn; the tick spacing is locked to one arithmetic step.

what_it_does: Sets position, minimum and maximum in one call so the three are validated together exactly once instead of clamping each other during the intermediate states.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:65-74 public section has no SetParams; each setter clamps immediately -- SetMin forces `if FPosition < FMin then FPosition := FMin` (TrackBar.pas:274-280) and SetMax forces the mirror (:282-288). grep -ri 'SetParams' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2779 `procedure SetParams(APosition, AMin, AMax: Integer);` with the comment 'allow to set the parameters in one go in order to call FixParams only once'; implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:159-171, and SetMin/SetMax at :209-213 route through it.
user_impact: Concrete data loss: a bar on 0..10 with Position=5 rescaled to 50..100 by `Min := 50; Max := 100;` has Position silently rewritten to 50 by the first assignment and it never comes back -- the user's value is gone before Max is even set. The LCL one-shot call is the documented way to avoid exactly this.

what_it_does: Two overloads that set position, range and (optionally) page size atomically, so no intermediate clamp can move Position.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBar.pas public section is SetPositionSnapped/Create/Destroy/GetStyleTypeKey/BeginThumbDrag/DragThumbTo/EndThumbDrag/Dragging (ScrollBar.pas:69-83) -- no SetParams; SetMin clamps FPosition up (:344-350) and SetMax clamps it down (:352-358) on each individual assignment. grep -ri 'SetParams' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:102-103 two public SetParams overloads; implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollbar.inc:93 and :130.
user_impact: Same silent-value-loss as the track bar: a host re-ranging a bar (grid row count changed) must remember to order Min/Max/Position assignments defensively, and the natural order destroys Position. This is the single most common call in code that drives a scroll bar from a model.

what_it_does: The increment used by StepIt -- how far one 'tick' of progress advances (default 10).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:43-60 publishes Min/Max/Position/Orientation/AnimationsEnabled/OnChange/Align/Anchors/StyleClass/Controller only. `grep -rn 'property Step\b'` over source/ hits only tyControls.Dial.pas:64 and tyControls.GearDial.pas:63 (a Double snap-step on unrelated controls); grep -ri 'StepIt'/'StepBy' returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1853 `property Step: Integer read FStep write SetStep default 10` (republished on TProgressBar at :1885); used by C:/lazarus/lcl/include/progressbar.inc:235-241.
user_impact: The idiomatic loop `for i := 1 to n do begin Work; ProgressBar1.StepIt; end` has no equivalent; every caller must track and assign Position itself.

what_it_does: StepIt advances Position by Step (clamped to Min/Max); StepBy(Delta) advances it by an ad-hoc delta.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:40-42 public section is only Create/Destroy; the sole way to move the bar is assigning Position (setter at ProgressBar.pas:206-240). grep -ri 'StepIt' and 'StepBy' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1845-1846 `procedure StepIt; procedure StepBy(Delta: Integer);` (public); implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/progressbar.inc:235 and :256.
user_impact: Every ported progress loop breaks at compile time, and the caller has to re-implement the clamp that StepIt does for free.

what_it_does: Draws the progress as text inside the bar, formatted from a value/limits/percent template.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:43-60 has no BarShowText and RenderTo (ProgressBar.pas:249-290) draws only the frame plus the fill rect -- it never calls DrawText. grep -ri 'BarShowText' over source/ returned nothing. The CONCEPT does exist elsewhere in the library and is simply not wired here: TTyTrackBar.ShowValue (tyControls.TrackBar.pas:88), TTyGauge.ShowValue + ValueFormat (tyControls.Gauge.pas:26-27), TTyCircularProgress.ShowValue (tyControls.CircularProgress.pas:49).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1855 `property BarShowText: boolean ... default False` (republished at :1890); the text template FBarTextFormat = '%v from [%l-%u] (=%p%%)' at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/progressbar.inc:48, setter at :312.
user_impact: The extremely common '47%' readout inside the bar is unavailable; users must overlay a separate label and keep it in sync, even though three sibling controls in this same library already know how to render their own value.

what_it_does: Switches the bar between determinate (fill tracks Position) and marquee/indeterminate (a segment sweeps continuously, for unknown duration).
ours_evidence: Not a property on TTyProgressBar -- tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:43-60 has no Style. The capability exists as a SEPARATE control: TTyActivityBar (tyControls.ActivityBar.pas:24), whose header explicitly calls itself 'the indeterminate sibling of TTyProgressBar', with `property Active` at ActivityBar.pas:45 in place of Style. grep -ri 'Marquee' over source/ hits only ListView/ShellListView/DefaultTheme (unrelated marquee selection).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1803 TProgressBarStyle = (pbstNormal, pbstMarquee) and :1854 `property Style: TProgressBarStyle ... default pbstNormal` (republished at :1886); setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/progressbar.inc:212.
user_impact: Porting break rather than a missing feature: `ProgressBar1.Style := pbstMarquee` (and any .lfm carrying Style=pbstMarquee) cannot be made to work -- the user has to delete the control and drop a TTyActivityBar in its place, and cannot flip one control between the two modes at run time, which is what a download that starts with an unknown size then learns its total actually needs.

what_it_does: Chooses between a continuous fill (Smooth=True) and the classic segmented/chunked block fill (Smooth=False, the default).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:43-60 has no Smooth, and the fill is always one continuous rounded rectangle (TyProgressFillRect at ProgressBar.pas:68-105 returns a single rect; RenderTo fills it in one call at :271-285). grep -ri 'Smooth' over source/ hits tyControls.ImageView.pas, tyControls.LevelMeter.pas and tyControls.Painter.pas -- image resampling and meter value smoothing, nothing to do with a chunked progress fill; `grep -rn 'property Smooth'` returns nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1852 `property Smooth: boolean read FSmooth write SetSmooth default False` (republished at :1884); setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/progressbar.inc:312-area SetSmooth.
user_impact: The segmented look -- which is the LCL DEFAULT and what a classic/Win7-era skin is expected to reproduce -- cannot be selected, so a classic-theme demo cannot match the native control it is imitating.

what_it_does: LCL's TProgressBarOrientation has four fill directions: pbHorizontal (left->right), pbVertical (bottom->up), pbRightToLeft and pbTopDown.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:8 `TTyProgressOrientation = (tpoHorizontal, tpoVertical)` -- only two; published at ProgressBar.pas:49. The fill helper hard-codes the two anchors: vertical grows from the bottom (`Result.Top := ATrack.Bottom - FillLen`, ProgressBar.pas:102) and horizontal from the left (`Result.Right := ATrack.Left + FillLen`, :104), so right->left and top->down are unreachable.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1801 `TProgressBarOrientation = (pbHorizontal, pbVertical, pbRightToLeft, pbTopDown)`; property at :1850 default pbHorizontal (republished at :1877).
user_impact: Two of four documented fill directions are missing (a right-to-left bar for RTL locales, a top-down bar for a 'draining' meter), and even the two we have carry different enum identifiers, so `Orientation := pbVertical` does not compile and a ported .lfm cannot stream its Orientation value.

what_it_does: Makes the text portion non-typeable while the spin buttons keep working -- 'choose with the arrows, do not type'.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 has no EditorEnabled. The nearest property, ReadOnly (SpinEdit.pas:67), is deliberately coarser: its own comment says 'ReadOnly locks the value entirely ... it blocks both inline text editing AND +/- stepping', and the guards prove it -- InsertEditChar exits on FReadOnly (SpinEdit.pas:332), DoMouseWheel exits on FReadOnly (:473), and MouseDown skips both button rects (:488). grep -ri 'EditorEnabled' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:79 `property EditorEnabled: Boolean read FEditorEnabled write SetEditorEnabled default True` (published on TSpinEdit at :182); setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:184, default at :217. LCL keeps this ORTHOGONAL to TCustomEdit.ReadOnly (C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:872).
user_impact: The 'arrows only, no keyboard' spin edit -- the standard way to force a value onto a legal grid (even numbers, multiples of 5) -- cannot be built: our ReadOnly kills the arrows too, so the control becomes inert instead of arrow-driven. Two independent LCL properties collapsed into one here.

what_it_does: Lets the field show BLANK rather than a number -- the 'no value entered yet / mixed selection' state -- and reports whether it is currently blank.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 has no ValueEmpty, and the buffer is unconditionally re-derived from the integer: SyncBufferToValue does `FEditText := IntToStr(FValue)` (SpinEdit.pas:262-267) and is called from the constructor (:132), from SetValue (:204), SetMinValue (:213), SetMaxValue (:222), CommitEdit (:323) and on Escape (:443) -- so the field can never be left empty. grep -ri 'ValueEmpty' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:84 `property ValueEmpty: Boolean read FValueEmpty write SetValueEmpty default False`; setter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:94, cleared on real input at :76.
user_impact: There is no way to render 'not set': a filter form or a property inspector row must show 0, which is a legal value and therefore a lie. Clearing the text with Backspace snaps back to a number on the next commit.

what_it_does: MaxValue's out-of-the-box value, which in LCL is 0 and -- because MaxValue<=MinValue means 'unbounded' -- makes a freshly dropped spin edit accept any integer.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:62 `property MaxValue: Integer ... default 100` (and MinValue default 0 at :61, set in the constructor at :120-121). Our own SetValue implements the same unbounded rule -- `if FMaxValue > FMinValue then` clamp, SpinEdit.pas:194-198, with a comment citing LCL's GetLimitedValue -- so the mechanism agrees; only the shipped default differs.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:37 `DefMaxValue = 0`, :163 `property MaxValue: Integer read GetMaxValue write SetMaxValue default 0` and :162 MinValue default 0; the unbounded rule is C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:223 GetLimitedValue.
user_impact: A .lfm ported from Lazarus almost never stores MaxValue (it equals LCL's default), so it silently arrives here as 0..100 and any user entry above 100 is clamped without a diagnostic. The failure looks like a data bug in the app, not a control default.

what_it_does: Read/write access to the raw text currently in the editor, independent of the parsed numeric Value.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 does not publish or expose Text; the buffer is protected only -- FEditText declared at SpinEdit.pas:27 under the comment at :25 'Inline edit buffer (lightweight, no selection/clipboard). Protected so headless access subclasses (tests) can reach the buffer'. The capability exists on the sibling: TTyEdit publishes `property Text: TCaption` at tyControls.Edit.pas:176.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:878 `property Text;` in TCustomEdit's public block; TCustomFloatSpinEdit routes it through RealGetText/RealSetText at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:52 and :60 so Text and Value stay in step.
user_impact: You cannot read what the user has typed before it commits, cannot preset the field to a non-canonical string, and cannot implement 'validate as they type'. Anything touching .Text on a ported TSpinEdit fails to compile.

what_it_does: Programmatic read/write of the selection inside the editor.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas has no selection state at all -- the only cursor state is `FCaret: Integer` (SpinEdit.pas:28) and the header comment at :25 says 'no selection/clipboard'. The capability is fully built one class over: TTyEdit exposes SelStart/SelLength/SelText at tyControls.Edit.pas:172-174 (with GetSelStart/SetSelStart etc.), and TTyMemo has them too -- it is simply not wired into TTySpinEdit, which descends from TTyCustomControl (SpinEdit.pas:10), not from TTyEdit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:873-875 SelLength, SelStart, SelText in TCustomEdit's public block (getters/setters at :812-814, :821-823).
user_impact: No 'select the digits so the next keystroke replaces them', no programmatic replace-selection, and no way for a host (a grid inplace editor) to place the selection when it activates the cell.

what_it_does: Select the whole text, drop the selection, or empty the field.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:57-59 public section is only Create/Destroy -- no SelectAll, ClearSelection or Clear; no VK_A/Ctrl handling in KeyDown either (SpinEdit.pas:427-451). TTyEdit has all of them (tyControls.Edit.pas:149-150 SelectAll/ClearSelection in its public block), so again the capability exists in the library but not on this control.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:844-846 `procedure Clear; procedure SelectAll; virtual; procedure ClearSelection; virtual;` in TCustomEdit's public block.
user_impact: The universal 'focus the field and select-all so typing overwrites' pattern must be hand-rolled, and it cannot be -- there is no selection model to drive. Ctrl+A does nothing.

what_it_does: Clipboard operations on the editor's text/selection.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:57-59 public section is Create/Destroy only; KeyDown (SpinEdit.pas:427-451) handles VK_UP/DOWN/RETURN/ESCAPE/BACK/DELETE/LEFT/RIGHT/HOME/END and nothing else, so Ctrl+C/X/V are dead, and UTF8KeyPress only routes single characters through InsertEditChar (:419-425). TTyEdit implements all three (tyControls.Edit.pas:154-156) over ReadClipboardText/WriteClipboardText hooks (Edit.pas:139-140).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:847-849 CopyToClipboard, CutToClipboard, PasteFromClipboard (public, virtual) in TCustomEdit; LCL's spin edit even whitelists ^C/^X/^V in its key filter at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:136.
user_impact: A user cannot paste a copied number into the field -- for a spin edit holding an ID or a measured value that is the single most common interaction after typing. Nothing about it can be worked around from outside the control.

what_it_does: Undo the last edit in the field, and query whether an undo is available.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas has no undo state or method (public section Create/Destroy at :57-59; no VK_Z handling in KeyDown at :427-451). grep -ri 'CanUndo' over source/ hits tyControls.Edit.pas, Grid.pas, Memo.pas and the shared tyControls.UndoStack.pas -- so a reusable undo stack unit already exists in this library and TTyEdit wires it (Edit.pas:160-163 Undo/Redo/CanUndo/CanRedo); TTySpinEdit does not use it.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:850 `procedure Undo; virtual;` and :860 `property CanUndo: Boolean read GetCanUndo` in TCustomEdit; ^Z whitelisted at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:136.
user_impact: Ctrl+Z in the field does nothing and there is no programmatic undo, even though the library ships an undo stack the sibling edit already reuses.

what_it_does: AutoSelect (default True) selects the whole text when the control receives focus; AutoSelected reports whether that auto-selection is still intact.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 has neither, and DoEnter only resets the caret blink (SpinEdit.pas:169-178) -- focus never selects anything (there is no selection model). grep -ri 'AutoSelect' over source/ returned nothing at all, so this one is absent library-wide, not merely unwired.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:838-839 AutoSelect (default True) / AutoSelected in TCustomEdit; TSpinEdit publishes AutoSelect at C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:177 and re-exposes AutoSelected publicly at :172.
user_impact: Tabbing into a spin edit leaves the caret in the middle of the existing number instead of selecting it, so the first keystroke appends digits to the old value rather than replacing it. This is LCL's default behaviour, so every ported form changes behaviour silently.

what_it_does: In LCL, OnChange is the EDIT's change notification: it fires on every text change (keystroke, paste, spin-button step), not only when a committed value differs.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:199-203 fires FOnChange only inside `if FValue <> Clamped then` in SetValue, and the typing path never reaches SetValue -- UTF8KeyPress goes to InsertEditChar (SpinEdit.pas:419-425, :327-346) which only mutates FEditText, and the value is committed on Enter or focus-loss via CommitEdit (:317-325, called from DoExit at :456). So keystrokes fire nothing, and a keystroke that returns to the same number fires nothing either.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:869 `property OnChange` on TCustomEdit, raised from TCustomEdit.Change (:805) which TextChanged drives (:803); TCustomFloatSpinEdit hooks the same chain at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:35 (Change) and :70 (TextChanged).
user_impact: A ported handler that recomputes something live as the user types goes quiet until the user presses Enter or tabs away, and the app looks frozen. Because both sides compile and both fire *sometimes*, the difference is only found at run time.

what_it_does: Read/write dirty flag: True once the user has edited the field, resettable by the host after a save.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas has no Modified property or flag (published list :60-79; no field of that name in :11-23). `grep -rn 'property Modified'` over source/ returns nothing; the case-insensitive hits (tyControls.Controller.pas, FileSystem.pas, ShellListView.pas) are file timestamps and theme bookkeeping, unrelated.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:867 `property Modified: Boolean read GetModified write SetModified` (getter :791, setter :794); TCustomFloatSpinEdit deliberately manages it at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:38-42.
user_impact: A form cannot ask 'did the user touch this field?' to drive an enable-Save / prompt-on-close decision without shadowing the value itself.

what_it_does: Read/write caret position in the editor.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:28 has `FCaret: Integer` but it is protected, exposed nowhere in the public/published sections (:57-79). The sibling TTyEdit publishes it: `property CaretPos: Integer read FCaret write SetCaretPos` at tyControls.Edit.pas:164 -- so the pattern exists in the library and was not applied here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:861 `property CaretPos: TPoint read GetCaretPos write SetCaretPos` in TCustomEdit (getter :809, setter :816).
user_impact: A host cannot place the caret when it activates the field (e.g. 'put the cursor where the user clicked in the cell'), and cannot read it to drive its own hints. Note the type also differs from LCL's TPoint, so even once added it will be a porting break.

what_it_does: Placeholder text shown greyed in an empty field.
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 has no TextHint, and RenderTo draws only FEditText (SpinEdit.pas:398-399). The capability is fully built and used elsewhere: TTyEdit publishes `property TextHint: TCaption` at tyControls.Edit.pas:180, and the theme already ships a TextHint ink token (grep -ri 'TextHint' hits tyControls.DefaultTheme.pas and tyControls.BuiltinThemeData.pas) -- it is simply not wired to the spin edit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:879 `property TextHint: TTranslateString read GetTextHint write SetTextHint` in TCustomEdit's public block (getter :815, setter :824).
user_impact: No placeholder on a spin edit. Combined with the missing ValueEmpty, an 'unset' numeric field cannot be communicated at all -- even though the theme token for the hint ink already exists.

what_it_does: Three public virtual seams: clamp a proposed value, format a value into the field's text, and parse the field's text back into a value.
ours_evidence: The three jobs exist in tyControls.SpinEdit.pas but all are private/inlined and none is virtual: clamping is inline in SetValue (:189-198), formatting is `FEditText := IntToStr(FValue)` inside SyncBufferToValue (:264), parsing is `StrToIntDef(Trim(FEditText), FValue)` inside CommitEdit (:321). grep -ri 'ValueToStr'/'StrToValue' over source/ returns nothing; 'GetLimitedValue' matches only the comment at SpinEdit.pas:193 that cites LCL's implementation.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:74-76 `function GetLimitedValue(...): Double; virtual; function ValueToStr(...): string; virtual; function StrToValue(...): Double; virtual;` (public); implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/spinedit.inc:223, :235, :240; TCustomSpinEdit overrides GetLimitedValue at spin.pp:159.
user_impact: A descendant cannot change the display or parse rules -- hex, thousands separators, a unit suffix like '12 px', or a snap-to-multiple clamp -- without reimplementing the control. LCL descendants routinely override exactly these three.

what_it_does: Veto hook fired before the position moves: the handler sets AllowChange := False to refuse the step.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85 publishes OnChange (post-hoc TNotifyEvent, :75) and OnArrowClick (:80) only; Step (UpDown.pas:173-188) computes the clamped value and assigns FPosition with no pre-change consultation. grep -ri 'OnChanging' over source/ hits tyControls.Grid.pas, tyControls.TabSet.pas and tyControls.TabStrip.pas -- so the veto-event PATTERN is established in this library, just not on the up/down.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1916 TUDChangingEvent = procedure(Sender; var AllowChange: Boolean), declared :1998, published on TUpDown :2042; enforced in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:332-341 (CanChange) and gated at :371 `if not CanChange then Exit`.
user_impact: There is no way to refuse a step (e.g. 'cannot exceed the quantity in stock'): OnChange fires after the fact, so the handler must push the value back, which re-enters the setter and fires OnChange again. LCL's veto is one line.

what_it_does: The richer veto hook: besides AllowChange it hands the handler the PROPOSED NewValue and the Direction (updUp/updDown) of the pending step.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85 has no equivalent; OnArrowClick carries only the direction and fires BEFORE the clamp with no proposed value and no veto (UpDown.pas:20 signature, :179-182 dispatch), and the computed candidate `v` at :183 is never shown to anyone. grep -ri 'OnChanging' over source/ returns no TTyUpDown hit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1917 TUDChangingEventEx = procedure(Sender; var AllowChange: Boolean; NewValue: SmallInt; Direction: TUpDownDirection), declared :1999, published :2043; FCanChangePos/FCanChangeDir are computed at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:345-370 and passed in at :340.
user_impact: A handler cannot decide 'allow this specific value but not that one' -- it sees neither the target value nor (with veto power) the direction. Any ported OnChangingEx handler has nowhere to go.

what_it_does: When True (LCL's default) the Up/Down arrow keys step the value -- including arrows pressed inside the ASSOCIATED control, which LCL forwards via AssociateKeyDown.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:36 declares `TTyUpDown = class(TTyGraphicControl)`, and TTyGraphicControl publishes no TabStop/TabOrder and no OnKeyDown/OnKeyUp/OnKeyPress (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141; the Tier-B key events at Base.pas:232-238 exist only on TTyCustomControl). The control overrides no KeyDown either (protected section UpDown.pas:58-64 is GetStyleTypeKey/Paint/MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp/MouseLeave). grep -ri 'ArrowKeys' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1992 `property ArrowKeys: Boolean read FArrowKeys write SetArrowKeys default True` (published :2019); the forwarding hook is AssociateKeyDown at comctrls.pp:1970 and TCustomUpDown descends from TCustomControl (:1922), so it is focusable and publishes TabStop/TabOrder (:2036-2037).
user_impact: The up/down is mouse-only: it can never be reached by Tab and no key can drive it, so a keyboard-only user cannot change the value. This is structural (graphic vs windowed control), not a one-property fix.

what_it_does: Which side of the associated control the button pair snaps to: udLeft, udRight (default), udTop or udBottom.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85 has no AlignButton; the control has no notion of a partner to align against (see the Associate gap) and positions nothing -- its only layout properties are Align/Anchors (:81-82). grep -ri 'AlignButton' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1991 `property AlignButton: TUDAlignButton read FAlignButton write SetAlignButton default udRight` (published :2017), enum at :1911; implementation UpdateAlignButtonPos, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:~300-330 (the SetBounds at :328).
user_impact: Even once Associate exists, the buttons cannot be placed on the left of the field (common in RTL layouts and in some form styles); today the user must position them by hand and re-position on every resize.

what_it_does: Floor on the auto-repeat interval while a button is held (default 100 ms, clamped to >= 25), i.e. how fast a held button accelerates.
ours_evidence: Auto-repeat exists but its timings are compile-time constants: tyControls.UpDown.pas:89-91 `cRepeatDelayMs = 400` and `cRepeatFastMs = 60`, applied at :280 (initial delay) and :258 (fast phase); nothing published (:68-85). grep -ri 'MinRepeatInterval' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1997 `property MinRepeatInterval: Byte read FMinRepeatInterval write SetMinRepeatInterval default 100` (published :2029); default at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:226, clamp at :666-670, acceleration loop at :245-247.
user_impact: Hold-to-repeat speed is not tunable: a range of 0..10000 is unusable at 60 ms/step, and an accessibility setting that wants it slower cannot be honoured.

what_it_does: Whether the position written into the associated control's text is grouped with thousand separators (LCL default True).
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85 has no Thousands and never formats text at all -- it draws two arrow glyphs and a divider (Paint, UpDown.pas:306-369) and has no Associate to write into. grep -ri 'Thousands' over source/ hits tyControls.Calculator.pas, Chart.pas, ListView.Layout.pas, NumericEdit.pas and TreeView.pas -- so the library has grouping logic (TTyNumericEdit.UseThousands, NumericEdit.pas:54, over TyFormatNumber at :61) but nothing on the up/down.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2003 `property Thousands: Boolean read FThousands write SetThousands default True` (published :2038); default C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:229, setter :731, used by UpdateUpDownPositionText :254.
user_impact: Dependent on Associate, so it is currently moot -- but it means a ported .lfm carrying Thousands=False cannot stream, and once Associate lands the grouping default (True in LCL) will differ.

what_it_does: The direction-carrying click event: tells the handler which arrow was pressed, per step, including each auto-repeat tick.
ours_evidence: We have it under a different name and a different type: `TTyUpDownClickEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; AButton: TTyUpDownButton) of object` (tyControls.UpDown.pas:20) published as `OnArrowClick` (:80), with the enum `TTyUpDownButton = (udbPrev, udbNext)` (:11) instead of TUDBtnType = (btNext, btPrev). The rename is deliberate and documented at UpDown.pas:13-19 (our OnClick is the inherited plain TNotifyEvent from Base.pas:116). Firing order also differs: ours dispatches BEFORE the step and unconditionally (UpDown.pas:179-182, ahead of the clamp at :183).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1915 TUDClickEvent, :1914 TUDBtnType = (btNext, btPrev), property at :2000, published :2044; dispatch is AFTER the position moves and only if CanChange allowed it -- C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:371-374.
user_impact: The trap the header comment describes is real in both directions: ported code assigning UpDown1.OnClick compiles here against a TNotifyEvent and silently loses the direction, and code assigning the direction handler must be renamed to OnArrowClick with btNext/btPrev rewritten to udbNext/udbPrev. On top of that a handler that reads Position inside the event sees the OLD value here and the NEW value in LCL.

what_it_does: How a step that runs past a bound wraps: LCL carries the overshoot around modularly (Min + (pos+Inc-Max) - 1), so the remainder is preserved.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:121-135 TyUpDownClamp wraps to the OPPOSITE BOUND exactly: `if Result > AMax then Result := AMin else if Result < AMin then Result := AMax` (:127-128), discarding the overshoot. Called from Step at :183.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customupdown.inc:354-355 `if Wrap then FCanChangePos := Max + (FCanChangePos - Increment - Min) + 1` and :365-366 `FCanChangePos := Min + (FCanChangePos + Increment - Max) - 1`; property at C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2005.
user_impact: Identical for Increment=1 (the common case) and different for every larger increment: on Min=0/Max=10/Increment=3 from 9, LCL lands on 1 and we land on 0. A stepper cycling non-unit increments drifts onto the wrong values, and only after several wraps -- the kind of thing that looks like an off-by-one in the app.

what_it_does: LCL types the range and value as SmallInt (-32768..32767); ours are Integer.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:39 `FMin, FMax, FPosition, FIncrement: Integer`, published as Integer at :69-71.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1995 `property Max: SmallInt`, :1996 `property Min: SmallInt`, :2002 `property Position: SmallInt` (fields at :1930,:1932,:1942; TUDChangingEventEx also passes NewValue as SmallInt at :1917).
user_impact: Ours is the wider type, so it accepts values LCL cannot hold -- fine going forward, but ported code that declares `var p: SmallInt; p := UpDown1.Position;` now needs a range check, and code that relied on the SmallInt ceiling behaves differently.

what_it_does: Stacks the two halves vertically (default) or side by side.
ours_evidence: tyControls.UpDown.pas:9 `TTyUpDownOrientation = (udoVertical, udoHorizontal)`, published at :73 with default udoVertical. Same two states as LCL and the same default, but the type and every enum identifier differ (udo* vs ud*), and the declaration order is reversed.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1912 `TUDOrientation = (udHorizontal, udVertical)`, property at :2001 `default udVertical` (published :2030).
user_impact: `UpDown1.Orientation := udHorizontal` does not compile, and a .lfm carrying Orientation=udHorizontal will not stream. Pure porting friction -- behaviour matches.

what_it_does: Per-instance switch between a flat and a raised/3D button pair.
ours_evidence: No such property (tyControls.UpDown.pas:68-85); grep -ri 'Flat' finds no `property Flat` in source/. The CONCEPT is covered, but by the theme rather than an instance property: the control resolves its own typeKey 'TyUpDown' (UpDown.pas:160-166) and the frame comes from DrawFrame + the resolved style (Paint, :339-340), where render-style bevel3d/inset3d and border tokens produce raised or flat (tyControls.Base.pas:801-822 TyApplyRenderStyle, :713-722 TyDrawBevelBorder); per-instance deviation goes through StyleClass/StyleOverride (Base.pas:135-139).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2004 `property Flat: Boolean read GetFlat write SetFlat default False` (published :2039); getter/setter GetFlat/SetFlat at :1950,:1961.
user_impact: Only a porting break, and arguably correct by this library's rules (visual values belong to the theme): `UpDown1.Flat := True` must be rewritten as a StyleClass or StyleOverride. Worth listing so the porting note exists.

what_it_does: Horizontal (tilt) wheel events; on TCustomUpDown they are wired to real behaviour -- DoMouseWheelLeft/Right are overridden so a tilt steps the value.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Base.pas:122-125 publishes OnMouseWheel/OnMouseWheelUp/OnMouseWheelDown only (both base classes), and TTyUpDown adds none (UpDown.pas:68-85); it also overrides no wheel handler at all (protected section :58-64). grep -ri 'OnMouseWheelHorz', 'OnMouseWheelLeft', 'OnMouseWheelRight' and 'DoMouseWheelHorz' over source/ all returned nothing -- absent library-wide.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2056-2058 published on TUpDown; the behaviour is the DoMouseWheelLeft/DoMouseWheelRight overrides at :1978-1979.
user_impact: A horizontal up/down cannot be driven by a tilt wheel (LCL's does), and ported handlers for the three events do not exist here.

what_it_does: The range ceiling a freshly dropped track bar starts with.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:77 `property Max: Integer read FMax write SetMax default 100`, set in the constructor at :134.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2784 `property Max: Integer read FMax write SetMax default 10`; constructor C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:56 `FMax := 10`.
user_impact: A .lfm ported from Lazarus that left Max at its default (so the value is not stored) silently becomes a 0..100 bar here, and every stored Position now means a tenth of what it used to -- the thumb lands near the left end instead of where the designer put it.

what_it_does: How far PgUp/PgDn moves the value by default.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:85 `property PageSize: Integer read FPageSize write SetPageSize default 10`, constructor :138; used by VK_PRIOR/VK_NEXT at :392-401.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2787 `property PageSize: Integer read FPageSize write SetPageSize default 2`; constructor C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:59 `FPageSize := 2`.
user_impact: Paging jumps five times as far as on the native control, and on the LCL default range (0..10) a page in LCL is a fifth of the range while ours would be the whole range. Not stored in a ported .lfm, so it changes behaviour invisibly.

what_it_does: Horizontal or vertical track.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:8 `TTyTrackOrientation = (toHorizontal, toVertical)`, published at :79 with default toHorizontal. Same two states and same default; type name and both enum identifiers differ.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2728 `TTrackBarOrientation = (trHorizontal, trVertical)`, property at :2786 default trHorizontal (republished :2820).
user_impact: `TrackBar1.Orientation := trVertical` does not compile and a ported .lfm carrying Orientation=trVertical will not stream. Note the type is also named TTyTrackOrientation, not TTyTrackBarOrientation, so it does not even follow the library's own naming.

what_it_does: LCL's SetOrientation swaps Width and Height (outside csLoading) so switching to vertical turns a wide short bar into a narrow tall one.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:331-336 SetOrientation only stores the value and calls Invalidate -- no bounds change. The constructor ships Width=160 / Height=TyDensityHeight(...,24) (:151-152), so a vertical bar stays 160 wide and ~24 tall: the groove now runs down 24 px and the thumb has almost no travel (MainLen uses ClientHeight for vertical, :176-177).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:128-148 -- `OldWidth:=Width; OldHeight:=Height; ... SetBounds(Left,Top,OldHeight,OldWidth);` guarded by `if not (csLoading in ComponentState)`, precisely so a .lfm's own consistent size is respected while a run-time switch is fixed up.
user_impact: Setting Orientation to vertical at run time (or in the designer, which is the same code path) produces a visually broken control -- a 160x24 'vertical' bar whose thumb can barely move -- instead of a tall slider. The user has to know to swap the bounds by hand.

what_it_does: Where the numeric scale is drawn relative to the groove: trLeft, trRight, trTop (default) or trBottom.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 has no ScalePos. The nearest thing is ShowValue (:88), which draws ONE number (the current value) in a reserved strip whose side is hard-coded -- right for horizontal, bottom for vertical (RenderTo :575-585, geometry :513-516) -- not a scale, and not positionable. grep -ri 'ScalePos' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2731 TTrackBarScalePos = (trLeft, trRight, trTop, trBottom) and :2790 `property ScalePos: TTrackBarScalePos ... default trTop` (republished :2828); default C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:62, setter :381.
user_impact: No scale annotation at all, and the single value readout we do have cannot be moved to the other side. A ported .lfm carrying ScalePos will not stream.

what_it_does: Lets the control size its cross-axis to what the groove, ticks and scale actually need (TCustomTrackBar overrides ShouldAutoAdjust so only the cross axis is auto-sized).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 does not publish AutoSize, and neither base class does (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 and :196-246). The capability is available and used widely elsewhere -- `property AutoSize` is published by ~35 units including tyControls.Button.pas, tyControls.TyLabel.pas and tyControls.CheckBox.pas -- so this is unwired here, not missing from the library.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2781 `property AutoSize;` published on TCustomTrackBar itself (unusual -- it is deliberate); the axis logic is ShouldAutoAdjust at :2775, implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/trackbar.inc:95-107.
user_impact: Bites exactly where this codebase has been bitten before: a skin that changes tick length, padding or the readout font makes a fixed Height=24 track bar clip its ticks or its value text, and there is no AutoSize to absorb it.

member: DragCursor / DragMode / OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnEndDrag / OnStartDrag / OnStartDock
what_it_does: LCL drag-and-drop participation: dmAutomatic starts a drag, the events let the control be a drag source or drop target, DragCursor picks the feedback cursor.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TrackBar.pas:75-95 publishes none of them, and neither base class does (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-246). The plumbing works fine in this library when published -- TTyMemo publishes DragCursor/DragKind/DragMode/OnDragDrop/OnDragOver/OnEndDrag/OnStartDrag at tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574 -- so this is an unpublished-surface gap, not a capability gap.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2811-2812 (DragCursor, DragMode) and :2843-2846, :2863 (OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDrag) on TTrackBar; TCustomProgressBar's sibling list also carries OnStartDock (:1906).
user_impact: A track bar cannot be a drop target (drop a colour or a file on the slider) and cannot be dragged, so any ported form that wired those events fails to compile -- even though the same events already work on TTyMemo.

what_it_does: Horizontal (tilt) wheel notifications, the natural gesture for a horizontal slider.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Base.pas:122-125 publishes OnMouseWheel/Up/Down only; TTyTrackBar adds none (TrackBar.pas:75-95) and DoMouseWheel handles the vertical wheel only (:469-481). grep -ri 'OnMouseWheelHorz'/'Left'/'Right' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2856-2858 published on TTrackBar.
user_impact: Tilt-wheel and horizontal-scroll trackpad gestures over a horizontal slider are unobservable and cannot be made to move it; ported handlers do not compile.

what_it_does: The orientation a freshly created scroll bar starts with.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBar.pas:90 `property Kind: TTyScrollBarKind read FKind write SetKind default sbVertical`, constructor :193 `FKind := sbVertical` (and the default bounds match: Width = --scrollbar-size, Height = 160, :212-213).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:105 `property Kind: TScrollBarKind read FKind write SetKind default sbHorizontal`; constructor C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollbar.inc:29 `FKind := sbHorizontal`.
user_impact: A .lfm ported from Lazarus that left Kind at LCL's default stores nothing, so the bar arrives here as VERTICAL while keeping the stored wide-and-short bounds -- a visibly wrong control. The reverse is true for any .lfm written here and read there.

member: DragCursor / DragKind / DragMode / OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnEndDrag / OnStartDrag
what_it_does: Drag-and-drop / docking participation for the scroll bar.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBar.pas:84-107 publishes none; the base class does not either (tyControls.Base.pas:196-246). Published successfully elsewhere in the library on TTyMemo (tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574), so the mechanism is available and simply not exposed here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:128-130 (DragCursor, DragKind, DragMode) and :149-152, :158 (OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDrag) on TScrollBar.
user_impact: Ported forms that wired drag events on a stand-alone scroll bar do not compile; the bar cannot act as a drop target.

member: DragCursor / DragKind / DragMode / OnDragDrop / OnDragOver / OnEndDrag / OnStartDrag / OnStartDock
what_it_does: Drag-and-drop / docking participation for the progress bar.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:43-60 publishes none, and TTyGraphicControl does not either (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141). Available in this library where published -- TTyMemo, tyControls.Memo.pas:566-574.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1869-1871 (DragCursor, DragKind, DragMode) and :1893-1895, :1906-1907 (OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnEndDrag, OnStartDock, OnStartDrag) on TProgressBar.
user_impact: Ported forms wiring these events do not compile; a progress bar cannot be a drop target (drop a file on the bar to start a transfer).

what_it_does: LCL's progress bar is a TWinControl, so it can take the focus and publishes the tab-order and focus events.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ProgressBar.pas:10 declares `TTyProgressBar = class(TTyGraphicControl)`; TTyGraphicControl is a TGraphicControl (tyControls.Base.pas:68) and therefore publishes no TabStop, TabOrder, OnEnter, OnExit or key events -- those live only on TTyCustomControl (Base.pas:210-211, :237-238). Not fixable by publishing: a graphic control has no handle to focus.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:1814 `TCustomProgressBar = class(TWinControl)`; published TabOrder :1887, TabStop :1888, OnEnter :1896, OnExit :1897.
user_impact: Low in practice -- almost nobody tabs to a progress bar -- but a ported .lfm carrying TabStop/TabOrder on a TProgressBar will not stream, and an accessibility pass that wants the bar in the focus order to announce progress cannot have it.

what_it_does: Sizes the edit's height to its font (LCL edits default AutoSize to True).
ours_evidence: tyControls.SpinEdit.pas:60-79 does not publish AutoSize and neither base class does (tyControls.Base.pas:196-246); the height is fixed in the constructor as `Height := TyDensityHeight(ActiveController, 28)` (SpinEdit.pas:128). ~35 other units in source/ do publish AutoSize (tyControls.Button.pas, tyControls.TyLabel.pas, ...), so the capability is present and unwired here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:178 `property AutoSize;` published on TSpinEdit; TCustomEdit re-declares it `default True` at C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:858.
user_impact: The same skin-variance trap this codebase already recorded: a theme with a larger font or bigger vertical padding clips the digits in a spin edit fixed at density-28, and there is no AutoSize to grow it. LCL's default is True, so ported forms lose behaviour silently.

what_it_does: Horizontal (tilt) wheel notifications on the spin edit.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Base.pas:122-125 publishes OnMouseWheel/Up/Down only; TTySpinEdit adds none (SpinEdit.pas:60-79) and its DoMouseWheel handles the vertical wheel only (:462-479). grep -ri 'OnMouseWheelHorz'/'Left'/'Right' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/spin.pp:216-218 published on TSpinEdit (and :136-138 on TFloatSpinEdit).
user_impact: Ported handlers do not compile; tilt-wheel gestures over the field are unobservable.

our_class: TTyDial, TTyLevelMeter, TTyMeter (also TTyGauge / TTyActivityIndicator / TTyAnalogClock — same bases)
what_it_does: Published TAntialiasingMode (amDontCare / amOn / amOff), default amDontCare; the one and only published member the whole industrial family adds. Its setter calls GraphicChanged, which Invalidates, so the user can force smooth or deliberately hard-edged rendering of the instrument's ink at run time and in the OI.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "antialiasingmode|amDontCare|amOn" over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned nothing. The only antialias-related code in the library is unconditional: tyControls.Painter.pas:473 (ABmp.FontQuality := fqFineAntialiasing) and the Canvas2D stroke paths in tyControls.Dial.pas:270-298, tyControls.Meter.pas:226-251, tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:308-328 — BGRA Canvas2D antialiases by default (bgracanvas2d.pas:310 exposes an `antialiasing: boolean` we never touch). Published blocks tyControls.Dial.pas:58-74, tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:65-80, tyControls.Meter.pas:51-66 and the bases tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 / 196-246 declare no such property.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/industrialbase.pp:22-24 (published AntiAliasingMode ... default amDontCare); setter at :43-48 calling GraphicChanged (:37-41).
user_impact: A .lfm/.dfm ported from an industrial control that carries AntiAliasingMode=amOff raises an unknown-property error on load, and on classic / pixel-exact skins there is no way to ask for hard-edged needles, segments or tick marks — every ty instrument is permanently antialiased.

what_it_does: TNotifyEvent fired as part of the control's paint, letting user code draw extra ink on the control's Canvas (a red-line limit mark, a unit label, a custom scale) without subclassing.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property OnPaint;" over source/ returned nothing; grep -rin OnPaint finds only two DIFFERENT hooks on other controls with a different signature — TTyPaintPanel.OnPaintSurface (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42, TTyPaintSurfaceEvent = painter + rect) and TTyPreviewBox.OnPaintPreview (tyControls.PreviewBox.pas:94). Neither base publishes OnPaint (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, 196-246) and none of the three instruments does (tyControls.Dial.pas:58-74, tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:65-80, tyControls.Meter.pas:51-66).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:90 (`property OnPaint;` on the concrete family member); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2457 (TGraphicControl.OnPaint: TNotifyEvent).
user_impact: Code ported from an LCL instrument that assigns Dial1.OnPaint := ... fails to compile, and a user who wants to overlay anything on a gauge/meter must descend a new class. Note the library's own trap: any such handler must run AFTER TTyPainter.EndPaint or the BGRA blit overwrites the GDI ink.

what_it_does: TDragDropEvent fired when a dragged object is dropped on the control — the control acting as a drag TARGET (e.g. dropping a signal/channel onto a meter).
ours_evidence: grep -rn OnDragDrop over source/ returns exactly ONE hit: tyControls.Memo.pas:571 (`property OnDragDrop;`, alongside DragCursor/DragKind/DragMode at :566-568). So the plain LCL passthrough is proven to work in this library but is wired to a single control; the shared bases (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, 196-246) and all three instruments (tyControls.Dial.pas:58-74, tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:65-80, tyControls.Meter.pas:51-66) publish nothing of the drag surface — and without DragMode published either, dmAutomatic cannot be set from the OI at all.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:76 (`property OnDragDrop;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1585 (TControl.OnDragDrop: TDragDropEvent).
user_impact: An instrument cannot be made a drop target from the designer; a ported form with OnDragDrop on a gauge/meter/knob fails to stream.

what_it_does: TDragOverEvent fired while a drag passes over the control, where the handler sets Accept — the only way to give accept/reject feedback before a drop.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property OnDragOver" over source/ returns tyControls.Memo.pas:572 (LCL passthrough) and tyControls.TreeView.pas:658 (a DIFFERENT, tree-specific TTyTreeDragOverEvent for internal node drags, not the LCL drag protocol). Nothing on the bases or the three instruments (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141/196-246; tyControls.Dial.pas:58-74; tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:65-80; tyControls.Meter.pas:51-66).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:77 (`property OnDragOver;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1586 (TControl.OnDragOver: TDragOverEvent).
user_impact: No hover-accept feedback is possible on an instrument, so even a code-driven BeginDrag cannot be validated per target.

what_it_does: TEndDragEvent fired when a drag that STARTED on this control finishes (dropped or cancelled) — the cleanup half of the drag lifecycle.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property OnEndDrag" over source/ returns only tyControls.Memo.pas:573; tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas:75 is a comment mentioning OnEndDrag, not a property. Absent on both bases (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, 196-246) and on all three instruments.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:78 (`property OnEndDrag;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1588 (TControl.OnEndDrag: TEndDragEvent).
user_impact: A drag begun on an instrument gives no completion notification, so state started in OnStartDrag can never be torn down; ported forms with the handler fail to load.

what_it_does: TStartDragEvent fired when a drag begins on the control, where the handler may substitute the TDragObject — the control acting as a drag SOURCE (e.g. dragging a knob's value onto a chart).
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property OnStartDrag" over source/ returns only tyControls.Memo.pas:574. Not on the bases (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, 196-246) nor on tyControls.Dial.pas:58-74 / tyControls.LevelMeter.pas:65-80 / tyControls.Meter.pas:51-66.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:92 (`property OnStartDrag;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1601 (TControl.OnStartDrag: TStartDragEvent).
user_impact: Instruments cannot act as drag sources from the designer; on TTyDial it also collides with its own left-button drag-to-set gesture, which is exactly the decision a user needs OnStartDrag+DragMode to arbitrate.

our_class: TTyDial, TTyLevelMeter, TTyMeter (base: TTyGraphicControl / TTyCustomControl — affects every ty control)
what_it_does: TMouseWheelEvent for HORIZONTAL wheel/trackpad input (WM_MOUSEHWHEEL, two-finger sideways swipe), with WheelDelta and a Handled flag.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "OnMouseWheelHorz|OnMouseWheelLeft|OnMouseWheelRight|hwheel|WheelHorz" over the WHOLE source/ directory returned nothing — the library has no horizontal-wheel surface anywhere. Both bases publish only the vertical trio OnMouseWheel / OnMouseWheelUp / OnMouseWheelDown (tyControls.Base.pas:121-123 and 220-222).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:87 (`property OnMouseWheelHorz;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1597 (TControl.OnMouseWheelHorz: TMouseWheelEvent).
user_impact: A trackpad sideways swipe or tilt-wheel over any ty control reaches no handler, so a horizontal LevelMeter cannot be scrubbed the way an LCL instrument can, and any ported .lfm carrying the handler fails to stream. LCL already dispatches the message — only the publish is missing.

our_class: TTyDial, TTyLevelMeter, TTyMeter (base: TTyGraphicControl / TTyCustomControl — affects every ty control)
what_it_does: TMouseWheelUpDownEvent — the pre-decoded 'wheel went left' half of horizontal wheel input, the sideways twin of OnMouseWheelUp.
ours_evidence: grep -rin OnMouseWheelLeft over source/ returned nothing (same whole-tree grep as OnMouseWheelHorz). Bases publish only OnMouseWheelUp/Down (tyControls.Base.pas:122-123, 221-222).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:88 (`property OnMouseWheelLeft;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1598 (TControl.OnMouseWheelLeft: TMouseWheelUpDownEvent).
user_impact: Users who wire the simple directional form (rather than decoding WheelDelta themselves) have no equivalent on any ty instrument; ported handlers fail to stream.

our_class: TTyDial, TTyLevelMeter, TTyMeter (base: TTyGraphicControl / TTyCustomControl — affects every ty control)
what_it_does: TMouseWheelUpDownEvent — the 'wheel went right' half of horizontal wheel input.
ours_evidence: grep -rin OnMouseWheelRight over source/ returned nothing. Bases publish only the vertical pair (tyControls.Base.pas:122-123, 221-222).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:89 (`property OnMouseWheelRight;`); declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1599 (TControl.OnMouseWheelRight: TMouseWheelUpDownEvent).
user_impact: Same as OnMouseWheelLeft: no sideways wheel handling on any ty control, and a porting break for forms that used it.

our_class: TTyDial, TTyLevelMeter, TTyMeter (and every other ty instrument)
what_it_does: The control's background colour, published on the concrete industrial control and settable in the OI or a .lfm.
ours_evidence: No ty control publishes a background Color: grep -rn "property Color" over source/ returns only tyControls.Chart.pas:237 (a data-series colour) and tyControls.Dialogs.Color.pas:119 (the colour a dialog picked) — neither is a control background. The themed equivalent DOES exist and is what a porter must use instead: per-instance StyleOverride and StyleClass (tyControls.Base.pas:135-139 / 240-245, e.g. StyleOverride='background: #RRGGBB;'), plus the control's own theme key ('TyDial' — tyControls.Dial.pas:121-126). Reported as name-mismatch, not absent, for that reason.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:60 (`property Color;` on the concrete family member; TControl.Color).
user_impact: A converted .lfm/.dfm containing `Color = clSkyBlue` on an instrument raises an unknown-property error at load; there is no per-instance colour under the name the porter (and the OI-trained user) looks for. Deliberate under the theme-token hard rule, so the fix is documentation/porting notes, not a published Color.

their_class: TIndustrialBase (family contract; note TGauge itself is absent from this LCL — see coverage_note)
what_it_does: The industrial family removes csSetCaption in its constructor, so a family instrument NEVER acquires its Name as caption text and publishes no Caption at all (TArrow's published list has none) — an instrument shows values, not a caption.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Gauge.pas:68 publishes `property Caption;`, and grep -n Caption tyControls.Gauge.pas returns ONLY that line — Paint (tyControls.Gauge.pas:325-348 → DrawLinear :270-281 / DrawArc :283-323 / DrawValueText :261-268) never reads Caption; it draws Format(FValueFormat,[FValue]) instead. grep -rn csSetCaption over the whole source/ returned nothing, so csSetCaption is never stripped and a designer drop auto-assigns Caption='TyGauge1'.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/industrialbase.pp:34 (`ControlStyle := ControlStyle - [csSetCaption];` in TIndustrialBase.Create); C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:53-93 published block contains no Caption.
user_impact: The OI shows Caption on a TTyGauge and typing into it changes nothing (a dead published property, the same class of bug as the recent ColorButton 'paint the Caption it has published all along' fix), while the auto-assigned 'TyGauge1' is silently written into every .lfm. Either paint it as the instrument's label or unpublish it and strip csSetCaption like the family does.

what_it_does: A whole child-layout sub-object on every TWinControl container: Layout (cclNone/cclLeftToRightThenTopToBottom/...), ControlsPerLine, EnlargeHorizontal/EnlargeVertical, ShrinkHorizontal/ShrinkVertical, LeftRightSpacing, TopBottomSpacing, HorizontalSpacing, VerticalSpacing. It turns a plain panel into an auto-arranging grid/flow of children without any Align/Anchor work.
ours_evidence: grep -ril "childsizing" over D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returned NOTHING — the item class TControlChildSizing is never referenced, never republished, and there is no equivalent (TTyGridPanel's ColumnSizes/RowSizes is a fixed-track grid of cell containers, not a child-spacing/auto-arrange policy; TTyRelativePanel.Spacing is a sibling gap for rule-based positioning only, tyControls.RelativePanel.pas:134).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2329 (TWinControl.ChildSizing, public), class declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1952 with published members at 1988-2001; republished on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1189 and on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:233.
user_impact: A ported .lfm that used Panel1.ChildSizing (a very common way to lay out a row of buttons or a form-field column in Lazarus) does not load/compile, and there is no substitute: the user must hand-place or hand-anchor every child. Inherited by TTyScrollBox/TTyPaintPanel/TTyGridPanel/TTyRelativePanel too.

what_it_does: Owner-draw hook fired from Paint with the control's Canvas ready, so a host can draw on top of (or instead of) the panel's own rendering.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "OnPaint" over source/ finds ONLY differently-named/differently-typed hooks: tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42 OnPaintSurface, tyControls.PreviewBox.pas:94 OnPaintPreview, tyControls.TreeView.pas:229 OnPaintText. Worse than plain absence: TCustomControl.OnPaint is PUBLIC (C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2486) so `Panel.OnPaint := @H` compiles, but TTyPanel.Paint (tyControls.Panel.pas:101-117) never calls inherited Paint, so the handler is never invoked.
theirs_evidence: Published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1243; declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2486; fired by TCustomControl.Paint at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customcontrol.inc:57-60.
user_impact: Assigning OnPaint on a TTyPanel (or any TTyPanel descendant — ScrollBox, GridPanel, RelativePanel) silently does nothing: no compile error, no runtime error, no drawing. Only TTyPaintPanel offers a (different) surface hook.

what_it_does: On LCL the panel caption IS TControl.Caption/Text: it is routed through GetText/SetText, csSetCaption is set, and RealSetText is overridden to Invalidate, so anything that writes the control's text (a TAction, SetTextBuf, a TControl-typed reference) updates what is painted.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Panel.pas:26 declares a NEW field-backed property `Caption: TCaption read FCaption write SetCaption` that shadows TControl.Caption; SetCaption (tyControls.Panel.pas:48-53) never calls inherited RealSetText/SetText, and RealSetText is not overridden anywhere in the unit. grep over source/ shows no TTyPanel Text/RealSetText wiring.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:29 (csSetCaption in ControlStyle), :237-244 (RealSetText override -> Invalidate), :158-186 (Paint reads Caption); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1188.
user_impact: Two concrete breakages: (1) `TControl(Panel).Caption := 'x'` or `Panel.Text := 'x'` sets the LCL text and paints nothing; (2) the base class publishes Action (tyControls.Base.pas:231) and TControl.ActionChange assigns `Caption := NewAction.Caption` statically bound to TControl.Caption (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/control.inc:2079-2080), so attaching an Action to a TTyPanel never shows its caption.

what_it_does: Makes the panel shrink/grow to fit its content (its caption and/or its children); TCustomPanel additionally opts into csAutoSize0x0 so an empty panel can collapse.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "AutoSize" over source/ shows the capability is published on ~35 other ty controls (e.g. tyControls.TyLabel.pas, tyControls.Button.pas, tyControls.Tag.pas) but NOT on TTyPanel — published list is tyControls.Panel.pas:25-32 (Caption, Alignment, Align, Anchors, StyleClass, Controller) plus tyControls.Base.pas:196-246. No CalculatePreferredSize override exists in tyControls.Panel.pas, so enabling AutoSize from code would collapse the panel to 0x0.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1789 (TControl.AutoSize), published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1179; csAutoSize0x0 set at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:30.
user_impact: A self-sizing panel (toolbar strip, caption band, wrapper that hugs its child) is not expressible; the user must compute and set Height/Width by hand and re-do it on every theme/DPI/skin change — exactly the case the codebase's own skin-variance rule warns about.

what_it_does: Right-to-left support: BiDiMode flips the caption alignment (BidiFlipAlignment) and sets TS.RightToLeft when drawing, and ParentBiDiMode inherits the mode from the parent.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "bidimode" over source/ returns exactly ONE hit, a comment declaring it out of scope: tyControls.Memo.pas:557 "Alignment/CharCase/BidiMode are out of scope". Nothing publishes or honours it; TTyPanel's caption draw (tyControls.Panel.pas:79-81) passes FAlignment through unflipped and TTyPainter.DrawText has no RTL parameter (tyControls.Painter.pas:109).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1834-1835 (BiDiMode / ParentBiDiMode), published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1185 and :1203; consumed in TCustomPanel.Paint at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:161-163.
user_impact: No Arabic/Hebrew layout on any container in the library: captions stay left/centre-aligned in the LTR sense and a ported RTL form loses its mirroring. Affects every TTyPanel descendant.

what_it_does: Wraps a long panel caption over several lines instead of keeping it on one line (TS.Wordbreak / TS.SingleLine).
ours_evidence: grep -rin "wordwrap" over source/ shows the capability EXISTS and is wired elsewhere — tyControls.TyLabel.pas, tyControls.Memo.pas, tyControls.HtmlLabel.pas, tyControls.Grid.pas, tyControls.Painter.pas — and TTyPainter.DrawText takes AMultiLine + ALineHeightLogical (tyControls.Painter.pas:109). TTyPanel.RenderTo (tyControls.Panel.pas:79-81) omits both arguments, so AMultiLine defaults to False, and it passes AEllipsis=True, so a long caption is clipped with an ellipsis instead.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1155 (WordWrap default false), published as Wordwrap on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1216; applied at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:168-169.
user_impact: A panel used as a caption/banner cannot show a two-line title — the text is silently ellipsised. Capability built (painter + labels), never wired to the panel.
