what_it_does: Positions the caption at the top, centre or bottom of the panel (taAlignTop/taAlignBottom/taVerticalCenter, default taVerticalCenter).
ours_evidence: grep -ril "verticalalignment" over source/ returned NOTHING. TTyPanel publishes only the horizontal Alignment (tyControls.Panel.pas:27) and hardcodes tlCenter in the caption draw (tyControls.Panel.pas:81).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1154 (VerticalAlignment, default taVerticalCenter), published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1214; mapped to TTextStyle.Layout at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:147 and :164.
user_impact: A caption cannot be pinned to the top or bottom of a panel — e.g. a section header band with the label at the top and children below is not expressible without abandoning the panel's own Caption.

what_it_does: Interprets '&' in the caption as a mnemonic marker: the '&' is removed and the next character is underlined (TTextStyle.ShowPrefix).
ours_evidence: grep -ril "accel|mnemonic" over source/ shows the whole facility exists — tyControls.Accel.pas (TyParseMnemonic / TyAccelShowing / TyAccelGatePos / TyIsAccelKey) — and is wired into ~10 controls, e.g. tyControls.Button.pas:656,697,701 which calls TyParseMnemonic then passes TyAccelGatePos(mp) to DrawText. TTyPanel.RenderTo (tyControls.Panel.pas:79-81) passes NO AMnemonicPos (defaults to 0, tyControls.Painter.pas:109) and never strips '&'.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1153 (ShowAccelChar default false), published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1209; applied at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:170.
user_impact: A panel Caption of 'File &Options' paints the ampersand literally, and there is no Alt-key underline on containers/group captions — inconsistent with every other ty control that already does mnemonics.

what_it_does: A SECOND, inner 3D frame drawn inside BorderWidth, independently raised or lowered from the outer one — the classic double-bevel panel look.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "bevel" over source/ finds tyControls.Bevel.pas (a separate standalone TTyBevel decoration control), tyControls.Base.pas:713-722 TyDrawBevelBorder and :801-822 TyApplyRenderStyle (ONE bevel, derived from the single border token), plus theme data. There is no second/inner frame anywhere: TTyPanel.RenderTo draws exactly one DrawFrame (tyControls.Panel.pas:71).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1161 (BevelInner default bvNone); painted as a second PaintBevel pass after the BorderWidth inset at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:154-157 and accounted for in AdjustClientRect at :198-203.
user_impact: The Win9x/classic double-bevel panel (raised outer + lowered inner) cannot be reproduced, even via the theme — the render-style token expands to a single bevel only. Blocks faithful classic-era skins for panels.

what_it_does: Per-instance 3D framing of the panel: raised/lowered/space/none, its thickness, and an explicit bevel colour (clDefault = derive from the system face).
ours_evidence: Equivalent exists but under theme names, not these: tyControls.Base.pas:801-822 TyApplyRenderStyle expands `render-style: bevel3d|inset3d` into border-style tbsOutset/tbsInset + border-width 2 + a border-colour derived from the background face, drawn by TyDrawBevelBorder (tyControls.Base.pas:713-722); per instance it is reachable only as StyleOverride text (tyControls.Base.pas:244), e.g. 'render-style: inset3d'. grep -rin "bevelouter|bevelwidth|bevelcolor" over source/ returned NOTHING.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1160 (BevelColor default clDefault), :1162 (BevelOuter default bvRaised), :1163 (BevelWidth default 1); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1181-1184.
user_impact: Porting break with a default change: a stock TPanel is bvRaised out of the box, a TTyPanel is flat, and the OI/.lfm names differ (BevelOuter vs StyleOverride/render-style), so every ported panel needs manual translation and the raised look must be re-authored as CSS.

what_it_does: Per-instance inner margin between the container's edge (or bevel) and its child controls — subtracted in AdjustClientRect so aligned children keep clear of the frame.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "borderwidth" over source/ returns ~50 files but every hit is the THEME token (S.BorderWidth / --border-width in tyControls.StyleModel.pas, tyControls.Painter.pas, DrawFrame in tyControls.Base.pas:844) — i.e. the stroke thickness, not a child inset. The only per-instance inner-inset property in the whole library is TTyGridCell.Padding (tyControls.GridPanel.pas:60); TTyPanel has none and does not override AdjustClientRect at all (tyControls.Panel.pas has no AdjustClientRect).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2324 (TWinControl.BorderWidth default 0), published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1186; consumed at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:155 and :197-203.
user_impact: Children of a TTyPanel sit flush against the frame; the only way to inset them is the theme's container padding (which moves every panel in the app) or manual per-child BorderSpacing. A single 'this panel has an 8px inner gutter' is not expressible per instance.

what_it_does: Published, designer/stream-settable CLIENT size: setting it sizes the control so its client area is exactly that big (frame/bevel/scrollbar excluded), and it is what a .lfm records for containers.
ours_evidence: Not published on any ty control: grep -rn "property ClientWidth|property ClientHeight" over source/ returns nothing (all ~55 ClientWidth/ClientHeight hits are internal reads such as tyControls.Panel.pas:111). Base published lists are tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 and :196-246 — neither includes them.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1796 and :1799 (TControl.ClientHeight/ClientWidth, public with stored guards); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1190-1191 and on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:234-235.
user_impact: A .lfm that stores ClientWidth/ClientHeight for a panel or scroll box (what the Lazarus designer writes when the frame is non-zero) will not stream onto a ty container, and the user cannot dimension a container by its usable interior.

what_it_does: LCL drag-and-drop configuration: dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down without any code, DragCursor is the cursor shown while dragging, DragKind selects drag vs dock.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "dragmode|dragcursor|dragkind" over source/ shows they are published on exactly ONE control, TTyMemo (tyControls.Memo.pas:566-568); the shared base classes publish none (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-246) and TTyPanel does not (tyControls.Panel.pas:25-32).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1570-1572 (DragCursor default crDrag, DragKind default dkDrag, DragMode default dmManual); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1196-1198, on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:238-241, on TPaintBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:489-491.
user_impact: Containers cannot participate in LCL drag-and-drop from the designer; a ported form that dragged panels around loses the behaviour. The capability is proven to work in this library (TTyMemo publishes it) — it is simply not wired to the containers.

what_it_does: The four events that make a control a drag SOURCE and a drop TARGET: accept/reject feedback while a payload hovers, handle the drop, and start/finish notifications.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "ondragover|ondragdrop|onstartdrag|onenddrag" over source/ returned NOTHING — no ty control publishes any of them, and neither base class does (tyControls.Base.pas:115-134, :212-239).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1585-1586 (OnDragDrop/OnDragOver), :1588 (OnEndDrag), :1601 (OnStartDrag); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1224-1227.
user_impact: No container in the library can be a drop target. This also strands the library's own feature: TTyScrollPanel.AutoPanTo is documented to be called "from a drag handler (OnDragOver, a rubber-band MouseMove)" (tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas:70-74), but no OnDragOver exists on any ty container to call it from.

member: DockSite / UseDockManager / OnDockDrop / OnDockOver / OnUnDock / OnStartDock / OnEndDock / OnGetSiteInfo / OnGetDockCaption
what_it_does: The docking surface: a panel can be declared a dock site, given a dock manager, and notified when a client docks/undocks; OnGetSiteInfo negotiates the drop and GetDefaultDockCaption/OnGetDockCaption supplies the tab caption.
ours_evidence: grep -ril "docksite|usedockmanager|ondockdrop|ondockover|ongetsiteinfo|ongetdockcaption" over source/ returned NOTHING — no docking surface anywhere in the library (no DockManager, no dock events, no GetDefaultDockCaption override).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2336 (DockSite), :2357 (UseDockManager), :2345-2346 (OnDockDrop/OnDockOver), :2352 (OnUnDock), :2320-2321 (OnGetSiteInfo/OnGetDockCaption); published on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1194, 1213, 1221-1222, 1226, 1230-1231, 1245-1247; TCustomPanel sets UseDockManager := True and implements GetDefaultDockCaption (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:43, :232-235).
user_impact: Dockable-pane IDE-style layouts (the most common reason a TPanel is used as a container in Lazarus/Delphi apps) cannot be built on ty containers at all; a ported form silently loses every dock relationship.

what_it_does: The accessibility identity a screen reader announces. LCL gives each concrete control a sensible default in its constructor: larGroup + a localized description for a panel, larResizeGrip for a splitter.
ours_evidence: grep -ril "accessiblerole|accessibledescription" over source/ returned NOTHING — no ty control sets either, so every one is left at TControl's default (larUnknown). The properties themselves are inherited PUBLIC from TControl, so a host can set them by hand, but the defaults are wrong.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/custompanel.inc:45-46 (AccessibleRole := larGroup; AccessibleDescription := rsTPanelAccessibilityDescription); C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:951-952 (larResizeGrip + rsTSplitterAccessibilityDescription); property at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1784.
user_impact: Screen readers announce every ty container and splitter as an unidentified control rather than a group / resize grip, so keyboard-and-screen-reader users lose the structural landmarks a stock LCL form gives them for free.

what_it_does: Two published sub-objects that ARE the scrolling API: Increment, Page, Position, Range, Smooth, Tracking and Visible per axis, settable in the OI and from code, plus Assign/IsScrollBarVisible/ScrollPos helpers.
ours_evidence: Both bars are PRIVATE fields with no public or published accessor: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:35-36 (FVScrollBar/FHScrollBar), created lazily in EnsureBars (:269-300); the public surface is only ContentWidth/ContentHeight/ScrollX/ScrollY, all read-only (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:138-141). grep -rn "HorzScrollBar|VertScrollBar" over source/ returns nothing. The ITEM class exists — TTyScrollBar publishes Min/Max/Position/PageSize/SmallChange/OnChange/OnScroll (tyControls.ScrollBar.pas published block) — it is simply not exposed on the box.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:207-208 (published HorzScrollBar/VertScrollBar); TControlScrollBar declared at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:99 with published Increment/Page/Smooth/Position/Range/Tracking/Visible at :157-163 and public IsScrollBarVisible/ScrollPos/ClientSizeWithBar at :148-155.
user_impact: None of the scrolling behaviour is configurable or observable from outside the control: no design-time scroll settings, and code that reads or writes ScrollBox1.VertScrollBar.* (the standard LCL/Delphi idiom) does not compile. Tracking (content follows the thumb during a drag) and Smooth have no equivalent at all.

what_it_does: Read AND write the current scroll offset per axis — the way a host scrolls programmatically (jump to top, restore a saved position, follow a selection).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:140-141 exposes ScrollX/ScrollY as READ-ONLY properties; the only mutator, ScrollByDelta, is PROTECTED (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:96, inside the protected section that starts at :50), and ScrollContentTo is private (:47). grep over source/ finds no public scroll setter on the box.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:160 (Position read/write, default 0), reachable via the published bars at :207-208; implementation SetPosition C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:130.
user_impact: An application cannot scroll its own scroll box: no 'scroll to top', no persisting/restoring the scroll position across sessions, no scrolling in response to a keyboard or search hit. The user is limited to the mouse wheel and dragging the thumb.

what_it_does: The scrollable content extent per axis, settable explicitly (Range) and overridable by a descendant (CalculateAutoRanges) — the way you scroll content that is DRAWN rather than made of child controls.
ours_evidence: The extent is derived exclusively from child controls: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:349-366 walks ContentHost.Controls and sets FContentW/FContentH inside MeasureAndDock, which is PRIVATE (declared :49). It is exposed only read-only as ContentWidth/ContentHeight (:138-139) and there is no virtual hook to supply an extent (no CalculateAutoRanges equivalent; grep over source/ finds none).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:161 (Range read/write, stored IsRangeStored) plus the protected virtual hook TScrollingWinControl.CalculateAutoRanges declared C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:181 and implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:116-141.
user_impact: A scrollable owner-drawn surface (a big diagram, a canvas, a custom timeline) cannot be built on TTyScrollBox: the only way to obtain a scroll range is to add real child controls sized to the content. Descendants have no supported override point either.

what_it_does: How far one 'line' scrolls — the step used by an arrow click and the wheel (default 8 px).
ours_evidence: The wheel step is hardcoded to the scrollbar thickness with no way to change it: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:646 `step := ScrollbarThick;   // one "line" ~ a scrollbar thickness of content`. The concept exists on the standalone bar as SmallChange (tyControls.ScrollBar.pas published, default 1) but the box's bars are private (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:35-36) and it never assigns SmallChange.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:157 (Increment: TScrollBarInc default 8), reachable via the published bars at :207-208.
user_impact: Wheel/step granularity is fixed and theme-dependent (it changes with --scrollbar-size), so a list of 20 px rows and a page of 200 px cards scroll by the same odd amount and neither can be tuned to a row height.

what_it_does: Per-axis opt-out/opt-in for a scrollbar: hide one axis entirely (vertical-only scrolling) or keep a bar reserved so the layout does not jump when content grows.
ours_evidence: Bar visibility is computed only, from the measured overflow: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:377-379 (wantV/wantH) then :411/:414 and :432/:435 assign FVScrollBar.Visible/FHScrollBar.Visible; the bars are private (:35-36) and nothing published gates an axis. grep over source/ finds no ShowScrollBars/ScrollBars-style property on the box.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:163 (Visible: Boolean default True) on the published bars at :207-208; HideScrollbars uses it at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:159-175.
user_impact: You cannot build a vertical-only scroll region (a wide child will always raise a horizontal bar), nor reserve a gutter to stop the content reflowing when a bar appears — the classic 'content jumps sideways as it grows' complaint.

what_it_does: Master switch for automatic scrollbars: True (TScrollBox's default) computes ranges and shows/hides bars as content changes; False hides both bars and stops the automatic range computation.
ours_evidence: TTyScrollBox has no AutoScroll: published list is tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:142-146 (Align, Anchors, StyleClass, Controller) plus the inherited TTyPanel/base sets. Automatic measuring is unconditional — Resize, Loaded and ControlsAligned all call UpdateScrollRange (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:664-668, 529-536, 538-545).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:195 (protected AutoScroll, default False, "auto show/hide scrollbars"), republished with a changed default on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:229 (`property AutoScroll default True`); setter at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:12-25.
user_impact: A ported .lfm carrying AutoScroll = False does not stream, and there is no way to freeze a scroll box as a plain clipping viewport (bars off, no measuring) — useful when the host drives the offset itself.

what_it_does: On LCL, AutoScroll on a scrolling container means 'automatically show/hide scrollbars and recompute ranges'. On TTyScrollPanel the same identifier means something unrelated: the master switch for edge AUTO-PAN during a drag.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ScrollPanel.pas:82 `property AutoScroll: Boolean read FAutoScroll write SetAutoScroll default True;` documented at :80-81 as "Master switch. When False AutoPanTo is a no-op (the panel still scrolls by wheel / scrollbar exactly like its TTyScrollBox base)"; setter at :209-214 only calls StopAutoPan.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:195 with the inline comment "// auto show/hide scrollbars", republished default True on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:229; implemented as UpdateScrollBars/HideScrollbars at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:12-25.
user_impact: A porter who sets ScrollPanel1.AutoScroll := False expecting the scrollbars to go away instead silently disables edge auto-pan while the bars keep appearing — same name, same type, same default, opposite subsystem. The collision is invisible at compile time.

what_it_does: Scrolls the minimum amount needed to bring a given child control fully into the viewport (clamping when the child is larger than the client area).
ours_evidence: grep -rn "ScrollInView" over source/ returned NOTHING. The capability exists under a DIFFERENT name on other controls — TTyCustomGrid.ScrollIntoView(ACol, ARow) (tyControls.Grid.pas:1203, impl :3449) and TTyListView.ScrollIntoView(AIndex) (tyControls.ListView.pas:477, impl :1909) — but nothing equivalent exists on TTyScrollBox, whose public surface is tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:121-141.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:205 (public ScrollInView), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:281-312.
user_impact: Focus/keyboard navigation inside a scroll box does not follow the content: tabbing to a child below the fold leaves it invisible, and the host has no one-liner to fix it (and no public scroll setter to hand-roll it, see the Position gap).

what_it_does: Public 'recompute ranges and refresh the bars now' entry point, called after the host changes content outside the normal notification paths.
ours_evidence: Present under a different name: tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:135 `procedure UpdateScrollRange;` (impl :302-325), documented at :132-134 as "Recompute the logical content extent ... then show/hide/position the two scrollbars and clamp the offset".
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:202 (public UpdateScrollbars), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:246-263.
user_impact: Pure porting friction: existing code calling ScrollBox1.UpdateScrollbars fails to compile and must be renamed; the two names also invite the belief that the ty version does something different.

what_it_does: On a scrolling container, ScrollBy is the public 'scroll the view by this delta' operation: TScrollingWinControl overrides it to do a widgetset scroll so the client origin AND the scrollbar state stay consistent.
ours_evidence: TTyScrollBox does NOT override ScrollBy (grep -n "ScrollBy" tyControls.ScrollBox.pas shows only the internal call sites at :599-601 plus the protected ScrollByDelta at :96/:547), so the inherited TWinControl.ScrollBy is what a caller gets: it just re-bounds every child. FScrollX/FScrollY are documented as "the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH" (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:19-23) and ScrollBy does not touch them, nor the bar Positions, nor re-dock the bars (that work lives in ScrollContentTo, :576-614).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:204 (`procedure ScrollBy(DeltaX, DeltaY: Integer); override;`) implemented as ScrollBy_WS at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/scrollingwincontrol.inc:276-279; the unoverridden base version that ours inherits is C:/lazarus/lcl/include/wincontrol.inc:6255-6268.
user_impact: Calling Box.ScrollBy(0, -50) — the documented LCL way to scroll a container — moves the children AND the two scrollbars off their docked edges while FScrollY stays 0. The very next UpdateScrollRange re-measures the moved children as a smaller content extent (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:359-362 adds FScrollX/FScrollY back), so the range and thumb are wrong and the next thumb drag makes the content jump.

what_it_does: Horizontal wheel / tilt-wheel / trackpad-swipe input, dispatched by TControl.DoMouseWheelHorz and DoMouseWheelLeft/Right.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "mousewheelhorz|mousewheelleft|mousewheelright" over source/ returned NOTHING. Both base classes publish only the vertical trio (tyControls.Base.pas:123-125 and :221-223), and TTyScrollBox overrides only DoMouseWheel (tyControls.ScrollBox.pas:638-662), where a horizontal scroll happens ONLY as a fallback when there is no vertical bar (:655-659).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1597-1599 (OnMouseWheelHorz / OnMouseWheelLeft / OnMouseWheelRight) with dispatchers DoMouseWheelHorz/DoMouseWheelLeft at :1537-1538; published on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp (OnMouseWheelHorz/Left/Right block) and on TPanel at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:1240-1242.
user_impact: A tilt wheel or two-finger horizontal swipe does nothing over a ty scroll box, and a box that scrolls in BOTH axes can never be panned horizontally by the wheel (the vertical bar always wins). No hook is available for the host to add it either.

what_it_does: Fires during size negotiation so a host can clamp MinWidth/MaxWidth/MinHeight/MaxHeight for this resize pass (var parameters), before the new bounds are applied.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "onconstrainedresize" over source/ returned NOTHING; neither base class publishes it (tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-246) and no ty control declares an equivalent. Only the static Constraints object is published (tyControls.Base.pas:130/:227).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1580 (OnConstrainedResize: TConstrainedResizeEvent); published on TScrollBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/forms.pp:257.
user_impact: Dynamic size limits (e.g. 'this pane may never exceed half the form') cannot be expressed — only the fixed Constraints values. A ported form loses the handler silently.

what_it_does: The single reason TPaintBox exists: a TNotifyEvent fired inside the paint pass with Canvas.Font/Brush already prepared, so the host draws with the ordinary TCanvas API.
ours_evidence: Present under a different name AND a different signature: tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42 `property OnPaintSurface: TTyPaintSurfaceEvent`, whose type is `procedure(Sender: TObject; APainter: TTyPainter; const AContent: TRect) of object` (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:24-25). The inherited public TCustomControl.OnPaint is assignable but dead: TTyPaintPanel.Paint (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:115-118) calls RenderTo and never inherited Paint. grep -rn "OnPaint" over source/ confirms only OnPaintSurface/OnPaintPreview/OnPaintText exist.
theirs_evidence: Published on TPaintBox at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:520; declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2457 (TGraphicControl); fired at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/graphiccontrol.inc:93-97 and gated in TPaintBox.Paint at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/paintbox.inc:43-47.
user_impact: An existing TPaintBox handler cannot be moved over: the parameter list differs, so every ported handler must be rewritten, and the familiar `OnPaint` name silently accepts an assignment that never fires (see the TTyPanel OnPaint gap).

what_it_does: TPaintBox is a GRAPHIC control: no window handle, it paints into its parent's DC, so it is transparent where it does not draw, can be layered over other controls, and never clips or occludes siblings.
ours_evidence: tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:27 `TTyPaintPanel = class(TTyPanel)` -> tyControls.Panel.pas:8 `TTyPanel = class(TTyCustomControl)` -> tyControls.Base.pas:143 `TTyCustomControl = class(TCustomControl)`, i.e. a real windowed control, and it additionally takes csAcceptsControls (tyControls.Panel.pas:37) plus DoubleBuffered (tyControls.Base.pas:900). The library does have a graphic base (TTyGraphicControl, tyControls.Base.pas:68) — it is just not what the paint surface uses.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:475 `TPaintBox = class(TGraphicControl)`; TGraphicControl declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2444 with no handle (Canvas at :2462, WMPaint into the parent DC).
user_impact: TTyPaintPanel cannot be used the way TPaintBox commonly is — as a transparent annotation/overlay layer on top of another control — and being windowed it clips and occludes what sits under it (the windowed-sibling clipping trap this codebase has already been bitten by). Substituting it for a TPaintBox changes z-order and transparency behaviour.

what_it_does: The size a freshly dropped control gets from the palette. TPaintBox chooses a square 105x105 because a drawing surface has no intrinsic aspect.
ours_evidence: TTyPaintPanel sets no size of its own — its constructor only calls inherited (tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:75-80) and there is no GetControlClassDefaultSize override anywhere in the unit — so it inherits TTyPanel's caption-band shape, Width := 185; Height := 41 (tyControls.Panel.pas:41-42).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/paintbox.inc:50-54 (GetControlClassDefaultSize -> 105x105), applied in the constructor at :17-18.
user_impact: A paint surface dropped from the palette arrives as a 185x41 letterbox strip, so the first thing a user must do is resize it; anyone previewing drawing code at the default size sees a clipped result.

what_it_does: Selects which side the splitter resizes (akLeft/akTop/akRight/akBottom) INDEPENDENTLY of Align — the documented second mode where Align=alNone plus AnchorSides plus ResizeAnchor drives an anchored layout; it also drives the cursor and the whole MoveSplitter geometry.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "resizeanchor" over source/ returned NOTHING. The axis is derived from Align only: tyControls.Splitter.pas:94-99 (Vertical := Align in [alLeft, alRight]) and FindResizeTarget's case statement handles only alLeft/alRight/alTop/alBottom (:149-158), so an alNone splitter finds no target and does nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:430 (ResizeAnchor: TAnchorKind default akLeft), republished on TSplitter at :453; setter (which also forces Align := alNone) at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:515-526; MoveSplitter branches on it throughout, e.g. :146-155, :159-168; the two-mode design is documented at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:361-369.
user_impact: Only the four Align-docked splitter arrangements work. An anchored splitter — the flexible mode LCL documents for anchor-based layouts, and the only way to split two anchored panes without Align — is silently inert: it paints, shows a resize cursor, and resizes nothing.

what_it_does: Public read/write property naming the control this splitter resizes: reading it resolves the current target, writing it repositions/re-anchors the splitter to that control.
ours_evidence: The target is private and transient: tyControls.Splitter.pas:18 (FTarget: TControl), assigned only on MouseDown (:181 `FTarget := FindResizeTarget`) and cleared on MouseUp (:229). grep -rin "resizecontrol" over source/ returned NOTHING.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:416 (`property ResizeControl: TControl read GetResizeControl write SetResizeControl`), getter C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:127-133, setter :527-543.
user_impact: Code cannot ask which pane a splitter drives, nor point it at a specific control — so no 'reset the sidebar to 200 px' or 'move the splitter next to this pane' logic, and no way to disambiguate when several siblings touch the splitter.

what_it_does: Public, virtual: move the splitter by Offset pixels and resize the affected pane(s) exactly as a drag would — the one entry point through which every programmatic and interactive move runs.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "movesplitter" over source/ returned NOTHING. The equivalent logic exists only as the PRIVATE ApplySize(ADelta) (tyControls.Splitter.pas:24, impl :163-175), reachable solely from MouseMove/MouseUp (:203, :222).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:418 (`procedure MoveSplitter(Offset: integer); virtual;`), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:143 and called by MouseMove/StopSplitterMove at :640-641 and :586-587.
user_impact: A splitter can only be moved by mouse. No keyboard resizing, no animated/scripted pane reveal, no 'nudge by 10 px' command, and no override point for a descendant that wants custom move rules.

what_it_does: Read and set the splitter's absolute position along its axis (Left for a vertical bar, Top for a horizontal one) — the natural way to persist and restore a layout.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "splitterposition" over source/ returned NOTHING; the public surface of TTySplitter is just the constructor (tyControls.Splitter.pas:36-37) plus the published properties (:38-52).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:419-420; implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:488-500 (SetSplitterPosition routes through MoveSplitter).
user_impact: Saving and restoring a user's pane sizes across runs — the most common thing an app does with a splitter — has no supported API. Writing Splitter.Left directly does not resize the pane, since nothing recomputes the neighbour.

what_it_does: Wires the splitter and a control together in one call: it anchors the control's side to the splitter and the splitter's opposite sides to the control's neighbours, building an anchor-based split without Align.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "anchorsplitter" over source/ returned NOTHING; the unit has no anchor-manipulation code at all (tyControls.Splitter.pas publishes Anchors at :50 and otherwise never touches AnchorSide).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:415 (public AnchorSplitter), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:956 onward (AnchorSplitterSides helper).
user_impact: Building an anchored (non-Align) split layout in code requires hand-writing several AnchorSide assignments and getting the opposite sides right; there is no one-call helper, and without ResizeAnchor the result would not resize anyway.

what_it_does: Returns the control on the OTHER side of the splitter, so a host (and MoveSplitter itself) can reason about both panes — e.g. clamp against the far pane's minimum size.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "getotherresizecontrol|otherresize" over source/ returned NOTHING. tyControls.Splitter.pas:136-161 FindResizeTarget deliberately searches ONE side only (the case statement tests only the anchored side).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:417 (public GetOtherResizeControl), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:135-141 on top of FindAlignOtherControl (:692).
user_impact: Neither the control nor the host can see the opposite pane, so a drag cannot respect the far pane's minimum — it just squeezes it (see the Constraints gap).

what_it_does: Draws a raised outer edge around the splitter bar (BDR_RAISEDOUTER) so it reads as a physical divider — the classic Delphi splitter look.
ours_evidence: grep -rin "beveled" over source/ hits only tyControls.Bevel.pas (a separate standalone TTyBevel decoration control) and tyControls.BuiltinThemeData.pas (theme text); TTySplitter has no Beveled and its RenderTo unconditionally draws three grip dots plus whatever the theme frame gives (tyControls.Splitter.pas:239-270, dots at :254-265).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:424 (Beveled: boolean default false), republished on TSplitter at :442; painted at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:879-881 (ThemeServices.DrawEdge with BDR_RAISEDOUTER).
user_impact: A ported .lfm with Beveled = True does not stream, and there is no per-instance way to give one splitter a raised edge (the theme's border tokens would change every splitter in the app).

what_it_does: Veto/adjust hook on the splitter OFFSET (var NewOffset, var Accept) — complements OnCanResize by letting the host constrain the movement itself (snapping to a grid, refusing a direction) rather than the resulting pane size.
ours_evidence: Only the size-based hook exists: tyControls.Splitter.pas:47 OnCanResize (type at :8), consulted in ApplySize at :171-173. grep -rin "oncanoffset" over source/ returned NOTHING.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:427 (OnCanOffset: TCanOffsetEvent, type at :357-358), republished on TSplitter at :459; consumed by CheckOffset at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:838-843.
user_impact: Snap-to-grid or direction-limited dragging cannot be implemented: by the time OnCanResize fires the offset has already been converted to a size, and the handler cannot see or alter the movement itself.

what_it_does: Same signature, different declared type: LCL uses the shared TCanResizeEvent so a handler can be reused across splitters/controls.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Splitter.pas:8 declares its own `TTySplitterCanResizeEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; var ANewSize: Integer; var AAccept: Boolean) of object;` used at :47 — structurally identical to LCL's type but a distinct, unrelated type name. The unit already uses ExtCtrls (:5) for TResizeStyle, so TCanResizeEvent was in scope and not reused.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:359-360 (`TCanResizeEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; var NewSize: Integer; var Accept: Boolean) of object;`), used for the property at :428.
user_impact: A handler declared as TCanResizeEvent (or a published method typed from LCL) cannot be assigned or shared without a cast/duplicate declaration; the field's type in a .lfm-adjacent codebase differs from the LCL one, so mechanical porting fails on the type name.

what_it_does: Three of the four styles defer the resize until mouse-up and give live feedback in the meantime: rsLine draws a solid rubber-band line, rsPattern a themed dotted band; rsNone shows nothing. Only rsUpdate resizes live.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Splitter.pas:46 publishes the full TResizeStyle, but the drag branch handles rsUpdate only and the else branch draws nothing at all for ALL three others: :203-209, whose own comment says "rsLine defers the resize to MouseUp and does NOT draw a live ghost line. Drawing a ghost overlay (XOR line / canvas paint) is a deferred Tier-2 enhancement." MouseUp then applies the size only for rsLine (:218-224), so rsPattern and rsNone drag with no feedback AND never resize.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:350-355 (the four styles, documented) and :431 (default rsUpdate); rubber band created for rsLine/rsPattern at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:553-567 (CreateRubberband with BLACK_BRUSH or ThemeServices.DottedBrush) and destroyed at :588-592; every style resizes at mouse-up via StopSplitterMove -> MoveSplitter (:583-587).
user_impact: Two published enum values are accepted and then behave wrongly: rsPattern and rsNone drag with no feedback and leave the pane at its original size, so the drag looks broken. rsLine resizes but shows nothing, so the user drags blind.

member: Constraints of the resized control (honoured during a drag)
what_it_does: LCL's MoveSplitter clamps the new size to the resized control's own Constraints.EffectiveMinWidth/MaxWidth (or Min/MaxHeight) as well as to MinSize, so a pane declaring MinWidth=200 cannot be dragged narrower.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Splitter.pas:163-175 ApplySize computes maxSize as Parent.ClientWidth - Width (or ClientHeight - Height) and calls TySplitterNewSize(Align, FStartSize, ADelta, FMinSize, maxSize, FAutoSnap) — the target's Constraints are never read. grep -n "Constraints" tyControls.Splitter.pas shows no hit; the only clamp inputs are the splitter's own MinSize and the parent's client size.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:180-195 (GetControlConstraintsMinSize / GetControlConstraintsMaxSize reading Constraints.EffectiveMinWidth / EffectiveMaxWidth / EffectiveMinHeight / EffectiveMaxHeight), used by MoveSplitter's clamping.
user_impact: A pane that declares its own limits via Constraints (the standard LCL way, and the only way when several splitters share a form) is ignored: it can be dragged below its MinWidth or above its MaxWidth, and the splitter's single MinSize is the only floor — one number for every pane it might touch.

what_it_does: LCL fires OnMoved once at the end of every splitter drag, unconditionally, as the 'the user finished moving me' notification.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Splitter.pas:226-229 fires it only when the target actually changed size: `if Assigned(FOnMoved) and (FTarget <> nil) and (AxisSize(FTarget) <> FStartSize) then FOnMoved(Self);` — with a comment claiming this "mirrors TCustomSplitter behaviour", which the LCL source contradicts.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:583-587: StopSplitterMove calls MoveSplitter only `if Offset <> 0` but then fires `if Assigned(OnMoved) then OnMoved(Self);` unconditionally for every completed drag.
user_impact: A handler that persists layout or re-lays dependent controls at the end of a drag does not run when the drag was vetoed, snapped back, or clamped to the same size — states where the app may still need to re-sync. Behaviour diverges from LCL exactly where the code claims parity.

what_it_does: LCL re-derives the splitter cursor from Enabled: a disabled splitter shows crDefault (and its band paints in the trBandDisabled state), and CM_ENABLEDCHANGED re-runs the derivation when Enabled flips.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Splitter.pas:101-104 UpdateCursor ignores Enabled entirely (`if Vertical then Cursor := crHSplit else Cursor := crVSplit;`) and is called from the constructor (:86), Loaded (:106-110) and MouseEnter (:112-120); there is no CM_ENABLEDCHANGED handler in the unit.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:597-607 (UpDateCursor -> crDefault when not Enabled) and :845-850 (CMEnabledChanged re-deriving it); disabled band state at :868-869.
user_impact: A disabled splitter still shows the resize cursor, inviting a drag that does nothing — the exact 'looks interactive, is inert' problem the recent fixes in this branch were about.

what_it_does: On TCustomSplitter, OnPaint does more than add drawing: assigning it SUPPRESSES the built-in themed band/gripper, so it is the documented way to give a splitter a custom look.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "OnPaint" over source/ finds no OnPaint on any ty control; TTySplitter.Paint (tyControls.Splitter.pas:234-237) always calls RenderTo, which always draws the frame plus three grip dots (:239-270) and never consults a handler nor calls inherited Paint (so even the inherited public TCustomControl.OnPaint at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2486 is dead here).
theirs_evidence: Published on TSplitter at C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:469; the suppression is in TCustomSplitter.Paint at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customsplitter.inc:908-911 (`if not Assigned(OnPaint) then DrawThemedPattern(ClientRect);`).
user_impact: A custom splitter appearance (a thin hairline, a branded handle, a hover chevron) can only be done by editing the theme for every splitter in the app or by subclassing; the per-instance escape hatch LCL provides has no counterpart.

what_it_does: Boolean, default True. When False the caption is drawn literally: '&' is a normal glyph and no letter is underlined/activated (DT_NOPREFIX).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "showaccelchar" over the whole D:/Projects/ty-controls/source/ returns NOTHING. source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:357 unconditionally calls TyParseMnemonic(Caption, dispCap, mp) and :420-422 passes TyAccelGatePos(mp) to DrawText; MeasureCaption:307 does the same. The only escape is '&&' (source/tyControls.Accel.pas:63-64). No property, no ControlStyle switch.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1600 (property ShowAccelChar: Boolean ... default true), published on TLabel at stdctrls.pp:1643; honoured in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:80-81 (Flags or DT_NOPREFIX), :284 (DialogChar early-exit) and :438-439 (Paint).
user_impact: A caption containing a real ampersand ('Research & Development', a Windows path with '&') silently loses the character and underlines the next letter, and there is no way to turn parsing off. Every ported .lfm line ShowAccelChar = False fails to stream.

what_it_does: OptimalFill=True binary-searches the largest Font.Height at which the caption still fits the label's fixed box, re-running on every bounds change; the two public methods expose that search.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "optimalfill|fittingfont|adjustfontforoptimal" over source/ returns NOTHING. source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:133-139 (ResolveFontSize) only picks theme font-size -> explicit Font.Size -> --font-size-base -> 9; the size never adapts to the box, and DoSetBounds:270-281 only re-wraps.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1603 (OptimalFill default false), public methods at stdctrls.pp:1606-1609; implementation C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:318-411, wired from DoSetBounds :208-209, UpdateSize :305-306 and SetOptimalFill :489-498.
user_impact: A caption that must fill a fixed banner/splash box cannot shrink-to-fit; the text is ellipsised/clipped instead. Loading an existing .lfm that carries OptimalFill = True raises an unknown-property read error.

what_it_does: Vertical placement of the caption block inside the control (tlTop/tlCenter/tlBottom).
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:93 property Layout: TTextLayout ... default tlCenter, and the ctor sets FLayout := tlCenter (:107). The property exists and works; only the default differs.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1599 property Layout: TTextLayout read FLayout write SetLayout default tlTop; TCustomLabel.Create (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:221-232) leaves FLayout at 0 = tlTop.
user_impact: A .lfm converted from TLabel omits Layout because tlTop was the default, so after the port every non-autosized label's caption jumps to the vertical centre of its box - a silent, whole-form text shift with nothing in the file to explain it.

what_it_does: AutoSize=True makes a label size itself to its caption; TCustomLabel turns it on in the constructor and re-declares the default as True.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:95 republishes AutoSize with NO default override, and the ctor (:102-110) never sets it; same for source/tyControls.LinkLabel.pas:68 with ctor :111-118. grep -r "AutoSize := True" over source/ returns NOTHING, so the inherited default stands (C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1789 -> default False). The machinery is all present (CalculatePreferredSize TyLabel.pas:314, TextChanged :258) - just off.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1612 (property AutoSize default True) and C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:229 (AutoSize := True in TCustomLabel.Create).
user_impact: Dropping a TTyLabel, or porting one from TLabel, gives a fixed box that clips the caption instead of growing with it; every label in a ported form needs AutoSize=True added by hand, and .lfm files omit the property precisely because it used to be the default.

what_it_does: TCustomLabel honours Font.Orientation: the caption is drawn at the requested angle and CalculatePreferredSize returns the rotated bounding box, so a vertical (900) label works out of the box.
ours_evidence: Font IS published (source/tyControls.Base.pas:112) so Orientation is settable and simply ignored: source/tyControls.Painter.pas:109 DrawText takes no angle argument, and TTyLabel.RenderTo:407/420-422 only ever draws horizontal lines. grep -rin "rotate|TextOutAngle" over source/ shows the capability EXISTS but is wired to exactly one place - source/tyControls.Menu.pas:876 (P.Bitmap.TextOutAngle(..., 900, ...) for the menu side banner) - and to no label.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:43-49 (rotates the preferred size via RotateRect) and :457-476 (the rotated draw path, with alignment/layout handled per angle).
user_impact: Setting Font.Orientation := 900 on a TTyLabel (a chart axis caption, a narrow sidebar title) is accepted in the OI and silently does nothing - the text stays horizontal and gets clipped by the tall thin box the user sized for it.

what_it_does: BidiMode flips alignment and enables RTL reading order for the caption; ParentBidiMode inherits it from the parent.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "bidimode" over source/ hits only source/tyControls.Memo.pas (its own internal use) - no label/shape/divider publishes it, and neither base class does (source/tyControls.Base.pas:101-141, :196-246). TTyLabel.RenderTo:407/420 passes FAlignment straight through with no bidi flip; TyDividerLayout (source/tyControls.Divider.pas:98-128) is LTR by construction.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1625 + 1638 (TLabel), :1127 + 1140 (TStaticText), C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:69 + 83; honoured in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:82-83 (DT_RTLREADING) and :446 (BidiFlipAlignment), and dividerbevel.pas:335-340 + 370-373 (RTL caption/bevel placement).
user_impact: An Arabic/Hebrew UI gets left-aligned, LTR-ordered captions on every ty label and divider; there is no RTL story anywhere in this control family and no property to stream from a ported form.

what_it_does: Color is the control's own background colour (painted when Transparent=False); TArrow.ArrowColor is the triangle's fill colour, default clBlack.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property Color" over source/ finds only tyControls.Chart.pas and tyControls.Dialogs.Color.pas - none of the six controls in this group publishes Color, and grep -ri "arrowcolor" returns NOTHING. The themed equivalent is StyleOverride (source/tyControls.Base.pas:139), documented for exactly this on the shape family: source/tyControls.Arrow.pas:12-14 and source/tyControls.Shape.pas:10-11 (StyleOverride := 'background: #E11; border-color: #700;').
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1613 (TCustomLabel public Color) + :1628 (TLabel published), :1131 (TStaticText, Color nodefault); C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:56 (ArrowColor default clBlack) + :60 (Color); C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:73.
user_impact: Porting break rather than a missing capability: every 'Color = clRed' / 'ArrowColor = clBlack' line in an existing .lfm fails to stream and must be rewritten as a CSS StyleOverride string, and there is no design-time colour picker for a one-off recolour.

what_it_does: sbsNone / sbsSingle / sbsSunken - a per-instance frame around the static text.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "borderstyle" over source/ hits Memo, Form, Popup, Menu, Notification, ScrollContent, Types (TTyBorderStyle) etc. but NOT TyLabel. TTyLabel gets a frame only when Transparent=False, and then it is whatever the theme says (source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:363-364 -> DrawFrame); there is no per-control border property (published block :83-97).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1087 (TStaticBorderStyle), :1112 (property BorderStyle ... default sbsNone), published at :1129.
user_impact: A ported TStaticText with BorderStyle=sbsSunken loses its frame (unknown property on load) and can only get it back by writing a theme rule or a StyleOverride string - the single most common reason people used TStaticText instead of TLabel.

member: DragMode, DragKind, DragCursor, OnDragDrop, OnDragOver, OnStartDrag, OnEndDrag (+ TShape's OnStartDock/OnEndDock)
what_it_does: The LCL drag-and-drop / docking surface: dmAutomatic starts a drag on mouse-down, and the events let the control be a drag source or drop target designed entirely in the OI.
ours_evidence: grep -ri over source/ for each name: DragMode -> only tyControls.CoolBar.pas + tyControls.Memo.pas; DragKind/DragCursor/OnDragDrop/OnStartDrag -> only tyControls.Memo.pas; OnDragOver/OnEndDrag -> Memo, ScrollPanel, TreeView; OnStartDock/OnEndDock -> NOTHING. Neither base class publishes any of them (source/tyControls.Base.pas:101-141 and :196-246), so no ty graphic control can drag or accept a drop.
theirs_evidence: Declared on TControl at C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1570-1572, 1585-1588, 1601; published by TLabel stdctrls.pp:1630-1632 + 1652-1654 + 1667, TStaticText :1134-1136 + 1156-1158, TShape C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:313-315 + 324-327 + 341-342, TArrow C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:76-78 + 92, TDividerBevel C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:75-77 + 96-98 + 105.
user_impact: Designer-authored drag-and-drop (drag a shape onto a canvas, drop a file on a label) is impossible on the whole family, and any ported .lfm carrying DragMode/OnDragOver fails to load.

their_class: TControl (published by TLabel, TStaticText, TShape, TArrow)
what_it_does: Horizontal-wheel / tilt-wheel / trackpad side-scroll notifications, the horizontal twins of the vertical wheel events.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Base.pas:123-125 publishes OnMouseWheel, OnMouseWheelUp, OnMouseWheelDown only (same at :219-221 for TTyCustomControl). grep -ri "onmousewheelhorz|onmousewheelleft|onmousewheelright" over the whole source/ returns NOTHING.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:1597 (OnMouseWheelHorz on TControl); published on TLabel stdctrls.pp:1663-1665, TStaticText :1167-1169, TShape C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:336-338, TArrow C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:87-89.
user_impact: Tilt-wheel and two-finger horizontal scroll gestures are unreachable from any ty control - not just these labels/shapes, the entire library - so horizontally scrolling content cannot be driven the way users expect.

what_it_does: TGraphicControl.Paint fires OnPaint after the control has drawn itself, so an app can annotate the graphic (a label inside the shape, tick marks, a highlight) without subclassing.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "onpaint" over source/ finds only tyControls.PaintPanel.pas:42 (OnPaintSurface, a DIFFERENT signature: Sender + TTyPainter + ContentRect), PreviewBox and TreeView. TTyGraphicControl publishes no OnPaint (source/tyControls.Base.pas:101-141) and, worse, TTyShape.Paint (source/tyControls.Shape.pas:281-284), TTyBevel.Paint (source/tyControls.Bevel.pas:251-254) and TTyArrow.Paint (source/tyControls.Arrow.pas:275-278) never call inherited Paint, so even a published OnPaint would never fire.
theirs_evidence: Declared C:/lazarus/lcl/controls.pp:2457; fired at C:/lazarus/lcl/include/graphiccontrol.inc:93-97; published by TShape C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:339 (and TCustomShape.Paint calls inherited for exactly that reason, C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:249-257), TBevel extctrls.pp:706, TArrow arrow.pp:90.
user_impact: No supported way to draw on top of a shape/bevel/arrow from application code; users must subclass and override RenderTo, and ported forms lose their OnPaint handler wiring.

their_class: TCustomLabel/TLabel (nearest LCL label; no TLinkLabel in this LCL)
what_it_does: Wraps the caption over several lines inside the control width instead of one clipped line.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.LinkLabel.pas:63-81 published block has no WordWrap; RenderTo:290 issues ONE P.DrawText with AMultiLine defaulted to False (source/tyControls.Painter.pas:109) and MeasureCaption:197 measures a single Canvas.TextWidth. grep -ri "wordwrap" over source/ shows the capability exists and is wired to TTyLabel (tyControls.TyLabel.pas:94, WrapText:283-290 -> TyWrapTextCJK) - just not to the link label.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/stdctrls.pp:1602 (WordWrap default false) published at :1647; wrapping path C:/lazarus/lcl/include/customlabel.inc:75-77 (DT_WORDBREAK) and :433-434.
user_impact: A long link ('Terms of Service and Privacy Policy') is drawn on one line and clipped, and the accent underline clamps to the content width (source/tyControls.LinkLabel.pas:296-304) so the mark stops mid-sentence - the visible symptom of the missing wrap.

what_it_does: Per-instance stroke and fill objects: Pen.Color/Width/Style (psSolid, psDash, psDot, psDashDot)/Mode and Brush.Color/Style (bsClear, bsHorizontal, bsCross, bsDiagCross...)/Bitmap, each with an OnChange that repaints.
ours_evidence: grep -rn "property Pen|property Brush" over source/ returns NOTHING. TTyShape fills with the resolved theme background and strokes with the theme border only (source/tyControls.Shape.pas:222-273; published surface :41-47). The theme's border vocabulary is TTyBorderStyle = (tbsSolid, tbsNone, tbsOutset, tbsInset) (source/tyControls.Types.pas:33) - no dashed/dotted - and TTyFill has no hatch/pattern kind, so StyleOverride cannot express it either.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:299-300 (public Brush/Pen), published at :311 and :318; applied in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:251-252 (Canvas.Pen := FPen; Canvas.Brush := FBrush), change hook :259-264, and the pen width drives the geometry inset :83-90.
user_impact: Dashed outlines and hatched fills - standard diagram idioms (a 'planned' box, a 'disabled' region) - are unreachable by property OR by theme; a ported .lfm's Pen/Brush sub-blocks fail to stream and their look cannot be reproduced.

member: TShapeType values stRoundSquare, stSquaredDiamond, stTriangleLeft, stTriangleRight, stTriangleDown
what_it_does: Five of the fifteen TShapeType kinds: the square-locked rounded rectangle and diamond, and the three non-upward triangles.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Shape.pas:28-29 TTyShapeKind = (tskRectangle, tskRoundRect, tskSquare, tskEllipse, tskCircle, tskTriangle, tskDiamond, tskLine) - the triangle is apex-up only (TyShapePolygon:81-88) and the diamond/roundrect have no square-locked variant (:89-97, RenderTo:178-190). grep -ri "triangleleft|triangleright|triangledown|roundsquare|squareddiamond" over source/ returns NOTHING; no other control supplies them.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:266-269 (TShapeType); drawn in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:93-99 (square-lock for stRoundSquare/stSquaredDiamond), :104-105, :143-153 (stTriangleLeft), :154-164 (stTriangleRight), :132-142 (stTriangleDown).
user_impact: A flowchart or state diagram needing a left/right/down-pointing triangle (flow-direction markers, play/back glyphs) has no equivalent, and those five .lfm enum values fail to load - 5 of 15 kinds unrepresentable.

what_it_does: A 5-point star, point-up or point-down, as one of the Shape enum values.
ours_evidence: We have a star, but as a SEPARATE component rather than a Shape kind: source/tyControls.StarShape.pas:36-56 TTyStarShape (published Points default 5, InnerRatio), registered next to TTyShape in designtime (registration list line 1056: TTyShape, TTyStarShape, TTyArrow, TTyChart). grep -ri "star" over source/ finds only that unit. It has no inverted/rotation option - TyStarPolygon always starts at 12 o'clock (tyControls.StarShape.pas:58-68) - so stStarDown has no counterpart at all.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:269 (stStar, stStarDown in TShapeType); geometry C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:40-69 + 165-204 (the FShape=stStarDown flag selects the mirrored angle table).
user_impact: Porting Shape = stStar means replacing the component class (and its whole .lfm entry) rather than editing a property; and a point-down star cannot be produced at all without adding rotation to TTyStarShape.

what_it_does: Shape=stPolygon asks the app for the vertices: the event hands back a TPointArray plus a Winding flag, so any polygon at all can be drawn (and the designer shows a dashed placeholder).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "shapepoints|stpolygon|winding" over source/ returns NOTHING. source/tyControls.Shape.pas:62/70-101 TyShapePolygon is a closed pure function over the fixed kind list with no hook for caller-supplied points, and RenderTo:157-206 builds the path only from FShape.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:271-272 (TShapePointsEvent), :303 (public OnShapePoints), :344 (published), :285 (setter); consumed in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:205-228 (FOnShapePoints(Self, P, PolygonWinding); ACanvas.Polygon(P, PolygonWinding)).
user_impact: This is TShape's extensibility escape hatch - the answer to every shape the enum lacks (hexagons, callouts, custom marks). Without it the missing kinds above are permanently missing and the app must write its own TTyGraphicControl descendant.

what_it_does: Fires on click only when the pointer is inside the actual drawn shape, as opposed to OnClick which fires anywhere in the bounding rectangle.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "onshapeclick" over source/ returns NOTHING. TTyShape does not override Click (whole class: source/tyControls.Shape.pas:31-48), so only the inherited whole-rect OnClick (source/tyControls.Base.pas:116) is available.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:302 (public), :343 (published); fired in C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:305-311 - inherited Click, then OnShapeClick only if PtInShape(ScreenToClient(Mouse.CursorPos)).
user_impact: On a diagram made of circles/triangles, a click in a shape's empty corner is reported as a hit on that shape; there is no 'clicked the ink' event, so hit accuracy has to be re-implemented per app.

what_it_does: PtInShape(P) answers whether a client point is on the drawn shape (via a monochrome mask re-render); CMShapeHitTest makes the LCL/designer hit-test shape-precise, so clicks off the shape fall through to whatever is behind it.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "ptinshape|maskhittest|cm_maskhittest|updatemask" over source/ returns NOTHING - no mask and no hit-test message handler anywhere in the library. TTyShape (source/tyControls.Shape.pas:31-48) exposes only Paint/RenderTo, so the control's whole rectangle is opaque to the mouse.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:296 (public PtInShape), :290 (CMShapeHitTest message CM_MASKHITTEST), :292 (UpdateMask); implementations C:/lazarus/lcl/include/shape.inc:31-38, :232-247 (mono FBitmapCopy mask), :313-322 (Message.Result := 0/1 by PtInShape).
user_impact: Overlapping shapes in a diagram each swallow their full bounding box, so a shape behind can never be clicked and designer selection picks the wrong one; an app cannot even ask 'is this point on the shape'.

what_it_does: Public override that copies Shape and Style from another TBevel, so a decoration can be cloned at runtime.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "assign" in source/tyControls.Bevel.pas returns NOTHING, and no TTyGraphicControl-level Assign exists (source/tyControls.Base.pas has none). TTyBevel (source/tyControls.Bevel.pas:32-52) therefore inherits TPersistent.Assign, which raises 'cannot assign' for a TTyBevel source.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:684 (procedure Assign(Source: TPersistent); override), implemented C:/lazarus/lcl/include/bevel.inc:26-34 (copies FShape and FStyle, else inherited).
user_impact: NewBevel.Assign(OldBevel) - the ordinary Pascal way to duplicate a component's settings when building UI in code - raises at runtime instead of copying Shape/Style.

what_it_does: The value sets behind Shape and Style; the property names match ours exactly, only the enum type names and every value identifier are renamed.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Bevel.pas:22-23 TTyBevelShape = (tbsBox, tbsFrame, tbsTopLine, tbsBottomLine, tbsLeftLine, tbsRightLine, tbsSpacer) and :25 TTyBevelStyle = (tbsLowered, tbsRaised); properties at :45-46 with the same defaults as theirs. Note the tbs* prefix is also TTyBorderStyle's = (tbsSolid, tbsNone, tbsOutset, tbsInset) in source/tyControls.Types.pas:33, which tyControls.Bevel.pas uses (:18) - three enums sharing one prefix in one scope.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/extctrls.pp:668-669 (TBevelStyle = (bsLowered, bsRaised); TBevelShape = (bsBox, bsFrame, bsTopLine, bsBottomLine, bsLeftLine, bsRightLine, bsSpacer)), properties :691 and :693.
user_impact: A pure porting break: the shapes/styles are all present with identical semantics, but 'Shape = bsFrame' in a .lfm fails to stream and 'B.Style := bsLowered' fails to compile - a find/replace over every bevel in an existing project.

what_it_does: Which way the arrow points; TArrowType = (atUp, atDown, atLeft, atRight) with default atLeft.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Arrow.pas:27 TTyArrowDirection = (tadRight, tadLeft, tadUp, tadDown), :44 property Direction ... default tadRight, ctor :170 FDirection := tadRight. grep -ri "arrowtype" over source/ returns NOTHING - a clean rename AND a flipped default.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:26 (TArrowType), :57 (property ArrowType ... default atLeft), ctor :301 (FArrowType := atLeft, commented 'set defaults to match TArrow component').
user_impact: Two breaks in one member: 'ArrowType = atUp' in a ported .lfm fails to load, and a freshly dropped arrow points RIGHT where TArrow pointed LEFT - so a form relying on the default silently reverses direction.

what_it_does: ArrowPointerAngle is the apex angle in degrees (default 60 = equilateral, clamped 20..160) of a 3-POINT TRIANGLE that TArrow scales to fit the client rect.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Arrow.pas:45-46 exposes HeadRatio/ShaftRatio instead - fractions of length/breadth clamped 0.1..0.9 (:66-70, ClampRatio :74-79) - and TyArrowPolygon:81-165 always builds a 7-POINT BLOCK arrow (tip, two barbs, four shaft corners). grep -ri "angle" in tyControls.Arrow.pas: nothing. No way to express an apex angle, and no way to get a plain triangle (the nearest is TTyShape's tskTriangle, apex-up only).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:58 (ArrowPointerAngle default 60), clamps :102-104 + :211, geometry :118-185 (CalcTrianglePoints -> TTrianglePoints, 3 points) drawn with Canvas.Polygon(FT) :288.
user_impact: Same-named control, different picture: a ported TArrow turns from a bare triangle into a block arrow with a shaft, and the one dimension the user tuned (the apex angle) has no counterpart - HeadRatio is a length fraction, not an angle.

what_it_does: ShadowType = (stNone, stIn, stOut, stEtchedIn, stEtchedOut, stFilled), default stEtchedIn, draws a 3D edge along the arrow (or an offset drop triangle for stFilled); ShadowColor (default cl3DShadow) is its colour.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "shadowtype|shadowcolor" over source/ returns NOTHING (source/tyControls.ShadowLabel.pas is a TEXT shadow, unrelated). TTyArrow.RenderTo (source/tyControls.Arrow.pas:210-273) fills and strokes the polygon and never calls DrawFrame, so even the theme's own shadow path (source/tyControls.Base.pas:833-834 / :1109-1110) is bypassed - this control can carry no shadow at all, from property or theme.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/arrow.pp:67-68 (ShadowType default stEtchedIn, ShadowColor default cl3DShadow), type :27, painted :240-271 (ShadowLine/ShadowTriangle) and :282-291.
user_impact: TArrow's DEFAULT look is etched (stEtchedIn), so every ported arrow loses its 3D edge and becomes flat, with no property and no theme token to restore it.

what_it_does: trHorizontal/trVertical (default trHorizontal). A vertical divider swaps the bevel axis and draws the caption rotated 900, and ShouldAutoAdjust flips which axis auto-sizes.
ours_evidence: grep -ri "orientation" over source/ hits CoolBar, GlyphButtons, LevelMeter, ProgressBar, Steps, TrackBar, UpDown - NOT Divider. source/tyControls.Divider.pas is horizontal by construction: TyDividerLayout (:33-34, :67-129) reasons in AClientWidth with a horizontal rule band, and RenderTo:230 calls it that way. The rotated-caption capability the library already owns (source/tyControls.Menu.pas:876 P.Bitmap.TextOutAngle(..., 900, ...)) is not wired here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:81-82 (property Orientation ... default trHorizontal), setter :145-156, layout :197-200 + :294-311 + :356-362, rotated caption :374-378, ShouldAutoAdjust :431-436.
user_impact: There is no vertical section divider: a two-column dialog or side-by-side panel pair cannot get a labelled vertical rule, and a ported .lfm with Orientation = trVertical fails to load.

what_it_does: BevelStyle (bsLowered/bsRaised, default bsLowered) picks a sunken or raised 3D rule; BevelWidth (default -1) sets its thickness, -1 meaning 'derive from the caption height' (max(3, textheight div 5)).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "bevelstyle|bevelwidth" over source/ returns NOTHING. source/tyControls.Divider.pas always strokes a flat band whose thickness is a fixed ruleThick := P.Scale(1) (:227-228) in the theme border colour (:214-218); the class (:37-63) has no thickness or 3D property. TTyBevel has Style/Shape but is a different control and cannot be a divider.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:67 (BevelStyle default bsLowered), :68 (BevelWidth default -1); auto thickness :183-195 (FBevelHeight := Max(3, FTextExtent.cy div 5)); drawn via Canvas.Frame3D :216.
user_impact: The divider is permanently a 1px flat hairline: no raised/lowered groove (the classic section-divider look) and no thicker rule to match a large-font heading; both .lfm properties fail to stream.

what_it_does: Pixels of clear space between the caption and the rule on each side, default 10.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas:225 hard-codes it: gap := P.Scale(6). grep -ri "captionspacing" over source/ returns NOTHING. It is neither a property nor a theme token - all inputs to TyDividerLayout are computed literals (:225-228), which also breaks this codebase's own rule that visual values must come from theme tokens.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:71-72 (property CaptionSpacing ... default 10), setter :131-136, used :328 and :349-359.
user_impact: The caption-to-rule gap cannot be changed by property or by skin, and a ported divider's 10px spacing silently becomes 6px, so a form's dividers no longer match the spacing rhythm they were designed for.

what_it_does: Pixel offset of the caption from the leading edge, default 60; 0 means flush to the edge and any negative value means 'centre the caption' - so it expresses alignment AND an exact indent.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas:58 property Alignment: TAlignment ... default taLeftJustify - three discrete positions only (TyDividerLayout:98-128 handles taRightJustify/taCenter/taLeftJustify). grep -ri "leftindent" over source/ returns NOTHING; the layout function takes no pixel-offset parameter at all (signature :33-34).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:80 (property LeftIndent ... default 60), setter :138-143, three-way logic :322-333 (>0 indent, =0 flush, <0 centred).
user_impact: TDividerBevel's default is a 60px indent, so every ported divider's caption jumps to the left edge; and a caption aligned to a form's label column (the usual reason for the indent) cannot be expressed. Ours does add taRightJustify, which theirs lacks.

what_it_does: Which decoration the rule is drawn with: gsSimple (default), gsDouble (two rules), gsHorLines / gsVerLines (repeating shadow+highlight line pairs), gsGripper (the themed splitter gripper) and gsButton (a themed button face).
ours_evidence: grep -ri "tgrabstyle|gsgripper|gsdouble|gshorlines" over source/ returns NOTHING; TTyDivider has no Style property at all (published block source/tyControls.Divider.pas:52-62) and always fills one solid band (StrokeSeg :178-188).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:89 (property Style: TGrabStyle ... default gsSimple); type C:/lazarus/lcl/comctrls.pp:2436 (gsSimple, gsDouble, gsHorLines, gsVerLines, gsGripper, gsButton); all six painted at dividerbevel.pas:215-277.
user_impact: Five of six divider looks are unavailable, including the gripper and button faces used as drag handles/section headers; a ported Style = gsGripper both fails to load and has no visual equivalent.

what_it_does: Boolean, default True. When False the control fills its client rect with Color before drawing the bevel and caption.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas:196-200 deliberately never paints a background ('The divider is a transparent overlay (like a default TTyLabel)... never paint the theme background fill') - it honours opacity only. grep -ri "transparent" over source/ shows the property IS published on the sibling label (source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:96 with SetTransparent:170-175 and the DrawFrame branch :363-364) but not on the divider: the pattern exists and was not wired here.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:90 (property Transparent ... default True), setter :165-170, honoured :284-288 (Canvas.FillRect(ClientRect) with Color when False).
user_impact: A divider over a photo/glass background cannot be given an opaque plate to keep its caption legible, and any theme rule that sets a background for TyDivider is ignored outright.

what_it_does: TDividerBevel auto-sizes by default: CalculatePreferredSize returns max(caption height, bevel height) on the layout axis and 0 on the other, ShouldAutoAdjust restricts growth to the right axis, and SetAutoSize re-fits immediately.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas:52-62 publishes no AutoSize, and the class (:37-63) implements neither CalculatePreferredSize nor ShouldAutoAdjust - the height is a one-shot constructor guess, Height := TyDensityHeight(ActiveController, 24) (:139), which never re-measures when caption, font or skin changes. The pattern exists on the sibling label (CalculatePreferredSize source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:314-340, size floor :201-238, theme-switch re-fit :240-256), so this is unwired rather than unavailable.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:65 (property AutoSize default True) set in the ctor :452; CalculatePreferredSize :410-429; ShouldAutoAdjust :431-436; SetAutoSize :394-401; TextChanged/FontChanged/BoundsChanged invalidate the cached size :381-408.
user_impact: A divider whose caption uses a large font or a roomier skin clips its text and nothing corrects it (the 24px ctor guess is frozen at construction), and a ported .lfm carrying AutoSize = True fails to stream.

what_it_does: TDividerBevel publishes TControl's own Caption, i.e. the control's Text, so Caption/Text are one string and a change routes through TextChanged/CM_TEXTCHANGED.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas:39 declares its OWN field FCaption: TCaption and :53 a NEW property Caption: TCaption read FCaption write SetCaption that HIDES TControl.Caption; SetCaption (:155-160) only Invalidates. So Text and Caption become two independent strings: TControl.SetName assigns Text := Value when csSetCaption is in ControlStyle (C:/lazarus/lcl/include/control.inc:3529-3540, and TControl.Create adds csSetCaption at :5264), which TTyDivider never removes. Every other ty label uses the inherited one (source/tyControls.TyLabel.pas:84 'property Caption;').
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:63 (property Caption; - TControl's), read back in Paint :313/:371/:377 and re-measured from TextChanged :403-408.
user_impact: Same name, different storage: dropping a TTyDivider in the designer sets Text to the component name and leaves Caption empty (TDividerBevel shows its name), and any generic/RTTI or LCL path that writes Text updates a string the divider never draws - with no repaint.

what_it_does: TDividerBevel's constructor adds fsBold to Font.Style, so a section divider's caption is bold unless the user clears it.
ours_evidence: source/tyControls.Divider.pas ctor (:133-140) sets no font, and the control is theme-locked: RenderTo passes S.FontWeight from the resolved style (:243), which for TyDivider resolves through the shared label rule 'TyLabel, TyHtmlLabel, TyLinkLabel, TyShadowLabel, TyGlowLabel, TyDivider, TyCharImage { ... font-weight: var(--font-weight-normal); }' (source/tyControls.DefaultTheme.pas:288-292). LCL Font.Style is ignored by the theme-locked text path, so setting fsBold in code or the OI changes nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/components/lazcontrols/dividerbevel.pas:448-449 (if (AOwner = nil) or not (csLoading in AOwner.ComponentState) then Font.Style := Font.Style + [fsBold]).
user_impact: A ported section divider loses its bold caption and cannot get it back the obvious way (Font.Style); it needs a theme rule or a StyleOverride string, so ported forms lose the visual weight that separated their sections.

what_it_does: One published set of ~32 behaviour flags the designer user flips in one place: goEditing, goRangeSelect, goRowSizing, goColSizing, goRowMoving, goColMoving, goTabs, goRowSelect, goAlwaysShowEditor, goAutoAddRows, goCellHints, goTruncCellHints, goCellEllipsis, goDblClickAutoSize, goFixedColSizing, goRowHighlight, goHeaderHotTracking, goHeaderPushedLook, goSelectionActive, goSmoothScroll, goScrollKeepVisible, goRelaxedRowSelect, goColSpanning, goFixedRowNumbering, goDontScrollPartCell, goFixedVertLine/goFixedHorzLine/goVertLine/goHorzLine.
ours_evidence: grep 'property Options' over tyControls.Grid.pas returned nothing; the only Options in the group are TTyHeader.Options (tyControls.Columns.pas:217) and TTyColumn.Options (tyControls.Columns.pas:96). The concepts are scattered as separate members: ReadOnly (Grid.pas:2192), SelectionMode (2196), ShowRowNumbers (1228), AlternateRows (1245), ShowFocusCell (1144), GridLineStyle (1242), MergeCells (2100). Row resizing is gated only on ShowIndicator (Grid.pas:4014), Tab navigation is unconditional (Grid.pas:7262) - neither has a toggle.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:86-120 (TGridOption enum), :1280 'property Options: TGridOptions ... default DefaultGridOptions', republished on TDrawGrid (:1639) and TStringGrid (:1884).
user_impact: Any .lfm that sets Options=[...] cannot be ported at all; each flag must be hand-translated and about eight of them (goAutoAddRows, goAlwaysShowEditor, goTruncCellHints, goFixedColSizing, goDblClickAutoSize, goHeaderPushedLook, goTabs off, goDontScrollPartCell) have nothing to translate to.

what_it_does: Second flag set: goScrollToLastCol / goScrollToLastRow (allow the last col/row to become LeftCol/TopRow), goEditorParentColor, goEditorParentFont, goCopyWithoutTrailingLinebreak.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'Options2\|goScrollToLast\|TrailingLinebreak' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:122-129 (TGridOption2), :1281 'property Options2 ... default DefaultGridOptions2'.
user_impact: Cannot let the user scroll so the last row sits at the top of the viewport, and clipboard text always carries whatever trailing newline our exporter emits.

member: Col, Row, Selection, Editor, EditorMode (on the draw-grid level)
what_it_does: LCL's TDrawGrid is a fully interactive grid: it has a cell cursor, a selection rectangle, an in-place editor and OnGetEditText/OnSetEditText, while still getting its content from the host. Only the storage is absent.
ours_evidence: TTyDrawGrid (Grid.pas:1327-1346) publishes exactly one member, OnGetCellText. FCol/FRow are declared on TTyStringGrid (Grid.pas:1405-1406) and Col/Row are published there (2188-2189); TTyCustomGrid.IsActiveCell is hard-coded False (Grid.pas:3810-3813). grep 'property Col\b' returned only the TTyStringGrid one.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1467 'property Col;', :1484 'property Row;', :1489 'property Selection;', :1471 'property Editor;', :1473 'property EditorMode;' - all republished public on TCustomDrawGrid, i.e. present on TDrawGrid.
user_impact: A TDrawGrid used as a virtual, host-fed but navigable grid has no counterpart: TTyDrawGrid cannot show a cursor or a selection at all, forcing a port onto TTyStringGrid and its cell storage even when the data lives elsewhere.

what_it_does: Read/write column count; setting it grows or shrinks the grid without touching a Columns collection.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ColCount' over source/ hits only local range parameters (Grid.pas:2133, 11441 'AColCount'). Columns are only reachable as Header.Columns (Grid.pas:1206) whose Count is read-only TCollection.Count.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1229 'property ColCount: Integer read GetColCount write SetColCount default 5', republished on TDrawGrid (:1607) and TStringGrid (:1852).
user_impact: Grid.ColCount := 8 - the single most common line in TStringGrid code - does not compile; the host must loop Header.Columns.Add / Delete itself.

what_it_does: Indexed read/write column width in pixels, the twin of RowHeights[].
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ColWidths' over source/ returned nothing. Ours has RowHeights[ARow] (Grid.pas:949) but the column twin only via Header.Columns.Items[i] cast to TTyColumn then .Width (Columns.pas:88; call pattern at Grid.pas:11455).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1236 'property ColWidths[aCol: Integer]: Integer read GetColWidths write SetColWidths', republished on TCustomDrawGrid (:1468).
user_impact: The RowHeights/ColWidths symmetry every LCL grid user relies on is broken; column width needs a two-step cast through the header.

what_it_does: Width new/unsized columns get, the column twin of DefaultRowHeight.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'DefaultColWidth' over source/ returned nothing. We publish DefaultRowHeight (Grid.pas:1212) but the column default is only TTyColumn.Width's 'default 100' literal (Columns.pas:88).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1237 'property DefaultColWidth: Integer read GetDefColWidth write SetDefColWidth stored DefaultColWidthIsStored'.
user_impact: Setting a uniform column width for a wide grid means writing a loop; and the theme's density axis cannot drive column width the way it drives DefaultRowHeight.

what_it_does: Single published property selecting ssNone / ssHorizontal / ssVertical / ssBoth / ssAutoHorizontal / ssAutoVertical / ssAutoBoth.
ours_evidence: Ours splits it in two: VertScrollBarMode and HorzScrollBarMode (Grid.pas:1124-1127), of type TTyGridScrollBarMode (gsbAuto/gsbAlways/gsbNever). Both sit in a **public** section (opened at Grid.pas:1119) - not published - so neither streams from a .lfm nor appears in the Object Inspector. grep 'ScrollBars' over source/ hits only other controls (ListBox, Memo, ScrollBox...).
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1293 'property ScrollBars: TScrollStyle read FScrollBars write SetScrollBars default ssAutoBoth', published on TDrawGrid (:1650) and TStringGrid (:1895).
user_impact: ScrollBars=ssNone in a ported .lfm raises 'Unknown property'; and even in code the ty equivalents cannot be set at design time.

what_it_does: The actual colour of the banded rows, plus a flag saying whether banding counts from the first fixed row or the first normal row.
ours_evidence: Ours has only the boolean AlternateRows (Grid.pas:1245, 'default False') and takes the colour from the TyGridCellAlt theme key. grep -ri 'AlternateColor\|AltColorStartNormal' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: C:/lazarus/lcl/grids.pas:1221 'property AlternateColor: TColor read FAlternateColor write SetAlternateColor stored IsAltColorStored', :1253 'property AltColorStartNormal'. Published on TDrawGrid (:1597) / TStringGrid (:1842).
user_impact: AlternateColor:=clMoneyGreen in ported code does not compile; and where the band should start cannot be chosen, so on a grid with fixed rows the stripes can land on the wrong parity.
