ours_evidence: grep -ril 'LoadFromFile|SaveToFile|LoadFromStream|SaveToStream' over source/ hits Controller, Grid, ImageView, PreviewBox, StyleModel, ThemeBundle, ThemeLint, ThemeRegistry — never tyControls.TreeView.pas.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3729-3732 LoadFromFile / LoadFromStream / SaveToFile / SaveToStream.
user_impact: No built-in tree persistence; with no node text storage either (see Text gap) there is nothing generic to serialise.

what_it_does: SortType (stNone/stData/stText/stBoth) keeps a tree auto-sorted as nodes are added; AlphaSort sorts by text with no handler; CustomSort(SortProc) sorts with a plain function.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'SortType|AlphaSort|CustomSort' over source/ returned nothing. Ours has only :562 `Sort(Node, Column, ADirection, DoInit)` and :564 `SortTree(Column, ADirection)`, both of which call :560 DoCompare, which returns 0 when OnCompareNodes (:650) is unassigned — so sorting without writing a compare handler is a silent no-op.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3704 `property SortType: TSortType ... default stNone`; :3709 AlphaSort; :3712 CustomSort(SortProc: TTreeNodeCompare); :978 TSortType.
user_impact: 'Sort this tree alphabetically' needs an OnCompareNodes handler, and there is no auto-resort-on-insert mode at all.

what_it_does: A node can show a different icon when selected, a second 'state' icon from a separate image list, and an overlay badge.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:117 declares `TTyVTImageKind = (ikNormal, ikSelected, ikState, ikOverlay)` and :120 OnGetImageIndex takes a Kind — but grep -n 'ikState|ikOverlay|ikSelected' tyControls.TreeView.pas shows the only call sites are :3813 and :4067, both passing ikNormal. The three other kinds are never requested, so no selected/state/overlay image is ever drawn. grep -ri 'StateImages' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3171 SelectedIndex; :3172 StateIndex; :3167 OverlayIndex; :3785-3786 StateImages/StateImagesWidth; :3686 OnGetSelectedIndex.
user_impact: The API advertises four image kinds but only the normal one works; a folder tree cannot show an open-folder icon on the selected node, and checkbox/state overlays via StateImages are impossible.

what_it_does: Per-node image draw effect (gdeNormal/gdeDisabled/gdeHighlighted/gde1Bit) — e.g. a greyed icon for a cut or unavailable node.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:120-122 OnGetImageIndex has `var Ghosted: Boolean`, and :3811-3813 sets `ghosted := False` then passes it to the handler — but the value is never read again: the icon is queued at :3817-3824 (pendingIcons X/Y/Idx only) with no effect field. grep -ri 'NodeEffect|Ghosted' over source/ finds Ghosted only in this dead path.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3166 `property NodeEffect: TGraphicsDrawEffect read FNodeEffect write SetImageEffect`; :3069 SetImageEffect; :2914 ncImageEffect.
user_impact: Setting Ghosted:=True in OnGetImageIndex looks supported and does nothing; there is no way to grey a node's icon.

what_it_does: The node image list. LCL accepts any TCustomImageList descendant.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:599 `property Images: TImageList read FImages write SetImages` (field :289 `FImages: TImageList`). TImageList is a descendant of TCustomImageList, so the property is NARROWER than LCL's: a TCustomImageList (or the library's own tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:168 `TTyVirtualImageList = class(TTyComponent)`) cannot be assigned.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3768 `property Images: TCustomImageList read FImages write SetImages`.
user_impact: Code that keeps its icons in a TCustomImageList descendant (including this library's own TTyVirtualImageList, which TTyListView requires) will not compile against TTyTreeView.Images.

what_it_does: Hide an individual node (and its subtree) without deleting it — used for filtering.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:50 TTyNodeState includes nsVisible and the walkers honour it (:2808, :2835, :2854, :2997, :3149), but :1918 `Result^.States := [nsVisible]` is the only place it is ever set and grep -n 'nsVisible' tyControls.TreeView.pas shows no Exclude/clear anywhere and no public Visible[Node] accessor (public indexed props are :516-526 Expanded/Selected/CheckType/CheckState/Checked/NodeHeight).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3179 `property Visible: Boolean read GetVisible write SetVisible default True`; setter :3079.
user_impact: Filtering a tree means deleting and re-adding nodes; the engine already supports invisible nodes but the switch is not exposed.

what_it_does: Grey out a single node so it cannot be selected, with a dedicated disabled ink colour, and skip such nodes when navigating.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:50-52 TTyNodeState has no nsEnabled member; navigation helpers :493-495 GetFirstVisibleNoInit/GetNextVisibleNoInit/GetPreviousVisibleNoInit take no enabled-only flag. grep -ri 'DisabledFontColor' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3180 `property Enabled: Boolean read GetEnabled write SetEnabled default True`; :3660 `DisabledFontColor: TColor ... default clGrayText`; :3108/:3120/:3121 GetFirstVisibleChild/GetNextVisible/GetNextVisibleSibling(aEnabledOnly).
user_impact: You cannot present an unavailable node; the whole tree is all-or-nothing enabled.

what_it_does: Mark a node as cut (dimmed, for clipboard cut) or as the current drop target (highlight box while dragging over it).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:50 TTyNodeState = (nsInitialized, nsHasChildren, nsExpanded, nsVisible, nsSelected, nsHeightMeasured, nsDeleting, nsClearing) — no cut/drop-target state. The only drop-target notion is :583 `property DropTargetNode: PTyTreeNode read FDropTarget` which is READ-ONLY and only meaningful during an internal toNodeDrag gesture (:276, cleared by :580 EndNodeDrag). grep -ri 'Cut' for a node state over source/ finds only TTyListItemState lisCut (tyControls.ListView.pas:46), i.e. the list has the concept, the tree does not.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3150 `property Cut: Boolean`; :3153 `property DropTarget: Boolean read GetDropTarget write SetDropTarget`; control-level :3762 `property DropTarget: TTreeNode read GetDropTarget write SetDropTarget`.
user_impact: External drag-and-drop cannot highlight the node under the cursor, and a cut/paste UI has no dimmed-source feedback.

member: InsertMarkNode / InsertMarkType / SetInsertMark / SetInsertMarkAt / GetInsertMarkAt (+ tvoAutoInsertMark)
what_it_does: Draws an insertion caret between nodes while dragging (as-first-child / as-prev-sibling / as-next-sibling), optionally maintained automatically.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'InsertMark' over source/ returned nothing. Ours has an internal drop mark only inside the toNodeDrag gesture: :276-277 FDropTarget/FDropMode with :584 read-only DropMode and :441 SetActiveDragState (protected), driven by :435 DropModeFromY — not settable from outside and not available for LCL drag-and-drop.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3770-3771 InsertMarkNode/InsertMarkType; :3718 GetInsertMarkAt; :3720 SetInsertMark; :3722 SetInsertMarkAt; :3374-3379 TTreeViewInsertMarkType; :3338 tvoAutoInsertMark.
user_impact: A reorder-by-drag UI built on standard LCL drag-and-drop has no way to show where the node will land.

member: TopItem / BottomItem / ScrolledLeft / ScrolledTop (writable scroll position)
what_it_does: Read and SET the scroll position: which node is at the top, and the pixel scroll offsets.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:529-531 exposes `OffsetY`, `OffsetX`, `RangeX` as READ-ONLY (`read FOffsetY` etc.); the only public way to move the view is :515 ScrollIntoView(Node). grep -n 'FOffsetY :=' shows all writes are internal (:1490, :1495, :1622-1626, :1693). grep -ri 'TopItem|BottomItem|ScrolledLeft|ScrolledTop' over source/ finds TopItem only in tyControls.Menu.pas; nothing for the tree.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3787 `property TopItem: TTreeNode read GetTopItem write SetTopItem`; :3759 BottomItem; :3698-3699 ScrolledLeft/ScrolledTop (republished public on TTreeView at :3800-3801).
user_impact: Save/restore of a tree's scroll position across a refresh is impossible; you can only re-scroll to a node.

what_it_does: Chooses which scrollbars exist (ssNone/ssHorizontal/ssVertical/ssBoth/ssAuto*).
ours_evidence: grep -n 'ScrollBars' tyControls.TreeView.pas / tyControls.ListView.pas shows only the internal `UpdateScrollBars` method (TreeView.pas:349, ListView.pas:402) and comments; there is no published ScrollBars property. Both controls always create both bars in the ctor (TreeView.pas:297-298 + :1814-1865; ListView.pas:222 + :829) and show/hide them automatically.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3777 `property ScrollBars: TScrollStyle read FScrollBars write SetScrollBars default ssBoth` (published TTreeView :3837); :1589 same on TCustomListView (published TListView :1733).
user_impact: A tree/list embedded in an outer scroller cannot suppress its own bars, and ssNone (fixed viewport) is unreachable.

what_it_does: Chooses the expander look (themed / +- / arrow / filled arrow / angle bracket), its size, line thickness and colour, or lets you draw it yourself.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:601 has only `ShowButtons: Boolean`. The glyph is hard-coded at :3714-3717: `P.DrawGlyph(btnRect, tgChevronDown/tgChevronRight, NodeStyle.TextColor, P.Scale(1), 2)` — note it calls TTyPainter.DrawGlyph directly rather than tyControls.Base.pas:787 TyDrawGlyph, so even the theme's --glyph-chevron-down override (tyControls.Base.pas:764-765) is bypassed. grep -ri 'ExpandSign' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3766 ExpandSignType (default tvestTheme, values :3366-3372); :3764 ExpandSignSize; :3765 ExpandSignWidth; :3763 ExpandSignColor; :3677 OnCustomDrawArrow.
user_impact: The expander is always a chevron in the node text colour — a Win-classic +/- tree or a custom arrow is impossible, and the theme's own glyph token does not even reach it.

what_it_does: Colour and pen style (psPattern/psDot/psSolid) of the connector lines between nodes.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:602 has ShowTreeLines on/off only. The paint code at :3673-3697 draws with `TyColorToBGRA(S.BorderColor)` — the control's own border colour token — and always with a solid `P.Bitmap.DrawLine(...)`; there is no dedicated theme token (grep over tyControls.DefaultTheme.pas for TyTree* keys yields only TyTreeView / TyTreeNode / TyTreeCheckBox / TyTreeHeader / TyTreeHeaderSection / TyTreeSelect — no tree-line key). grep -ri 'TreeLineColor|TreeLinePen' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3788 `property TreeLineColor: TColor ... default clWindowFrame`; :3789 `property TreeLinePenStyle: TPenStyle ... default psPattern`.
user_impact: Tree lines cannot be recoloured or dotted, and they silently inherit whatever the theme sets as the control's border colour — so no themed equivalent exists either.

what_it_does: Draws a horizontal separator line under each top-level row, in a settable colour.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'ShowSeparators|SeparatorColor' over source/ returned nothing; the tree's published display flags are :601-605 (ShowButtons/ShowTreeLines/ShowRoot/ToggleOnDblClick/HotTrack). The list view has GridLines (tyControls.ListView.pas:505) but the tree has no row-rule concept.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3703 `property ShowSeparators: Boolean ... default false` (published TTreeView :3846); :3784 SeparatorColor default clGray; :3349 tvoShowSeparators.
user_impact: No row rules in a tree; a report-style tree cannot show the separators the LCL control offers.

what_it_does: Automatically expands the node that gains focus and collapses the previous one.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'AutoExpand' over source/ returned nothing. Options set is tyControls.TreeView.pas:31-33 (toMultiSelect, toCheckSupport, toFullRowSelect, toAutoTristateTracking, toVariableNodeHeight, toIncrementalSearch, toOwnerDraw, toEditable, toNodeDrag) — no auto-expand member; the only expand automation is :513-514 FullExpand/FullCollapse.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3654 `property AutoExpand: Boolean read GetAutoExpand write SetAutoExpand default False` (published TTreeView :3805); :3336 tvoAutoExpand.
user_impact: A navigation tree that opens as you move through it must be hand-coded in OnFocusChanged.

what_it_does: A right-click moves the selection to the clicked node before the popup menu opens.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'RightClickSelect' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.TreeView.pas MouseDown (:448, body around :4400+) reacts to mbLeft only for selection; PopupMenu comes from tyControls.Base.pas:226 with no node-selection hook.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3695 `property RightClickSelect: Boolean ... default False` (published TTreeView :3835); :3344 tvoRightClickSelect.
user_impact: A context menu on a tree acts on whatever was selected before the right-click — the classic 'wrong node' bug.

what_it_does: When the control loses focus the selection highlight is hidden (or kept, if False).
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'HideSelection' over source/ hits tyControls.DefaultTheme.pas, tyControls.Grid.pas and tyControls.Memo.pas — the concept exists in the library but neither tyControls.TreeView.pas nor tyControls.ListView.pas has it. Selection styling comes from the resolved 'TyTreeNode'/'TyListViewItem' :selected style with no focus qualifier (TreeView.pas:3700-3760 paint path; ListView.pas:340 StatesFor).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3656-3657 `property HideSelection: Boolean ... default True` on TCustomTreeView (published TTreeView :3822); :1584 same on TCustomListView (published TListView :1717).
user_impact: Two side-by-side lists both show a strong selection, so the user cannot tell which one has focus — the exact problem HideSelection exists to solve.

what_it_does: Automatic per-item tooltip showing the full text when a caption is clipped by the column/viewport.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'ToolTips' over source/ hits only tyControls.Chart.pas. The tree/list rely on the inherited single-string Hint (tyControls.Base.pas:208-209 Hint/ShowHint); nothing measures a clipped caption to raise a hint (TreeView.pas:3826-3840 caption path just clips, ListView.pas:2696 likewise).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3705 `property ToolTips: Boolean ... default True` (published TTreeView :3853), backed by FHintWnd :3463 / UpdateTooltip :3542; :1599 ToolTips on TCustomListView (published TListView :1745).
user_impact: Long file names in a narrow column are unreadable — there is no way to reveal the full text on hover.

what_it_does: Controls what multi-select is allowed to do: ctrl-click, shift-range, visible nodes only, siblings only.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'MultiSelectStyle' over source/ returned nothing. Ours has only the on/off flag toMultiSelect (tyControls.TreeView.pas:31) with hard-coded Ctrl/Shift behaviour in KeyDown/MouseDown (:453, :448) and helpers :505 SelectRange / :371 AddRangeToSelection.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3774-3775 `property MultiSelectStyle: TMultiSelectStyle ... default DefaultMultiSelectStyle`; :2902-2903 TMultiSelectStyles; :3361 DefaultMultiSelectStyle (published TTreeView :3829).
user_impact: A tree that should only allow selecting siblings (or only visible nodes) cannot be restricted; the gesture set is fixed.

what_it_does: The four most-used TTreeView switches: full-row selection, multi-select, connector lines, and whether F2/click editing is allowed.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:31-33 exposes RowSelect as the option `toFullRowSelect` and MultiSelect as `toMultiSelect` inside `Options` (:587), not as Boolean properties; ShowLines is spelled `ShowTreeLines` (:602); ReadOnly is inverted into the opt-in option `toEditable` (:26-27 comment, :31-33) so editing is OFF by default whereas LCL ReadOnly=False means editing is ON. grep -ri 'RowSelect' over source/ finds tyControls.ListView.pas:506 (the list DOES have a RowSelect property), which makes the tree's naming inconsistent inside the library too.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3697 RowSelect (published :3836); :3662 MultiSelect (published :3828); :3701 ShowLines (published :3844); :3694 `ReadOnly: Boolean ... default False` (published :3834).
user_impact: Every ported line — Tree.RowSelect := True, Tree.MultiSelect := True, Tree.ShowLines := False, Tree.ReadOnly := False — fails to compile, and the ReadOnly default is inverted, so ported code silently loses inline editing.

what_it_does: Default row height, optionally auto-derived from the font.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:595 `property DefaultNodeHeight: Integer read GetDefaultNodeHeight write SetDefaultNodeHeight stored FDefaultNodeHeightExplicit` — different name; and there is no auto-from-font mode: unset it follows the theme's --item-height token (:191-194, :329). grep -ri 'DefaultItemHeight' over source/ hits only tyControls.ListGroupPanel.pas.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3761 `property DefaultItemHeight: integer read FDefItemHeight write SetDefaultItemHeight stored DefaultItemHeightIsStored`; :3339 tvoAutoItemHeight; :3634 UpdateDefaultItemHeight.
user_impact: Tree.DefaultItemHeight := 24 does not compile, and rows never follow the control's Font size (they follow the theme token instead).

what_it_does: The one selected/current node — read it, or assign a node to select it.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:517 `property Selected[Node: PTyTreeNode]: Boolean read GetSelected write SetSelected` — SAME NAME, an indexed Boolean, so `Tree.Selected` is not a node. The nearest equivalent is :518 `property FocusedNode: PTyTreeNode read GetFocusedNode write SetFocusedNode`. grep over source/ shows no `Selected: PTyTreeNode` style property anywhere.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3778 `property Selected: TTreeNode read GetSelection write SetSelection`.
user_impact: The single most-typed line in TreeView code (`if Tree.Selected <> nil then ... Tree.Selected.Text`) compiles to something completely different or not at all — a silent porting trap rather than a clean error.

what_it_does: Random-access to the multi-selection list plus its count.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:506 `function SelectedCount: Integer` (different name, Integer not Cardinal) and :509-510 GetFirstSelected/GetNextSelected — a linear walk only; there is no Selections[i] indexed property. grep -ri 'GetFirstMultiSelected|SelectionCount' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3783 `property Selections[AIndex: Integer]: TTreeNode read GetSelections`; :3780 SelectionCount: Cardinal; :3736-3737 GetFirstMultiSelected/GetLastMultiSelected; TTreeNodes :3275 GetSelections, :3302 SelectionCount.
user_impact: `for i := 0 to Tree.SelectionCount-1 do Use(Tree.Selections[i])` — the standard multi-select loop — has to be rewritten as a pointer walk.

member: Select(Node, ShiftState) / Select(array of TTreeNode) / Select(TList)
what_it_does: Programmatically set the selection, either honouring a shift-state (as if clicked) or replacing it with a whole set of nodes at once.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas public selection API is :504 InternalSetSelected, :505 SelectRange(AAnchor, ATarget), :508 SelectAll, :512 ClearSelection and the indexed :517 Selected[Node] — one node or a contiguous range at a time; no set-based Select and no shift-state-aware variant. grep -ri 'procedure Select(' over source/ finds no such overloads.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3738-3740 `procedure Select(Node: TTreeNode; ShiftState: TShiftState = []); procedure Select(const Nodes: array of TTreeNode); virtual; procedure Select(Nodes: TList); virtual;`
user_impact: Restoring an arbitrary saved multi-selection means looping and toggling per node, firing change events repeatedly.

member: StoreCurrentSelection / ApplyStoredSelection / LockSelectionChangeEvent / UnlockSelectionChangeEvent / SelectionVisible / MakeSelectionVisible / ClearInvisibleSelection
what_it_does: Save the selection by text path and restore it after a refresh, suppress OnSelectionChanged while doing bulk work, and scroll/clean the selection.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'StoreCurrentSelection|ApplyStoredSelection|LockSelectionChangeEvent|ClearInvisibleSelection' over source/ returned nothing; 'SelectionVisible' hits only tyControls.ListBox.pas. Ours has :515 ScrollIntoView(Node) (single node) and fires :630 OnSelectionChanged with no lock/unlock pair.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3744-3745 StoreCurrentSelection/ApplyStoredSelection; :3734-3735 LockSelectionChangeEvent/UnlockSelectionChangeEvent; :3741-3743 SelectionVisible/MakeSelectionVisible/ClearInvisibleSelection.
user_impact: The standard 'rebuild the tree and put the user back where they were' pattern must be written from scratch, and bulk selection changes storm OnSelectionChanged.

member: MoveToNextNode / MoveToPrevNode / MovePageDown / MovePageUp / MoveLeft / MoveRight / MoveExpand / MoveCollapse / MoveHome / MoveEnd
what_it_does: Public keyboard-motion API so an external toolbar/shortcut can drive the tree exactly as the arrow keys do.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'MoveToNextNode|MovePageDown|MoveHome' over source/ returned nothing. The equivalent logic lives only inside tyControls.TreeView.pas:453 `procedure KeyDown(var Key: Word; Shift: TShiftState); override` with no callable entry points; the public API has :369 MoveFocusOnly (private) and :518 FocusedNode.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3746-3755 MoveToNextNode/MoveToPrevNode/MovePageDown/MovePageUp/MoveLeft/MoveRight/MoveExpand/MoveCollapse/MoveHome/MoveEnd (each with ASelect: Boolean).
user_impact: Up/Down buttons on a toolbar, or a search-next command, cannot reuse the tree's own navigation semantics.

member: FindNodeWithText / FindNodeWithTextPath / FindNodeWithData / FindNode / IndexOfText / GetTextPath / PathDelimiter
what_it_does: Locate a node by its caption, by a delimited caption path ('Root/Child/Leaf'), or by its Data pointer; and produce a node's text path.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'FindNodeWithText|GetTextPath|IndexOfText' over source/ returned nothing; 'PathDelimiter' hits tyControls.Dialogs.SelectPath.pas / ShellComboBox / ShellTreeView / StyleModel / ThemeBundle / ThemeLint — never tyControls.TreeView.pas. The tree offers no search at all (public API :485-510); the only text lookup is the internal incremental-search walk :335-337 GetNodeSearchText/NodeMatchesSearch/DoIncrementalSearch, which are private.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3262-3265 FindNodeWithData/FindNodeWithText/FindNodeWithTextPath/FindTopLvlNode; :3105 TTreeNode.FindNode; :3133 IndexOfText; :3130 GetTextPath; :3693 PathDelimiter.
user_impact: 'Select the node for this path' — the core operation of any settings or file tree — has to be written by hand, and there is no node-by-data lookup even though nodes carry a data blob.

member: GetPrev / GetNextSkipChildren / GetLastSubChild / GetFirstSibling / GetLastSibling / GetNextChild / GetPrevChild / GetParentNodeOfAbsoluteLevel
what_it_does: The rest of the node-traversal vocabulary: full-tree backwards walk, skip a subtree, jump to the deepest last node, first/last sibling, child stepping, ancestor at a given level.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:485-495 provides GetFirstChild, GetLastChild, GetNextSibling, GetPrevSibling, GetParent, GetNodeLevel, GetFirst, GetNext, GetFirstVisibleNoInit, GetNextVisibleNoInit, GetPreviousVisibleNoInit — no GetPrev (grep -n 'GetPrev' tyControls.TreeView.pas shows only GetPrevSibling :488/:2729 and GetPreviousVisibleNoInit :495/:2840), and grep -ri 'GetNextSkipChildren|GetLastSubChild|HasAsParent' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3123 GetPrev; :3119 GetNextSkipChildren; :3112 GetLastSubChild; :3107 GetFirstSibling; :3111 GetLastSibling; :3115 GetNextChild; :3124 GetPrevChild; :3122 GetParentNodeOfAbsoluteLevel; TTreeNodes :3270-3273 GetLastExpandedSubNode/GetLastNode/GetLastSubNode/GetLastVisibleNode.
user_impact: Any algorithm that walks a tree backwards, or skips a subtree, must reimplement the pointer arithmetic — and GetPrev's absence is easy to miss because GetPrevSibling is present.

what_it_does: Delete just a node's children, expand every ancestor so a node becomes reachable, scroll it into view, and select a whole sibling group.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:464 DeleteNode(Node) deletes the node itself and :465 Clear() empties everything — there is no children-only delete (SetChildCount(Node,0) at :462 is the closest, and it is a virtual-mode count setter). grep -ri 'DeleteChildren|ExpandParents|MakeVisible|MultiSelectGroup' over source/ returned nothing; :515 ScrollIntoView is the MakeVisible equivalent but does NOT expand collapsed ancestors (:1447-1504 only adjusts FOffsetY).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3138 DeleteChildren; :3141 ExpandParents; :3143 MakeVisible; :3145 MultiSelectGroup.
user_impact: Refreshing one branch means deleting children one by one, and revealing a node found by search does not open its ancestors — the node stays invisible.

member: DisplayRect / DisplayTextLeft / DisplayExpandSignRect / Node.Top / Node.Bottom / GetNodeWithExpandSignAt
what_it_does: Per-node geometry: the row rect, the text-only rect, the expander rect, and the node's absolute Y — used for custom hit-tests, in-place editors and drag feedback.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:548 `function GetCellRect(Node, Column; out ACellRect): Boolean` covers the cell rect only (device px, visible nodes only — returns False for a scrolled-off node). Text-only and expander rects are computed inside protected helpers (:415 CellTextRect, :393 InternalCellRect) and are not public; a node's absolute top is only available as the out-param of :497 GetNodeAt(Y, out ANodeTop). grep -ri 'DisplayRect|DisplayTextLeft|DisplayExpandSign' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3100 DisplayRect(TextOnly); :3102 DisplayTextLeft; :3097 DisplayExpandSignRect; :3096/:3098 DisplayExpandSignLeft/Right; :3176 Top; :3092 Bottom; :3717 GetNodeWithExpandSignAt.
user_impact: Custom overlays/tooltips anchored to a node's text (not its whole cell) cannot be positioned, and off-screen node geometry is unavailable.

what_it_does: Standard hit-test result set (htOnItem, htOnButton, htOnIcon, htOnLabel, htOnIndent, htNowhere, htOnRight...).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:554/:556 `GetNodeAtPoint(X, Y; out APart: TTyTreeHitPart[; out AColumn])` with :12-14 TTyTreeHitPart = (hpNowhere, hpButton, hpImage, hpLabel, hpIndent, hpHeaderSection, hpHeaderDivider, hpCheckBox); tyControls.ListView.pas:476 `GetHitPart(X, Y): TTyListHitPart` with tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:47 TTyListHitPart = (lhpNowhere, lhpIcon, lhpLabel, lhpCheck, lhpHeader, lhpDivider). grep -ri 'GetHitTestInfoAt|THitTests' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3715 `function GetHitTestInfoAt(X, Y: Integer): THitTests` (TCustomTreeView); :1637 same on TCustomListView; also :3716 GetNodeAt(X, Y) whose 2-arg form ours does not have (see separate entry).
user_impact: Ported hit-test code (`if htOnButton in Tree.GetHitTestInfoAt(X,Y)`) will not compile; the enums are single-valued, so 'on item AND on label' cannot be expressed.

what_it_does: Returns the node at a client point.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:497 `function GetNodeAt(Y: Integer; out ANodeTop: Integer): PTyTreeNode` — the SAME NAME with a different meaning: the first argument is Y (not X) and the second is an out-param, not a coordinate. The X,Y form is spelled :554 GetNodeAtPoint.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3716 `function GetNodeAt(X, Y: Integer): TTreeNode`.
user_impact: `Tree.GetNodeAt(X, Y)` compiles against ours (Y is taken as the scroll-space Y, X's value is written into ANodeTop) and returns the wrong node instead of failing — the worst kind of porting break.

what_it_does: Fires before the selection moves; setting AllowChange := False cancels it (e.g. 'you have unsaved edits on this node').
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas events :617-659 include OnChange (:624), OnFocusChanged (:625), OnSelectionChanged (:630) — all post-facto notifications — plus vetoable OnExpanding/OnCollapsing (:620/:622) and OnChecking (:627), so the veto pattern exists in this control but not for selection. grep -ril 'OnChanging' over source/ hits Grid, TabSet, TabStrip — never TreeView/ListView.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3669 `property OnChanging: TTVChangingEvent read FOnChanging write FOnChanging` (published TTreeView :3864); type :2928-2929 with `var AllowChange: Boolean`; gate :3564 CanChange.
user_impact: You cannot keep the user on a node with pending edits; the selection has already moved by the time you hear about it.

what_it_does: Fires when a node is added, when one is about to be freed (release app-side data), and when any node property changed (with a TTreeNodeChangeReason).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:617 has `OnFreeNode` (the OnDeletion analogue) but nothing for addition or per-node change: grep -ri 'OnAddition|OnDeletion|OnNodeChanged' over source/ returned nothing. The published event list is :617-659.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3663 OnAddition; :3678 OnDeletion; :3690 OnNodeChanged (reason enum :2910-2922).
user_impact: An app mirroring the tree into its own model gets no add/change notifications, only OnFreeNode.

member: OnCustomDraw / OnCustomDrawItem / OnAdvancedCustomDraw / OnAdvancedCustomDrawItem (whole-control and staged draw)
what_it_does: Custom drawing of the whole control or a whole node row, with pre/post stages and a DefaultDraw veto, plus PaintImages control.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:639-640 publishes OnDrawNode and OnAfterCellPaint — both are per-CELL and post-composite (documented at :148-166: OnDrawNode fires only when toOwnerDraw is in Options, OnAfterCellPaint is an overlay, and OnBeforeCellPaint is explicitly DEFERRED/not implemented). There is no whole-row or whole-control hook, no stage argument and no DefaultDraw veto. grep -ri 'OnCustomDraw|OnAdvancedCustomDraw' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3675 OnCustomDraw; :3676 OnCustomDrawItem; :3664 OnAdvancedCustomDraw; :3666 OnAdvancedCustomDrawItem (types :2946-2957, stages via TCustomDrawStage).
user_impact: You cannot repaint a whole row (e.g. a full-width status band behind the node) or draw beneath the default content — only after it, cell by cell.

what_it_does: OnEdited hands back the edited string for validation/rewrite; OnEditingEnd fires once whether the edit was committed or cancelled (Cancel: Boolean).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:655 `OnNewText: TTyTreeNewTextEvent` — different name and, per :98-99, `const NewText: string` (NOT var), so the handler cannot rewrite/normalise the committed text; :656 OnEditCancelled covers only the cancel half. grep -ri 'OnEditingEnd' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3679 `property OnEdited: TTVEditedEvent` with type :2937-2938 `var S: string`; :3681 OnEditingEnd with type :2935-2936 `Cancel: Boolean`.
user_impact: An edit cannot be validated-and-corrected on commit (the text is const), and 'the editor closed, re-enable my buttons' needs two handlers instead of one.

what_it_does: Function event asked whether a node has children, so a lazy tree can show an expander without materialising the children.
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:619 OnInitChildren + :618 OnInitNode with :54-55 TTyNodeInitState = (ivsHasChildren, ivsExpanded, ivsSelected, ivsReInit) — the has-children answer is a flag returned once from OnInitNode, not a re-askable function. grep -ri 'OnHasChildren|NodeHasChildren' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3688-3689 `property OnHasChildren: TTVHasChildrenEvent`; type :2962-2963 `function(...): Boolean`; :3628 NodeHasChildren.
user_impact: A node that gains children later (a directory that becomes non-empty) cannot be re-asked; you must re-init the node with ivsReInit.

what_it_does: LCL's OnDragOver is the standard drag-and-drop hook: procedure(Sender, Source: TObject; X, Y: Integer; State: TDragState; var Accept: Boolean).
ours_evidence: tyControls.TreeView.pas:658 publishes `OnDragOver: TTyTreeDragOverEvent` — declared at :110-111 as `procedure(Sender: TTyTreeView; Src, Target: PTyTreeNode; Mode: TTyTreeDropMode; var Allowed: Boolean)`. Same published name as TControl.OnDragOver, completely different signature, and it only fires for the internal toNodeDrag gesture (:31-33, :285).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3878 `property OnDragOver;` on TTreeView (the inherited TControl event, TDragOverEvent); DragOver override at :3612-3613.
user_impact: You cannot use the tree as an LCL drop target at all — the property that would do it is taken by an unrelated internal event, and assigning a normal TDragOverEvent handler is a type error.

member: DragMode / DragKind / DragCursor / OnDragDrop / OnStartDrag / OnEndDrag
what_it_does: The standard LCL drag-and-drop surface: start a drag automatically, choose the drag cursor, accept drops, and be notified at start/end.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'DragMode' over source/ hits only tyControls.CoolBar.pas and tyControls.Memo.pas; 'OnDragDrop|OnStartDrag' hit only tyControls.Memo.pas. tyControls.Base.pas:196-245 (TTyCustomControl published) publishes no drag members, and neither tree (:585-660) nor list (:492-546) adds them; the tree's only drag is the internal node-reorder machine (:267-286, :580-584).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3814-3816 DragKind/DragCursor/DragMode and :3877/:3882/:3908 OnDragDrop/OnEndDrag/OnStartDrag on TTreeView; :1711-1713 and :1768-1797 the same on TListView.
user_impact: Dragging a node/row out to another control (or dropping a file onto the list) is impossible without subclassing — the whole DnD contract is unpublished.

what_it_does: Horizontal wheel / trackpad-swipe scrolling and its events.
ours_evidence: grep -rn 'DoMouseWheelHorz|OnMouseWheelHorz|WheelLeft|WheelRight' over the whole source/ returned NOTHING — the library has no horizontal-wheel support anywhere. tyControls.Base.pas:121-124 publishes OnMouseWheel/OnMouseWheelUp/OnMouseWheelDown only; the tree overrides only :445 DoMouseWheel (list :450).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3901-3903 OnMouseWheelHorz/Left/Right on TTreeView (override DoMouseWheelHorz at :3607-3608); :1790-1792 on TListView; :4156-4158 on THeaderControl.
user_impact: A wide report tree/list cannot be scrolled sideways with a trackpad or tilt-wheel — only by dragging the horizontal bar.

what_it_does: Selected returns (or sets) the selected ITEM OBJECT; ItemFocused is the focused item; LastSelected the previous one.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:472 `property Selected[AIndex: Integer]: Boolean read GetSelected write SetSelected` — same name, indexed Boolean; the focused row is :491 `ItemIndex: Integer` (an index, not an item). grep -ri 'ItemFocused|LastSelected' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1684 `property Selected: TListItem read GetSelection write SetSelection`; :1673 ItemFocused; :1685 LastSelected.
user_impact: `if LV.Selected <> nil then Edit1.Text := LV.Selected.Caption` — the canonical ListView idiom — does not port; ours is an index-first API throughout.

what_it_does: A second, independent icon per row drawn from a state image list (status lights, overlay marks) beside the main icon.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:55-89 TTyListItem has Caption/SubItems/ImageIndex/GroupIndex/Data/States only — no StateIndex; the control publishes just :513-514 LargeImages/SmallImages. grep -ri 'StateIndex|StateImages' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1085 `property StateIndex: TImageIndex read GetStateIndex write SetStateIndex`; :1597-1598 StateImages/StateImagesWidth (published TListView :1741-1742).
user_impact: Row status marks (the classic sync/error overlay column) cannot be drawn; only one image per row exists.

what_it_does: An icon per sub-item, so columns 1..N can each carry a small image.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:83 SubItems is a plain TStrings and :84 ImageIndex is a single value for the row; the virtual accessor :411 `GetItemImageIndex(AIndex, AColumn)` takes a column and the event :155-156 OnGetItemImage carries AColumn — but the collection item has no per-sub-item image storage, so only OwnerData/override mode can vary an icon by column. grep -ri 'SubItemImages' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1087 `property SubItemImages[const AIndex: Integer]: Integer read GetSubItemImages write SetSubItemImages`; storage via :1034/:1052.
user_impact: With the built-in Items collection you cannot put an icon in a non-first column (e.g. a per-column status glyph).

what_it_does: The on-screen rect of a row, its icon, its label or its select-bounds — and the same for a sub-item cell.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:55-89 TTyListItem has no geometry methods, and the control exposes NO public item-rect function: the public API is :475-480 GetItemAt/GetHitPart/ScrollIntoView/AutoFitColumn. The real geometry lives in tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:140 `TyListItemRect(ADisplayPos, ACount, M, ...)`, which needs a TTyListMetrics and a DISPLAY position — and both the metrics (:404 CurrentMetrics) and the index mapping (:389 DisplayToItem) are PROTECTED. grep -ri 'DisplayRect|ItemRect' over source/ finds only the internal TyListItemRect/TyListGroupItemRect uses.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1067 `function DisplayRect(Code: TDisplayCode): TRect`; :1068 DisplayRectSubItem; :986 TDisplayCode = (drBounds, drIcon, drLabel, drSelectBounds).
user_impact: You cannot position a popup, badge or custom editor over a row — the control knows every rect but hands none of them out.

what_it_does: Free placement of icons in icon view: read or set an item's pixel position (drag icons anywhere, save the arrangement).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:55-89 TTyListItem has no position fields; every cell rect is derived from the display position by tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:140 TyListItemRect (auto-flow grid, see the flow table at :34-36). grep -ri 'AutoArrange|IconOptions' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1083 `property Position: TPoint read GetPosition write SetPosition`; :1080 Left; :1088 Top.
user_impact: lvsIcon is always an auto-arranged grid — a desktop-like view where the user drags icons to arbitrary spots is impossible.

what_it_does: Read/write an item's display state directly on the item: focused, drop-target highlight, selected.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:46 `TTyListItemState = (lisChecked, lisCut, lisDisabled)` — no focused/selected/drop-target member; :79 States is the whole per-item state surface. Selection/focus live on the control instead (:472 Selected[idx], :491 ItemIndex) and there is no drop-target concept at all (grep -ri 'DropTarget' over source/ hits only tyControls.TreeView.pas's internal drag state).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1077 Focused; :1076 DropTarget; :1084 Selected; :1070 GetStates; :980 TListItemState = (lisCut, lisDropTarget, lisFocused, lisSelected).
user_impact: A drag-over row cannot be highlighted, and item-centric code (`Item.Selected := True`) must be rewritten against the control's index API.

what_it_does: Search the items for a caption (partial/whole, wrapping, from an index) or for a Data pointer.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:94-109 TTyListItems adds only Add/Items[]/OnChange on top of TCollection (which gives Clear/Delete/Insert/Exchange/Move/Count/BeginUpdate/EndUpdate — classesh.inc:548-567 — but no search). grep -ri 'FindCaption|FindData' over source/ returned nothing. The control has a type-ahead prefix matcher (tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:197 TyListPrefixMatch) but it is used only from the private :344 GetDisplayText path.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1175-1179 `function FindCaption(StartIndex, Value, Partial, Inclusive, Wrap, PartStart): TListItem; function FindData(...)` (also on the control at :1634/:1636).
user_impact: 'Select the row for this record' needs a manual loop, even though the control already has a prefix matcher inside.

what_it_does: The row image lists.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:513-514 `property LargeImages: TTyVirtualImageList ...; property SmallImages: TTyVirtualImageList ...` — and tyControls.ImageCollection.pas:168 declares `TTyVirtualImageList = class(TTyComponent)`, i.e. NOT a TCustomImageList descendant at all. So a plain LCL TImageList cannot be assigned. (The tree, by contrast, takes a TImageList — tyControls.TreeView.pas:599 — so the two controls in this same group disagree.)
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1586 `property LargeImages: TCustomImageList index Ord(lvilLarge) read GetImageList write SetImageList`; :1592 SmallImages (published TListView :1722/:1736).
user_impact: Every app that already has a TImageList of file icons must rebuild it as a TTyImageCollection + TTyVirtualImageList before it can show any icon in the list.

what_it_does: The report columns collection, plus index shortcuts.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:503 `property Header: TTyHeader read FHeader write SetHeader` — columns are reached as LV.Header.Columns (tyControls.Columns.pas:211 `property Columns: TTyColumns read FColumns`), and the item class is TTyColumn (:52) not TListColumn. There is no Columns property and no Column[i]/ColumnCount shortcut; grep -ri 'ColumnCount' over source/ finds none on the list.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1582 `property Columns: TListColumns read FColumns write SetColumns` (published TListView :1708); :1664 Column[AIndex]; :1665 ColumnCount.
user_impact: LV.Columns[0].Width := 120 and LV.ColumnCount do not compile; the extra Header hop also changes what the .lfm looks like, so designer files are not portable.

what_it_does: A column that keeps itself sized to its content/caption automatically.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Columns.pas:87-97 TTyColumn publishes Width/MinWidth/MaxWidth/Position/Alignment/CaptionAlignment/Text/ImageIndex/Options/Tag — no AutoSize. The nearest facilities are the one-shot method tyControls.ListView.pas:480 `AutoFitColumn(AColumn)`, the single-column tyControls.Columns.pas:215 `AutoSizeIndex` (one column absorbs slack) and :26 coAutoSpring (proportional resize) — none of which re-fit to content when data changes.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1247 `property AutoSize: Boolean read FAutoSize write SetAutoSize default False`; :1580 AutoWidthLastColumn (published TListView :1702).
user_impact: Columns do not re-fit when the data changes; AutoFitColumn must be called by hand after every refresh, and AutoWidthLastColumn has to be emulated via Header.AutoSizeIndex.

what_it_does: Each column carries its own siNone/siAscending/siDescending arrow, optionally maintained automatically on sort.
ours_evidence: tyControls.Columns.pas has no per-column sort state; the arrow is driven by the single header-level pair :213-214 `SortColumn: Integer` / `SortDirection: TTySortDirection` and drawn only for that one column (tyControls.ListView.pas:2638 `if (hoShowSortGlyphs in FHeader.Options) and (col.Index = FSortColumn)`). grep -ri 'SortIndicator|AutoSortIndicator' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1255 `property SortIndicator: TSortIndicator read FSortIndicator write SetSortIndicator default siNone`; :1208 TSortIndicator; :1579 AutoSortIndicator (published TListView :1701).
user_impact: A multi-key sort (or an indicator on a column that is not the active sort key) cannot be shown.

what_it_does: An icon in a column header, next to the caption.
ours_evidence: The model HAS the properties — tyControls.Columns.pas:95 `property ImageIndex: Integer ... default -1` and :216 `property Images: TCustomImageList read FImages write FImages` — but nothing paints them: grep -n 'ImageIndex' tyControls.ListView.pas shows hits only for TTyListItem/row images (:59-84, :156, :411), and grep -n 'Header.Images|FHeader.Images' over tyControls.ListView.pas AND tyControls.TreeView.pas returned NOTHING. The header renderers (ListView.pas:354 RenderHeader / :2625-2650; TreeView.pas header band) draw caption + sort glyph only.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1249 `property ImageIndex: TImageIndex read FImageIndex write SetImageIndex default -1` on TListColumn (drawn by the widgetset header).
user_impact: Setting Header.Images and a column's ImageIndex looks like it should work and silently draws nothing — a built-but-unwired capability.

what_it_does: Icon / small-icon / list / report view selection.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:493 `property ViewStyle: TTyListViewStyle ... default lvsReport`, enum at tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:36 `TTyListViewStyle = (lvsIcon, lvsSmallIcon, lvsList, lvsReport, lvsTile)` — different identifiers (lvs* vs vs*) and a different DEFAULT (lvsReport vs LCL vsList).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1600 `property ViewStyle: TViewStyle read FViewStyle write SetViewStyle default vsList`; :1287 TViewStyle = (vsIcon, vsSmallIcon, vsList, vsReport).
user_impact: `LV.ViewStyle := vsReport` does not compile, and a control left at its default shows a report instead of a list — a silent layout change on port.

what_it_does: SortType (stNone/stData/stText/stBoth) selects what auto-sorting compares; AlphaSort sorts column 0 ascending; CustomSort takes a plain compare function.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:511 `property SortKind: TTyListSortKind ... default lskText` with tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:42 `TTyListSortKind = (lskText, lskNumber, lskDateTime)` — a different name and different axis (cell TYPE, not text-vs-data); :464 `procedure Sort` and :512 AutoSort exist, but grep -ri 'AlphaSort|CustomSort|SortType' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1594 `property SortType: TSortType ... default stNone`; :978 TSortType; :1627 AlphaSort; :1629 CustomSort(ASortProc: TLVCompare; AOptionalParam: PtrInt).
user_impact: LV.SortType := stText does not compile; sorting by the item Data pointer (stData) has no equivalent, and a non-method compare function cannot be used.

what_it_does: The published owner-draw surface: OwnerDraw switches it on, OnDrawItem draws a whole report row, and the custom-draw family gives per-item/per-subitem/staged hooks with a DefaultDraw veto.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas has NO published draw event (published list :493-546). The only seam is the PROTECTED virtual :437-438 `procedure RenderItem(P: TTyPainter; AIndex; const ACell; const AStyle; AStates); virtual;` — subclassing is the only way in. grep -ri 'OwnerDraw' over source/ hits only tyControls.TreeView.pas (its toOwnerDraw option + OnDrawNode/OnAfterCellPaint at :639-640), so the tree got a draw event and the list did not.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1588 OwnerDraw (published TListView :1726); :1619 OnDrawItem (published :1770); :1616-1618 OnCustomDraw/Item/SubItem; :1620-1622 OnAdvancedCustomDraw*.
user_impact: Custom row rendering in a list requires deriving a new class, while the sibling tree control can do it with a handler — an inconsistency inside this very group.

what_it_does: OnChange says WHICH item changed and HOW (ctText/ctImage/ctState); OnChanging can veto the change.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:535 `property OnChange: TNotifyEvent read FOnChange write FOnChange` — Sender only, no item, no reason, and there is no OnChanging at all (grep -ril 'OnChanging' over source/ hits Grid/TabSet/TabStrip, not ListView). :338 DoChange fires it unconditionally.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1601 `property OnChange: TLVChangeEvent` with type :1292-1293 `(Sender; Item: TListItem; Change: TItemChange)`; :1602 OnChanging with `var AllowChange: Boolean` (:1294-1295); :1286 TItemChange.
user_impact: A handler cannot tell which row or what aspect changed (so it must re-scan everything), and a change cannot be refused.

what_it_does: Fires when an item is inserted, and when one is about to be deleted (release the Data payload).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas published events :528-540 are OnGetItemText/Image/State, OnCompare, OnColumnClick, OnItemActivate, OnSelectItem, OnChange, OnItemChecked, OnEditing, OnEdited, OnGetItemGroup, OnGroupCollapsed — no insert/delete notification; TTyListItems.Notify (:102) only forwards to :108 OnChange internally. grep -ri 'OnInsert|OnDeletion' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1613 OnInsert (published TListView :1777); :1610 OnDeletion (published :1767); type :1313/:1320.
user_impact: Items carrying an owned object in Data leak: there is no hook to free it when the row goes away.

what_it_does: Virtual-mode support beyond text: OnDataHint pre-fetches a visible index window, OnDataFind resolves searches in the app's store, OnDataStateChange reports selection/state changes over a range.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas OwnerData mode (:500) is served by :528-530 OnGetItemText/OnGetItemImage/OnGetItemState (the OnData analogue) only; grep -ri 'OnDataHint|OnDataFind|OnDataStateChange' over source/ returned nothing. The protected intake (:409-418) has no range/prefetch entry point either.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1608 OnDataHint (type :1302); :1607 OnDataFind (type :1297-1300); :1609 OnDataStateChange (type :1303-1304) — all published on TListView :1763-1765.
user_impact: A million-row virtual list cannot batch-fetch the visible window (one call per cell instead), and search/selection in virtual mode has no delegation point.

what_it_does: Lets the app supply its own TListItem descendant so rows can carry typed fields.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:105 `constructor Create(AOwner: TPersistent)` fixes the item class (implementation passes TTyListItem) and there is no hook to override it; grep -ri 'OnCreateItemClass' over source/ returned nothing. Note the library DOES have this pattern elsewhere — tyControls.Columns.pas:126 `constructor Create(AOwnerHeader; AItemClass: TCollectionItemClass)` — so the capability exists and is not wired here.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1605 `property OnCreateItemClass: TLVCreateItemClassEvent` (type :1342, published TListView :1758); :1526 CreateListItem virtual.
user_impact: Row payloads must go through the untyped Data pointer instead of a typed item subclass.

what_it_does: Fires for both select AND deselect, with a Selected: Boolean saying which.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:534 `property OnSelectItem: TTyListItemEvent` with type :162 `procedure(Sender: TObject; AIndex: Integer)` — no selected/deselected flag; :339 DoSelectItem fires it only when an item becomes current.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1615 `property OnSelectItem: TLVSelectItemEvent`; type :1323-1324 `(Sender; Item: TListItem; Selected: Boolean)`.
user_impact: A handler cannot tell selection from deselection, so multi-select bookkeeping has to re-scan the whole selection on every event.

what_it_does: Icon-view layout options: icons arranged top-down or left-right, auto re-arrange, and whether long captions wrap.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'IconOptions|AutoArrange' over source/ returned nothing; 'WrapText' hits only Notification/Painter/TyLabel. Flow direction is hard-coded per view style (tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:34-36 'Flow direction is derived from the style, see the table in TyListItemRect') and there is no wrap/arrangement switch on tyControls.ListView.pas:493-546.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:992 TIconOptions = class(TPersistent) with :1007 Arrangement (iaTop/iaLeft), :1008 AutoArrange, :1009 WrapText; :1672 `property IconOptions: TIconOptions read FIconOptions write SetIconOptions` (published TListView :1718).
user_impact: Icon view is take-it-or-leave-it: no left-to-right arrangement and no caption wrapping, so long file names are simply clipped.

what_it_does: Viewport queries (first visible item, how many rows fit, the bounding rect of all items) and the readable/writable scroll origin.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas keeps the offsets PRIVATE (:221 `FOffsetX, FOffsetY: Integer`) and exposes no accessor at all — the public API is :458-491 (BeginUpdate…ItemIndex) with :477 ScrollIntoView the only way to move the view; even the scrollbars are protected (:400-401). grep -ri 'TopItem|VisibleRowCount|BoundingRect|ViewOrigin' over source/ finds TopItem only in tyControls.Menu.pas and VisibleRowCount only in Grid/ValueListEditor. (The tree at least publishes read-only OffsetX/OffsetY — TreeView.pas:529-530.)
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1687 TopItem; :1689 VisibleRowCount; :1660 BoundingRect; :1688 `property ViewOrigin: TPoint read GetViewOrigin write SetViewOrigin`.
user_impact: Saving and restoring a list's scroll position across a refresh is impossible, and page-sized navigation cannot be computed by the app.

what_it_does: Find the item nearest to a point in a given direction, and step from an item in a direction filtered by state — the primitives behind icon-view arrow navigation.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas public hit-testing is :475-476 GetItemAt(X,Y)/GetHitPart(X,Y) — an exact hit only. Directional stepping exists as the pure tyControls.ListView.Layout.pas:176 `TyListNavigate(ACurrent, ACount, AKey: TTyListNavKey, ...)` but it is used only from the control's KeyDown (:448) and takes display positions, not points or state filters; grep -ri 'GetNearestItem|GetNextItem' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1645 GetNearestItem(APoint, Direction); :1651 GetNextItem(StartItem, Direction, States); :1290 TSearchDirection.
user_impact: 'Select the item nearest where the user clicked/dropped' and state-filtered stepping must be reimplemented from the layout primitives.

what_it_does: Control-level convenience: empty the list, and append a captioned row with a payload in one call.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas public methods :458-489 include BeginUpdate/EndUpdate/ItemsChanged/Sort/SelCount/SelectAll/ClearSelection/GetNextSelected/GetItemAt/GetHitPart/ScrollIntoView/AutoFitColumn/Editing/BeginEdit/EndEdit — no Clear and no AddItem (grep -n 'procedure Clear' tyControls.ListView.pas returns only :333 ClearAllBits and :469 ClearSelection). You must go through Items.Clear / Items.Add plus field assignment.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1631 `procedure Clear;`; :1626 `procedure AddItem(Item: string; AObject: TObject);`
user_impact: LV.Clear — used in nearly every refresh routine — does not compile; it also does not reset ItemCount in OwnerData mode, which Items.Clear cannot do.

what_it_does: How hot-tracking looks: hand cursor, underline always, or underline on hover.
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:507 has the on/off `HotTrack: Boolean` only; hover styling is whatever the theme's TyListViewItem:hover resolves to (:340 StatesFor). grep -ri 'HotTrackStyles' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1671 `property HotTrackStyles: TListHotTrackStyles read FHotTrackStyles write SetHotTrackStyles default []`; :1366-1367 TListHotTrackStyle = (htHandPoint, htUnderlineCold, htUnderlineHot).
user_impact: A web-style link list (hand cursor + underline on hover) cannot be configured per control; only the theme can change it globally.

what_it_does: Whether the user can rename a row in place (F2 / click-on-label).
ours_evidence: tyControls.ListView.pas:521 `property ReadOnly: Boolean read FReadOnly write FReadOnly default True` — inverted relative to LCL, and documented as deliberate at :519-520 ('Inline rename is opt-in, like TTyTreeView's toEditable and UNLIKE LCL TListView.ReadOnly=False').
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:1681 `property ReadOnly: Boolean index Ord(lvpReadOnly) read GetProperty write SetProperty default False` (published TListView :1731).
user_impact: A ported form that never mentions ReadOnly loses inline rename silently — the .lfm streams nothing, so nothing hints at the change.

member: Sections as a collection of section OBJECTS
what_it_does: THeaderSections is a TCollection of THeaderSection (TCollectionItem) — editable in the Object Inspector, streamed into the .lfm, addressable as objects with per-section properties, Add/Insert/Delete/AddItem.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:28-34 `TTyHeaderSection = record Text; Width; Alignment; SortDirection; end;` + `TTyHeaderSectionArray = array of TTyHeaderSection`, stored in :62 FSections. Access is by value through :108 `property Sections[AIndex: Integer]: TTyHeaderSection read GetSection write SetSection` (getter :287 returns a COPY, so you must read-modify-write the whole record), and nothing is published for streaming — the published list is :113-125 (OnSectionClick/OnSectionResize/OnSectionTrack/TabStop/Align). grep -rn 'TTyHeaderControl' over source/ shows the control is used nowhere else, and the library's own collection-based header model (tyControls.Columns.pas:52 TTyColumn / :103 TTyColumns / :171 TTyHeader) is NOT wired to it.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3956 THeaderSection = class(TCollectionItem); :4004 THeaderSections = class(TCollection) with :4014-4018 Add/AddItem/Insert/Delete/Items[]; :4099 `property Sections: THeaderSections read FSections write SetSections` (published THeaderControl :4134).
user_impact: A THeaderControl is normally set up entirely in the designer and saved in the .lfm; TTyHeaderControl must be filled by code in FormCreate every time, and its sections cannot be edited, streamed, subclassed or referenced as objects.

what_it_does: An icon in a header section, from an image list on the control.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:28-33 the section record has Text/Width/Alignment/SortDirection only, and the control publishes no Images (:113-125). The paint path :89 RenderTo / :155+ draws caption + divider + sort triangle. The capability exists elsewhere in the library and is simply not connected here: tyControls.Columns.pas:216 `property Images: TCustomImageList` and :95 `property ImageIndex: Integer` (which, as noted separately, no renderer consumes either).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4097 `property Images: TCustomImageList read FImages write SetImages`; :4098 ImagesWidth; :3991 `property ImageIndex: TImageIndex ... default -1` on THeaderSection (published THeaderControl :4131-4132).
user_impact: No icons in a standalone header strip at all.

what_it_does: Per-section resize constraints, enforced during the drag.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:28-33 the record has no min/max; the only floor is the unit-wide const :15 `TyHeaderMinSectionWidth = 16` applied in :322 SetSectionWidth / the resize path (:92 MouseMove). By contrast the shared column model does have them (tyControls.Columns.pas:89-90 MinWidth default 10 / MaxWidth default 10000) — again not wired to this control.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3992-3993 `property MaxWidth: Integer ... default 10000; property MinWidth: Integer ... default 0`; enforcement :3978 CheckConstraints.
user_impact: You cannot pin a narrow fixed-width section (a 24px checkbox column) or cap a wide one; every section shares one 16px floor.

what_it_does: Hide a section without deleting it, so column visibility can be toggled and restored.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:28-33 the record has no Visible flag, and the tiler walks every entry (:86 DeviceWidths -> :133 TyHeaderSectionRects). Deleting is the only way to remove one (:99 DeleteSection), which loses its width and sort state. The shared column model has coVisible (tyControls.Columns.pas:22) — not available here.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3996 `property Visible: Boolean read FVisible write SetVisible default true`; setter :3975.
user_impact: A 'choose columns' menu cannot hide/show sections; it must delete and rebuild them.

what_it_does: The on-screen left/right edge of a section — needed to align a control or a popup under it.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas public surface :98-112 offers SectionCount/Sections[]/SectionText[]/SectionWidth[]/Sort[]/ScaledGrip/AddSection/DeleteSection/ClearSections/ToggleSort — no per-section rect. The geometry is only reachable as the unit-level pure function :133 `TyHeaderSectionRects(const AWidths: array of Integer; const AClient: TRect)`, i.e. the caller must first build the device-width array itself (:86 DeviceWidths is PRIVATE). grep -ri 'OriginalIndex|GetSectionAt' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3984-3985 `property Left: Integer read GetLeft; property Right: Integer read GetRight;`
user_impact: Placing a filter box or a dropdown under section N requires re-deriving the whole tiling by hand.

what_it_does: Query/force a section's visual state, and address a section by an index that survives user reordering.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas keeps the hover state private (:63 `FHotIndex: Integer`) with no accessor, has no pressed state at all, and no stable identity for a section (order == array position, :62). grep -ri 'OriginalIndex|SectionFromOriginalIndex' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:3986 `property State: THeaderSectionState read FState write SetState`; :3950-3955 THeaderSectionState; :3988 OriginalIndex; :4084 `property SectionFromOriginalIndex[OriginalIndex: Integer]: THeaderSection`.
user_impact: Nothing can be keyed to a section reliably once positions move, and the pressed/hot state cannot be read for coordinated painting.

what_it_does: Lets the user drag sections into a new order, with a vetoable OnSectionDrag(FromSection, ToSection, var AllowDrag) and an end-of-drag notification.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'DragReorder|OnSectionDrag|OnSectionEndDrag' over source/ returned nothing. tyControls.HeaderControl.pas MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp (:91-93) implement click-to-sort and divider-resize only. The library HAS a full column drag-reorder engine — tyControls.TreeView.pas:310-316 (FDragColumn/FDragPending/FDragging/FDragTargetPos) + :648 OnColumnReorder, gated by hoDrag/coDraggable (tyControls.Columns.pas:38/:25) — so the capability exists but the standalone header control does not use it.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4096 `property DragReorder: boolean read FDragReorder write FDragReorder`; :4101 OnSectionDrag (type :4023-4024); :4103 OnSectionEndDrag; :4071 SectionDrag.
user_impact: Users cannot reorder columns on a standalone header strip, although they can on TTyTreeView — an inconsistency inside the library.

what_it_does: Fires when the user double-clicks a divider — the standard 'auto-fit this column' gesture.
ours_evidence: grep -ri 'OnSectionSeparatorDblClick' over source/ returned nothing; tyControls.HeaderControl.pas does not even override DblClick (protected list :89-94 is RenderTo/Paint/MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp/MouseLeave). The gesture exists on the list — tyControls.ListView.pas:478-480 'Also bound to a double-click on the column's right divider' → AutoFitColumn — so again the concept is present elsewhere and missing here.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4110-4111 `property OnSectionSeparatorDblClick: TCustomSectionNotifyEvent`; :4069 SectionSeparatorDblClick; :4090 DblClick override.
user_impact: Double-clicking a divider on a TTyHeaderControl does nothing; there is no hook to auto-size the section.

what_it_does: Public hit-test: which section is at this client point.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas public methods :98-112 contain no hit-test; the pure function :138 `TyHeaderSectionAtX(const AWidths; const AClient; X)` is unit-level and needs the device-width array from the PRIVATE :86 DeviceWidths. grep -ri 'GetSectionAt' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4091 `function GetSectionAt(P: TPoint): Integer;`
user_impact: A context menu on the header cannot tell which section was right-clicked without re-deriving the tiling.

what_it_does: Per-section paint seam a descendant overrides to draw one section its own way.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:89-90 has only whole-strip `RenderTo(ACanvas, ARect, APPI)` and `Paint`; the per-section loop is inside RenderTo (implementation from :155 onward) with no virtual hook and no draw event (published list :113-125). grep -ri 'PaintSection' over source/ returned nothing.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4093 `procedure PaintSection(Index: Integer); virtual;`
user_impact: Customising one section's look means rewriting the whole strip renderer.

what_it_does: Collection-style section management, including inserting at a position.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:98-100 `function AddSection(const AText: string; AWidth: Integer = TyHeaderDefaultSectionWidth): Integer; procedure DeleteSection(AIndex: Integer); procedure ClearSections;` — different names, and there is NO insert-at-position (grep -n 'Insert' tyControls.HeaderControl.pas returns nothing).
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4014-4017 `function Add: THeaderSection; function AddItem(Item, Index): THeaderSection; function Insert(Index): THeaderSection; procedure Delete(Index);`
user_impact: Header setup code does not port (HC.Sections.Add.Text := 'x' → HC.AddSection('x')), and adding a section anywhere but the end requires rebuilding the strip.

what_it_does: LCL passes the HeaderControl and the THeaderSection object; OnSectionTrack additionally reports the phase (tsTrackBegin / tsTrackMove / tsTrackEnd).
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas:37-40 `TTyHeaderSectionEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; AIndex: Integer)` and `TTyHeaderResizeEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject; AIndex, AWidth: Integer)`, used at :114/:119/:121 — index-based (no section object, consistent with the missing item class) and OnSectionTrack has no phase argument, so a handler cannot distinguish drag-start from drag-move (:120-121 documents it as 'fires continuously').
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4025-4026 TCustomSectionNotifyEvent(HeaderControl, Section); :4022 TCustomSectionTrackEvent(HeaderControl, Section, Width, State); :4021 TSectionTrackState = (tsTrackBegin, tsTrackMove, tsTrackEnd).
user_impact: Handlers do not port; and 'begin a live preview on drag-start, tear it down on drag-end' cannot be expressed — only the width stream is available.

what_it_does: Standard layout properties: anchor the strip to its parent's edges; reserve an inner border.
ours_evidence: tyControls.HeaderControl.pas published list :113-125 has Align (:124) and TabStop (:123) but NOT Anchors, and tyControls.Base.pas:196-245 (TTyCustomControl published) publishes neither Anchors nor BorderWidth. Both sibling controls in this group DO publish Anchors (tyControls.TreeView.pas:611, tyControls.ListView.pas:544), so the header is the odd one out.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4122 `property Anchors;`; :4124 `property BorderWidth;` on THeaderControl.
user_impact: A header strip cannot be anchored (e.g. left+right+top with a fixed height) in the designer — only Align-docked.

what_it_does: Right-to-left layout: sections tile from the right, captions and sort glyphs mirror.
ours_evidence: grep -ril 'BiDiMode' over the whole source/ hits only tyControls.Memo.pas (and that is a comment/pass-through, not a published property). tyControls.HeaderControl.pas tiles strictly left-to-right (:133 TyHeaderSectionRects 'Tile AWidths left-to-right across AClient'), and tyControls.Base.pas publishes no BiDi member for any control.
theirs_evidence: comctrls.pp:4123 `property BiDiMode;` and :4136 `property ParentBiDiMode;` on THeaderControl (TControl-level RTL support).
user_impact: No RTL support anywhere in this control family: an Arabic/Hebrew UI gets a left-to-right header over a left-to-right list.
